# Changelog

## 2.11.0 (unreleased)

> Modeling **full BPMN authoring** plan (eadbf967, phases 2–7). The release ships together with the
> separate BPMN 2.0 XML converter plan (decision Q6); until the owner confirms it, the packages are
> prepared (version, changelog, docs, JSON documentation, local pack + clean-host smoke test) but
> NOT tagged or published. Everything below is additive and opt-in — the migration table at the end of
> this section lists every behavior a 2.10.0 host could notice, with a before/after. It also carries the
> core `TmChart` funnel-label work (plan 8fa7319c, phase 1), the `TmScheduler` day-granularity
> timeline (phase 2) and the `TmQRCode` accessible-name/token/download work (phase 3), none of which
> depends on the Modeling release gate.

### Added — modeling authoring (`Tempo.Blazor.Abstractions`, `Tempo.Blazor.Modeling`, `Tempo.Blazor.Mcp`)

- **Change set v2 (`MODELING-AUTHORING-CHANGESET`).** `ModelingModelChangeSet` gains `AddedElements`, `AddedRelationships`, `RemovedElementIds`, `RemovedRelationshipIds`, `ViewChanges` (view nodes/connections upserts and removals), `ModelingElementChange.ParentId` (pool/lane/subprocess moves) and `ModelingRelationshipChange.SourceElementId`/`TargetElementId` (re-targeting). The `null = unchanged` rule is load-bearing: `""` clears a parent, an empty waypoint list clears routing. One save = one atomic batch whose application order (added elements parents-first → updates → removed relationships → added relationships → relationship updates → removed elements descendants-first → view changes) is owned by the new `ModelingChangeSetTranslator.ToOperationBatch`, which also rejects a self-contradictory set (an id in more than one of added/updated/removed) with `duplicate_id`. The editor expands a cascade delete itself (every descendant, every incident relationship, the per-view removals) and no writer or engine cascades silently.
- **Writer capabilities (`MODELING-WRITER-CAPABILITIES`).** `IModelingModelWriter.Capabilities` (a **default interface member** = `Content`, so every 2.10.0 writer compiles and behaves unchanged) declares `Content`, `Structure` and `Layout`. The editor gates every action on it and HIDES an action without the capability instead of rendering it disabled; `TmModelingEditor.WriterCapabilities` can only narrow what the writer advertises. A content-only host therefore never sees the palette, the edge tool, delete, the parent move or Arrange.
- **One operation engine (`MODELING-UNIFIED-OPERATION-ENGINE`).** `ModelingOperationEngine` moved from the internal `Tempo.Blazor.Mcp.Modeling` into `Tempo.Blazor.Abstractions` (namespace `Tempo.Blazor.Modeling`, no new package) and is now the single implementation behind the editor's structural/geometry commits and `modeling_apply_operations`: `Apply` (typed batch), `ApplyJson` (the MCP JSON front-end, message strings byte-compatible), `Clone`, `ValidateRelationship` (the ONE verdict the editor's type picker and the commit share) and the new `set_properties` operation. Error codes are machine-readable (`parse`, `unknown_op`, `missing_field`, `duplicate_id`, `not_found`, `parent_cycle`, `parent_not_found`, `still_referenced`, `still_has_children`, `invalid_relationship`, `unsupported_relationship`, `viewpoint_disallowed`, `property_required`, `property_type`, `property_range`, `property_pattern`, `property_enum`, `property_reference`, `unsupported_operation`) while the `Message` keeps its wording.
- **Property schema and host lookups (`MODELING-PROPERTY-SCHEMA`).** `IModelingPropertySchemaProvider` (per provider key, version pinned per pair) and `IModelingLookupProvider` (search, plus an optional `ResolveAsync` default member for label re-resolution) drive a schema-rendered inspector: ordered sections with typed fields (`String`, `MultilineText`, `Markdown`, `Integer`, `Number`, `Boolean`, `Enum`, `Date`, `DateTime`, `Duration`, `Url`, `EntityReference`, `EntityReferenceList`, `StringList`, `StructuredList`), required/type/range/pattern/enum/reference errors inline and as issues, a save gate that only counts issues the pending change set touches, and entity references stored as `{type,id,display,snapshotAt}` values. The shared `ModelingPropertySchemaValidator` is used by the inspector, the editor's save and the MCP batch; `ModelingPropertySchemaResolver.PreloadAsync` bridges the async provider into the synchronous engine. With no provider registered the inspector is exactly 2.10.0's.
- **Layout persistence and structural authoring (phases 3–4).** The authoring editor replaces the old "diagram node" palette insert with a SEMANTIC insert (`add_element` + `set_view_node`, the container's growth in the same batch), pairs every drawn edge with a `set_view_connection` under the notation rules, seeds a `"default"` view in the same transaction when the model has none, persists node moves/resizes/waypoint drags/lane drops as ONE undoable `SetModelingViewLayoutCommand` (`set_view_node` + `set_view_connection` + `update_element parentId`), resolves the layout parent by GEOMETRY with the node's subtree excluded, grows a container around a dropped child (and its ancestor pools) in the same transaction, and offers the deterministic relationship-ranked `ModelingLayoutArranger` behind the non-drag **Arrange** action (and a **Move to container** sheet). Ten keyboard nudges over one element set inside 800 ms merge into one undo step. Both embedded editors load with `SnapDocumentOnLoad="false"` so a reload never re-snaps a host's persisted layout, position-less elements are auto-placed inside their rendered container (opt-in `ModelingDiagramGenerationOptionsDto.AutoPlaceElementsWithoutViewNode`) instead of vanishing, BPMN pools/lanes render as flush bands with token-based swimlane headers, and every drag has a tap/keyboard alternative (WCAG 2.5.7).
- **`TmModelingViewer` (`MODELING-READONLY-VIEWER`).** A chrome-less read-only presentation surface (portal/documentation/diff): `Model`, `ViewId`, `FitMode` (`Width`/`Page`), `Zoom`, `ShowZoomControls`, `HighlightElementIds`, two-way `SelectedElementId`, `OnElementClick`, `DiffOverlay`, `Heatmap`, `ShowLegend`, `ShowElementList`, `ElementListContent`, `Height`, `LayoutMode`, `Class`, `AriaLabel`, plus `ExportSvgAsync(DiagramSvgTheme)` and print support. Its text alternative is a roving-tabstop button list in BFS order (a "Removed" group resolves names from `DiffOverlay.BaselineModel`), every overlay reading is also text, and the diff/heatmap paint goes through the public diagram model only (`Data["viewerState"]`, `Data["viewerBadge"]`, `Data["viewerTitle"]`, `DiagramEdge.Title`) — the new renderer reads no DiagramEditor internals.
- **Headless diff.** `ModelingModelDiff.Compute(baseline, current)` (Abstractions) returns the `ModelingDiffOverlayDto` the viewer renders: added/removed ids in model order, changed semantic fields, layout-only view geometry/membership (in ANY view; a semantic change beats a layout change), added/removed/changed relationships (the new additive `ModelingDiffOverlayDto.ChangedRelationshipIds`), property values compared by JSON value (a different kind is a change; member order is not) and `BaselineModel` for naming removed items. A host or an MCP agent can build the overlay without the Blazor package.
- **MCP parity and new tools (phase 7).** `modeling_apply_operations` now runs the SAME `ModelingOperationPolicy.Authoring` the editor's save runs: view operations (`set_view_node`, `remove_view_node`, `set_view_connection`, `remove_view_connection`) are accepted and a `ParentId` change re-validates every relationship incident to it after the batch; the tool takes an optional `viewpointRules` provider and returns the applied `diff` (ids + counts) in its success payload. New read tool `modeling_get_property_schema` returns the host's schema (sections, typed fields, constraints, lookup descriptors) resolved through the same provider rule and request shape the batch is validated with. `ModelingMcpParityTests` pins the contract: the same batch through the MCP tool and through a reference host writer yields the same model JSON and the same error messages/codes (including a missing required property, a parent move that invalidates a flow and a stale concurrency token); `ModelingMcpContractSnapshotTests` pins the exact response JSON in `tests/Tempo.Blazor.Mcp.Tests/Fixtures/modeling-mcp-contract.snapshot.json`; `ModelingMcpToolsDocumentationDriftTests` makes the MCP catalog complete.
- **Docs.** New [docs/modeling-hosting-guide.md](docs/modeling-hosting-guide.md) — the writer implementation pattern with optimistic concurrency (capabilities, atomic apply through the translator + engine, layout/view changes, schema/lookups, issue mapping, MCP wiring, verification recipe). [docs/modeling-authoring.md](docs/modeling-authoring.md) carries the design contract and §6.5 "as implemented (phase 7)"; [docs/modeling-editor.md](docs/modeling-editor.md) the component contract; [docs/modeling-mcp-tools.md](docs/modeling-mcp-tools.md) the living MCP catalog and the "What 2.11.0 changed" table; AGENTS.md gained the authoring bullet list.
- **Tests.** `ModelingModelDiffTests`, `TmModelingViewerOverlayTests` (a changed relationship), the phase 3–6 suites already in the tree, `ModelingMcpParityTests`, `ModelingViewOperationToolsTests`, `ModelingPropertySchemaToolsTests`, `ModelingMcpContractSnapshotTests`, `ModelingMcpToolsDocumentationDriftTests`; the JSON documentation overlays are regenerated and `validate --fail-on-drift` is clean.

### Added — BPMN 2.0 XML converter (plan 6fca9139, phases 1–4: design, corpus, secure import, BPMNDI layout, export and round-trip)

- Design document [docs/modeling-bpmn-xml.md](docs/modeling-bpmn-xml.md): the headless
  `Tempo.Blazor.Modeling.BpmnXml` package proposal (dependency on `Tempo.Blazor.Abstractions`
  only), the `IBpmnXmlImporter`/`IBpmnXmlExporter` API, the BPMN 2.0 XML → semantic type
  mapping table, the host/tool extension mechanism and the loss-report contract (approved —
  decision MODELING-BPMN-XML-API).
- Test corpus `tests/Tempo.Blazor.Tests/Modeling/BpmnCorpus/` — 21 hand-authored,
  license-clean BPMN 2.0 fixtures (MIT) mimicking the Camunda/Signavio/Bizagi/bpmn.io
  dialects, guarded by `BpmnCorpusTests` (safe-parse, well-formedness, unique NCName ids,
  dangling-reference and BPMNDI-presence checks), plus adversarial `Hostile/` fixtures
  (XXE, billion laughs, malformed XML, wrong root, size/depth/element-count probes).
- **Phase 2 — `Tempo.Blazor.Modeling.BpmnXml` package** (`AddTempoBpmnXml()`): safe,
  bounded, deterministic BPMN 2.0 XML → `ModelingModelDto` import. DTD prohibited and no
  XML resolver; `MaxInputBytes`/`MaxDepth`/`MaxElements` options enforced on non-seekable
  streams; malformed XML returns `HasErrors` with the line number — the importer never
  throws for bad input. Elements keep their BPMN ids (stable generated ids for anonymous
  elements), element order follows the XML, and `BpmnModelSplit.PerProcess` (default) maps
  each collaboration participant's process to its own model with pools, nested lanes and
  cross-model `messageFlow` links carrying an `externalModelRef`; `SingleWithPools` imports
  one model. Event definitions (timer/message/error/signal/escalation/compensation/
  conditional/link/terminate/cancel), `conditionExpression` → `ConditionalFlow`, gateway
  `default` → `DefaultFlow`, boundary-event `attachedToRef`/`cancelActivity` as properties
  only, data-association implicit-endpoint resolution (ioSpecification/`<property>` ids
  resolve to the enclosing activity), data objects/stores, annotations, groups and the
  catch-all attribute rule (`bpmn:*`/prefixed foreign attributes preserved verbatim in
  `Properties`). Nothing is silently dropped: unsupported or approximated constructs
  (choreography/conversation, loop characteristics, ad-hoc ordering, transaction
  compensation, unused global definitions, unrecognized extension namespaces preserved
  under `foreignExtensions`, …) land in `BpmnImportResult.Losses` with element id, XML
  path, construct, reason and severity, mirrored as `bpmn-import` issues on the owning
  model together with structural validation results (dangling flow endpoints, broken
  boundary attachments, start/end-event flow violations, duplicate ids).
- **Tests.** `BpmnXmlImporterSecurityTests` (XXE/billion-laughs/limits/malformed, the
  mandatory security suite), `BpmnXmlImporterTests` (mapping semantics, collaboration
  splits, loss report, validation issues, determinism, DI registration, catalog parity),
  `BpmnImportGoldenTests` (normalized JSON goldens for the whole corpus, regeneration via
  `TEMPO_REGENERATE_BPMN_IMPORT_GOLDEN=1`), `BpmnPackageBoundaryTests` (headless boundary:
  Abstractions-only references, no UI/server stack in the closure, not part of
  `Tempo.Blazor.All` — the DocumentFormats/Engine precedent). JSON documentation
  participates in the bundle pipeline (`tempo-blazor-bpmnxml.json`, overlays, aggregate;
  `validate --fail-on-drift` clean via `DocumentationValidationTests`).
- **Not in this phase (per the plan):** BPMNDI view import (phase 3), export/round-trip
  (phase 4), Camunda/Signavio/Bizagi tool plugins and MCP tools (phase 5). The
  `BpmnImportOptions` knobs those phases honor already exist.
- **Phase 3 — BPMNDI view import and headless auto-layout.** BPMNShape bounds import as
  view nodes and BPMNEdge waypoints as view connections: one `bpmn2` view per BPMNPlane
  (per covered model under `PerProcess`, so a collaboration plane reaches every pool model
  and a collapsed subprocess keeps its internals on their own second plane), with
  `ParentNodeId` nesting for shapes inside lane/pool/expanded-subprocess shapes per DI
  `isExpanded`. A connection is imported only when BOTH ends are nodes of that view —
  cross-model message flows keep their full DI polyline on the relationship as
  `bpmndi:waypoints` + `bpmndi:planeId` for the export round-trip instead. DI flags on
  shapes and edges (`isExpanded`, `isHorizontal`, `isMarkerVisible`,
  `messageVisibleKind`, `sourceElement`/`targetElement`, …) are preserved as `bpmndi:*`
  element/relationship properties and `BPMNLabel` bounds as `bpmndi:labelBounds` JSON
  (the `labelStyle` reference as `bpmndi:labelStyle`); `BPMNLabelStyle` definitions and
  `di:extension` payloads are reported as losses. DI referencing unknown elements, shapes
  without usable bounds and missing edges/positions are filled from the new deterministic,
  headless `BpmnAutoLayout` — `O(V+E)` with an iterative Kahn longest-path layering (no
  recursion; a 100k-node chain lays out in milliseconds), back edges ignored for ranking,
  layer blocks centred so a plain chain renders as one horizontal line, boundary events
  anchored to a separate row inside their activity's column, pools/lanes as stacked bands —
  and reported as losses/warnings, never dropped. Each missing element joins only the view
  holding its nearest semantic ancestor, offset below the view's DI bounding box, so no
  ElementId is duplicated across views. Auto-layouted connections carry NO waypoints — the
  diagram generator auto-routes them. Documents without BPMNDI (or `ImportBpmndi=false`)
  get a full auto-layout view plus a warning. Nothing breaks for hosts: `BpmnImportResult`
  only gains views inside the existing models; `BpmnModelBuilder` was split into partial
  classes to satisfy the 1200-line source ceiling.
- **Tests.** `BpmnViewImportTests` (shape/edge geometry, multi-plane and per-model
  partitioning, collapsed/expanded subprocess nesting, `bpmndi:*` flags, label bounds and
  edge attributes, waypoints/planeId round-trip properties, the both-ends connection rule
  with a generator no-missing-end check, `SingleWithPools` one-view coverage with pool root
  parents, nearest-ancestor partial-DI fill without duplicates/overlaps), `BpmnAutoLayoutTests`
  (determinism, overlap freedom, layer centring, loops, boundary events, pools/lanes/
  subprocess bands, a 50k reversed-declaration layering with no stack overflow and a 100k
  chain under 5 s), `BpmnViewRenderTests` (bUnit: imported and auto-layouted coordinates
  render through `TmModelingEditor`), the regenerated corpus goldens; JSON documentation
  covers `BpmnAutoLayout`/`BpmnAutoLayoutOptions` and `validate --fail-on-drift` is clean.
- **Phase 3 review hardening (findings 1–10):** the longest-path layering is an iterative
  Kahn topological sort (a 50 000-node reversed-declaration chain cannot overflow the
  stack) and the whole layout is O(V+E) with relationship indices built once and one-pass
  layer bucketing (100k chain < 5 s; the 200k flat-task import budget was raised to 20 s
  with a comment — it guards near-linearity, not wall time, and flaked at 10 s under
  parallel load); a chain renders as one horizontal line (per-layer stacks centred on the
  tallest layer); auto-layout emits no waypoints (the generator auto-routes); view
  connections require both ends in the view (cross-model message flows keep their geometry
  on the relationship); partial-DI fill targets the nearest-ancestor view below the DI
  bounds with no duplicate ElementId; edge/label DI attributes (`messageVisibleKind`,
  `sourceElement`/`targetElement`, `labelStyle`) are preserved as `bpmndi:*` properties
  while `BPMNLabelStyle` definitions and `di:extension` are reported as losses; E2E
  screenshots of the BPMN DI rendering are deferred to phase 5 (bUnit render tests cover
  phase 3).
- **Phase 4 — BPMN 2.0 XML export and round-trip.** `IBpmnXmlExporter`/`BpmnXmlExporter`
  (`AddTempoBpmnXml()` now registers the exporter too) converts `ModelingModelDto` back to
  deterministic BPMN 2.0 XML: stable ordering, invariant-culture numbers, LF line endings, no BOM.
  `BpmnExportOptions` adds the `Standard`/`WithHostExtensions` profiles (the latter serializes every
  non-native property into `<extensionElements><tempo:properties>` as canonical JSON under the
  configurable host namespace), `EmitBpmndi`, `TargetNamespace`, tool-extension hooks
  (`ToolExtensions`) and an `ExtensionNamespaces` prefix→URI map (pre-seeded with the
  Camunda/Signavio/Bizagi dialect namespaces) for writing foreign attribute properties back.
  Multi-model export (`Export(IReadOnlyList<ModelingModelDto>)` — an additive overload next to the
  approved single-model API) rebuilds ONE `definitions` with a `collaboration`: pools become
  participants, every populated pool keeps its process, cross-model message flows are re-wired
  between participants, and `Properties["bpmnDefinitions"]` restores the global
  message/signal/error/escalation definitions (data stores and group category values rebuild from
  their referencing elements). The catch-all write-back emits `bpmn:*`/`bpmndi:*` properties as
  attributes/DI (`labelBounds` → `BPMNLabel`, `labelStyle` reference kept, edge `waypoints` for
  cross-model message flows from the relationship properties), `foreignExtensions` payloads embed
  verbatim, event definitions/conditions/data associations/boundary attachments/ad-hoc and
  transaction subprocesses/lane sets (lanes stay transparent containers — flow nodes stay
  process-level children referenced by `flowNodeRef`) all round-trip natively. View geometry
  exports as one `BPMNPlane` per distinct view id (a collaboration plane merges the per-model views
  that share it; the plane's `bpmnElement` is derived deterministically — a fully-enclosing
  collapsed subprocess plane references that subprocess); auto-layouted connections with empty
  waypoints get synthesized endpoints (§5.4), elements/relationships without geometry are filled
  from the deterministic auto-layout. Nothing is dropped silently: unrepresentable constructs land
  in `BpmnExportResult.Losses`. Definitions-root `extensionElements` in the host namespace now
  restore model-level properties on import (previously ignored). No breaking changes — everything is
  additive; hosts that only import are untouched.
- **Tests.** `BpmnXmlExporterTests` (document structure, profiles, host/foreign extension
  write-back, escaping/injection safety, multi-model collaboration, global-definition rebuild,
  determinism/LF/no-BOM, cancellation, DI registration), `BpmnExportGoldenTests` (XML goldens for
  the whole corpus regenerated via `TEMPO_REGENERATE_BPMN_EXPORT_GOLDEN=1`, plus structural
  validity: safe parse, namespace correctness, unique ids, every `bpmnElement`/flow/`flowNodeRef`
  reference resolves and every emitted `*Ref` attribute — `dataObjectRef`, `dataStoreRef`,
  `messageRef`, `signalRef`, `errorRef`, `escalationRef`, `attachedToRef`, `default`,
  `categoryValueRef`, `processRef`, `activityRef` — resolves, and the Camunda-style
  `incoming`/`outgoing` wiring is consistent), `BpmnRoundTripTests` (import → export → import
  equals the normalized model for all 21 corpus fixtures with exact view membership/positions/DI
  flags, and export(import(export(x))) is byte-identical to export(x)); the JSON documentation
  covers the new public API and `validate --fail-on-drift` is clean.
- **Phase 4 review hardening (findings 1–12 and 14):** text annotations export their body in a
  standard `<text>` child (never a `name` attribute) and the import reads the `<text>` child with
  a direct-text fallback (new `text-annotation-text.bpmn` corpus fixture); the root declares
  `xmlns:xsi` and `conditionExpression`, `timeDuration`/`timeDate`/`timeCycle`, conditional-event
  `condition` and ad-hoc `completionCondition` all carry `xsi:type="tFormalExpression"`; a plane
  holding participant/message-flow DI references the collaboration and an empty
  `<collaboration/>` is never emitted; one `<dataObject id name isCollection>` is synthesized per
  distinct `dataObjectRef`; process attributes (`isExecutable` — default `"false"` —,
  `camunda:versionTag`, `camunda:historyTimeToLive`, …) import into the model properties via a
  catch-all and are written back on `<process>`, and `definitions` carries
  `exporter="Tempo.Blazor"` + `exporterVersion`; robustness — catch-all names written natively
  are skipped, `XmlConvert.VerifyNCName` guards every property-derived attribute name (invalid
  names become losses, never exceptions), invalid XML 1.0 characters are stripped with an
  `Approximated` loss, and event definitions with a missing/unknown type are reported instead of
  silently terminating; duplicate element ids across models export the first occurrence only (a
  shared element instance is not a duplicate) and duplicate relationship ids are reported;
  generated namespace prefixes come from the stable FNV-1a `StableId` (no `GetHashCode`),
  reserved prefixes (`bpmndi`/`dc`/`di`/`xsi`/`xml`/host) are never shadowed — collisions rename
  deterministically to `{prefix}_1` with an info loss — and repeated `xmlns` declarations inside
  preserved `foreignExtensions` payloads are stripped; element `Tags`/`Governance` and
  relationship tags ride the host payload under `WithHostExtensions` (restoring the typed DTO
  fields) and are reported as losses under `Standard`; children and relationships are pre-indexed
  by parent/source/target (a 5000-task/5000-flow export stays under 2 s); flow nodes emit
  Camunda-style `<incoming>`/`<outgoing>` wiring and generated `{id}_di` ids step aside
  (`{id}_di_1`) of colliding element ids; legacy unprefixed Camunda `calledElementBinding`/
  `calledElementVersion` and the `multiple` trigger flag (which has no BPMN 2.0 schema construct)
  export in schema-valid form, verified by the new `npm run test:bpmn-interop` lane
  (`bpmn-moddle` fromXML over every export golden, zero warnings, `bpmn:Definitions` root) and an
  opt-in XSD validation test (`TM_BPMN_XSD_DIR`, skipped when unset). `BpmnExporterReviewTests`
  pins every finding.
- **Phase 5 — tool dialect plugins, MCP tools and the demo.** The built-in
  `BpmnCamundaToolExtension`/`BpmnSignavioToolExtension`/`BpmnBizagiToolExtension` plugins
  (exposed together as `BpmnBuiltInToolExtensions.All` and registered by `AddTempoBpmnXml()`)
  map their dialects' `extensionElements` into typed properties and restore them on export:
  Camunda `properties` → `camunda:*` keys, `camunda:documentation` → the element description and
  every other Camunda payload (listeners, connectors, input/output) preserved verbatim under
  `camundaExtensions` for a loss-free re-export; Signavio `signavioMetaData` → `signavio:*`
  element keys and diagram-level `signavioDiagramMetaData` → `signavio:*` model properties;
  Bizagi `BizagiProperty` name/value pairs → `bizagi:*` keys. `IBpmnToolExtension` gains the
  additive default member `OwnsAttributeExport` (Signavio/Bizagi serialize their scalars in the
  dialect-native payload shape; Camunda keeps the attribute shape), and the attribute catch-all
  normalizes the known tool namespaces to their canonical lowercase prefixes (`Bizagi:property`
  → `bizagi:property` — the seeded `ExtensionNamespaces` key is renamed `Bizagi` → `bizagi`, the
  only visible export change: the same URI declared under the lowercase prefix). The DI-resolved
  importer/exporter pick the registered plugins up automatically (an explicitly populated
  `ToolExtensions` options list still wins), so `new BpmnXmlImporter()` stays plugin-free and the
  existing corpus goldens only changed for the Bizagi prefix normalization. New MCP tools
  `modeling_import_bpmn` (model + full loss report, optional per-model persistence through the
  document provider, 2M-character input cap) and `modeling_export_bpmn` (XML + export loss
  report, `Standard`/`WithHostExtensions` profiles) run the built-ins; the contract snapshot
  gained both responses plus a `toolClassificationByEffect` map (write: `modeling_apply_operations`,
  `modeling_import_bpmn` when `save=true`), and the catalog in `docs/modeling-mcp-tools.md` is
  complete. The `/modeling-editor` demo page imports BPMN 2.0 XML (file picker / pasted XML /
   corpus sample, or the `?bpmn=<sample>` deep link) and previews it in `TmModelingEditor`, shows
  the loss report as a dialog table, and exports a downloadable `.bpmn` — localized in en/cs/sk/fr.
  New corpus fixture `partial-bpmndi.bpmn` (DI covering only some nodes/edges) with regenerated
  goldens; `npm run test:bpmn-interop` stays green.
- **Tests.** `BpmnToolExtensionTests` (per-dialect import mapping from the corpus fixtures,
  export round-trips keeping every `camunda:*`/`signavio:*`/`bizagi:*` key, the
  plugin-free default importer unchanged, explicit options winning over the DI fallback,
  DI registration), `ModelingBpmnToolsTests` (MCP import/export incl. size limits, save
  persistence, profile validation, host-extensions round trip), E2E
  `ModelingBpmnXmlConverterE2ETests` (dialog/file/paste/deep-link import, loss report dialog,
  export download re-imported through the paste path) and `ModelingBpmnDiRenderingE2ETests`
  (carry-forward c59bf3f1: DI rendering screenshots for 3 DI corpus files + no-DI + partial-DI +
  collapsed plane at 1440/390 in light/dark, `#blazor-error-ui` hidden and PNG > 2 KB per shot);
  JSON documentation overlays regenerated and `validate --fail-on-drift` clean.
- **Phase 5 review hardening (findings 1–10).** Demo corpus samples load through an absolute
  `NavigationManager.ToAbsoluteUri` URL (the Server/InteractiveAuto `HttpClient` targets the API;
  the Server host maps the `.bpmn` content type so its static web assets actually serve)
  with a Server-host `?bpmn=` E2E; the 24 DI rendering shots + the loss-report shot are committed
  evidence in `__screenshots__/modeling-bpmn-di/`. Export merges tool plugins first-wins by
  `NamespaceUri` (explicit options before the DI fallback) so dialect payloads never double-write.
  `modeling_import_bpmn` validates `name` at 200 characters, reports malformed XML as
  `validation_failed`, and saves each document independently — a failure returns the exact
  partial progress (`saved`/`failedAt`/`failed`). The demo BPMN controls hide only below 768 px
  (localized mobile hint otherwise), the loss table carries a localized caption, `scope="col"`,
  the xmlPath in its own column and localized severities, the status line is an always-rendered
  `role="status"` element and both dialogs restore focus to the Import BPMN trigger; oversized
  files get a localized message. The `otp-input` role is unambiguously `TmOtpInput`'s again
  (`TmMaskedTextBox` keeps only `masked-input`).
- **Phase 6 — documentation and release preparation.** The design document became the
  user guide [docs/modeling-bpmn-xml.md](docs/modeling-bpmn-xml.md): installation and DI
  registration, import/export examples, the options/limits table, the loss-report contract,
  host and tool extension points, the MCP tools, security notes (safe XML settings, input
  limits), the opt-in XSD validation (`TM_BPMN_XSD_DIR`) and the `bpmn-moddle` interop
  check. The package README ([src/Tempo.Blazor.Modeling.BpmnXml/README.md](src/Tempo.Blazor.Modeling.BpmnXml/README.md))
  is packed into the nupkg; AGENTS.md and COMPONENTS.md index the package. Release prep per
  repo conventions: `2.11.0` version set in the csproj, `eng/nuget-packages.txt` lists the
  project, `ReleaseContractTests`/`ProvenanceComparisonTests` cover the announcement, local
  `dotnet pack -c Release` verified (dependencies: `Tempo.Blazor.Abstractions` + the
  TFM-matched `Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection.Abstractions` only, README + XML
  docs + symbols in the package) and a clean console-host smoke test (no Blazor) imports
  the whole corpus, exports and round-trips it. No tag/publish — the release waits for the
  owner's confirmation together with the full BPMN authoring plan.
- **Phase 2 review hardening (all 10 findings):** O(n) import backed by per-model id sets and a
  global element index (200 000 flat tasks import in seconds under the default limits —
  `MaxElements` default raised to 500 000); the bounded reader never disposes the caller's stream
  and honors cancellation mid-read; the string overload decodes through a `TextReader` so a utf-16
  encoding declaration cannot fail the import; any unexpected load/build failure (e.g. hostile
  assignment endpoints, participant-less collaborations with message flows — both now covered by
  hostile fixtures) returns a generic `HasErrors` failure instead of throwing; the attribute
  catch-all also covers relationships (messageRef/isImmediate/foreign attributes) while skipping
  per-type mapped attributes; tool plugins are invoked once per `(extensionElements, namespace)`;
  loss paths carry `[@id]`/positional predicates via the shared `BuildPath`; referenced global
  message/signal/error/escalation definitions are kept on the model as canonical
  `Properties["bpmnDefinitions"]` JSON (design §4); goldens compare with normalized line endings.

### Added — `Tempo.Blazor.DiagramEditor` (additive; consumed by the authoring editor and the viewer)

- **`TmDiagramEditor.SnapDocumentOnLoad`** (`bool`, default `true`) — when `false`, loading a document does NOT snap its nodes to the grid, so a host's persisted geometry renders exactly as saved while an interactive drag/drop/resize still snaps. The Modeling editors pass `false`; `GridSize="0"` is once again a valid "snapping off" setting (the guards no longer divide by zero, and the JS honours `gridSize: 0`).
- **`TmDiagramEditor.OnHistoryRequested`** (`EventCallback<bool>`, `false` = undo, `true` = redo) — opt-in: when a host binds it, the editor's undo/redo buttons raise this callback instead of running the editor's own command stack, so an outer editor (the modeling dialog / a host undo stack) owns history. Unbound = today's behavior.
- **Node/edge DOM hooks for presentation overlays** — `TmDiagramCanvas` renders `Data["viewerState"]` as `data-viewer-state` on `.tm-diagram-node`, the optional `Data["viewerBadge"]` glyph and the `Data["viewerTitle"]` `<title>`; `DiagramEdge.Title` renders an edge `<title>` (new additive member). Read-only consumers restyle their presentation copy through these public hooks; no editor behavior changed.
- **Swimlane clamp rule** — a node inside a container whose stencil is a pool/lane BAND is no longer clamped to that band while dragging (the band is a container the user drags ACROSS; the drop re-resolves the lane). The canvas marks such nodes with `data-swimlane="true"`. A logical group still clamps.
- **`--tm-diagram-node-stroke`** — a new component-local token on the diagram root (`var(--tm-paper-ink)` by default) that the BPMN node stencils and the editor chrome read, so a host or a high-contrast theme recolours node outlines without editing the package. Paper-token swimlane headers/toggles and the `bpmn2` marker SVG re-shown behind a transparent native primitive arrived with the same phase.

### Added — core (`Tempo.Blazor`)

- **`TmMultiSelect.SingleSelection`** (`bool`, opt-in) — the same combobox in single-value mode: one stored value, a pick replaces the selection and closes the list, the chip set renders the one value. The modeling inspector uses it for `EntityReference` fields (the stored display snapshot must render before any lookup call), and it is a public core knob rather than an inspector-private hack.
- **`TmMarkdownEditor` ARIA parameters** — `AriaLabelledBy`, `AriaDescribedBy`, `AriaInvalid` and `AriaRequired` let a host name and describe the content surface (`role="textbox"` / `aria-multiline`) without wrapping it in a second form control. The modeling inspector's markdown field uses them for its label, help text and required/invalid state.
- **`TmChart` funnel labels (`FunnelLabelPlacement`, `FunnelMinSegmentWidth`)** — the funnel's stage labels become a host choice, a theme contract and a type scale that answers the RENDERED size ([docs/chart-funnel.md](docs/chart-funnel.md)). `FunnelLabelPlacement` (`Auto` default / `Inside` / `Outside`) decides whether a label sits in the stage band or in a gutter beside the shape; `Outside` narrows the funnel to 62 % of the plot width, starts it at the plot's left edge and reads the gutter as one column — sized from the LONGEST stage label and value line, and, past 45 % of the width, answered with an ellipsis plus the full text in the label's `<title>`. A stage label and its value line are `tspan`s of ONE `<text>` (`dy` in `em`), so the gap between them follows the font. The ink is token-driven — `--tm-chart-funnel-label-inside`, `…-inside-on-light`, `…-outside` (an alias of `--tm-text-secondary`, re-declared on the dark roots) — and an inside label takes the variant that measures ≥ 4,5:1 against its resolved fill: the built-in palette reached only 2,0–4,4:1 against the old hardcoded `#ffffff`, which is why **the inside label is dark ink on most palette fills** after this release. The colour reader behind that choice lives in `ChartColorContrast` and understands hex, `rgb()` with percentage channels and `hsl()`. A stage whose value is 0 (or `NaN`, drawn as 0) no longer collapses to a zero-width path: it keeps a `FunnelMinSegmentWidth`-wide (default 4 viewBox units) visible band and its `0 (0 %)` label. The funnel also renders a visually hidden stage/conversion table (`value / first (pct %)`, localized, the numbers formatted with the READER's culture — `49,19 %` under `cs-CZ`, `49.19 %` under `en-US`) as its screen-reader alternative. **The type scale is no longer a fixed unit count**: the viewBox type is multiplied by the scale the SVG meets at, which is height-limited on a wide desktop card as well as on a phone, so the label rendered at ≈ 9,6 px in a 672 × 320 card and ≈ 6,6 px on a phone. The funnel root is now a named `@container` and the plot a `container-type: size` box, and `font-size` is `max(token, token × 600 / 100cqw, token × 400 / 100cqh)` (`@supports`-gated, with two discrete viewBox steps as the fallback) — a stage label never renders below 12 px and a value line never below 11 px at any container size.

- **`TmScheduler` day-granularity timeline (`TimelineScale`)** — `TmSchedulerTimelineScale.Days` turns the Timeline view from one day of hour slots into the days of the range with one row per resource, the "channel × day" board a campaign planner needs ([docs/scheduler.md](docs/scheduler.md)). `Hours` is the default and every earlier behavior is unchanged. The scale is part of `SchedulerRangeOptions`, so the range a host's `DataProvider` is queried with, the toolbar title and Previous/Next are the Week view's: seven days from `FirstDayOfWeek` (`WeekDays="WorkWeek"`: five), a step of seven days and the inclusive week as the title. Rows are resources with the sticky label column, columns are the days; a narrow container scrolls horizontally with the column pinned (no forced degradation), and print lays every column out on one page. A day cell paints one chip per event (localized time + title, or `EventTemplate` with a visually hidden accessible name; an all-day event prints `TmScheduler_AllDay`, and an event that started earlier keeps the continuation edge and paints on every day it covers), overlapping events take the shared `SchedulerLayout` lanes as a CSS grid (`data-lane`, `--tm-scheduler-lanes`) and the per-cell cap is `MaxVisibleEvents` (kept on a mobile layout too) with the plural `TmScheduler_More` overflow whose fallback opens that day in the Day view. The move contract is shared: HTML5 drop, the touch hold-and-drag (`scheduler.js` gained the day-board branch that commits the day and the resource with `-1` for the minute axis, so the time of day is kept, and the moving chip is lifted by the same `.tm-scheduler-event--moving` rule the other views use, so the finger's hit-test reaches the cell underneath) and the Alt+Arrow alternative (Alt+Left/Right a day, Alt+Up/Down a resource, Alt+Shift+Left/Right the end ± one day) announced as a date. A drop on a **continuation** chip moves the whole span by the days the pointer crossed, not onto the dropped day. The grid has one tab stop: Enter/F2 on a cell steps onto its first chip, ArrowUp/Down walk the cell's widgets and Escape returns to the cell. `ScrollToTime` has no minute axis there, so it scrolls the first event's day column into view (and re-applies once the layout resolves; the HOUR timeline keeps its one-and-only scroll). The board paints scroll-edge shadows only while it actually overflows. New component-local tokens `--tm-scheduler-timeline-day-width` (9rem; 7.5rem on a mobile layout), `--tm-scheduler-timeline-day-cell-height`, `--tm-scheduler-scroll-shadow-size` and `--tm-scheduler-scroll-shadow-color`. New keys `TmScheduler_TimelineDaysGrid` and `TmScheduler_MoveHint_TimelineDays` (en/cs/sk/fr), demo card "Channels × days" on `/scheduler`, and the E2E spec `SchedulerTimelineDaysE2ETests` (WASM + Server + InteractiveAuto). The full toolbar also keeps the date title above the view buttons: a bar narrower than 60rem of its own container collapses the pill switcher to the compact view dropdown instead of clipping the active view.
- **Event time in a narrow column** — a week cell, a week of resources or a phone used to cut `9:00 AM – 10:00 AM` mid-token at the card's edge. The card now prints a full reading and a compact one that shares one meridiem (`9:00 – 10:00 AM`) and the stylesheet picks by the CARD's width (`@container`: ≥ 8rem full, 4.5 – 8rem compact, < 4.5rem no time at all), the full reading wraps instead of overflowing, and the wrapper's `title` always carries the full range. `SchedulerTimeText` normalizes the ICU narrow no-break space to U+00A0, so a time never breaks between the clock and its meridiem ("10:00 AM") and the only break points are the two plain spaces around the en dash. Applies to `TmSchedulerTimeGrid` (Week/Day) and the timeline bars/chips; `EventTemplate` opts out as before.
- **`TmKanbanBoard` collapsible columns (plan a98e4a71, phases 2–3)** — a column can now be collapsed into a narrow strip and is STILL a drop target, so a board with many columns stays usable at a glance. `ColumnsCollapsible` (default `false`, so every 2.10.0 board renders identical markup) puts one native `<button type="button" class="tm-kanban__column-toggle">` in every column header — classic layout and the swimlane layout's sticky header row alike — and always OUTSIDE `ColumnHeaderTemplate`, so a host header can never lose it. The toggle carries `aria-expanded` (the state the chevron rotates on) and an `aria-label` from the new keys `TmKanban_CollapseColumn` / `TmKanban_ExpandColumn`, and it is a real button: no `role`, no `tabindex`, no Enter/Space emulation. A collapsed column keeps its `<div data-testid="board-column-…">` element, gains `tm-kanban__column--collapsed`, drops the card body (so `<Virtualize>` renders nothing) and reports itself as `role="group"` with the plural summary `TmKanban_CollapsedColumnSummary` ("To Do, 2 cards" — a real plural family in en/cs/sk/fr). The strip keeps the title (vertical, `writing-mode: vertical-rl`), the count and the WIP badge, and `tm-kanban__column--over-limit` survives the collapse because collapsing is pure view state. Dropping a card anywhere on the strip appends it (`OnItemMoved` with `TargetIndex` = the column's card count, `TargetBeforeItem` = `null`) and highlights the strip with `tm-kanban__column--drop-target`; a collapsed column never draws the horizontal `__drop-indicator` line. In the swimlane layout the collapsed column narrows the sticky header cell AND every `cell-{col}-{lane}` (the grid stays aligned, the narrowed cell keeps catching `(col, lane)` drops and appends). `Disabled` keeps the collapse (view state) but leaves every drop zone inert — no highlight, no callback. State is host-owned when supplied: `CollapsedColumns` / `CollapsedLanes` (`IReadOnlyCollection<string>?`, `null` = internal state) with `CollapsedColumnsChanged` / `CollapsedLanesChanged` carrying the complete new set for `@bind-…`; the trailing "no value" lane is addressed by the new public constant `TmKanbanBoard<TItem>.NoSwimlaneId` (still `null` in `KanbanMoveEvent.ToSwimlane`). New CSS: `tm-kanban__column--collapsed`, `tm-kanban__column-toggle`, `tm-kanban__column--drop-target`, the host knob `--tm-kanban-collapsed-width` (48px), one chevron shared with `__swimlane-toggle` (keyed off `aria-expanded`), a forced-colors-safe focus ring and a `prefers-reduced-motion` entry. Demo `/kanban` turns the feature on for both boards. Review fze-2 closed the parity and target-size gaps: the swimlane layout's collapsed header cell now renders the SAME strip as the classic column (vertical title, colour dot, count and WIP stacked, the sticky header row stretching to it through the host knob `--tm-kanban-collapsed-header-height`) instead of hiding the furniture, a header-only column keeps its WIP breach visible (the tint lands on its header, which is otherwise transparent), both toggles are 24×24 controls that grow to `--tm-touch-target` on a coarse pointer and hover through tokens, the collapsed `aria-label` appends `TmKanban_CollapsedColumnWip` and — only when the count exceeds `MaxItems` — `TmKanban_CollapsedColumnOverLimit`, the classic strip carries the column name as its `title` tip, and clicking anywhere on a collapsed header expands it (pointer-only, no key emulation; the native toggle fences its own click with `@onclick:stopPropagation` so one gesture never toggles twice). `IsColumnCollapsed` honours `ColumnsCollapsible`, so a host-supplied `CollapsedColumns` set is ignored while the feature is switched off, and the new `TmKanbanCollapseCssTests` / `KanbanCollapseE2ETests` pin the strip, the targets and the click path. Phase 3 landed the drop zones a collapsed lane used to lack: a collapsed swimlane renders `tm-kanban__swimlane-slots` — one `.tm-kanban__lane-slot` per column (`data-testid="lane-slot-{column}-{lane}"`, the no-value lane reads `none`, like `cell-…-none`) whose widths copy the grid through the new host knobs `--tm-kanban-column-width` (280px) and `--tm-kanban-lane-slot-height` — instead of no body at all, so the lane keeps catching `(column, lane)` drops while the column headers stay aligned (a slot under a collapsed column is narrow, `tm-kanban__lane-slot--collapsed`). A drop anywhere in a slot appends (`ToColumn`/`ToSwimlane`/`TargetIndex` = the cell's card count, `TargetBeforeItem` = `null`; the no-value lane still maps to `null`). The board root carries `tm-kanban--dragging` for exactly the length of a gesture; outside a drag the slots are a low, quiet strip (`border: 1px dashed transparent`), during one every slot advertises itself as a target and the slot under the pointer (or the classic collapsed strip) adds `tm-kanban__lane-slot--drop-target` / `tm-kanban__column--drop-target` — an outline and wash from the `--tm-color-primary` pair that measures 4.75:1 light and 3.48:1 dark against the target's own translucent wash (4.70:1 / 4.07:1 against the muted panel it replaces) — ≥3:1, WCAG 1.4.11 — and never appears on a `Disabled` board. `TmKanbanBoardCollapseTests` lost its last ten skipped phase-3 facts, `TmKanbanCollapseCssTests` pins the slots' quiet/target rules, the grid width knobs and the contrast pair, and the new `KanbanDropZonesE2ETests` captures the in-flight target in both themes and verifies a real committed move.
- **`TmKanbanBoard` non-drag card move (plan a98e4a71, phase 4 — WCAG 2.5.7)** — every card is now a focusable element (one roving tab stop per column/cell, `role="group"` with the localized `aria-roledescription` and `aria-describedby` at the board's visually hidden instructions) and carries a visible "Move…" trigger in its corner (24×24, `--tm-touch-target` on a coarse pointer) that opens a `TmContextMenu` listing Move up / Move down for the card's own cell plus one target per column — per column × swimlane when swimlanes are on, collapsed columns and collapsed lanes INCLUDED — presented as the shared bottom sheet on a phone (`PanelPresentation.Auto`). A keyboard reader opens the same menu with `M` or `Alt+ArrowDown` on the focused card, so moving a card never requires a drag. Every choice reports the SAME contract as a drop: a target appends to the chosen cell (`OnItemMoved`, `TargetIndex` = the cell's card count, `TargetBeforeItem` = `null`), a nudge reports `OnItemReordered` at the position the card ends up before. The board announces the outcome once through one polite live region ("{0} moved to {1}", `TmKanban_CardMoved`) and hands the focus back to the moved card — or to the target zone when the destination is a collapsed strip or a collapsed lane's slot. Card activation follows [docs/keyboard-activation-convention.md](docs/keyboard-activation-convention.md): the card is non-native, so Enter (auto-repeat guarded) and Space (keyup) raise `OnCardClick`, while the card's content and the menu are fenced on keydown AND keyup so a control inside `CardTemplate` keeps its own keys. New parameters `ShowMoveMenu` (default `true` — a drag-only card is the 2.5.7 failure) and `CardLabelSelector` (the name the trigger, the sheet title, the "(current)" entry and the announcement use; without it the board falls back to the item's `ToString()` only when the type overrides it, otherwise to the localized "card {n}"). `Disabled` hides the action and keeps the drag markup inert. Review fze-4 closed the a11y follow-ups: the cell keeps exactly ONE tab stop — the new additive `TmContextMenu.TriggerTabIndex` (`int?`, default `0`) makes the card's trigger `-1`, so `Tab` leaves the card for the NEXT cell instead of walking the card's own trigger; the menu names the cell the card already sits in as "To Do (current)", `disabled` with `aria-current="true"`, instead of offering a no-op target; the "Enter to open a card" sentence is only in the instructions when the host actually bound `OnCardClick`; `M` / `Alt+ArrowDown` ignore a Ctrl/⌘ chord (a browser shortcut); a `VirtualizeCards` cell whose window no longer renders the roving card re-points its single stop at the first rendered card instead of dropping out of the tab order; and `ShowMoveMenu="false"`/`Disabled` no longer emit `data-focus-target` or the drop zones' `tabindex="-1"`. New CSS: `tm-kanban__card--movable`, `tm-kanban__card-content`, `tm-kanban__card-actions`, `tm-kanban__card-move`, `tm-kanban__card-move-trigger`, a `:focus-visible` ring on the card, and the card's reserved corner; the kanban sheet never restyles the context menu's own trigger. Tests: `TmKanbanBoardMoveTests` (39 cases: every activation once, the append/reorder contract, the collapsed-zone focus, a host that applies the move by replacing the item, the live region, one tab stop per cell in the classic/swimlane/virtualized layouts, the Ctrl/⌘ guard, the "(current)" target and the positional card label) and `KanbanMoveE2ETests` (keyboard move without a mouse, `Tab` walking cells rather than a card's own controls, the menu and the mobile sheet captured in both themes). The phase-3 review follow-ups landed with it: a `tm-kanban--dragging .tm-kanban__column--collapsed` wash so every strip advertises itself for the whole gesture like the lane slots do, `@ondragover:preventDefault="@(!Disabled)"` on every drop zone so a disabled board never claims a drop it will refuse, and the contrast guard now includes the target's own translucent wash as a surface.

- **`TmKanbanBoard` collapsed-surface review (plan a98e4a71, phase 5)** — the swimlane layout's sticky header row and every lane row now start at the SAME horizontal inset. A lane cell begins after its lane's border plus its body's padding, while the header row is a sibling with neither, so a header cell sat 9px to the LEFT of the lane cells it heads (measured by the new `KanbanCollapsedLayoutE2ETests` from real `getBoundingClientRect` boxes, not from a class list). Both sides now read one pair of component-local knobs on `.tm-kanban`: `--tm-kanban-lane-padding` (the body/slots padding, `var(--tm-space-2, 0.5rem)`) and `--tm-kanban-lane-inset` (`calc(padding + var(--tm-border-width))`, consumed by `.tm-kanban__column-headers`), and the lane's own border reads `--tm-border-width` instead of a repeated `1px`. The same review fixed two contrast defects the collapsed strip made unreadable: its WIP badge ("/ 5", 11.2px) read in `--tm-text-tertiary`, 4.39:1 light / 4.04:1 dark on the muted panel — under WCAG AA — and is now `--tm-text-secondary` (6.87:1 / 6.97:1); and a WIP breach on a COLLAPSED strip leaned on the decorative `--tm-color-danger-soft-border` / `--tm-color-danger-subtle` pair (~1.3:1, i.e. invisible in the one place the strip has no card body left to show it), so `tm-kanban__column--collapsed.tm-kanban__column--over-limit` now states the breach at the non-text 3:1 level — a solid `--tm-color-danger` edge plus a 2px outline (4.39:1 light / 3.74:1 dark on the muted panel) and `--tm-color-danger-text` numbers (7.6:1 / 5.46:1) — while the D4 drop-target rule still wins for the length of a gesture. Tests and captures: the new `KanbanCollapsedLayoutE2ETests` (one left edge and width shared by the header cell, every lane cell and every collapsed-lane slot before and after a column collapses; a drop into the narrowed cell reports `ToColumn` AND `ToSwimlane` and appends, and the widened/narrowed slot lands on the collapsed header's edge), `KanbanVisualE2ETests` (committed baselines under `tests/Tempo.Blazor.E2E/__screenshots__/kanban/`, light and dark: expanded board, collapsed column, collapsed lane, collapsed column in the swimlane layout, the in-flight drop highlight over a collapsed strip, the collapsed over-limit strip and the keyboard focus ring on the collapse toggle and on a card), the `KanbanDropZonesE2ETests` extension (a drop on a collapsed classic strip lands at the END of the column and at the end of the demo's persisted order) and two `TmKanbanCollapseCssTests` guards (the inset knob, and the two contrast floors per theme).

- **`TmKanbanBoard` documentation (plan a98e4a71, phase 6)** — the board's behaviour contract is now a page of its own: [docs/kanban-board.md](docs/kanban-board.md) covers the layouts, the collapsed column and collapsed swimlane contracts (including the one drop slot per column), the drop contract (`TargetIndex` vs `TargetBeforeItem`), the WCAG 2.5.7 non-drag move, accessibility, the stable `data-testid` set, the localization keys, the wireframe citizen check (the `kanban-board` UI role is unchanged — a collapsed column is a view state, not a new UI role) and the verification recipe. [COMPONENTS.md](COMPONENTS.md) gained the full parameter, CSS-class and component-knob tables (`--tm-kanban-column-width`, `--tm-kanban-collapsed-width`, `--tm-kanban-collapsed-header-height`, `--tm-kanban-lane-slot-height`, `--tm-kanban-lane-padding`, `--tm-kanban-lane-inset`, `--tm-kanban-virtual-max-height`), the `KanbanColumn` / `KanbanSwimlane` / `KanbanMoveEvent` / `NoSwimlaneId` model table and the `@bind-CollapsedColumns` / `@bind-CollapsedLanes` example; AGENTS.md points the DataDisplay row at the new doc. The JSON documentation overlay was extended (the `tm-kanban__cards--virtual` class plus the a11y/move notes) and the bundles regenerated — `validate --fail-on-drift` is clean.

### Added — `Tempo.Blazor.Codes` (`TmQRCode`: accessible name, colour tokens, SVG download)

- **The graphic is named.** The SVG used to be an unnamed image — no `role`, no `aria-label`, no
  `<title>` — so a screen reader announced nothing. It is now `role="img"` with an accessible name from
  the new `AriaLabel` parameter or the localized `TmQRCode_DefaultLabel` fallback ("QR code"), and a
  `<title>` carrying the same text as the native tooltip. The name is HTML-encoded, so a host label with
  quotes or `<` cannot break the markup.
- **Colours have a token home.** `ForegroundColor`/`BackgroundColor` accept hex, `rgb()`/`hsl()`, a CSS
  named colour, `currentColor`, or a `var(--token)` reference. The first four are valid SVG `fill`
  presentation attributes and are written as attributes; a `var()` reference is **not** valid there
  (browsers do not substitute custom properties in presentation attributes), so it — and only it — is
  written as a `fill` declaration inside a `style` attribute. `UseThemeColors` (default `false`) is the
  CSP-clean path: the ink becomes `currentColor` driven by `--tm-qr-code-foreground` and the surface
  reads `--tm-qr-code-background`, both component-local knobs on `.tm-qr-code` whose defaults are the
  **paper** tokens (`var(--tm-paper-ink)`, `var(--tm-paper)`). The paper tokens are white in every theme
  on purpose, so the four-module quiet zone stays light in dark mode and the code keeps scanning; an
  explicit colour still wins over the token. An unusable value is rejected (no injected declaration can
  reach the attribute), falls back to the default and logs one warning per parameter pair.
- **Contrast check.** With both colours absolute, the component measures their WCAG ratio and logs one
  warning below **3:1** (WCAG 1.4.11 for graphical objects) — a scanner needs the modules to stand out
  from the quiet zone. Token and `currentColor` values skip the check (they cannot be resolved here, and
  guessing would warn on every render). The component's only logging is optional: no `ILoggerFactory`
  registered means no warning, never a missing-service exception.
- **No inline style on the default and theme paths.** The old markup painted the quiet zone with
  `style="background-color: …"` on the `<svg>`; the surface rectangle now paints the same pixels with a
  `fill` attribute (or the `--tm-qr-code-background` token), so the component renders under a strict
  `style-src` without `'unsafe-inline'`. Only the explicit `var()` colour path writes a `style`
  attribute, documented as such.
- **Direct renderer, same pixels.** The SVG is generated from QRCoder's module matrix (merged dark runs,
  exactly the rectangles `SvgQRCode` emits) instead of post-processing the library's SVG string with
  regular expressions. The geometry is pinned to QRCoder's own output by a bUnit test, so the default
  hex rendering is unchanged; the modules now live in one `<g class="tm-qr-code__modules">` and the
  viewBox is unchanged (`0 0 {modules × 10} {modules × 10}`).
- **SVG download without JavaScript.** `ShowDownload` (opt-in, default `false`) renders a localized
  "Download SVG" link — a native `<a download>` whose `href` is a `data:image/svg+xml;base64,` URL of
  `GetStandaloneSvg()`, so no Blob, no interop and no round trip. The exported file carries absolute
  colours (`#000000`/`#ffffff` when the page painted from tokens), so it renders when opened on its own.
  `DownloadFileName` defaults to `qr-code.svg`. The public `GetSvg()` (the markup as rendered) and
  `GetStandaloneSvg()` (the self-contained file) let a host drive its own button.
- **Responsive sizing actually applies.** The stylesheet's SVG rule was scoped and therefore never
  matched the `MarkupString` SVG (Blazor isolation cannot put its scope attribute on injected markup);
  it is now `::deep`, so a code wider than its container shrinks instead of overflowing.
- **Localization:** `TmQRCode_DefaultLabel` and `TmQRCode_Download` (en/cs/sk/fr) plus
  `MockTmLocalizer`; the CSS contract is guarded by `TmQRCodeCssTests` (component tokens, no colour
  literal, no dark-theme block, no animation).
- **Demo and E2E:** the `/new-components` QR section gained theme colours, a download card and a named
  graphic, and the section stayed light-on-white in both themes; `TmQRCodeE2ETests` (WASM) checks the
  name, the inline-style-free markup, the quiet zone's computed fill in LIGHT and DARK and the decoded
  download payload, with `TmQRCodeServerE2ETests` / `TmQRCodeInteractiveAutoE2ETests` smoke runs.


### Breaking changes and migration

**No source-breaking change.** Every new member is additive or a default interface member; every new component is new. The behavior changes below are the complete list a 2.10.0 consumer can notice, with before/after:

| Change | Before (2.10.0) | After (2.11.0) | Migration |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ModelingOperationPolicy` on `modeling_apply_operations` | `Strict`: view operations rejected with `unsupported_operation`; a parent change re-validated nothing after the batch | `Authoring` (the editor's save policy): view operations accepted; every relationship incident to a changed `ParentId` is re-validated after the batch | None for a valid batch; a batch that persisted an invalid model after a lane move now fails with `invalid_relationship` — that is the editor's long-standing verdict. Callers that want the old semantics pass `Strict` to the engine directly |
| `properties` / `removedProperties` on add/update operations | Accepted as members but silently ignored | Applied (the payload is one contract with `set_properties`); a malformed payload (`properties` not an object / `removedProperties` not a string array) fails with `property_type` | Remove the redundant follow-up `set_properties` op, or keep it — applying the same values twice is idempotent. Fix a malformed payload that used to be skipped |
| `ModelingOperationEngine` | Internal type in `Tempo.Blazor.Mcp.Modeling` | Public `Tempo.Blazor.Modeling.ModelingOperationEngine` in Abstractions | No public 2.10.0 API removed; a host that needs the engine now references Abstractions (already referenced) |
| `TmDiagramEditor` load-time snapping | Every load snapped node positions to the grid | Opt-out `SnapDocumentOnLoad="false"`; default `true` = unchanged | None unless a host opts out |
| `TmDiagramEditor` undo/redo with `OnHistoryRequested` bound | Editor stack always owned history | A bound callback takes over (the buttons stop touching the editor stack) | Unbound = unchanged; a host that binds it must implement undo/redo |
| `GridSize="0"` | Produced `NaN` positions and the JS still snapped at 8 | Genuinely disables snapping (`GridSize`/`SnapDocumentOnLoad` stay plain parameters) | None — this restores the documented meaning |
| `ModelingDiffOverlayDto` | Six id collections + `BaselineModel` + `LegendTitle` | Adds `ChangedRelationshipIds` (additive; empty for an overlay that never sets it) | None |
| `TmModelingViewer`, `ModelingModelDiff`, `ModelingPropertySchemaValidator`, `ModelingPropertySchemaResolver`, the schema/lookup contracts, `ModelingChangeSetTranslator`, `ModelingModelWriterCapabilities`, the view operation DTOs | Did not exist | New public API | None — opt-in; no provider = 2.10.0 behavior |
| Editor behavior | Read-only/content-only unless a host opted in | Unchanged unless a host opts in (`AllowModelEditing` + writer capabilities + schema provider) | None; the MO2 read-only default is test-guarded |
| `TmChart` funnel — inside label ink | Hardcoded `#ffffff` (2,0–4,4:1 on the built-in palette — under WCAG AA) | Token ink; the inside label picks `--tm-chart-funnel-label-inside` or `…-inside-on-light` by the variant that clears 4,5:1 against the resolved fill | None at the API level; the default LOOK changes (dark ink on a light fill). A host that wants white on every fill sets both inside tokens to `#ffffff` and accepts the measured contrast — see [docs/chart-funnel.md](docs/chart-funnel.md) |
| `TmChart` funnel — beside-the-funnel label ink | Hardcoded `#6b7280` | `--tm-chart-funnel-label-outside` (`var(--tm-text-secondary)`) | None; a host that pinned the old grey sets `--tm-chart-funnel-label-outside: #6b7280` |
| `TmChart` funnel — a stage with value 0 | Zero-width path: the row was invisible | A `FunnelMinSegmentWidth`-wide (default 4 viewBox units) visible band with its `0 (0 %)` label; `NaN` drawn as 0 | None; pass `FunnelMinSegmentWidth="0"` to restore the old geometry |
| `TmChart` funnel — label `<text>` attributes | Inline `fill` + `font-size` per label | Placement/ink class + `--tm-chart-funnel-label-*` tokens | None; markup selectors that targeted the `fill` attribute must target the class instead |
| `TmChart` funnel — label markup | Two sibling `<text>` nodes (stage name, value line) | One `<text>` with two `<tspan>`s; the value line carries `dy="1.25em"`, the name `dy="-0.2em"` | None; both lines keep their `tm-chart__funnel-label` / `tm-chart__funnel-value` class, so a selector on either still matches |
| `TmChart` funnel — type scale | Fixed 12 / 10 viewBox units, so ≈ 9,6 px on a desktop card and ≈ 6,6 px on a phone | Tokens with a RENDERED floor: ≥ 12 px label, ≥ 11 px value, at every container size (`--tm-chart-funnel-label-size*`, `…-value-size*`) | None; a host that pinned the old look sets the `-size-viewbox` / `-narrow` pair to `12px` / `10px` |
| `TmChart` funnel — stage numbers | Invariant formatting (`1000`, `45 %`) | The reader's culture (`1,000` / `1 000`), two decimals at most, a non-breaking space before `%` | None at the API level; a test that asserted the invariant string must format with the same culture |
| `TmChart` funnel — screen-reader output | Only the `role="img"` SVG name | The SVG name plus a visually hidden stage/conversion table | None; an unrelated `table` query in a host test could now match the hidden table (`[data-testid='chart-funnel-table']` names it) |
| Event time markup (time grid, timeline, day board) | One `<span class="…-event-time">9:00 AM – 10:00 AM</span>` | The wrapper keeps the `title` with the full range and holds two spans: `.tm-scheduler-event-time-full` (the culture's full range) and `.tm-scheduler-event-time-compact` (`9:00 – 10:00 AM`); the stylesheet shows exactly one by the card's width | None for behaviour. A host selector that targeted the wrapper still matches; a selector that expected the time TEXT inside `.tm-scheduler-event-time` must target `.tm-scheduler-event-time-full` (or read the wrapper's `title`). The full reading now joins the time to its meridiem with U+00A0, so a test that asserted `9:00 AM – 10:00 AM` with plain spaces has to normalise or expect the non-breaking space |
| `TmKanbanBoard` card markup (`ShowMoveMenu` defaults to `true`) | A card was a plain draggable `<div class="tm-kanban__card">` wrapping the host's `CardTemplate` verbatim; a pointer could drag it and a click raised `OnCardClick` | Every card is a focusable `role="group"` with one roving tab stop per cell (`tabindex` `0`/`-1`), a localized `aria-roledescription`, `aria-describedby` at the board's visually hidden instructions, and a `tm-kanban__card-content` wrapper around the host template fenced on keydown AND keyup; Enter (keydown, repeat-guarded) and Space (keyup) raise `OnCardClick`; `M` / `Alt+ArrowDown` open the card's "Move…" `TmContextMenu` whose trigger is `tabindex="-1"` (the new `TmContextMenu.TriggerTabIndex`), so a cell keeps exactly ONE tab stop. The menu lists Move up / Move down plus one target per column × lane, with the cell the card already sits in named "(current)", `disabled` and `aria-current="true"`. The board root gains `data-focus-target` (the hand-back destination) and the drop zones `tabindex="-1"`, and the board renders one visually hidden instructions `<p>` plus one polite live region (`data-testid="kanban-status"`) | None for behaviour: every control and every key the host renders inside `CardTemplate` keeps its own events (the wrapper fences propagation, and the card's key handlers never see a key a child handled). A host that wants the 2.10.0 card byte-for-byte — no wrapper, no tab stop, no aria attributes, no menu, no live region, `OnCardClick` on a pointer only — sets `ShowMoveMenu="false"` (also rendered by a `Disabled` board). A card template that relied on its own Enter/Space bubbling to the card's click keeps working through the default (the card emulates the activation) or opts out with `ShowMoveMenu="false"` |
| `TmKanbanBoard` collapsed swimlane markup (`SwimlanesCollapsible` defaults to `true`) | A collapsed lane rendered no body at all — its `(column, lane)` cells vanished, so a card could not be dropped there | A collapsed lane renders `.tm-kanban__swimlane-slots` with one `.tm-kanban__lane-slot` per column (`data-testid="lane-slot-{column}-{lane}"`, widths copying the grid), so every `(column, lane)` drop keeps working while the lane is collapsed; the slots are visually quiet outside a drag and highlight as targets (`--drop-target`) for the length of one | None at the API level; the addition is presentational and only renders while a lane IS collapsed. A selector scoped to `.tm-kanban__swimlane-body` no longer matches a collapsed lane — target the slots instead |
| `TmQRCode` accessible name | SVG without `role`/`aria-label`/`title` — an unnamed graphic | `role="img"` + `aria-label` (the host's `AriaLabel` or the localized "QR code") + a matching `<title>` | None to render code; a QR that is genuinely decorative must be hidden by the HOST (`<div aria-hidden="true">`) — the component always names it |
| `TmQRCode` background painting | `<svg style="background-color: {BackgroundColor}">` (an inline style, blocked by a strict `style-src`) | The surface `<rect fill="{BackgroundColor}">` paints the same pixels; the SVG carries no inline style any more | None visually. A selector that read the SVG's `style` attribute must target `svg > rect` (or `.tm-qr-code__surface` in theme mode); a host with a CSP without `'unsafe-inline'` now gets the background |
| `TmQRCode` colour parameters | `string` properties defaulting to `#000000`/`#ffffff` and used verbatim in the markup | `string?` (`null` = the same defaults), validated: hex/`rgb()`/`hsl()`/named/`currentColor` as a `fill` attribute, a `var(--token)` as a CSS `fill` declaration, anything else rejected with a dev warning | None for a valid hex; code that READS the parameter must handle `null`, and an invalid value can no longer reach the attribute |
| `TmQRCode` default markup | `<svg … >`, one `<rect>` per dark run, inline background style | `<svg role="img" aria-label … ><title>…</title><rect …/><g class="tm-qr-code__modules" fill="#000000">…</g></svg>` — the same rects, wrapped in one group | None; `svg rect` still matches every module, a selector that assumed modules are `svg > rect` must target `.tm-qr-code__modules rect` |
| `TmQRCode` SVG sizing | `.tm-qr-code svg { max-width: 100% }` was scoped and never matched the injected SVG | The rule is `::deep` and applies: a code wider than its container shrinks instead of overflowing | None at the API level; a host that relied on the overflow sets an explicit width |
| `TmQRCode` SVG download | Did not exist | Opt-in `ShowDownload` (localized `<a download>` with a `data:` URL) plus the public `GetSvg()` / `GetStandaloneSvg()` | None — opt-in; the demo shows both |


### Release preparation

- Package versions bumped to `2.11.0` across every packable project so `ReleaseContractTests` (csproj ↔ first CHANGELOG heading) agrees; JSON documentation bundles regenerated; `validate --fail-on-drift` clean.
- The packages were packed locally and smoke-tested in a clean host implementing `IModelingModelWriter` (Structure + Layout) and `IModelingPropertySchemaProvider` against a BPMN model — see `docs/modeling-hosting-guide.md` §9 for the recipe.
- **Not released.** Tagging `v2.11.0` and publishing to the feed are gated on the owner's confirmation and ship together with the BPMN 2.0 XML converter plan (decision Q6); the PromptHelper *Upgrade Tempo.Blazor* plan is announced only after that release.

## 2.10.0 (unreleased)

- **New demo page `/ai-agent-visualizations`** (plan d67b33af, phase 9) with its host-side simulator and its demo-only sample data (`src/Tempo.Blazor.Demo.SharedUI/Pages/AiAgentVisualizationsPage.razor`, `AiAgentVisualizationsPage.razor.cs`, `AiAgentVisualizationsSamples.cs`, `src/Tempo.Blazor.Demo.SharedUI/Services/AiAgentRunSimulator.cs`): ONE simulated multi-agent run rendered by **every** agent surface of the package at once — lanes, graph, fan-out, parallel attempts, handoff chain, fallback chain, autonomy dial, memory panel, delegate board, scheduled runs, conflict radar and the presence overlay. No library component, parameter default, CSS class or public API changed: the page is a HOST, exactly as an application would drive these components.
  - **The simulator.** `AiAgentRunSimulator` owns a `TimeProvider`-driven change log and the reducer, and hands the components a bounded snapshot. One change is one `AiAgentRunEvent` with a `Sequence` that grows by exactly one (the contiguity `AgentEventStream<T>` defines as "delivered"); the timer applies **ten events per second at 1×** — five at 0,5× and twenty at 2×. The four-beat cycle opens a block on an agent's lane, calls a tool along a graph edge, completes the oldest open block and retires the oldest finished block once the lane reached its cap, and every completion advances the forty-unit fan-out queue by one unit (starting the next queued unit or retrying a failed one with an incremented attempt). The state is BOUNDED — twelve blocks, eight handoffs and the same forty units looping back into the queue — so two minutes at ten events per second cost what the first second costs; every mutable field sits behind ONE gate, because on Blazor Server the timer callback and the circuit's UI thread both reach the run — a tick that arrives after a pause or a dispose is dropped, the change event is raised outside the gate, and a failing subscriber is recorded on `LastTickError` instead of being thrown out of the timer callback (an unhandled thread-pool exception would take the Server host down). The page repaints through `AgentRenderThrottle` (a 200 ms window), and a tick inside the window is folded into the trailing paint instead of being dropped. The simulator and the three surfaces its data changes (lanes, graph, fan-out) live in their own demo component, `AiAgentRunLiveSurfaces`: the first version painted all thirteen surfaces once per 100 ms and the WASM renderer needed ~200 ms per paint, so only 44 of a window's 100 events reached the state — the split is what makes the ten-events-per-second budget hold.
  - **The controls.** Play/Pause (which names the action the press performs), a `TmSegmentedControl` speed (`0,5×` / `1×` / `2×` → 5 / 10 / 20 events per second), Reset (back to the opening snapshot, the generator stopped, the change log restarted) and the read-outs (state, applied events, events per second, sequence, open blocks, finished units) plus the last applied change as one sentence. The controls keep the focus where the reader pressed them; the graphics are the components' own SVG/CSS.
  - **The surfaces.** The lanes render the seeded and the simulated blocks with handoffs, an approval marker and a running block; the graph is the ONE surface fed the incremental path (each tool call travels as its own `AgentGraphCall` and pulses its edge, and a hole makes the page reload the snapshot the calls re-base on); the fan-out carries forty units over four workers with a retry; the attempts keep three scored drafts; the handoff chain, the fallback chain (view and editor), the autonomy dial (ceiling at Act, two enforced locks), the memory panel (twenty facts in four categories with an inline edit, pause/resume, review, forget + undo), the delegate board (eight tasks over three agents, the Assign menu, the automatic pass and a full agent's refusal), the week of scheduled runs, the conflict radar (three agents over twenty-five files with **four** real conflicts and a merge that waits for the last decision) and the presence overlay (four cursors anchored to the page's own paragraphs).
  - **Accessibility.** Every graphical surface has a text or table alternative a keyboard reaches: the components with their own switcher keep theirs (lanes, graph, handoff chain, fallback chain, scheduled runs) and the page adds a table presentation for the fan-out (40 rows), the attempts (3), the memory (20), the delegate board (8), the conflict radar (every change plus the four decisions) and the presence roster (4) — a native `<table>` with a caption and scoped headers, reachable from a native action button whose label names the presentation the next press shows — it deliberately carries no `aria-pressed`, so the changing name and a pressed state cannot contradict each other (WCAG 4.1.2) — and switching REPLACES the graphical surface so the same data is never in the accessibility tree twice. The page owns exactly ONE polite live region, which announces the simulator's own controls only: the simulated events are visible text (a reader would otherwise hear the whole run), and every reader action is announced by the component that owns it, so nothing is said twice. The page's own action buttons carry a 44 px target (`min-h-11`), the components keep their coarse-pointer and `forced-colors` contracts, reduced motion is honoured by the components, and every section stays inside a 375 px phone without widening the page.
  - **Demo data.** `AiAgentVisualizationsSamples` is the page's host content (agents, batch names, memory sentences, the twenty-five repository paths and the four overlapping ones, the fictional model catalogue, six scheduler windows and four runs). The page labels it as invented data in a visible notice and states that nothing calls a model provider.
  - **Localization:** the demo tables `DemoResources.json` / `.cs` / `.sk` / `.fr` gain the `TmAiAgentVizDemo_*` family (page title and description, the notice, the simulator's title, hint, controls, read-outs, the four event words and the event sentence, the section hints, the "Show the table view" / "Show the visual view" labels, the table captions and column headers, "Not decided yet", "No estimate" and the five paragraphs of the presence document).
  - **Docs:** [docs/ai-agent-visualizations.md](docs/ai-agent-visualizations.md) — the simulator's contract, the controls, the bounded state and the paint gate, the surfaces, the accessibility contract and how the page is tested; [docs/ai-agents.md](docs/ai-agents.md) gains a "Usage examples — every surface" section with a compiling snippet per component plus the live-data path, and the AI row of AGENTS.md names the page and the new doc.
  - **Wireframe:** no new component and no changed component, so no stencil or UI role changed (checked against `BuiltInComponentSchemas`).
  - **Tests:** `AiAgentRunSimulatorTests` (xUnit on `FakeTimeProvider`: the seeded paused snapshot, one event per base interval, pause/resume, the three speeds and the rejected one, the contiguous sequence, the four-beat kinds and the retirement, the bounded block list across 600 ticks, the queue's retry and its loop, no growth across 2 000 ticks, the contiguous call log, the anchored cursors, the reset, the tick callback and the dispose) and `AiAgentVisualizationsPageTests` (bUnit on `FakeTimeProvider`: every section without a raw key and ONE live region, play/pause counters, the speed choice and its announcement, reset, each table alternative with its row count, forget + undo, settling every conflict and merging, the lanes and graph selections with their own table switches, the dial's keys and locks, the six view switches' missing `aria-pressed` and flipping label, and the simulator's thread safety — concurrent `Step`/`Reset`/`Retry` loops, a throwing subscriber and a stale tick after `Dispose`); `AiAgentVisualizationsE2ETests` (WASM: the simulator, the lanes' keyboard selection and table, the graph's arrow walk and table, the delegate board's cross-list POINTER DRAG plus its Assign menu, memory forget + undo and the table, the radar settled from the keyboard and merged, the dial's keys with the focus hand-back, every table alternative, and a scoped axe scan per section) with a Server smoke class, `AiAgentVisualizationsVisualE2ETests` (light and dark at 1440 px, the phone sweep at 375 px with the width and 44 px assertions, the table alternatives on the phone and the reduced-motion cursor) and `AiAgentVisualizationsPerformanceE2ETests` (category `Performance`: ten events per second for two minutes, the rate asserted per window, a press still answered in under three seconds and the JS heap plateaus). The JSON documentation bundles were regenerated and `validate --fail-on-drift` is clean.
- **New `TmConflictRadar`** (`Tempo.Blazor.Components.AI`, package `Tempo.Blazor.AI`) with the `ChangedPath` / `AgentBranchChanges` / `ConflictResolution` / `ConflictMergeRequest` records and the `ChangeKind` / `ConflictResolutionKind` enums (in `Tempo.Blazor.Abstractions`, namespace `Tempo.Blazor.AI.Models`) plus the internal `ConflictMatrix` model (plan d67b33af, phase 8): the agents' branches as ONE file × agent grid, where a cell names the change one agent made to one file, a path more than one agent changed is a conflict the reader settles, and the merge action waits for the last decision. No existing component, parameter default or CSS class changed.
  - **The models.** `ChangedPath` is one touched path — `Path` (REQUIRED: a blank value throws `ArgumentException`, because the path is the row key and the reader's decision is stored under it), `Kind`, `PreviousPath` (only meaningful for `Renamed`) — and a record VALUE. Separators are normalised to `/` so the same file reported as `src/AI/Foo.cs` and `src\AI\Foo.cs` is ONE row, while a CASE difference stays two rows: folding `Foo.cs` into `foo.cs` would hide a change nobody resolved. `AgentBranchChanges` is one agent's branch (`Agent` required, `Branch` blank renders the localized "No branch", `ChangedPaths` collapsed by path where the LAST entry wins because a receipt that lists a file twice describes the newer fact second). `ConflictResolution` is one decision (`Kind` `Agent` or `Manual`; `AgentId` REQUIRED for an agent side — "keep the agent's side" without an agent would pick a winner by accident) and `ConflictMergeRequest` the payload of the merge (every file the merge touches — separators normalised to `/` and each path present once, because a file named twice would be merged twice — conflict-free ones included, plus the accepted decision per conflict).
