  - **The matrix.** `ConflictMatrix` is pure C#: one column per agent that changed something (the same agent id reported twice is ONE column whose lists are merged, and an agent with no changes is no column), one row per path with cells aligned to the columns (a null cell means "this agent did not touch it", an "unchanged" cell never exists), a conflict when ≥ 2 agents changed the row, conflicting rows FIRST and each group in ordinal path order, directory groups derived from that row order (so the directory holding the first conflict is the first group), and `Unresolved` / `IsReadyToMerge` / `BuildMergeRequest` — a decision that names an agent which does not change the file does NOT settle it.
  - **The surface.** `Agents` (the branches), `@bind-Resolutions` (the reader's decisions; a same-instance re-render cannot undo them and a NEW list replaces them), `OnMerge(ConflictMergeRequest)`, `@bind-ConflictOnly` (the "Only conflicts" filter, whose summary keeps reporting the whole picture), `Title` / `ShowTitle` / `HeadingLevel` / `AriaLabel` / `Class`.
  - **The table.** A NATIVE `<table>` that declares **no** ARIA role: a `<th scope="col">` per agent (its `TmAgentBadge` and its branch), a `<th scope="rowgroup">` per directory, a `<th scope="row">` per file and a resolution cell whose `headers` names that file row — with the file column sticky. Every cell names its change with an icon AND a word ("Added", "Modified", "Deleted", "Renamed", "was src/Old.cs"), and an untouched file is an em dash plus the spoken "No change" — never an empty box. A conflicting row carries the danger frame AND a "Conflict" badge with an icon and a word. Files are grouped by directory behind a native disclosure whose button states `aria-expanded` and the group's counts in words.
  - **The side choice and the merge.** One NATIVE radio group per conflicting file (its options are the agents that really changed it plus "Merge by hand"), so the browser's arrow keys apply and each file is its own group; the radios are re-mounted (`@key` with a version counter) when the host replaces the decision list, so a host-driven revert cannot leave a stale checked mark in the browser. The merge action is DISABLED — with a hint stating how many conflicts are open — until every conflict carries an accepted decision, is ready immediately when the agents do not conflict at all, and is disabled when there are no files (merging nothing is not an action).
  - **Accessibility.** Every state is a word plus an icon; ONE polite live region announces a resolution, a merge, the filter change and a collapsed directory and re-announces an identical sentence through an invisible marker; `(pointer: coarse)` raises the side LABELS (not the radio glyph), the merge action and the directory buttons to the 44 px `--tm-touch-target`; `forced-colors: active` hands the frame, the toned words and the disabled action to `CanvasText`/`Canvas`/`GrayText` and every focus ring to a 2 px `Highlight` outline, and that block paints no `--tm-*` colour at all. The table declares no `role="grid"` and no explicit row/columnheader/rowheader/cell roles (and no `aria-rowcount`/`aria-colcount`, which the filter and the collapsed directories make wrong) — a grid role without a roving tabindex makes NVDA/JAWS switch to focus mode and expect arrow keys the surface does not handle, while the native semantics are what table navigation needs; the side-choice labels are 24 px tall with a `--tm-space-2` row gap so a wrapped row keeps the WCAG 2.5.8 spacing exemption. The partial declares no transition and no animation.
  - **CSS classes:** `.tm-ai-radar`, `--conflicts-only`, `__header`, `__title`, `__summary`, `__filter`, `__merge`, `__merge-icon`, `__merge-text`, `__instructions`, `__merge-hint`, `__empty`, `__grid-wrap`, `__grid`, `__head-row`, `__cell`, `__cell--file`, `__cell--agent`, `__cell--change`, `__branch`, `__group`, `__directory-row`, `__directory-cell`, `__directory-toggle`, `__directory-icon`, `__directory-name`, `__directory-meta`, `__row`, `__row--conflict`, `__file-name`, `__file-path`, `__conflict`, `__conflict-icon`, `__conflict-text`, `__none`, `__none-mark`, `__change`, `__change--added` / `--modified` / `--deleted` / `--renamed`, `__change-icon`, `__change-kind`, `__change-from`, `__row--resolution`, `__resolution-cell`, `__sides`, `__side`, `__side-input`, `__side-text` — tokens only; the conflict and change tones are knobs a rule SETS and the base rule READS. Guarded by `AiMarkdownViewCssTests` and `TmConflictRadarCssTests`.
  - **Localization:** `TmConflictRadar_*` (title and area label, the summary, the instructions, the filter, Merge, the ready and unresolved sentences as a plural family, the file column, Conflict, No change, the four change words, "was {0}", the repository-root and no-branch fallbacks, the resolve label, "Merge by hand", the directory meta format, the file/conflict count plural families, both empty states and the announcements) in English, Czech, Slovak and French plus `MockTmLocalizer`.
  - **Wireframe:** the new `conflict-radar` UI role (synonyms in both languages) plus the `TmConflictRadar` schema (`title`, `agents`, `files`, `conflicts`, `resolved`, `conflictsOnly`) and its declarative stencil, which draws the heading, the filter chip, the file column, one agent column per supplied agent and one row per file with its change words, its "Conflict" badge and the Merge action.
  - **Docs:** [docs/conflict-radar.md](docs/conflict-radar.md) — the models, the matrix rules, the grid, the side choice, the merge, accessibility and CSS; [docs/ai-agents.md](docs/ai-agents.md) links it as the branch-overlap surface.
  - **Demo:** the `/ai-agents` page gains a conflict section over three branches (two paths changed by two agents each, one more by a third pair) and is the STORE: the page echoes the reported decision list back and turns the merge request into a log line, because the demo has no repository.
  - **Tests:** `ConflictMatrixTests` (the records, the path normalisation and the rejection of a blank path, the branch collapse and its `Find`, the columns and the rows, a conflict being ≥ 2 agents, the ordering, the directory groups, the cell alignment, both duplicate-agent cases, both separator cases, the case difference, the empty matrix, the resolution rules and the merge request, the normalised and de-duplicated file list) and `TmConflictRadarTests` (bUnit: the native table with NO grid/row/columnheader/rowheader/cell role and its agent headers with their branches, the directory row-group and file row headers, the resolution row pointing at its file row through `headers`, the rows and their order, the conflict marking in words, the cells' icon + word and the "No change" cell, the summary, the directory groups and their collapse, the conflicts-only filter and its two-way binding, the radiogroup per file with its native name, an agent pick and a manual pick, the host's checkmarks, the reader's pick surviving a host echo, one decision per file, the merge's disabled state and its hint, the merge request, a conflict-free merge, both empty states, the single live region, the fallbacks and the chrome) plus `TmConflictRadarCssTests`.
- **New `TmAgentPresenceOverlay`** (`Tempo.Blazor.Components.AI`, package `Tempo.Blazor.AI`) with the `PresenceMarker` record and the `PresenceActivity` enum (in `Tempo.Blazor.Abstractions`, namespace `Tempo.Blazor.AI.Models`) plus the internal `AgentPresenceInterop` and the package's `tm-agent-presence.js` ES module (plan d67b33af, phase 8): the collaborators' cursors over ANY host content — labelled pointers anchored to an element or to a fraction of the content box, with the activity, the shared agent palette, an optional roster as the text alternative and one polite live region. No existing component, parameter default or CSS class changed.
  - **The model.** `PresenceMarker` is one cursor — `Id` (a missing id is generated, so two cursors for one agent stay two markers), `Agent` (REQUIRED), `AnchorId?` (a `data-presence-anchor` value) or `X`/`Y` (fractions of the content box, normalised into `0…1`, so a host that hands over a pixel offset still paints inside the content), `Activity`, `Label?` (the host's own sentence, used INSTEAD of the localized word) — and a record VALUE. An ANCHOR wins over a point, because it is measured from the real DOM and survives a scroll, a resize and a reflow.
  - **The surface.** `Markers`, `ChildContent` (rendered FIRST and untouched), `ShowRoster` (default `false`; the roster names every present agent and what they are doing, and says "No one is present." instead of rendering an empty list), `RosterLabel`, `AnnounceChanges` (default `true`; `false` renders NO live region at all rather than a second, competing one), `Class` / `AdditionalAttributes`.
  - **The measurement.** An anchored marker is placed by the package's ES module imported through `IJSObjectReference` (no `<script>` tag, no eval): it finds each marker's anchor inside the content, measures both boxes and writes `--tm-presence-x` / `--tm-presence-y`, so a moving cursor NEVER re-renders the component (on a Server circuit that would be a message per keystroke of a collaborator). A `ResizeObserver` watches the content and every anchor, a `MutationObserver` watches the content so a re-rendered anchor is found again, window `resize`/`scroll` (including a scroll inside the content) ask for a new pass, and the work is throttled (rAF plus an 80 ms minimum interval). A marker whose anchor disappeared is HIDDEN — the stylesheet reveals `[data-presence-placed="true"]` only — instead of being left at a stale position, and `detach()` releases every observer, listener and pending measurement (the component calls it from `DisposeAsync`).
  - **No JavaScript, no loss.** A point marker is painted from the host's own fractions and the roster needs no interop, so where the module cannot be imported (prerender, a disconnected circuit, a host without the static assets) only the MEASURED position of an anchored marker is missing — never a throw into the render loop.
  - **Motion.** Movement is the ONE animation (160 ms between measured positions) and the `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` block removes it, so a reader who asked for less motion gets the finished position at once. The module itself never animates, so there is one motion source only.
  - **Accessibility.** The visual layer is `aria-hidden`, `pointer-events: none` and never in the tab order (a pointer that took focus would fight the editor underneath); the roster is its text alternative; exactly ONE polite live region announces a join, an activity change and a leave — a join (or a changed agent NAME) reads "{0} is {1}." while an activity change reads "{0} is now {1}.", so the reader hears that something CHANGED rather than that the agent joined again — several simultaneous changes produce ONE sentence (the first in the host's order) and an unchanged state is never re-announced; `(pointer: coarse)` raises the roster row to the 44 px `--tm-touch-target`; `forced-colors: active` hands the cursor and the labels to `CanvasText`/`Canvas`/`Highlight` with `forced-color-adjust: none`.
  - **CSS classes:** `.tm-ai-presence`, `__content`, `__layer`, `__marker`, `__cursor`, `__pointer`, `__label`, `__name`, `__activity`, `__roster`, `__roster-title`, `__roster-empty`, `__roster-list`, `__roster-item`, `__roster-activity` — tokens only; the runtime knobs `--tm-presence-x` / `--tm-presence-y` / `--tm-presence-color` have declared defaults and the inline style always outranks them. Guarded by `AiMarkdownViewCssTests` and `TmAgentPresenceOverlayCssTests`, and the module by `npm run test:ai`.

- **New `TmAutonomyDial`** (`Tempo.Blazor.Components.AI`, package `Tempo.Blazor.AI`) with the `AutonomyLevel` / `AutonomyLock` records (in `Tempo.Blazor.Abstractions`, namespace `Tempo.Blazor.AI.Models`) plus the public `AutonomyDialPresentation` type and the internal `AutonomyPresentation` helper (plan d67b33af, phase 6): how much an agent may do on its own — the grades the host declares, the ceiling a plan imposes and the limits somebody else enforces. No existing component, parameter default or CSS class changed.
  - **The models.** `AutonomyLevel` is one stop — `Value` (the grade a host persists and a ceiling compares against), `Label`, `Description` — and a record VALUE a host recomposes with `level with { … }`; a blank label or description renders the component's own localized fallback or no line at all. `AutonomyLock` is a limit the surface cannot lift — `ActionLabel`, `Source` (who enforces it), `Reason?` — and a blank source prints no "enforced by" line instead of a line with a blank source. `AutonomyDialPresentation.Dial` is the DEFAULT (0), so an unset presentation lands on the slider rather than on a cast integer, and an unknown value falls back to the dial.

The host's stops are copied, nulls dropped, a duplicate `Value` kept once and the list sorted ascending — ArrowRight always means "more autonomy". A stop the host left unlabelled prints the localized `Level {n}` fallback.
  - **The dial and the radio group.** `Presentation="Dial"` (the default) renders a real `role="slider"` with ONE tab stop: `aria-valuemin`/`aria-valuemax` are the allowed grades (the ceiling lowers the max), `aria-valuenow` is the invariant number and `aria-valuetext` is the grade's LABEL; ArrowRight/ArrowUp and ArrowLeft/ArrowDown step one grade, Home/End jump to the ends of what is ALLOWED, and a key past an end changes nothing and announces nothing.   - **The ceiling and the locks.** `MaxAllowed` is the highest `AutonomyLevel.Value` a plan allows. The stops above it still render — marked `data-available="false"`, dashed and dimmed, disabled in the segmented presentation — and a line under the dial states "Levels above {grade} are not available." plus the host's `MaxAllowedReason` or the localized default. `Locks` lists what somebody else enforces with its action, its source and its reason; a lock is a FACT, never a control (not a tab stop, and the glyph is `aria-hidden` because the sentence carries it).
  - **The confirmation.** `ConfirmAbove` holds a change at or above it in a `role="group"` whose message names the grade AND its description; the focus moves to the confirm button, Enter/Space on the native button commits (one `ValueChanged`), Escape or Cancel drops it and the focus returns to the slider (WCAG 2.4.3). A `Value` above the ceiling (or between two stops) renders the nearest allowed grade; the component never writes the host's state behind its back.
  - **Accessibility.** ONE polite live region announces a COMMITTED grade ("Autonomy level: {label}") and re-announces an identical sentence through an invisible marker; a refused key announces nothing, and the confirmation needs no second region because its message is already in front of the reader. `(pointer: coarse)` raises the step and confirmation buttons to the 44 px `--tm-touch-target`; `forced-colors` hands the track and lock borders to `CanvasText`, the fill and the reached dot to `Highlight` and every focus ring to a 3 px `Highlight` outline. The only movement is the track fill's travel (`--tm-transition-fast`), and `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` removes it.

- **New `TmMemoryPanel`** (`Tempo.Blazor.Components.AI`, package `Tempo.Blazor.AI`) with the `MemoryItem` / `MemoryReview` / `MemoryBulkActionRequest` records and the `MemoryItemStatus` / `MemoryReviewDecision` / `MemoryBulkAction` enums (in `Tempo.Blazor.Abstractions`, namespace `Tempo.Blazor.AI.Models`) plus the public `MemoryForgetMode` / `MemoryStatusFilter` types and the internal `MemoryPresentation` helper (plan d67b33af, phase 6): what an agent remembers, with the review of what it proposed, an inline edit, pause/resume, a removal with an undo window, a search, a status filter and bulk actions. No existing component, parameter default or CSS class changed.
  - **The models.** `MemoryItem` is one fact — `Id`, `Category`, `Text`, `Status`, `Confidence?` (a RATIO), `Source?`, `CreatedAt`, `UpdatedAt?` — and a record VALUE; `MemoryItemStatus.Active` is the DEFAULT (0) so an unclassified memory never reads as forgotten, a blank id is REJECTED with `ArgumentException` (an id invented at construction would change on every rebuild and silently drop the row's selection, edit and undo state), and a blank category means "no category" (every uncategorised memory shares the ONE localized Uncategorized group). Nothing is invented: a confidence outside `0…1` or NaN and a missing source print nothing at all, and `UpdatedAt` is optional (a fact that was never edited says "Learned {date}" instead). `MemoryReview` carries the decision about a proposal, `MemoryBulkActionRequest` a COPIED selection plus what to do with it, `MemoryForgetMode.UndoWindow` is the DEFAULT (0) so losing a fact without a way back is never the unset behaviour, and `MemoryStatusFilter.All` is the default view.
  - **The groups.** Rows are grouped by trimmed category, the groups are ordered by their display name in the current culture, and each group is an APG disclosure on a NATIVE button with `aria-expanded`/`aria-controls`, its count inside the button's accessible name and an opt-in select-all. `CollapsedCategories` is two-way and a collapsed group keeps nothing in the DOM; collapsing never moves the focus.
  - **The master switch.** `@bind-Enabled` turns storage off while what is already known stays readable — with NO action offered (no edit, pause, forget, review or selection) and the switch itself still usable. The reader's pick wins until the host MOVES the parameter, so a host re-rendering the same value cannot undo it.
  - **A row and the inline edit.** A row states its status as an icon + a localized word + a tone (`data-status`), then the confidence as a percentage, the source and the timestamp. Edit turns the text into a `<textarea>` and moves the focus into it: Enter commits, Shift+Enter writes a new line, Escape rolls back, and Save/Cancel are the pointer alternative (WCAG 2.5.7); an unchanged draft closes without a second report, opening another row's editor discards the first draft, and the committed text is shown immediately while `OnEdit` reports the new instance. The focus moves into the SAVED ROW (a `tabindex="-1"` container, so the browser's remaining Enter key sequence has nothing to activate) and back to the Edit button on a cancel (WCAG 2.4.3).
  - **Forgetting with an undo window.** `Forget` removes the row at once; with `UndoWindow` (the default) the host is told only when the window closes, and one undo bar shows the memory, an Undo action and the remaining seconds from the injected `TimeProvider` (no animation). Undo restores the row and the host is never told; expiry reports `OnForget` exactly once; a second window reports the previous removal IMMEDIATELY; disposing the panel (navigation) closes the window the reader can no longer reach and still reports the pending removal, because the component is `IAsyncDisposable` and must not lose a removal the reader confirmed; a zero-length window behaves like `Immediate`, which reports at once and offers no undo.
  - **Review, search, filter and bulk.** Approve/Reject report `OnReview(new MemoryReview(item, decision))` and the row becomes active or forgotten. The search (`type="search"`) narrows by text, category and source and hides empty groups; the status filter is a segmented radio group with the stable slugs `all|active|paused|pending-review|forgotten`; both are two-way and neither reports to the host, and each change is announced once ("Showing {n} of {total} memories." — a plural family). With `Selectable` (the default) a bar above the groups offers Pause / Resume / Forget / Clear, and a bulk action is ONE `OnBulkAction(new MemoryBulkActionRequest(items, action))` with a copy of the selection — a bulk removal does not fire `OnForget` per row, and a selection the filter hides is pruned.
  - **Async callbacks.** Every action awaits its callback: while it runs the row's buttons disable (no doubled request) with a "Saving…" note and the root carries `data-busy="true"` / `aria-busy="true"`; a callback that THROWS prints the localized "The change could not be saved: {message}", announces it and leaves the row untouched.
  - **Accessibility.** Every state is a WORD plus an icon (the tone is the third cue); groups are native disclosures and every checkbox a native input (Space is never emulated); ONE polite live region announces every change INCLUDING a failure (the visible error text is that announcement) and re-announces an identical sentence through an invisible marker; `(pointer: coarse)` raises buttons, the search field and even the checkboxes to the 44 px `--tm-touch-target`; `forced-colors` hands the borders and notes to `CanvasText` and every focus ring to a 3 px `Highlight` outline. The partial declares no transition and no animation.
  - **CSS classes:** `.tm-ai-memory`, `--off`, `__header`, `__title`, `__switch`, `__hint`, `__off-note`, `__toolbar`, `__search`, `__filter`, `__bulk`, `__bulk-count`, `__bulk-actions`, `__bulk-action`, `__groups`, `__group`, `__group-head`, `__group-title`, `__group-toggle`, `__group-chevron`, `__group-name`, `__group-count`, `__group-select`, `__list`, `__item`, `__select`, `__body`, `__text`, `__edit-box`, `__edit-actions`, `__save`, `__cancel`, `__meta`, `__status`, `__status-icon`, `__status-text`, `__confidence`, `__source`, `__updated`, `__actions`, `__action`, `__action--danger`, `__busy`, `__empty`, `__error`, `__undo`, `__undo-text`, `__undo-action`, `__undo-timer` — tokens only; a status modifier SETS `--tm-memory-status-ink`/`-fill`/`-border` and the base chip READS them, and a forgotten row keeps `text-decoration: line-through` as a second, non-colour cue. - **New `TmScheduledRuns`** (`Tempo.Blazor.Components.AI`, package `Tempo.Blazor.AI`) with the `RunWindow` / `RunSegment` / `ScheduledRun` / `ScheduledRunMoveRequest` records and the `ScheduledRunStatus` enum (in `Tempo.Blazor.Abstractions`, namespace `Tempo.Blazor.AI.Models`) plus the public `RunViewMode` type and the internal `RunWindowPlanner` strategy (plan d67b33af, phase 7): runs placed into a scheduler's supply windows, with the capacity each window offers, the load the host already committed, a run split across windows, an overloaded window called out, a week/day/table presentation and a move by drag or by menu. No existing component, parameter default or CSS class changed.
  - **The models.** `RunWindow` is one window — `Id` (REQUIRED: a blank value throws `ArgumentException`, because the plan and the reader's placement are keyed by it), `Start`, `End` (**exclusive**, so two adjacent windows partition the day instead of overlapping by an instant), `Capacity`, `Used` — and a record VALUE. A window that closes before it opens offers no time (the planner skips it), a negative capacity or load reads as zero, `Available` is never negative, and a window the host committed BEYOND its capacity is `IsOverloaded` with an `Overflow` of its own. `ScheduledRun` is one run — `Id` (REQUIRED), `Title`, `EstimatedUnits`, `Segments`, `Status` — and its `Segments` are the placement the host committed: the FIRST segment's window is the run's preferred start window and the rest is informational, because the planner recomputes the slices so they add up to the capacity it draws. `ScheduledRunStatus.Planned` is the DEFAULT (0), so an unclassified run is planned work and never finished work.
  - **The plan.** `RunWindowPlanner` is the pure, unit-tested half: usable windows in their own time order (a tie keeps the host's order), first-fit placement from the run's preferred window (the reader's move first, then the run's own first segment), a run SPLIT into one slice per window when it does not fit in one, gaps filled in the host's declaration order, and the units that fit NOWHERE reported as `UnitsUnplaced` instead of overflowing a window. A slice's time is proportional to its units (a three-hour window accepting four units gives each unit 45 minutes), and the committed `Used` shifts a slice later in its window.
  - **The three views.** `ViewMode` (`@bind-ViewMode`, default `Week`) shows every supplied window grouped by day, one day in full with `Previous day` / `Next day` stepping through the days the windows actually cover (`aria-disabled`, never the native `disabled`, so the focus never drops to `<body>`), or the same schedule as one TABLE — the text alternative (WCAG 1.3.1), which carries every run, its window, its slice time, its units, its status and the same move menu. `SelectedDay` is two-way and defaults to the first day with windows. The reader's pick wins until the host MOVES the parameter.
  - **The capacity bar.** Each window draws one decorative (`aria-hidden`) bar — the host's committed fill, then one slice per placed run coloured from the shared agent palette — painted from the SAME segments the rows show, so the picture and the numbers cannot disagree; every number it draws is also a sentence in the header ("Units used: 1 of 6", "Free: 3 units" / "Full", "Overloaded by 2 units" with an icon and the danger tone). A run with more than one slice carries "Part 1 of 2".
  - **Moving a run.** The pointer drag is the shared `tm-sortable.js` over `pointer-drag.js` through `TmSortableList`'s group support (each window is a transfer-only list, kept attached while it has no rows so an empty window accepts a run at slot `0`), and every run's menu lists every window with the current one named "(current)" and disabled, so nothing is drag-only (WCAG 2.5.7). The menu's trigger paints the `MoreVertical` glyph (`data-icon="more-vertical"`), never a second copy of the drag grip beside it. A move is applied to the reader's own overlay and the plan is rebuilt; when the target window has no room for even the first slice the move is REFUSED — the run stays where it was and both the notice line and the live region say why — because the surface never reports a placement the plan did not make. The overlay entry is dropped when the host supplies a NEW instance of the run.
  - **Accessibility.** Every state is a word plus an icon (status, full, overloaded); ONE polite live region announces a committed move and a refusal and re-announces an identical sentence through an invisible marker; the window lists render no region of their own; `(pointer: coarse)` raises the day buttons and the move menu to the 44 px `--tm-touch-target`; `forced-colors: active` hands the palette to `CanvasText`/`Canvas`/`Highlight`. The partial declares no transition and no animation.
  - **CSS classes:** `.tm-ai-runs`, `--week` / `--day` / `--table`, `__header`, `__title`, `__summary`, `__view`, `__day-nav`, `__day-step`, `__current-day`, `__instructions`, `__notice`, `__empty`, `__board`, `__day`, `__day-title`, `__windows`, `__window`, `--overloaded`, `--full`, `__window-head`, `__window-title`, `__window-meta`, `__bar`, `__bar-committed`, `__bar-slice`, `__overload`, `__overload-icon`, `__overload-text`, `__full`, `__full-icon`, `__full-text`, `__free`, `__run`, `__run-dot`, `__run-body`, `__run-title`, `__run-meta`, `__status`, `--planned|--running|--succeeded|--failed|--paused`, `__status-icon`, `__status-text`, `__units`, `__part`, `__run-actions`, `__move`, `__move-trigger`, `__table-wrap`, `__table`, `__caption`, `__row`, `--unplaced`, `__cell`, `--run`, `--actions` — tokens only; the runtime knobs (`--tm-runs-slice-start`, `--tm-runs-slice-size`, `--tm-runs-run-color`) have declared defaults on the root and the inline style always outranks them. Guarded by `AiMarkdownViewCssTests` and `TmScheduledRunsCssTests`.

  - **Wireframe:** the new `scheduled-runs` UI role (synonyms in both languages) plus the `TmScheduledRuns` schema (`title`, `runs`, `windows`, `view`, `overloaded`) and its declarative stencil, which draws the heading, the view chip, a day heading and one window card per supplied window with its capacity line, capacity bar, free/overloaded line and run rows.

- **New `TmDelegateBoard`** (`Tempo.Blazor.Components.AI`, package `Tempo.Blazor.AI`) with the `DelegateTask` / `DelegateAgent` / `DelegateMoveRequest` records and the `DelegateTaskPriority` enum (in `Tempo.Blazor.Abstractions`, namespace `Tempo.Blazor.AI.Models`) plus the internal `DelegateAutoAssigner` strategy and `DelegatePresentation` helper (plan d67b33af, phase 7): work handed out to agents as a backlog column and one column per agent, with a task moved by pointer drag, by its own Assign menu or by an automatic pass. No existing component, parameter default or CSS class changed.
  - **The models.** `DelegateTask` is one unit of work — `Id` (REQUIRED: a blank value throws `ArgumentException`, because the board's overlay is keyed by it and an invented id would move a task back to the backlog on every rebuild), `Title`, `EstimatedDuration?`, `Priority?`, `AssignedAgentId?`. Nothing is invented: a missing, zero or negative duration is "not estimated" (no duration line and no projected end), a missing priority is NOT `Normal` (it is no grade at all), and a blank assignee is the backlog. `DelegateAgent` is one column — `Agent` (`AgentRef`, required), `MaxConcurrency` (default 1, clamped to at least 1), `ActiveCount`, `BusyUntil?` — and capacity is the HOST's numbers: `RemainingSlots` is `MaxConcurrency - ActiveCount` clamped at zero, a stale `BusyUntil` in the past means free NOW, and the number of cards a column shows never decides capacity. `DelegateMoveRequest` describes an assignment, a return to the backlog and a hand-over with one record (`Task`, `From?`, `To?`, `AssigneeId`, `IsAssignment`, `IsUnassignment`, `IsHandover`).
  - **The board.** A `role="group"` of columns: the backlog first (dashed frame) and one column per agent, each heading a real heading one level below the surface title. A card states its title (or the localized "Untitled task"), its priority as a WORD plus a flag plus a tone (`data-priority` carries the stable slug) and its estimate ("Estimated 1 h 30 min"), or nothing when there is none. A column states the host's capacity ("1 of 3 running"), how many cards it holds, when the agent is free, and — at capacity — "Full" with an icon.
  - **The occupied-until preview.** Each column prints "Free now", "Occupied until 14:20", or "Occupied until 14:50 with this task" while a card with an estimate is pointed at, computed as the agent's own free time plus the task's estimate (`DelegatePresentation.Project`). It follows FOCUS as well as hover, and the column carries `data-preview` and `data-state` (`free` / `busy` / `preview`) so no host has to parse the sentence. A leave is deferred by a 150 ms grace window that the next enter cancels, so stepping between two cards of one column never blinks the projection off (`focusout` bubbles from every card).
  - **Moving a task.** The pointer drag is the shared `tm-sortable.js` over `pointer-drag.js`, driven through `TmSortableList`'s group support — the columns are TRANSFER-ONLY lists, so nothing announces an order inside a column and the component writes no gesture of its own. Every card carries an Assign menu (the keyboard and tap alternative, WCAG 2.5.7 — and the only keyboard path) with one item per agent plus "Move back to the backlog"; a full agent is named "Planner (full)" and its item is disabled, and a drop on a full column is REFUSED with a visible notice and one announcement.
  - **The automatic pass.** `AutoAssign` (`@bind-AutoAssign`) hands every unassigned task to the first free agent — the one that becomes free earliest, ties keeping the host's order — and one pass fills the slots it consumes, so three tasks never all land on the first agent. A task the reader puts BACK in the backlog stays there until the switch is re-armed, so the pass never fights the reader, and the pass announces one summary sentence instead of one per task.
  - **The overlay.** The board shows the reader's move at once and drops its copy the moment the host supplies a NEW instance of the task, so a host re-rendering the same snapshot cannot undo the move and a host that accepted it is never fought. A task assigned to an agent the board does not show stays in the backlog.
  - **Accessibility.** Every state is a word plus an icon; ONE polite live region announces every committed move and every refusal and re-announces an identical sentence through an invisible marker; the transfer-only lists render no region of their own, so a board has exactly one; the Assign menu's wrapper is the tab stop and carries a real focus ring; `(pointer: coarse)` raises it to the 44 px `--tm-touch-target`; `forced-colors: active` hands the toned chips and the borders to `CanvasText`/`Canvas` and every focus ring to a `Highlight` outline. The partial declares no transition and no animation.
  - **CSS classes:** `.tm-ai-delegate`, `__header`, `__title`, `__summary`, `__auto`, `__hint`, `__instructions`, `__notice`, `__board`, `__column`, `--backlog`, `--agent`, `--full`, `__column-head`, `__column-title`, `__column-meta`, `__capacity`, `__separator`, `__queued`, `__availability`, `__full`, `__full-icon`, `__full-text`, `__task`, `__task-head`, `__task-title`, `__priority`, `--low|--normal|--high|--urgent`, `__priority-icon`, `__priority-text`, `__task-meta`, `__task-icon`, `__task-actions`, `__assign`, `__assign-trigger`, `__empty`, `__empty--agents` — tokens only; a priority modifier SETS `--tm-delegate-priority-ink`/`-fill`/`-border` and the base rule READS them, and the availability line is toned through `--tm-delegate-availability-ink` by its `data-state`. Guarded by `AiMarkdownViewCssTests` and `TmDelegateBoardCssTests`.

- **`TmSortableList` gained cross-list transfers (additive)** (core, plan d67b33af phase 7): `Group`, `ListId`, `OnTransfer` (`SortableTransferArgs`) and `AllowLocalReorder`. Two lists that pass the same non-empty `Group` accept each other's rows; `tm-sortable.js` resolves the target list from its own registry, follows the pointer in both axes and marks the list it would drop into with `tm-sortable-list--drop-target`. The transfer is reported ONCE on the SOURCE list and the component announces nothing for it — the host owns that sentence, because only it knows whether the drop was accepted. `AllowLocalReorder="false"` drops the in-list keyboard model and the per-row move menu (and the list's own live region) while keeping the pointer transfers; such a row also stops calling itself a "sortable item" (no `aria-roledescription`, no per-row `aria-describedby`, no tab stop — the list keeps the instructions), because a screen reader would otherwise announce every card with a keyboard grab that does not exist. An EMPTY list of a group stays attached to the module (and keeps a one-touch-target hit box via `__items--empty`) so an empty column, an emptied backlog or an empty run window can still receive the first row; a row dropped over an empty target is reported at slot `0`. Every default keeps today's behaviour: a list without `Group` drags, reorders and announces exactly as before, and `docs/sortable-list.md` documents the new contract. Tests: 11 new bUnit facts in `TmSortableListTests` and 7 new node tests in `tm-sortable.test.mjs`.

The arrows between two steps are decorative SVG (`aria-hidden`): the list already carries the order.

Every item is its kind's icon, its label and the localized kind word; a lost item prints `Reason: …` when the host supplied one. `ExpandedStepIds` is two-way (`@bind-ExpandedStepIds`): `null` (the default) opens EVERY step, an empty list closes them all, and the reported value is materialised in CHAIN order. An empty list says so ("Nothing was passed on." / "Nothing was lost.") instead of rendering nothing.

No existing component, parameter default or CSS class changed.
  - **The models.** `FallbackAttempt` is one attempt — `ModelId`, `Label`, `Status`, `FailureReason?`, `LatencyMs?`, `At?` — and a record VALUE; `FallbackAttemptStatus.NotTried` is the DEFAULT (0) so an unclassified attempt never claims an answer was produced, a blank model id is generated at construction, and the `Label` falls back to the id so no branch is blank. A missing or negative `LatencyMs` stays UNMEASURED (`HasLatency` / `Latency`): the flow renders no latency at all and the table states the localized "not measured", because a zero would be a measurement the host never made. `FallbackChainEntry` is one model in the ordered chain (`ModelId`, `Label`, `DisplayName`, `FromModel(AiModelInfo)`), and `FallbackResolutionPolicy` defaults to `Pin` so an unset policy never falls back to another model silently.
  - **The flow.** An ordered list of labelled nodes ("Attempt {n}", the model, the result as an icon + a localized word + a tone, the failure/skip reason, the measured latency and the time), joined by decorative SVG arrows (`aria-hidden`). The FIRST `Succeeded` attempt ends the chain, so the Answer node names it ("Answered by {model}"); the branch arrow and the card are tinted with the success tone only when an answer exists (`data-success` / `data-answered`), and an unanswered chain says "No answer yet". `ViewMode="Table"` (`FallbackChainViewMode`) carries the same attempts, results, reasons, latencies and times as one table; the View switcher is two-way with `@bind-ViewMode`. The run view REPORTS the resolution policy as a word (`data-policy` hook) instead of offering to change it, and `ShowPolicy="false"` hides it.
  - **The editor.** `Mode="Edit"` (`FallbackChainMode`, a plain parameter the HOST owns) swaps the flow for the chain editor: the ordered rows go through the shared `TmSortableList<FallbackChainEntry>` (pointer drag, per-row move menu and the keyboard grab/move/drop model — WCAG 2.5.7), a native `<select>` of the `AvailableModels` that are not already in the chain adds one from the catalogue, a labelled button per row removes one, and the policy is a segmented radio group (`Pin` | `Fallback` | `Auto`). `Chain` is two-way with `@bind-Chain` and `ChainChanged` fires once per committed change with a NEW list; when `Chain` is null the editor derives its starting chain from `Attempts`, drops duplicate model ids, and keeps its own working copy so an unrelated host render never resets a reorder in progress. The Add control disables itself and explains why ("Every available model is already in the chain." / "No models are available to add."). The policy group's label in Edit mode is an INSTRUCTION (`TmFallbackChain_PolicyEditLabel`, "Choose how the chain resolves") rather than the run view's noun phrase, so the editor does not read as a second read-out.
  - **Accessibility.** Every attempt is a list item with real text and decorative arrows; a result is an icon, a word and a tone and a failure always prints its reason; the editor's controls are native with visible labels or an `aria-label` containing their visible text (WCAG 2.5.3); ONE polite live region announces an ADD and a REMOVE while a reorder is narrated by the sortable list's own region (nothing is announced twice); the focus is handed back after an edit that removes or disables the control the reader was on (WCAG 2.4.3) — a removed row passes it to the row that took its place, an emptied chain to the Add control, and an add that exhausts the catalogue to the row it created, with the editor hint (`tabindex="-1"`) as the last resort; the position and the latency follow the bound `Culture` instead of `CultureInfo.CurrentCulture`; `(pointer: coarse)` raises the remove/add buttons and the model select to the 44 px `--tm-touch-target`; `forced-colors` hands the borders to `CanvasText`, the fills to `Canvas` and the focus rings to a 3 px `Highlight` outline. - **Agent visualizations — the shared foundation** (plan d67b33af, phase 1; `Tempo.Blazor.Abstractions` + `Tempo.Blazor.AI`): the identity model, the live-data contract and the colour palette every agent surface in the AI package is built on. No existing component, parameter default or CSS class changed.
  - **Models** (`src/Tempo.Blazor.Abstractions/AI/Agents/`, namespace `Tempo.Blazor.AI.Models`): `AgentRef` — the one way an agent is named (stable `Id`, display `Name`, optional `Role` and `AvatarUrl`, and `ColorIndex`) as a record **value** a host recomposes with `agent with { … }`; `ColorIndex` is normalised into `0…7` on assignment, `ColorToken` names the palette token, `Initials` derives the avatar glyph ("Data analyst" → `DA`, "Bedřich Novák" → `BN`, one word → one letter, no letter → `?`) from whole text elements, and `PaletteSize`/`PaletteToken`/`NormalizeColorIndex` are the shared arithmetic. `AgentActivityStatus` — `Idle` | `Queued` | `Running` | `WaitingForApproval` | `Succeeded` | `Failed` | `Cancelled`, the transport-neutral vocabulary a host maps its own backend onto.
  - **`AgentEventStream<TEvent>`** — the live contract that all eleven surfaces share: a **snapshot** (parameters) plus incremental **events** with a monotonic `Sequence`. `Apply` sorts a batch by the sequence (a merged or re-delivered page cannot apply a block before the event that opened it), drops what was already applied (idempotent — a hub redelivers after a reconnect), and never papers over a hole: a missing sequence rejects the WHOLE batch, sets `HasGap` and raises `GapDetected` **once** with the first sequence the stream does not have, so the applied tail is always contiguous and the repair (`ResetToSnapshot` / reload) is exact. A fresh stream needs no baseline (the first batch may start at 0, at 1 or at a restarted number), `ResetToSnapshot` may move it backwards, a redelivery does not clear a gap, and the class is thread-safe so a hub callback and a poll may feed one stream. `GapDetected` is the one callback raised **after** the stream's gate is released (with `HasGap` already true), so a handler may hand the repair to another thread and wait for it instead of deadlocking against the applying one. 50 000 events apply in one ordered pass.
  - **`AgentRenderThrottle`** — the shared paint gate: at most one render per **100 ms** (`DefaultInterval`) measured on an injected `TimeProvider`, so a 10 events/s hub collapses into ten paints a second instead of ten renders per event — the STATE is never throttled, only the paint. `ShouldRender()` opens a window, `DelayUntilNextRender()` counts one down (never negative), `Reset()` lets a host that repainted for its own reason through, and `TimeSpan.Zero` opts out entirely.
  - **Tokens:** `--tm-agent-color-0` … `--tm-agent-color-7` plus `--tm-agent-color-ink` in `tokens.css` (700-tones under white ink) and `tokens-dark.css` (300-tones under the dark ink, restated in the light island), with the bundled stylesheet rebuilt. Both pairs hold WCAG AA (4.5 : 1) for the initials — **measured**, never assumed, by `AgentColorTokenTests` — and the eight slots are asserted distinct in each theme, so two agents in one visualization can never share a colour.

- **New `TmAgentLanes`** (`Tempo.Blazor.Components.AI`, package `Tempo.Blazor.AI`) with the `AgentLaneBlock` / `AgentHandoffLink` / `AgentLaneEvent` / `AgentLanesSnapshot` records and the `AgentLaneBlockKind` / `AgentLaneBlockMarker` / `AgentLaneEventKind` enums (in `Tempo.Blazor.Abstractions`, namespace `Tempo.Blazor.AI.Models`) plus the internal `AgentLanesLayout` and `AgentLanePresentation` helpers: a multi-agent run as one LANE per agent on a shared time axis. No existing component, parameter default or CSS class changed.
  - **The models.** `AgentLaneBlock` is one piece of work by one agent — `Id`, `AgentId`, `Start`, `End?`, `Status`, `Label`, `Kind`, `Marker?` — and a record VALUE a host recomposes with `block with { … }`; `End == null` means *still running*, so a surface draws it up to its own "now" instead of inventing a duration, and `EndAt(now)` clamps an end before the start (a negative duration is never meaningful). `AgentHandoffLink` is one handover (`FromBlockId` | `FromAgentId`, `ToAgentId`, `At`, `Label?`): the block anchor is the accurate picture, the agent anchor the fallback for a block the snapshot does not contain, and a link that names no source is counted as unresolved instead of guessed. Handoffs are append-only and identified by ALL their fields, so a redelivered link is one arrow while an edited `Label` is a new one — a host that needs an editable handover models it as a block (`BlockUpserted`), which is identified by its `Id` alone and replaces the previous version. `AgentLanesSnapshot` is the complete state at one moment (`Sequence`, `Agents`, `Blocks`, `Handoffs`) and `Apply(events)` folds the incremental tail into a NEW value — the snapshot it was given is never edited. `AgentLaneEvent` (`BlockUpserted` / `BlockRemoved` / `HandoffAdded`) is the concrete incremental change, so a host of any transport builds one small record per change.
  - **The layout is pure C#** (`AgentLanesLayout`, unit-tested by `AgentLanesLayoutTests`): the range is derived from the blocks (an open block reaches "now"), padded and aligned to a "nice" step from a fixed ladder (1 s … 1 week), so a label reads `09:10` and never `09:07:23`; a very short run is widened to a readable minimum and an empty run still draws an axis around "now"; the axis is drawn in the offset of the supplied `now`, and a range crossing midnight makes every label carry the date; geometry is PIXELS (`PixelsPerHour` × `RowHeight`), so blocks and SVG connectors line up exactly; overlapping work inside one lane is stacked into sub-rows (a row is reused as soon as it is free); a block naming an agent the snapshot forgot gets a lane appended after the declared ones (named through the localized fallback) so a run is never silently incomplete; a handoff starts at the handed-over block's trailing edge (or at the handover moment on the source lane), bends at the horizontal midpoint and ends on the target lane — an unresolvable link is counted, never drawn.
  - **Live data.** `Snapshot` is the baseline and `Events` the tail, fed through the shared `AgentEventStream<AgentLaneEvent>`: a batch is ordered by `Sequence`, already-applied events are dropped (a hub redelivers after a reconnect), and a HOLE rejects the whole batch, raises `OnGapDetected` once with the first sequence the stream does not have and announces that live updates are behind instead of painting stale data. The component re-bases its stream when the snapshot's sequence changes (a reload) and keeps the view it already has when a host rebuilds an equal snapshot. Every accepted event is folded into that view immediately — and only the NEWLY accepted tail is folded in, never a replay of everything the session ever sent, so a parameter set costs the size of the batch and not the length of the run; only the PAINT is gated by `AgentRenderThrottle` (`RenderThrottle`, default `null` → the shared 100 ms, `TimeSpan.Zero` paints every batch), with one trailing paint scheduled at the end of the window on the injected `TimeProvider`, and the state is never throttled.
  - **Zoom and the "now" line.** `PixelsPerHour` (two-way, clamped to `MinPixelsPerHour`–`MaxPixelsPerHour`, default 120 / 24–2400) is the whole zoom: the +/− buttons multiply/divide by 1.5 and announce the level; `FitToViewAsync` measures the scrollport and divides the room by the run's length, keeping the current zoom where nothing can be measured (prerender, no JavaScript) instead of jumping to a guess. Ctrl+wheel (a trackpad pinch) and a two-finger pinch arrive through the CORE `_content/Tempo.Blazor/js/pointer-gesture.js` helper, imported across the static-asset boundary by the package's new `tm-agent-lanes.js` (node-tested through `npm run test:ai`) — never a second gesture implementation — and a gesture reports its level to the host once, when it ends, so a bound `PixelsPerHour` does not re-render mid-gesture. The "now" line and the open blocks' growth read the injected `TimeProvider` and tick only while a block is open.
  - **The text alternative.** `ViewMode="Table"` (`AgentLanesViewMode`) renders exactly the same snapshot as two plain tables — the blocks (agent, activity, kind, start, end, state, marker) and the handoffs (from, to, at, label) — with the same row action selecting a block, so a screen reader, a keyboard-only reader or a narrow phone loses no fact.
  - **Accessibility.** Every block is a native `<button>` (Tab walks them, Enter/Space select natively, `aria-pressed="true"` marks the picked one) named by its visible ACTIVITY first, then its agent, kind, start, end (or the localized "Now"), state and marker, so a voice-control user can say what the block shows (WCAG 2.5.3); a state and a marker are always an icon AND a word, never colour alone. The scrollport is a tab stop (`role="group"`, named by the localized "Agent timeline", described by the keyboard instructions) so the horizontal axis is reachable without a pointer. ONE polite live region announces a selection, a zoom change and a stream hole; the ticking "now" line and the connector SVG are `aria-hidden` and nothing is announced twice. `(pointer: coarse)` grows the zoom buttons, the table action and a very short block to the 44 px `--tm-touch-target` (the block's axis position and the table's exact timestamps stay authoritative). `forced-colors` hands every focus ring back to `Highlight`, keeps a `CanvasText` edge on each block and paints the picked block's ring in `Highlight`, because a tone border and a tinted fill collapse under Windows high contrast. The surface declares **no transition and no animation** — a live run repaints while it streams — so the package reduced-motion enumeration is unchanged.

  - **The models.** `FanOutTask` is one unit of work — `Id`, `Label`, `Status`, `Worker?` (`AgentRef`), `WorkerId?`, `Attempt`, `MaxAttempts?`, `StartedAt?`, `EstimatedEndAt?`, `CostMicroUnits?`, `Error?` — and a record VALUE a host recomposes with `task with { … }`; a blank id is generated at construction, an attempt below 1 reads as 1 and a `MaxAttempts` of zero or less reads as NO limit, so a host that never set one can never block a retry. - **New `TmAgentGraph`** (`Tempo.Blazor.Components.AI`, package `Tempo.Blazor.AI`) with the `AgentGraphNode` / `AgentGraphEdge` / `AgentGraphCall` / `AgentGraphSnapshot` records and the `AgentGraphNodeKind` enum (in `Tempo.Blazor.Abstractions`, namespace `Tempo.Blazor.AI.Models`) plus the `AgentGraphPosition` / `AgentGraphViewMode` public types, the internal `AgentGraphLayout` / `AgentGraphPresentation` helpers and the internal `AgentGraphInterop` (plan d67b33af, phase 3): agents and the tools they call as ONE network — a box per node in the column its kind belongs to, a curve per connection whose thickness is how often it was called, and a short pulse on the curve every time a new call arrives. No existing component, parameter default or CSS class changed; the only edit to a shipped file is the additive `AgentRef.InitialsOf(string?)`, which the shared initials rule now lives in (an agent graph's tool, resource and human nodes need the same initials an agent paints).
  - **The models.** `AgentGraphNode` is one node — `Id`, `Label`, `Kind`, `Status`, `Group?`, `Agent?` — and a record VALUE a host recomposes with `node with { … }`; a blank id is generated at construction, an AGENT node may carry the shared `AgentRef` (so it paints the agent's palette slot and initials) and a tool, a resource or a human carries none, because painting them in an agent's colour would claim an identity they do not have. `AgentGraphEdge` (`From`, `To`, `CallCount`, `LastCallAt?`, `IsActive`) is one connection; a negative `CallCount` is clamped to zero, so an edge only ever grows, and `From == To` is a legal self loop drawn beside the node. `AgentGraphSnapshot` is the complete state (`Sequence`, `Nodes`, `Edges`) and `Apply(calls)` folds an incremental tail into a NEW value (an unknown edge id is ignored rather than invented, and a batch that changes nothing returns the SAME instance). `AgentGraphCall` is the incremental change (`Sequence`, `EdgeId`, `At?`, `Count`): one small record per call, or a page of identical calls at once.
  - **The layout is pure C#** (`AgentGraphLayout`, unit-tested by `AgentGraphLayoutTests`): columns follow the node KIND (human, agent, resource, tool) and are then tightened so every edge points forward — an agent delegating to another agent pushes the target one column right instead of drawing a line back across the picture, and a tool feeding an agent pushes the AGENT right, because that is the direction the data flows; an empty kind column is collapsed. A cycle is broken by a depth-first pass in declaration order and the edge that closes it is still drawn, but BELOW the boxes. Rows inside a column are ordered by a barycenter heuristic (four alternating sweeps), which is what stops the curves from crossing, and members of one `Group` are kept in one contiguous run with ONE labelled box around them. The stroke width is a LOG scale (`EdgeWidth`, 1.5 px … 7 px over `log(1 + count) / log(1 + maxCount)`), so ten calls out of a hundred sit at half the width range instead of at a tenth of it. A host may pin a node through `NodePositions` (`AgentGraphPosition`): it keeps its exact coordinate, is flagged `data-pinned` and the canvas grows to contain it. Same snapshot, same numbers — a live surface re-runs the pass on every paint.
  - **Live data.** `Snapshot` is the baseline and `Events` the tail, fed through the shared `AgentEventStream<AgentGraphCall>`: a batch is ordered by `Sequence`, already-applied calls are dropped, and a HOLE rejects the whole batch, raises `OnGapDetected` once with the first sequence the stream does not have and announces that live updates are behind (a gap repaints at once, because the reader has to be told). Every accepted call is folded into the view immediately — `Count` is added to the addressed edge, `LastCallAt` moves forward and never back, the edge turns active — and lights the edge up for `PulseDuration`; only the PAINT is gated by `AgentRenderThrottle` (`RenderThrottle`, default `null` → the shared 100 ms), and the state is never throttled. A `PulseDuration`/`MaxPulses` pair bounds the animation: at most `MaxPulses` edges pulse at once and the NEWEST calls win, so a fan-out burst cannot light up the whole picture.
  - **The drawing.** The scrollport — ONE `role="group"` named by the localized "Agent graph" and described by its keyboard instructions — wraps a plain, unlabelled `<svg>` (a second group carrying the same name would be announced twice and would add a tab stop in front of the graph). Every node is a NATIVE `<button>` inside a `<foreignObject>` (the DiagramEditor's proven pattern), which is what gives it wrapped text, the shared icon components, a real focus ring, native Enter/Space activation and a 44 px coarse-pointer target with no emulation anywhere; the roving tabindex keeps the whole graph ONE tab stop while the scrollport stays `tabindex="-1"` (focusable programmatically, never a second stop). The ARROW keys walk the REAL CONNECTIONS (the neighbour furthest in that direction wins, then the cross-axis distance, then the painting order), Home/End jump to the first and the last node. Every node is named by its label, kind, state and call count, the visible label is ellipsized to two deterministic lines and the full label stays in the tooltip and the accessible name. `WaitingForApproval` is painted, not tinted: the whole border takes the attention tone AND the state row spells it out with an icon and a word; a failed node takes the danger tone. A selection marks the node, its DIRECT neighbours and the connections it touches, and dims (never hides) everything else with a TOKEN change rather than an opacity, because a dimmed node is still an active button whose label has to keep its contrast.
  - **The text alternative.** `ViewMode="Table"` (`AgentGraphViewMode`) renders exactly the same snapshot as two plain tables — every connection (from, to, kind, calls, last call) and every node (name, kind, state, calls) — with the node row action selecting exactly as the drawing does, so a screen reader, a keyboard-only reader or a narrow phone loses no fact.
  - **Zoom and pan.** `Zoom` (two-way, clamped to `MinZoom`–`MaxZoom`, default 1 / 0.5–2.5) is applied through the canvas `viewBox`, the +/− buttons step by 1.25 and announce the level, and `FitToViewAsync` measures the scrollport and keeps the current zoom where nothing can be measured (prerender, no JavaScript) instead of jumping to a guess. PAN is native scrolling of the viewport — a mouse, a wheel, a scrollbar and the keyboard all keep working — and the package's new `tm-agent-graph.js` only imports the CORE `_content/Tempo.Blazor/js/pointer-gesture.js` helper across the static-asset boundary for pinch/ctrl+wheel zoom plus the two-finger pan delta, so there is no second drag implementation and no `<script>` tag. Node tests: `npm run test:ai`.
  - **Accessibility.** ONE polite live region announces a selection, a zoom change, a lost selection and a stream hole; the nodes, the icons and the group labels announce nothing, so no change is spoken twice. A selected node the host removes clears the selection and hands the focus back to the scrollport instead of dropping the reader onto the body. The page scroll an ARROW key may produce is accepted rather than suppressed — a render-time `@onkeydown:preventDefault` cannot be per-key and would swallow Tab and the button's own native activation (the same decision `TmTabs` and `TmTopBar` document). The call pulse is the ONE animated subject and its `prefers-reduced-motion` block removes the movement while keeping a still, dashed, Highlight-toned highlight, so a reader who asked for less motion still learns that something happened. `(pointer: coarse)` raises the zoom buttons and the table's row actions to the 44 px `--tm-touch-target`; `forced-colors` hands the curves, the group boxes and the arrow heads (an SVG `fill` the system palette does not remap) to `CanvasText` and every Highlight-toned mark to `Highlight`, with selection and approval as a `Highlight` BORDER and focus as its own thicker OUTLINE, so a focused node can never be mistaken for a selected one (WCAG 2.4.7), while the dims are dropped (`opacity: 1`) instead of lowering system-colour contrast.
  - **CSS classes:** `.tm-ai-agent-graph`, `__header`, `__title`, `__toolbar`, `__view`, `__zoom`, `__zoom-button(--fit)`, `__zoom-value`, `__empty`, `__tables`, `__table`, `__table-node`, `__table-select`, `__detail`, `__viewport`, `__canvas`, `__groups`, `__group`, `__group-box`, `__group-label`, `__edges`, `__edge`, `__edge--{back|active|pulse|highlighted|dimmed}`, `__arrow-head`, `__node`, `__node--{idle|queued|running|approval|succeeded|failed|cancelled|pinned|selected|neighbor|dimmed}`, `__node-body`, `__node-avatar`, `__node-initials`, `__node-kind-icon`, `__node-text`, `__node-label`, `__node-state`, `__node-state-icon`, `__node-state-text` — tokens only (no colour literal, no raw palette step, no `[data-theme]` block); every knob is declared on the root (`--tm-agent-graph-node-fill`, `-border`, `-tone`, `-avatar`/`-ink`, `--tm-agent-graph-edge(-active/-pulse/-selected)`, `--tm-agent-graph-group-*`, `--tm-agent-graph-max-block-size`, `--tm-agent-graph-pulse-duration`), a state modifier SETS `--tm-agent-graph-node-tone` while the base rule READS it (so source order cannot decide a colour), the eight agent slots paint `--tm-agent-color-{0..7}` through `data-color`, the pulse window is written onto the root inline from `PulseDuration` (the stylesheet's `--tm-agent-graph-pulse-duration` is only its fallback, so the animation and the timer share one value), and the group boxes and the curves are `pointer-events: none` so they never steal a click. Guarded by `AiMarkdownViewCssTests`, `TmAgentGraphCssTests` and `ReducedMotionSelectorTests`.

- **New `TmPromptLibrary`** (`Tempo.Blazor.Components.AI`, package `Tempo.Blazor.AI`) with its `PromptTemplate` / `PromptVariable` / `PromptTemplateUse` / `PromptTemplateBuildResult` / `PromptTemplateSegment` / `PromptTemplateValidationError` records, the `PromptVariableKind` / `PromptTemplateValidationErrorKind` enums and the `PromptTemplateParser` helper (in `Tempo.Blazor.Abstractions`, namespace `Tempo.Blazor.AI.Models`): a library of reusable prompt templates whose body is text with `{{variable}}` placeholders.
  - **The assembly is plain text substitution.** `PromptTemplateParser` finds the placeholders (`{{  name  }}` is the same variable, Unicode names such as `{{téma}}` work), honours the template's own `Variables` declaration when it has one (a placeholder the declaration does not name stays literal), supports the `{{{{` / `}}}}` escapes, and **never evaluates anything** — `{{1 + 2}}` is literal text and a value that happens to contain `{{name}}` is never re-expanded. `Build` always returns the prompt (an unfilled variable keeps its literal placeholder) together with the resolved variables, the rendered segments, the effective values and the validation errors; `ToUse` refuses an invalid assembly, so an incomplete prompt cannot reach a host by accident.
  - **The component** is a two-pane library: a searchable list (title, description, category and body are matched ignoring case and diacritics) with a `TmSegmentedControl` category filter ("All", every host category with its count, and the localized "Uncategorised" through the public `TmPromptLibrary.UncategorisedCategoryValue`), and a detail with one `TmFormField` per variable — `TmTextInput` for `Text`, a `TmTextArea` (immediate) for `Multiline`, and a `TmSelect` over `Options` for `Select`. Defaults pre-fill the fields, a field's error is withheld until the reader touched it or pressed Use, and every edit — and the draft reset the selection change performs — is reported through `@bind-Values`.
  - **The live preview** renders the same `Build` pass the payload comes from: a filled variable is a `mark`, an unfilled one is a `mark` with the dashed `--empty` modifier **and** the localized "Unfilled" word (colour is never the only signal). Use is offered only with a bound `OnUse`, is **ARIA-disabled** (`aria-disabled="true"`, so it stays in the tab order and pressing it says what is missing) while the prompt is incomplete, and hands over the assembled prompt, the template id/title and the effective values (`OnUse(PromptTemplateUse)`). Copy writes the assembled prompt to the clipboard and never claims success when the clipboard refuses. Create / Edit / Delete render only when their callback is bound — a read-only host offers no edit action.
  - **Responsive:** `LayoutMode.Auto` measures the component's own container. A phone gets a list → detail drill-down with a Back action: opening moves the focus into the detail, Back returns it to the row that opened it (falling back to the row's newest position when the list was filtered), so a reader is never left behind on a control that disappeared.
  - **Accessibility:** the root is a group named by its visible heading, the list is a labelled list of native buttons (no key emulation), the preview is a `role="group"` named by its own label, the selected row carries `aria-current="true"`, each field's error is tied to its control through `aria-describedby`, the phone Back action is named by its visible text rather than a duplicated `aria-label`, an unavailable Use stays in the tab order through `aria-disabled` so its reason is reachable, and the component owns exactly ONE polite live region — a persistent `role="status"` whose keyed child carries the copy result and the validation summary (the fields are not `role="alert"`, so nothing is announced twice). `(pointer: coarse)` raises the rows and every action to the 44 px `--tm-touch-target`; `forced-colors` hands every focus ring back to `Highlight` and keeps a variable mark distinguishable without colour (`forced-color-adjust: none`, a dashed border on an unfilled one). The surface declares **no motion** — the preview re-renders on every keystroke.

- **New `TmContextUsage`** (`Tempo.Blazor.Components.AI`, package `Tempo.Blazor.AI`) with its `ContextUsageSnapshot` / `ContextUsageSection` / `ContextUsageItem` / `ContextUsageRemoval` records, the `ContextUsageKind` / `ContextUsageVariant` enums and the `ContextUsageMath` helper (in `Tempo.Blazor.Abstractions`, namespace `Tempo.Blazor.AI.Models`): what a context window is made of — the system prompt, the tools, the memory, the files, the conversation and the tool results — measured against the model's budget. The component renders a SNAPSHOT it never mutates and never polls; a host pushes a new instance as the conversation grows.
  - **The picture** is `Variant`: `Bar` (default — one stacked bar whose segments are the sections), `Grid` (a hundred cells, one per percent of the BUDGET, so the free headroom is visible) or `Treemap` (the sections, and their entries, as areas through the core `TmChart`). The bar is measured over the BUDGET, so its tail is the headroom that is still free — the same fact the grid paints — and every picture is decorative (`aria-hidden`); the **legend table** under it is the reader's representation — label, tokens, whole percentage and the localized Required / Summarized / Omitted words — so the facts are never painted twice. The shares come from a largest-remainder split (`ContextUsageMath.Shares`), so the rounded percentages add up to exactly 100 %, and a section with tokens whose rounded share is zero reads "< 1 %" and still paints a 0.5 % sliver (the bar clips the floor, so the card cannot grow).
  - **The total** is one `role="meter"` element with `aria-valuemax` = the budget, `aria-valuenow` = the used tokens **clamped to the budget** (ARIA forbids a value above the maximum, and a browser may cap it on its own) and a localized `aria-valuetext` that always names the REAL total and the real percentage, so an over-budget context is never under-reported; the visible read-out repeats that sentence for sighted users and is `aria-hidden`, so the amount is heard once. The cache-hit badge and the over-budget line (an icon plus the exact excess, never colour alone) are the meter's `aria-describedby`.
  - **Reading and acting:** a section with `Items` expands into them through a native disclosure button (`aria-expanded`, plus `aria-controls` while open); a section with `CanRemove` offers the section-level Remove and an entry with `CanRemove` its own — both raise `OnRemoveItem(ContextUsageRemoval)` (the whole section when `Item` is null) and the host decides what to do, because the component never edits the snapshot. The Compact action is rendered only when `OnCompact` is bound and is DISABLED while no section is compactable (`ContextUsageMath.IsCompactable`: optional, not yet summarised, not yet omitted, carrying tokens). After a removal the focus is handed back to the section's disclosure button (an entry removal keeps the section), or to the component root (`tabindex="-1"`) when the section itself left, lost its entries or the host dropped it in the same update — a stored disclosure reference that no longer renders is pruned, and a focus move the browser rejects is swallowed, so a lost focus move can never become an error UI or a dead Server circuit.
  - **Accessibility:** every control is a native `<button>` (Enter/Space are never emulated); hovering a grid cell highlights its section AND focusing a legend row highlights that section's cells, so the highlight has a keyboard path; the cells are not 100 extra tab stops (`aria-hidden` decoration); ONE polite live region announces a budget CROSSING only ("The context window is over its budget." / "… back within its budget.") and a repeated sentence toggles one invisible marker, so a page load never talks over the reader; `(pointer: coarse)` raises the disclosure / Remove / Compact controls to the 44 px `--tm-touch-target`; `forced-colors` hands every focus ring back to the system `Highlight`, opts the tone-coded segment / cell / swatch out of the palette collapse (`forced-color-adjust: none`) and keeps the bar and the free cells outlined in `CanvasText`. The surface declares **no motion** — a polling host must not make it flicker.
  - **Tokens:** the per-kind tones are component-local knobs declared on the root (`--tm-context-usage-system`, `-tools`, `-memory`, `-files`, `-chat`, `-results`, `-other`), each aliasing a semantic `--tm-color-*` token, so a host re-points one section without touching the package.

- **New `TmModelPicker`** (`Tempo.Blazor.Components.AI`, package `Tempo.Blazor.AI`) with its `AiModelInfo` / `AiModelSelection` / `AiModelEffortLevel` records and the `AiModelGroupBy` enum (in `Tempo.Blazor.Abstractions`, namespace `Tempo.Blazor.AI.Models`): the model a conversation runs on. The trigger names the chosen model plus its state tags (extended thinking, effort level, deprecated); the popup lists the host's catalogue as a `role="listbox"` grouped by **provider** (default), **family** or nothing, searched live — the hits are marked by `TmHighlightedText`, a group whose models all filtered out disappears, and a model that reports no provider/family lands in the localized "Other" group instead of vanishing. Every row compares the models: a speed bar (the model's 0–5 score), a quality bar (the same), a price bar **relative to the most expensive model in the catalogue**, a context-window chip ("200k context") and capability chips — each bar is `aria-hidden` decoration next to its value in WORDS ("Speed 4/5", "$3.00 / 1M input"), so nothing is colour-only. A model that reports no score, price or window renders no bar and no chip for it — "not reported" is never painted as a zero — and a deprecated model stays selectable with the localized "Deprecated" chip in its row and in the trigger.
  - **The answer is ONE value:** `@bind-Selection` is an `AiModelSelection` (model id + extended thinking + effort level). A pick of a DIFFERENT model starts from that model's defaults; re-picking the SAME model keeps the reader's reasoning options, so opening the list again is not a reset. A host may stay uncontrolled: its pick still renders and a stale `Selection` parameter never overwrites it.
  - **Reasoning options** of the SELECTED model sit ABOVE the list, never inside a `role="option"` (an option is a leaf of the listbox and may not contain a switch or a radio): the extended-thinking `TmToggle` is offered when the model supports it and the effort `TmSegmentedControl` (its radio-group pattern, with a localized "Default" option stored as `null`) is offered when the model reports levels. `ShowExtendedThinking` / `ShowEffort` opt out individually and the whole block is absent for a model that offers neither.
  - **Price estimate:** `EstimatedPromptTokens` (with a selected model that reports an input price) renders "Estimated prompt cost ≈ {amount}" in the popup footer — a comparison aid, never a bill; no tokens or no price renders no estimate. `Culture` decides the number/currency formatting (the culture's own symbol, symbol position and decimal digits) and `PriceFormatter` replaces it for a host with credits or a fixed exchange rate.
  - **Keyboard (APG):** the trigger is a native button (so Enter/Space are never emulated; ↓/↑ open it too), focus moves into the search field once the popup is actually displayed, the search field is the popup's `combobox` carrying `aria-activedescendant`, and with `ShowSearch="false"` the listbox itself is the tab stop and owns the arrows, Home/End, Enter (keydown), Space (keyup) and type-ahead (a repeated letter cycles through the matches of that letter). Escape closes through the overlay and returns the focus to the trigger, an outside pointer closes it without stealing the focus the click earned, and a pick closes it and returns the focus itself. `CloseOnSelect="false"` keeps the list open for comparison and marks the picked row in place.
  - **Accessibility:** ONE polite live region per picker (the pick, both reasoning changes and the search match count — nothing else is live); the trigger is named by its own visible text (a visually hidden "Model:" prefix, the model, its provider and every state tag, so a deprecated or reasoning model is announced) and carries `aria-haspopup="listbox"`, `aria-expanded`, `aria-controls` while open and a localized keyboard instruction as its description — a host-supplied `AriaLabel` replaces the name and the tags move into the description; the listbox is single-select and named by the localized "Models" label (not the popup title, which already names the card / sheet); the active row is marked with a border AND a tone, the picked row with `aria-selected` and its own border; `(pointer: coarse)` raises the option rows, the trigger and the search field to the 44 px `--tm-touch-target`; `forced-colors` hands the three focus stops back to the system `Highlight`, marks the picked row with a 2 px `SelectedItem` border, the active row with a `Highlight` outline, and keeps the bars readable (a `CanvasText` track outline plus a repainted fill). The surface declares **no motion at all** — the reader may keep it open while a run streams behind it.
  - **Presentation:** the popup is the core `TmOverlayPanel` — an anchored popover on a wide layout and a bottom sheet on a phone (`MobilePresentation`, default `Auto`; `LayoutMode` pins a mode for a host or a test). The list scrolls inside the panel; the page never scrolls sideways.

- **New `TmAgentRunTree` and `TmAgentMonitor`** (`Tempo.Blazor.Components.AI`, package `Tempo.Blazor.AI`) with their `AgentRunNode` / `AgentRunRollup` / `AgentRunRollupResult` / `AiCostFormatter` / `AgentMonitorStep` models and the `AgentRunNodeKind` / `AgentRunFilter` / `AgentStepKind` enums (in `Tempo.Blazor.Abstractions`, namespace `Tempo.Blazor.AI.Models`): one agent run on two surfaces — the tree of agents, sub-agents, tool calls and steps with the subtree totals of their parents, and the live monitor that folds into one status bar. Both render the host's snapshot and never poll anything: a host pushes new nodes/steps as the run reports them.
  - **`TmAgentRunTree`** is a `role="treegrid"` over the columns name / status / model / time / cost / tokens. The node list is FLAT and the tree comes from `AgentRunNode.ParentId`: a node whose parent names no supplied node is an ORPHAN attached under the root and marked, a parent cycle is REJECTED (no row, its children become orphans, nothing loops) and a duplicate id is read once. A parent row shows the SUM over its subtree for time, cost and tokens, prefixed with a decorative `Σ`, marked `data-rollup="true"` and named in full for a screen reader ("Total for {node} including its sub-agents: …"); the arithmetic is the PUBLIC `AgentRunRollup.For(nodeId, nodes, now)` / `AgentRunRollup.ForAll(nodes, now)` helper, so a host computing the same numbers elsewhere cannot drift from the row. Every value keeps the "not reported" contract (`null`, never zero), and a running node with no `CompletedAt` contributes the time from its `StartedAt` to the caller's `now`. The `ShowOnly` filter (`All` | `Running` | `Failed`) never breaks the tree: a row survives when it matches OR when a surviving descendant needs it as its ancestor, so "only failed" still shows the chain that failed. `@bind-SelectedNodeId` + `DetailTemplate` render the selected node in a named region; the component never mutates `Nodes`.
  - **`TmAgentMonitor`** answers the four questions a watcher asks: the current step (the last `Running` one, else the last step), a clock that ticks only while the run is `Running` (from the injected `TimeProvider`, sampled once per render, stopping on `CompletedAt`), the cost so far in micro-units through `AiCostFormatter` (the culture's currency with the CURRENCY'S OWN decimal places — two for USD, none for JPY — and six decimals below one hundredth of a unit so a cheap call is not painted as "0.00") and the steps' timeline with a kind glyph plus a hidden localized kind word (`IconResolver` overrides the glyph, never the word). The host's `PendingApproval` slot renders in its own `role="group"` named "Waiting for your approval"; a decision that starts waiting is announced in the component's polite live region. `@bind-Collapsed` folds the strip into one bar that keeps the state, title, current step, clock and cost and drops the timeline — while a pending decision stays visible as a marker in the bar; `AllowCollapse="false"` removes the toggle and ignores a pinned `true`. The run title, the current step and every step title/detail WRAP (WCAG 1.4.10 Reflow at 320 px) instead of being cut to an ellipsis nothing reveals; only the short elapsed/cost/model values keep one line, and the model carries its full id in a `title`.
  - **Accessibility (both):** the tree is an APG treegrid with ONE roving tab stop — ↑/↓ move, Home/End jump, → expands or walks into the first child, ← collapses or walks to the parent, Enter selects on keydown (auto-repeat guarded) and Space on keyup; the row's disclosure is `tabindex="-1"` + `aria-hidden` and stops its events, so one key press activates once. The keys the rows handle do not scroll the page: `js/tm-agent-run-tree.js` (imported as an ES module, node-tested through `npm run test:ai`) cancels only those defaults on a row of THIS grid — never Tab, never a control inside the row, never a browser shortcut. Each surface has ONE polite live region (tree: selected/expanded/collapsed/filter count; monitor: the fold and a pending approval that appears) while the ticking clocks are `aria-live="off"`; every state is an icon AND a word; the tree's focus ring is an INSET outline (a scroller clips an outward ring) and `forced-colors` repaints the rings and the selected-row marker in the system `Highlight` colour; `(pointer: coarse)` grows rows and toggles to the 44 px `--tm-touch-target`. Neither surface declares a transition or an animation.

  - **Layout:** the tree's grid is the ONE scroll owner in both axes, its header sticks to that scrollport and every row uses the same cell widths, so a phone scrolls the columns sideways INSIDE the component (the page never does); the cell widths are the `--tm-agent-run-tree-*` knobs and the cap is `--tm-agent-run-tree-max-height`. The tree's clipped name and model cells carry their whole text in a `title` (a host without a `DetailTemplate` still has a full-text path); the monitor wraps its prose and only ellipsizes the short metric values (see above).
