- **New `TmAgentPlan`** (`Tempo.Blazor.Components.AI`, package `Tempo.Blazor.AI`) with its `AgentPlanStep` / `AgentPlanEdit` records and the `AgentStepStatus` / `AgentPlanEditKind` / `AgentPlanMode` enums (in `Tempo.Blazor.Abstractions`, namespace `Tempo.Blazor.AI.Models`): the agent's plan of steps — reviewed and edited before a run, then watched while it runs. The component NEVER mutates `Steps`: every edit raises `OnPlanChanged(IReadOnlyList<AgentPlanStep> steps, AgentPlanEdit edit)` with the whole proposed list plus the operation that produced it, and the host applies it, exactly the controlled contract `TmSortableList` follows for its order. `OnPlanChanged` is a plain delegate because an edit carries two values, so a host that stores the list must call `StateHasChanged()` itself (documented on the parameter and in the docs).
  - **Review mode** is the editable surface. **Rename** opens an inline editor from a click on the title button or **F2**; **Enter** saves, **Escape** cancels, the save/cancel pair is the pointer and touch path, a whitespace-only title is refused with the editor left open, and the focus returns to the title button that owned it. **Add** inserts *below a row* (per-row action) or *at the end* (footer action); the new row carries the localized "New step" title and opens in its editor. **Remove** is immediate and confirmed through an **Undo strip** instead of a modal: the `AgentPlanEdit.Remove` carries the removed step and Undo emits `AgentPlanEdit.Add` at the same index (one shape for insert and restore), every other edit retires the offer, and a host that refused the removal (its list still contains the step) is not offered an undo at all. **Reorder** rides the core `TmSortableList`: decorative grip for the pointer, the ROW as the keyboard grip (Enter/Space grab, arrows move, Enter/Space drop, Escape rollback, Tab leaves without a move) and the per-row move menu as the WCAG 2.5.7 tap alternative.
  - **Running mode** is read-only: no rename, no add, no remove, no reorder and no Approve / Run. It adds the live clock of a `Running` step (`Elapsed` from `StartedAt` to the injected `TimeProvider`'s now, ticking only while something runs, a finished step keeping its recorded duration), the plan total in the summary ("4 of 7 done · 1:24" — an invariant `m:ss`/`h:mm:ss` clock-style duration, because it is a duration and not a quantity of a unit), the failure (the step's `Error` under the title) and **Retry from this step** (`OnRetryFrom(step)`), which is the only action a running plan offers.
  - **Surface:** `Steps`, `Mode`, `OnPlanChanged`, `OnApprove`, `OnRun`, `OnRetryFrom`, `Title`, `ShowTitle`, `HeadingLevel` (clamped 2–6), `ShowSummary`, `AllowEditing`, `EmptyContent`, `AriaLabel`, `Class` (+ inherited `DataTestId`/`TestIdPrefix`); public `BeginRename(int)` / `ClearUndo()` and read-only `Announcement` / `CanEdit` / `CanUndoRemove` / `DoneCount`. Models: `AgentPlanStep` (`Id` generated when omitted, `Title`, `Description`, `Status`, `StartedAt`, `CompletedAt`, `Error`, `IsEditable` default `true`, computed `IsFinished` / `Duration` / `Elapsed(now)`), `AgentPlanEdit` (`Kind`, `Index`, `StepId`, `Title`, `FromIndex`, `ToIndex`, `Step`, built only through `Rename`/`Add`/`Remove`/`Reorder`), enums `AgentStepStatus` (`Pending`|`Running`|`Done`|`Failed`|`Skipped`), `AgentPlanEditKind` (`Rename`|`Add`|`Remove`|`Reorder`) and `AgentPlanMode` (`Review`|`Running`).
  - **Accessibility:** a `role="group"` named by the rendered heading (so the name a reader hears is the one they see) or by `AriaLabel`, described by hidden keyboard instructions; every state is an icon AND a word; ONE polite live region for the plan's own events (renamed, cancelled, added, removed, restored, refused title) while a move is narrated only by the nested sortable list, so nothing is read twice; the ticking clock and the summary are `aria-live="off"`; native buttons only (no key emulation); `(pointer: coarse)` grows every action to the 44 px `--tm-touch-target` and reflows the row into two columns; `forced-colors` repaints every ring in the system `Highlight` colour and keeps the error block edged. The plan declares no transition and no animation, so the package's reduced-motion enumeration is unchanged.
  - **CSS classes:** `.tm-ai-agent-plan`, `--running`, `__header`, `__heading`, `__title`, `__summary`, `__actions`, `__action(--icon)`, `__step`, `__index`, `__status`, `__status-text`, `__body`, `__title-button`, `__title-text`, `__description`, `__error`, `__time`, `__step-actions`, `__retry`, `__rename-editor`, `__rename`, `__footer`, `__undo`, `__undo-text`, `__empty` — tokens only, no `[data-theme]` block, guarded by the package token gate and `TmAgentPlanCssTests`.

  - **Wireframe:** the new `agent-plan` UI role plus the `TmAgentPlan` schema (`title`, `steps`, `mode`, `showSummary`, `showAddStep`) and its declarative stencil, which draws the numbered rows, a check / filled dot / cross-plus-Retry per state, the add row and the Approve / Run pair, all branching on `mode`.

The **Undo strip and its announcements name the step by title** ("Step 3 removed: Review with the team") because the number it had no longer points at a visible row after the renumbering, and a removal raises no strip at all when no `OnPlanChanged` handler exists, while a stale offer is retired instead of inserting a second row with the same `Id`. A **refused empty title** is now visible, not only announced: the field carries `aria-invalid="true"` and the reason is rendered under it, cleared by typing, saving or cancelling (WCAG 3.3.1), and `forced-colors` keeps a `CanvasText` edge on the invalid field. A step the host passed **without a title reads as "Untitled step"** in the row too (dimmed and italic), not just in the accessible name. The row clock and the plan total now sample `TimeProvider` **once per render**, so they never describe two instants. Escape on a freshly added row keeps the placeholder row in the plan (cancelling the NAME must not report a second, destructive edit); the row is removed with its own Remove action.
- **New `TmSortableList<TItem>`** (`Tempo.Blazor.Components.DataDisplay`) with its `SortableReorderArgs` model and the `SortableHandleMode` / `SortableReorderSource` enums: a generic list whose rows the reader can reorder — by pointer, by keyboard, or from a per-row move menu that is the non-drag alternative WCAG 2.5.7 requires. The component NEVER mutates the host's list: every committed move raises `OnReorder(SortableReorderArgs)` with the indexes of the host's own `Items` and the `Source` that committed it (`Pointer` | `Keyboard` | `Menu`), and the next render shows the order the host reports — a host that ignores the callback keeps its order and the row snaps back. Applying a move is `RemoveAt(FromIndex)` + `Insert(ToIndex, item)`, which reproduces the gesture exactly because every intermediate keyboard step is an adjacent swap of the same row.
  - **Keyboard:** the ROW is the focus stop in both handle modes — one tab stop per row, never two (the decorative grip is `tabindex="-1"` + `aria-hidden`). It is a `role="listitem"` naming itself the localized "sortable item", named by its own content through `aria-labelledby` and described by the hidden keyboard instructions. `Enter` (keydown, auto-repeat guarded) or `Space` (keyup) picks the row up, `↑`/`↓` move it, `Home`/`End` jump it to the edges, `Enter`/`Space` drops it, `Escape` rolls the pending order back and raises nothing, and `Alt`+`↑`/`↓` moves it one position without grabbing. Emulation follows [docs/keyboard-activation-convention.md](docs/keyboard-activation-convention.md) (a non-native focusable emulates `Enter` on keydown and `Space` on keyup). The page-scroll guard of a grabbed row lives in `tm-sortable.js` (`shouldPreventGrabbedKey`), not in a render-time `@onkeydown:preventDefault`: while the row carries `data-grabbed="true"` the module stops the default action of `↑`, `↓`, `Home`, `End`, `Enter`, `Space` and `Escape` **only when the event target is the row itself**, so a control inside `ItemTemplate` keeps its own keys. `Tab` is never prevented — it cancels the grab and moves the focus out, so a grabbed row is not a keyboard trap (WCAG 2.1.2).
  - **Pointer:** `tm-sortable.js` rides the shared `pointer-drag.js` (capture by `pointerId`, threshold, touch long-press, `Escape`/`pointercancel`/`lostpointercapture` rollback, click swallowing) and `createAutoScroller` from `pointer-gesture.js` for the edge scroll — it owns only the list geometry: the dragged row follows the pointer with an inline `transform`, the rows it passes shift by one row height + gap, and the landing slot comes from the PURE `resolveTargetIndex`. Blazor is told exactly once, on release (`OnSortableReorderCommitted`), so a 200-row list does not re-render per pointer event; every cancel path restores the inline styles verbatim and reports nothing. `HandleMode=Handle` (the default) drags from the decorative grip with `touch-action: none`; `HandleMode=WholeItem` makes the row the drag surface and passes a 400 ms touch long-press, so a tap and a page scroll keep working.
  - **Accessibility:** `role="list"` of `listitem` rows, ONE polite live region for the whole list (picked up / moved to position *p* of *n* / dropped / cancelled / boundary) instead of one per row, kept sticky and re-announced with an invisible marker when two consecutive transitions would produce the same sentence. The focus indicator is an INSET outline (a list inside a scroller would clip an outward ring exactly where it is needed) and `forced-colors` keeps the system palette in charge (no `forced-color-adjust` opt-out, so the row border still follows its hover/disabled state) while re-declaring the grabbed and dragged states in `Highlight`; `(pointer: coarse)` grows the handle to the 44 px `--tm-touch-target`; the row transition is enumerated in the `animations.css` reduced-motion block. `Disabled` keeps the rows readable but removes the focus stop, the menu, the drag and every announcement.
  - **Tap alternative:** each row renders an APG menu button ("Move {row}") offering Move up / Move down / Move to top / Move to bottom over `TmContextMenu`, with the inapplicable entries disabled; the menu's wrapper (and the row's content element, so a template input or link keeps its keys) fences its keys off with `@onkeydown:stopPropagation` / `@onkeyup:stopPropagation`, so no child's `Enter`, arrows or `Escape` ever reach the row's grab handler.

  - **Review polish:** the announced row name no longer falls back to `KeySelector` (a database key read aloud names nothing; a string item names itself, everything else uses the localized "Item {n}" with its position), the six live-region sentences lost their leading "Item"/"Položka" prefix (which produced "Item Item 3" with the fallback label and forced feminine agreement in Czech/Slovak), a `KeySelector` that repeats a key degrades the whole list to index keys instead of a Blazor diff exception, and `SortableReorderArgs` properties are `init`-only so a later field is additive.
- **Demo pages `/analytics-kit` and `/trace-waterfall`; the phase-9 documentation and E2E sweep.** `/analytics-kit` assembles the whole data and analytics kit into one reporting screen over a deterministic order history: a reporting period picked through `TmDateRangePicker` **with its comparison window** (the `PreviousPeriod` mode derived by the picker and read back by the page), KPI cards (`TmStatCard` with delta, sparkline and an animated value), a change summary (`TmTrendList` in its table layout, one row per metric with its sparkline), a comparison chart (`TmChart` Line with `TooltipMode=Index`: the period and its comparison as two series in one card), the channel breakdown (`TmBreakdownCard` with its period switcher flipping to the comparison window, which re-sorts the rows), a faceted order filter (`TmFacetFilter` with **host-computed** counts — an option's number applies every other group's selection, so removing a chip re-counts the rest — and `ResultCount` behind the phone sheet's counted confirmation) and the quota meter (`TmUsageMeter` in its warning state, with the category table, the reset date, the daily sparkline, the near-limit call to action and buttons that walk it over the limit). Every heading, option, chip and status word of both pages resolves through `ITmLocalizer` — 103 new demo keys in English, Czech, Slovak and French. `/trace-waterfall` renders one generated agent run of **152 spans** (a planning call, a nested sub-agent, thirty-two decision rounds with their tool/HTTP/DB children, six retries, a timed-out `SELECT`, a failed `POST /v1/notifications` and the streamed answer) with the host metric columns, a span detail template (kind, status, duration, timestamps, attributes and metrics) and the live toggle that republishes the run with running spans so the bars grow. Both pages are in the demo nav and both are guarded by bUnit page tests (`AnalyticsKitPageTests`, `TraceWaterfallPageTests`) that pin the sections, the comparison-window arithmetic, the facet re-count, the breakdown reorder and the live toggle.
  - **E2E (WASM):** `AnalyticsKitE2ETests` covers the chart's arrow-key walk with its single polite live region and Escape, the facet filter's apply-on-toggle plus chip removal with re-counted options, the phone bottom sheet with its counted confirmation, a preset moving the period AND the comparison window, the segmented trays moving by arrow/Home/End and re-sorting the breakdown, a 375 px page that never scrolls sideways and a scoped axe scan of three sections. `TraceWaterfallPageE2ETests` covers the ~150-row treegrid, the disclosure by pointer, the roving tabindex with Enter selecting (and the detail following), the zoom group and its reset, the live toggle on and off, the grid's own horizontal scroll on a phone and a scoped axe scan. Both specs end with a **visual sweep** of light and dark at 1440 and 375 px — the dark shot is taken through the demo's own theme toggle, so the whole frame repaints.
  - **Docs:** new [docs/date-range-picker.md](docs/date-range-picker.md) (presets from an injected `TimeProvider`, the localized labels, the comparison modes and the public `DateRangeComparisonCalculator` the backend can call, the visual contract and the stable `data-comparison*` attributes), the AGENTS.md category table now names both demo pages and the picker's comparison surface.
  - **Review polish (demo only, no library API change):** the KPI cards take the currency symbol AND its side from two localized demo keys (`TmAnalyticsKitDemo_CurrencyPrefix` / `…Suffix` — `$` in front of the amount for English, behind it for Czech, Slovak and French, so no translator is stuck with the English order), the comparison window is spelled with the reader's own short-date pattern (`"d"`) instead of a fixed `dd.MM.yyyy`, and the comparison chart sits in a `<figure>` named by its section heading, because the SVG's own text alternative only says "Line chart". `/trace-waterfall` now reads the clock through an injected `TimeProvider` (the shared demo registration `AddTempoDemoClock()`, also handed to `TmTraceWaterfall`'s live mode) instead of `DateTimeOffset.UtcNow`, so a test can pin the generated run and the running duration is measured against the same clock as the bars. The post-fix visual sweep caught two more demo-only slips and they are fixed here: the picker now uses the SAME culture pattern as the comparison line it sits beside (`DateFormat="d"` instead of its `dd.MM.yyyy` default, which put two date conventions on one card), and the trace page's cost shows a plain two-decimal number under a translated `Cost ($)` / `Cena ($)` / `Coût ($)` label instead of the generic currency sign (`¤12.42`) that a `"C"` format produces on the demo's neutral culture.
- **`TmDateRangePicker` compares the reported range against a second window.** Additive: `Comparison` defaults to `DateRangeComparison.None`, which renders the pre-2.10 markup and raises nothing. `PreviousPeriod` derives the equally long window ending the day before the range starts (10–14 October is compared against 5–9 October) and `PreviousYear` the same window one year earlier, with a leap day clamped by the calendar; both come from the public `DateRangeComparisonCalculator`, so a backend computes exactly what the header shows. `Custom` lets the reader (or the host) pick the second window, with a target switcher deciding which window a calendar click edits. `ComparisonRange` is two-way bound and `ComparisonRangeChanged` reports every derived change. The trigger appends the comparison summary (part of its accessible name, per WCAG 2.5.3), the popup adds a labelled block with a decorative swatch, and the calendar marks the compared days with the neutral `--tm-cal-comparison-bg` fill and a **dashed** `--tm-cal-comparison-border` on both ends — so it never reads as a second reported range, and the marking survives a reader who cannot see colour (forced colors keep a `CanvasText` dashed edge and every marked day is `aria-describedby`-ed by a visually hidden description). Hosts and tests key off the root's `data-comparison` / `data-comparison-start` / `data-comparison-end`. **Presets now come from a clock:** the new `DateRangePresets.Create(TimeProvider, ITmLocalizer)` factory labels the five presets through the localizer and pins them to the injected clock's day (an unregistered `TimeProvider` falls back to `System`), while the 2.9.x static members stay byte-identical and are deliberately not `[Obsolete]`. Docs: [docs/date-range-picker.md](docs/date-range-picker.md).
- **New `TmSegmentedControl<TValue>`** (`Tempo.Blazor.Components.Inputs`) with its `SegmentedOption<TValue>` model and the `SegmentedControlSize` / `SegmentedControlRole` enums: a value out of a small set, drawn as one segmented tray with a sliding highlight. The control offers TWO APG patterns through `Role`: `RadioGroup` (the default — the segments pick a value, so it is a `radiogroup` of `radio` options with `aria-checked`) and `Tabs` (the segments switch content, so it is a `tablist` of `tab` options with `aria-selected` and an `aria-controls` pointing at the host's panel; `PanelId`, or a per-option `SegmentedOption.PanelId`, names that panel, and with neither the tab carries no `aria-controls` at all, because an idref to a missing element is worse than none). Both use a ROVING TABINDEX: exactly one segment is in the tab order (the selection, else the first enabled one), the arrow keys move the focus and the selection together — wrapping at both ends and SKIPPING disabled segments — Home/End jump to the first/last ENABLED segment, and Enter/Space are left to the native `<button>` elements so one key press activates exactly once (no emulation, per `docs/keyboard-activation-convention.md`). Re-selecting the current value raises nothing, so a two-way binding cannot loop. The tray is the horizontal SCROLL container (a long set scrolls instead of clipping its last segment; the segment the keyboard moved to is focused, which scrolls it into view) and its focus indicator is an INSET outline rather than the two-layer ring, because an ancestor with `overflow` clips a box-shadow — the ring that disappears exactly where it is needed is worse than none, and the inset outline is painted in the system `Highlight` colour under forced colors. The sliding highlight is measured in the browser (`TmSegmentedControl.razor.js`: `place`, `focusOption`, `release`, a `ResizeObserver` on the tray AND on every segment, so a font swap or a container resize never strands the strip on the wrong segment) and written as a `transform` on a decorative `aria-hidden` strip; without JavaScript the strip is never claimed (`data-tm-indicator` stays absent) and the selected segment paints its own surface instead — a complete design, not a degraded one. `Size` is `Sm`/`Md`/`Lg` (32/38/44 px, mirroring the input heights) and every size grows to the 44 px `--tm-touch-target` on `(pointer: coarse)`; `FullWidth` shares the container width equally between the segments; `Count` and `Badge` render as TEXT inside the option (so they are part of its accessible name — "Inbox 12", never an unlabelled 12) and the icon is always `aria-hidden`. ONE polite nothing: the control renders no live region, because the option's own `aria-checked`/`aria-selected` state is what a screen reader announces and a second announcement per change would be noise. Docs: [docs/segmented-control.md](docs/segmented-control.md).
  - **Surface:** `Options`, `Value`/`ValueChanged` (`@bind-Value`), `Size`, `FullWidth`, `Role`, `Label`, `AriaLabel`, `AriaLabelledBy`, `PanelId`, `Disabled`, `Class` (+ inherited `DataTestId`/`TestIdPrefix`); model `SegmentedOption<TValue>` (`Label`, `Value`, `Icon`, `Count`, `Badge`, `IsDisabled`, `PanelId`); enums `SegmentedControlSize` (`Sm`|`Md`|`Lg`) and `SegmentedControlRole` (`RadioGroup`|`Tabs`).
  - **Accessible name:** an optional VISIBLE `Label` named through `aria-labelledby` — the name a screen reader reads is the name a reader sees (WCAG 2.5.3), so no `AriaLabel` is layered on top of it; a whitespace-only label counts as no label and the localized default ("Options") applies. `AriaLabelledBy` wins over both.
  - **CSS classes:** `.tm-segmented`, `--sm`/`--md`/`--lg`, `--full-width`, `--tabs`, `--disabled`, `__label`, `__track`, `__indicator`, `__option`, `__option--selected`, `__option--disabled`, `__option-label`, `__icon`, `__count`, `__badge`, plus `__track[data-tm-indicator="sliding"]` for the measured presentation. No new design token is needed — the tray reads `--tm-bg-muted`, the selection `--tm-bg-surface` + `--tm-border-color-strong` + `--tm-shadow-sm`. The two animated subjects `.tm-segmented__indicator` and `.tm-segmented__option` are enumerated in the `animations.css` reduced-motion block.
- **New `TmHighlightedText`** (`Tempo.Blazor.Components.DataDisplay`): renders text with every occurrence of a search term wrapped in `<mark class="tm-highlighted-text__match">`, so a reader of a combobox row sees WHERE the term hit instead of re-reading the row. It renders a FRAGMENT — no wrapper element — because the call sites are option rows, table cells and picker lines that already own their box and their typography, and the rendered text is exactly the text that was passed in (a copy/paste and the accessible name both get the original string). The term is matched LITERALLY, never as a regular expression: a query is user data, and handing it to `Regex` would make `(` throw and `.*` match everything, which is a correctness bug and a denial-of-service surface in one. Matching ignores casing by default and — unless `AccentInsensitive` is turned off — diacritics on BOTH sides ("usti" finds "Ústí" and "Ústí" finds "Usti"), and the marked run is always the ORIGINAL text, never the folded query. A null, empty or whitespace-only query renders the text unchanged, so the component is safe to render while the user is still typing. It is not a live region: the combobox already announces the search state and a per-row announcement would be noise.
  - **Surface:** `Text`, `Query`, `CaseSensitive`, `AccentInsensitive`, `MatchClass`; CSS class `.tm-highlighted-text__match` (tokens only, plus a forced-colors `Highlight`/`HighlightText` pair because the UA drops the background).
- **Combobox match highlighting — additive `HighlightMatches`** on `TmMultiSelect`, `TmFilterableDropdown`, `TmEntityPicker` and `TmUserPicker`. Default `false`, which is exactly today's markup: the option renders its plain display text. When `true`, only the matched slice is wrapped in `<mark>` (through `TmHighlightedText`), the match ignores casing (and diacritics, and for `TmFilterableDropdown` it follows its existing `AccentInsensitiveFilter` switch), and the option's accessible name stays the WHOLE display text.
- **`TmMultiSelect` gains inline create — additive `AllowCreate` + `OnCreate(string)`.** With `AllowCreate="true"` the popup appends a "Create “{text}”" row as the LAST option of the SAME listbox whenever the filter text matches no option exactly (ignoring case and surrounding whitespace), so a screen reader walking the list meets the same choices a pointer does. The row is reached with ArrowDown past the results (it becomes the `aria-activedescendant`, so what Enter will do is spoken, and it paints the same `--focused` style as a regular option so a sighted keyboard user sees the highlight move onto it) and picked with Enter; it raises `OnCreate` with the trimmed text and closes the popup. The row's accent tone is `--tm-color-primary-text` rather than the raw primary step, because the hover/focus panel behind it leaves the raw step at 4.07:1 in the dark theme; the primary-ink token measures 7.92:1 light and 5.74:1 dark. The component never fabricates an item — it does not know how to build a `TItem` from a string, and a made-up value would be a lie in the host's data — so the host adds the option, de-duplicates when a `DataProvider` only returned a filtered page, and decides whether to select it. Creating is host-reported: the popup closes and focus returns to the trigger, so the host must announce the result in its own polite live region (the component renders none for the selection) and select the new value so the chip reflects it.
  - **`TmMultiSelect` now derives from `TmComponentBase`** (it was a plain `ComponentBase`). Additive in practice: it gains the two standard parameters `DataTestId` and `TestIdPrefix`, and the new create row's `data-testid` is namespaced by the latter. A host attribute that happens to be called `DataTestId` or `TestIdPrefix` used to land in `AdditionalAttributes` and now binds to the parameter.
- **`TmBreakdownCard` period switcher — Breaking (DOM only, no API change).** `PeriodOptions` + `@bind-Period` still drive the same switcher and raise the same `PeriodChanged`; the switcher is now a `TmSegmentedControl` instead of a `TmRadioGroup Appearance="Segmented"`. The reason is the phase-8 requirement: the tray needs the measured sliding highlight and the overflow scroller that a native-radio row cannot provide, and two look-alike segmented presentations in one library is the drift this plan exists to remove.
  - **DOM before:** `div.tm-breakdown-card__period > .tm-radio-group.tm-radio-group--segmented` with `.tm-radio-group-options`, a `.tm-radio-group-label` and one `<label class="tm-radio-segment">` wrapping a visually hidden `<input type="radio">` per period.
  - **DOM after:** `div.tm-breakdown-card__period > .tm-segmented.tm-segmented--sm > .tm-segmented__label` + `.tm-segmented__track[role="radiogroup"]` (named by the visible label) with one `.tm-segmented__option[role="radio"][aria-checked]` per period. **Migrating a selector:** `.tm-breakdown-card__period input[type='radio']` → `.tm-breakdown-card__period [role='radio']` (click, not `Change()`, in bUnit); `.tm-radio-group-label` → `.tm-segmented__label`. Nothing else changed: same values, same `PeriodChanged`, same label text.
- **Wireframe:** the new `segmented-control` UI role plus the `TmSegmentedControl` schema (`label`, `options`, `active`, `sizeVariant`, `showCount`, `badge`, `disabled` — the size prop is named `sizeVariant` because the stencil expression context already owns `size` for the element box) and its declarative stencil, which draws every one of those knobs.
- **Localization:** `TmSegmentedControl_DefaultLabel` and `TmMultiSelect_CreateOption` in English/Czech/Slovak/French plus `MockTmLocalizer`.
- **Demo:** a `/data-display` section with the radio-semantics tray (three sizes, a count, a disabled badge segment), the tab-semantics tray over one panel (`aria-controls`) and a deliberately narrow copy that scrolls sideways; a `/forms` section where the multi-select marks the typed term and offers the create row (`HighlightMatches` + `AllowCreate`), and the filterable dropdown next to it does the same.
- **Docs:** [docs/segmented-control.md](docs/segmented-control.md) rewritten — the previous page argued that no `TmSegmentedControl` should exist and pointed at `TmTabs` / `TmRadioGroup`; it now documents the component and keeps the "which control when" table, and [docs/combobox-match-highlight.md](docs/combobox-match-highlight.md) documents the opt-in highlighting and the create row.

- **New `TmUsageMeter`** (`Tempo.Blazor.Components.DataDisplay`) with its `UsageCategory` model: how much of a quota is gone. The track is a `role="meter"` element carrying `aria-valuemin`/`aria-valuemax`/`aria-valuenow` (invariant, so a culture's group separator can never turn the value into a different number) and a culture-formatted `aria-valuetext` ("8,200 of 10,000 credits, 82%"); the percent symbol and its spacing come from `NumberFormatInfo.PercentPositivePattern`, so Czech renders `82 %`. `WarningThreshold` (default `0.8`) and `CriticalThreshold` (default `1.0`) are RATIOS of the limit and are checked critical-first; the state is carried by an ICON, a WORD and a colour (`data-state`, `tm-usage-meter--warning` / `--critical`), never by colour alone. Usage above the limit is NOT hidden: `aria-valuenow` reports the true amount, the percentage keeps counting (`112%`), the fill stays capped at 100 % of its box and `data-over-limit="true"` plus a localized over-limit line state the exact excess. `Categories` paint decorative (`aria-hidden`, no hover-only `title`) segments inside the filled part of the track and list the same data as a real `<table>` (caption, `th scope="col"` headers, a `th scope="row"` per category) whose shares round with the largest-remainder method so they add up to exactly 100 %; `Used` stays the headline, usage the categories do not explain becomes an explicit localized "Other" row, and an inconsistent host (categories claiming more than `Used`) is tolerated because the weights are measured against the larger of the two. ONE polite live region announces a THRESHOLD TRANSITION only (into warning, into critical, back within the limit) — a freshly rendered meter says nothing and a re-render inside the same state says nothing, and when two transitions would produce the same sentence an invisible marker is toggled so the region still sees a change. `Title` is a real, visible heading (`h2`–`h6` selected by `HeadingLevel`, default `3`, clamped to 2–6) that also NAMES the meter; `Compact` keeps the track, the visible title (a plain label rather than a heading), the amount, the percentage and the state and drops the reset line, the daily sparkline and the category table (a breakdown without its numbers would be colour-only). Edge cases are explicit: a non-positive `Limit` means an UNKNOWN limit (0 of 0, normal state whatever the thresholds say, no division by zero), `NaN` thresholds fall back to their documented defaults and negative ones count as `0`, a negative `Used` counts as zero, a malformed `ValueFormat` falls back to `N0` instead of throwing out of a render. The fill's width transition is enumerated in the `animations.css` reduced-motion block; forced-colors keeps the track edged in `CanvasText` and the painted surfaces opt out of the substitution. Docs: [docs/usage-meter.md](docs/usage-meter.md).
  - **Surface:** `Used`, `Limit`, `Unit`, `ValueFormat`, `ValueFormatter`, `Culture`, `WarningThreshold`, `CriticalThreshold`, `ResetsAt`, `DailyUsage`, `Categories`, `Compact`, `Title`, `HeadingLevel`, `AriaLabel`, `NearLimitContent`, `Class` (+ inherited `DataTestId`/`TestIdPrefix`); model `UsageCategory` (`Key`, `Label`, `Used`, optional `Color` validated as a CSS colour).
  - **CSS classes:** `.tm-usage-meter`, `--compact`, `--warning`, `--critical`, `__title`, `__track`, `__fill`, `__segment(--tone-1..6|--remainder)`, `__readout`, `__amount`, `__percent`, `__state`, `__state-text`, `__over`, `__over-icon`, `__reset`, `__reset-icon`, `__daily`, `__sparkline`, `__cta`, `__table`, `__row(--other)`, `__label`, `__label-inner`, `__swatch(--tone-1..6|--remainder)`, `__value`, `__share`. No new design token is needed — the fill uses `--tm-color-primary` / `-warning` / `-danger` and the fallback tones the categorical palette already ships.
  - **Wireframe:** the new `usage-meter` UI role plus the `TmUsageMeter` schema (`title`, `used`, `limit`, `unit`, `showReset`, `showDaily`, `showCategories`, `compact`) and its declarative stencil, which derives the warning and critical state from `used`/`limit`.
  - **Demo:** a `/data-display` section with a monthly credit quota in the warning state, the category table, the reset date, the daily sparkline, the `NearLimitContent` call to action, a compact copy and two buttons that walk the meter through critical and over the limit.
- **New `TmTraceWaterfall`** (`Tempo.Blazor.Components.Observability`) with its `TraceSpan` / `TraceSpanKind` / `TraceSpanStatus` / `TraceMetricColumn` models (in `Tempo.Blazor.Abstractions`, namespace `Tempo.Blazor.Models`): a generic span waterfall for traces. One row per span, indented by its place in the tree, with a bar measured against one shared time axis, the duration and any host-declared metric columns. The span list is FLAT — the tree comes from `TraceSpan.ParentId`: a span whose parent names no supplied span is an ORPHAN attached under the root (never silently dropped) and a parent cycle (A→B→A, or a span parented to itself) is REJECTED and reported, so a malformed trace neither throws nor recurses forever. Running spans (no `EndedAt`) extend to the caller's "now", which comes from the injectable `TimeProvider`.
  - **Surface:** `Spans`, `Title`, `AriaLabel`, `SelectedSpanId`/`SelectedSpanIdChanged` (`@bind-SelectedSpanId`), `DetailTemplate`, `MetricColumns`, `Culture`, `LiveMode`, `LiveTickInterval`, `TimeProvider` (default `TimeProvider.System`), `MaxHeight`, `ShowZoom`, `Class` (+ inherited `DataTestId`/`TestIdPrefix`); models `TraceSpan` (`Id`, `ParentId`, `Name`, `Kind`, `StartedAt`, `EndedAt`, `Status`, `Metrics`, `Attributes` — the two default maps are one shared `ReadOnlyDictionary`, so a caller that casts the interface back cannot mutate every default span), enums `TraceSpanKind` (`Llm`|`Tool`|`Agent`|`Http`|`Db`|`Custom`) and `TraceSpanStatus` (`Ok`|`Error`|`Running`|`Cancelled`), record `TraceMetricColumn` (`Key`, `Label`, `Format`).
  - **Accessibility:** the surface is a div-based treegrid — `role="treegrid"` with `row`/`columnheader`/`gridcell` children, `aria-labelledby`-style `aria-label`, `aria-rowcount`/`aria-colcount`, `aria-level` and `aria-expanded` per row and `aria-selected` on the selected row. A roving tabindex: exactly one row is `tabindex="0"`; ↑/↓ move it, Home/End jump to the first/last visible row, → expands (or moves to the first child) and ← collapses (or walks to the parent). Enter selects on KEYDOWN (guarded against auto-repeat) and Space selects on KEYUP, exactly where a native button fires its click; the disclosure is a native `<button>` that stops propagation, so toggling never also selects. The keys the rows handle (↑/↓/←/→, Home/End, Space) do NOT also scroll the page or the row area: a render-time `@onkeydown:preventDefault` cannot be per key (it would swallow Tab and trap focus in the grid), so the decision lives in the small `tm-trace-waterfall.js` ES module every row's keydown bubbles through — Tab, Enter and the zoom shortcuts keep their default, and a key targeting a control inside a row (the disclosure) is left alone. Kind colours ship with an ICON and a visually hidden kind name, an error ships an icon AND localized text, and the slowest LEAF span carries a localized badge. ONE polite live region announces a user action (select, expand/collapse, zoom) — never a live tick.
  - **Axis, zoom and metrics:** ticks choose ms / s / min from the visible range and are culture-formatted; `+`, `−` and reset (native buttons with localized `aria-label`s and `aria-keyshortcuts`) narrow/restore the visible window, and the same keys work from a focused row (handled on the grid, not the component root, so typing `+` inside a host's `DetailTemplate` never zooms the trace). `MetricColumns` renders one cell per column; a span that does not report the key renders a dash (never a zero) and a span with children also shows its subtree sum (Σ) behind a localized accessible name.
  - **Detail panel placement:** `DetailTemplate` renders to the RIGHT of the grid on a wide container and BELOW it on a narrow one — a container query on the component's own root, never the viewport.
  - **Responsive grid:** the treegrid is the ONE scroll owner in both axes — its track minimums (name / timeline / duration / metrics) can exceed a 360–390 px container, so the rows keep the full template (`min-inline-size: max-content`) and the grid scrolls sideways, while the HEADER STICKS to the top of the same scrollport. That is what keeps the header over its columns: a second, inner horizontal scroller is exactly how a header and its rows drift apart, and `overflow-x: visible` cannot be paired with `overflow-y: auto` (CSS computes the first to `auto`). `MaxHeight` therefore caps the grid (the sticky header is counted in it) rather than a separate row box, and the overflow stays INSIDE the grid, so the page itself never scrolls sideways. A `@container tm-trace-waterfall (width < 640px)` query tightens the track KNOBS (`--tm-trace-waterfall-name-width`, `--tm-trace-waterfall-timeline-width`, `--tm-trace-waterfall-duration-width`, `--tm-trace-waterfall-metric-width`); `RootStyle` emits the template from those variables, so the component writes no pixel size of its own.
  - **Virtualization:** above 200 rows the body switches to `Virtualize` (`ItemSize=32`, overscan 8), so a thousand-span trace does not put a thousand rows in the DOM on every tick.
  - **Live mode:** with `LiveMode` the component redraws every `LiveTickInterval` through `InvokeAsync(StateHasChanged)` and ONLY while some span is running; the `ITimer` is created from the supplied `TimeProvider` — and RE-created when the host swaps that `TimeProvider` while `LiveMode` is on, so the replaced clock's timer never keeps driving redraws — and disposed in `IDisposable` (a tick that loses the race with `Dispose` is a no-op). A fake clock drives the whole path in tests, which is how the running bar's growth is proven without waiting.

New `--tm-trace-*` kind tokens exist in light and dark (`tokens.css`, both blocks of `tokens-dark.css`); the one animated subject `.tm-trace-waterfall__bar` is enumerated in the `animations.css` reduced-motion block; forced-colors keeps every bar and its track bordered and the selected row outlined in `Highlight`; every focusable control carries the two-layer `--tm-focus-ring` with a transparent outline that survives forced-colors.
  - **Wireframe:** the new `trace-waterfall` UI role plus the `TmTraceWaterfall` schema (`title`, `expanded`, `showZoom`, `showMetrics`, `live`) and its declarative stencil, drawing every one of those knobs.
  - **Demo:** a `/data-display` section with a generated agent run (LLM, tool, HTTP and DB spans, one failed request), the host metric columns, a selected span's detail and a live-trace toggle.
  - **Docs:** [docs/trace-waterfall.md](docs/trace-waterfall.md).

- **New `TmFacetFilter`** (`Tempo.Blazor.Components.Filters`) with its `FacetGroup` / `FacetOption` models (in `Tempo.Blazor.Abstractions`, namespace `Tempo.Blazor.Models`) and the `FacetFilterPresentation` enum: the faceted filter surface — labelled groups of checkbox options with result counts, a search box inside a long group, a "Show {n} more" truncation, the active filters as removable chips (`TmFilterChip`) and a clear-all action. `@bind-Selected` is an `IReadOnlyDictionary<string, IReadOnlySet<string>>` (group key → the set of selected values); every gesture raises ONE immutable snapshot through `SelectedChanged` (a fresh dictionary of fresh sets, a group with nothing selected omitted), while `Selected` stays an INPUT: a host value that did not change never undoes what the reader picked, and a host key that matches no group is preserved untouched and rendered as a removable chip labelled with the raw value. `Presentation` picks the surface: `Popover` (the default) is a trigger plus an anchored dialog popover (`TmOverlayPanel`, `Role="dialog"`, focus trapped, Escape closes and overlay.js restores the trigger's focus) and becomes the core bottom sheet (`TmDrawer`, `Position=Bottom`) on a phone band; `Inline` renders the groups in the page flow with no trigger and no sheet. Filters apply on every toggle; `ResultCount` opts into the confirmation step — the footer's primary action becomes "Show {n} results" (the grammatical form comes from `Loc.Plural`: "Show 1 result" / "Zobrazit 5 výsledků") and confirming raises `OnApply` after closing the surface. Counts are formatted with `Culture` (default: the ambient one) and travel into the checkbox's accessible name ("Electronics (512)"), so the number is never visual-only; a group's search box appears at `options.Count >= SearchThreshold` and matches accent-insensitively (`usti` finds "Ústí"); a disclosure's selected count is part of its name ("Status (selected: 2)"). ONE polite live region announces a changed result count — nothing else is announced, because a checkbox's state and a disclosure's count are already spoken natively. Native buttons and native checkboxes only (no key emulation); `(pointer: coarse)` grows the rows and the actions to the 44 px target; forced-colors gives every focusable control its own `Highlight` outline and keeps the count badge with a system edge. Docs: [docs/facet-filter.md](docs/facet-filter.md).

The one animated subject `.tm-facet-filter__chevron` is enumerated in the `animations.css` reduced-motion block.
  - **Wireframe:** the new `facet-filter` UI role plus the `TmFacetFilter` schema (`title`, `presentation`, `showSearch`, `showCounts`, `showChips`, `collapsed`) and its declarative stencil, drawing every one of those knobs.
  - **Demo:** a `/data-display` section with the popover presentation (host-computed `ResultCount`, an applied-count read-out) and the inline presentation over the same groups.
  - **Focus handoff (accessibility, WCAG 2.4.3):** every gesture that removes the control holding focus hands focus on after the render that removed it, so it never falls to the page body. Removing a chip focuses the remove button of the chip that takes its place (the previous one when the removed chip was last) and the trigger when the row empties; the page-level clear-all (the whole chip row disappears) focuses the trigger; the footer clear-all (its own button disables itself) focuses the confirmation action of the still-open surface; "Show {n} more" (which removes itself) focuses the checkbox of the first option it revealed. `Presentation="Inline"` has no trigger, so its fallback is the first group's disclosure (the heading, which now carries `tabindex="-1"`, when there are no groups). The target is armed by the gesture only and applied once in `OnAfterRenderAsync`, so a parameter-driven re-render never moves focus. The chip wrappers are keyed by group + value (a surviving chip's DOM is never recreated) and the option inputs, chip remove buttons, confirmation action and trigger carry stable positional `id`s; the moves run through the shared `overlay.js` `focusById`.
  - **`TmFilterChip.RemoveButtonId` (additive):** optional DOM id for the chip's remove button. `TmFacetFilter` sets it so it can hand focus to the neighbouring chip; null (the default) renders no id, so every existing consumer's markup is unchanged.
  - **Fixed:** the Czech group-search placeholder read "Hledat v skupině {0}"; Czech needs "ve" before the "sk-" cluster, so it is now "Hledat ve skupině {0}" (`TmFacetFilter_Search`). The string is also the search box's accessible name, so the slip reached screen readers.
  - **Docs:** [docs/facet-filter.md](docs/facet-filter.md) now states that a host which REFUSES a change must pass a NEW `Selected` dictionary to force a reset (a re-supplied reference cannot be told apart from an ordinary re-render) and documents the focus handoff; `FacetGroup` carries a `<remarks>` that its generated equality compares `Options` by reference.
- **New `TmTrendList`** (`Tempo.Blazor.Components.DataDisplay`) and its `TrendItem` / `TrendListLayout` model: a compact list of metrics and their change over a period. One row per `TrendItem`, rendered as a semantic `<ul>` (default) or a real `<table>` with a caption, `th scope="col"` headers and a `th scope="row"` per metric (`Layout="TrendListLayout.Table"`; `LabelHeader`/`ValueHeader`/`ChangeHeader` override the localized wording). The delta is formatted with the culture's own percent convention (`+12.5%` in English, `+12,5 %` in Czech — the symbol and its spacing come from `NumberFormatInfo.PercentPositivePattern`; `DeltaFormat` overrides the number's shape), and the direction travels as an arrow icon, a `data-trend` slug, a tone class and a `tm-sr-only` word, so colour is never the only carrier. `TrendItem.PositiveIsGood` decides the TONE only, so a falling churn rate reads "Decrease" and is painted as good news. Also: `NumericValue` (wins over the string `Value`, formatted with `ValueFormat`/`Culture`), an optional per-row `Sparkline` (`TmSparkline`), an optional `Href` that renders one native `<a>` (relative/`http`/`https`/`mailto` only; a refused value means NO target, and control characters are refused outright because a browser strips them before reading the scheme), an empty state and a loading state (skeletons, `aria-busy`, hidden "Loading values"). No live region, no animation. Docs: [docs/trend-list.md](docs/trend-list.md).
  - **Surface:** `Items`, `IsLoading`, `Layout`, `Title`, `AriaLabel`, `DeltaFormat`, `ValueFormat`, `Culture`, `LabelHeader`, `ValueHeader`, `ChangeHeader`, `Class` (+ inherited `DataTestId`/`TestIdPrefix`); model `TrendItem` (`Id`, `Label`, `Value`, `NumericValue`, `Delta`, `PositiveIsGood`, `Sparkline`, `Href`).
  - **CSS classes:** `.tm-trend-list(--table)`, `__title`, `__items`, `__item`, `__label`, `__link`, `__value`, `__trend(--positive|--negative|--neutral)`, `__delta`, `__sparkline`, `__table`, `__row`, `__change`, `__empty`, `__skeleton`. No animation → the reduced-motion enumeration is unchanged for this component.
- **New `TmBreakdownCard`** (`Tempo.Blazor.Components.DataDisplay`) and its `BreakdownPart` model: a whole in parts. The rounded shares come from a **largest-remainder** split, so they add up to exactly 100 % (three equal parts are `34 %` + `33 %` + `33 %`, never 99 %). `Total` declares the whole: null (default) means the parts' sum; a bigger declared total adds an explicit localized "Other" row (and segment) for the rest; a total below the sum is ignored so no share can exceed 100 %. Rows render biggest-first with a stable tie-break; a negative value counts as zero for the share while the row stays visible. `BreakdownPart.Color` is validated as a CSS colour (token reference, hex, `rgb`/`hsl`/`oklch`/`color-mix`, named colour — a class name or a payload carrying `;`, `{`, `}`, `url(` emits no style) and written into the segment's and the swatch's inline `background-color`, winning over the rotating `--tm-category-*` tone. The proportional strip is `aria-hidden` and the `<table>` is the accessible presentation (caption, `Item`/`Value`/`Share` columns, `th scope="row"` per part) — one fact, read once. `PeriodOptions` + `@bind-Period` render a segmented switcher (currently through `TmRadioGroup Appearance=Segmented`; phase 8 switches it to `TmSegmentedControl` with no contract change). A re-sorted order animates with a CSS-only FLIP: `BreakdownFlip` computes each moved row's shift, the row carries it as `--tm-breakdown-card-row-shift` plus the `--flip` class, and one keyframe animation (`tm-breakdown-row-flip`) slides it home in a single render — no JavaScript, no layout measurement, and a versioned row key so a second reorder restarts it. `BreakdownPart.Id` is the row identity (the `@key` and the FLIP key) and should be unique; duplicate and empty ids are TOLERATED — the card derives a private row key so every row still renders, and only a row without a unique id misses the reorder animation. The row header stays a real `th`: the swatch + label layout rides an inner `.tm-breakdown-card__label-inner` (a `display:flex` on the `th` would cost the row-header role in WebKit/VoiceOver), the swatches are `aria-hidden`, and forced-colors keeps the strip and swatches (`forced-color-adjust: none` plus a `CanvasText` bar edge). `AnimateReorder="false"` turns the FLIP off and `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` clamps the animation to 0.01 ms. Docs: [docs/breakdown-card.md](docs/breakdown-card.md).
  - **Surface:** `Parts`, `Title`, `AriaLabel`, `Total`, `ValueFormat`, `Culture`, `ShowTotal`, `ShowBar`, `AnimateReorder`, `IsLoading`, `PeriodOptions`, `Period`/`PeriodChanged`, `PeriodLabel`, `Class` (+ inherited `DataTestId`/`TestIdPrefix`); model `BreakdownPart` (`Id`, `Label`, `Value`, `Color`).
  - **CSS classes:** `.tm-breakdown-card`, `__title`, `__period`, `__total(--label|--value)`, `__bar`, `__segment(--tone-1..6|--remainder)`, `__table`, `__row(--remainder|--flip)`, `__label(--inner)`, `__swatch(--tone-1..6)`, `__value`, `__share`, `__empty`, `__skeleton`. The one animated subject `.tm-breakdown-card__row--flip` is enumerated in the `animations.css` reduced-motion block.
- **`TmChart` gains an index tooltip (`ChartTooltipMode`).** Additive: the default `TooltipMode` is `ChartTooltipMode.Point`, so a chart that does not set it renders the pre-2.9.1 per-point tooltip, its handlers and its markup unchanged. `TooltipMode="ChartTooltipMode.Index"` divides the plot into one full-height hover zone per category, draws a vertical crosshair on the active category and shows ONE card listing every visible series at that index (colour dot, series label, value). The chart becomes a single tab stop: `→`/`←` walk the indices (the first press lands on the first/last category), `Home`/`End` jump to the edges, `Esc` hides the card without leaving the chart, focus alone shows nothing, and leaving the chart clears the index. `aria-keyshortcuts` advertises the keys and `aria-describedby` points at a visually hidden hint. The card lives inside the `role="img"` SVG, so exactly ONE polite atomic live region announces the index ("Q1: Licenses 100, Services 120") — nothing is announced before the plot is explored. `TooltipIndexTemplate` (`RenderFragment<ChartIndexTooltipContext>`) replaces the card's rows while keeping its edge-aware placement; `ChartIndexTooltipContext` carries `Index`, `Label`, `Series` (`ChartIndexSeriesValue`: `DatasetIndex`, `Label`, `Value`, `Color`) and `Total`. Legend-hidden series, `NaN` gaps and series shorter than the index are absent from both the card and the announcement. Card text is culture-formatted; SVG geometry stays invariant. Supported by `Line`, `Area`, `Bar`, `StackedBar` and `StackedArea`; every other type falls back to `Point` rather than rendering half a crosshair. The hover zones paint ABOVE the marks (that is what makes one zone serve a whole category), so in index mode `OnSegmentClick` reports the index once with the first visible series' value. The chart's `aria-label` moved from the hardcoded `"{Type} chart"` to the localized `TmChart_AriaLabel` (`"{0} chart"`, so the English output is byte-identical). Docs: [docs/chart-tooltip.md](docs/chart-tooltip.md).
  - **Surface:** `TooltipMode`, `TooltipIndexTemplate`; model `ChartTooltipMode` (`Point`|`Index`), `ChartIndexTooltipContext` (`Index`, `Label`, `Series`, `Total`), `ChartIndexSeriesValue` (`DatasetIndex`, `Label`, `Value`, `Color`).
  - **DOM after (index mode only):** a wrapper `<g class="tm-chart__index-zones">` with one `<rect class="tm-chart__index-zone" data-testid="chart-index-zone-{i}">` per category, `line.tm-chart__crosshair`, `circle.tm-chart__index-dot` per series on Line/Area, the index card (`foreignObject` + `.tm-chart__tooltip--index` with `.tm-chart__tooltip-series` rows) and two `tm-sr-only` spans (the keyboard hint and the live region). Point mode adds none of it. No new animation → the reduced-motion enumeration is unchanged for the chart.
- **`TmSparkline` gains a text alternative, a colour override and an opt-in tooltip.** Additive: nothing is set by default, so an existing sparkline renders the pre-2.9.1 markup. `AriaLabel` (null = a localized summary of minimum, maximum and last value in the current culture, `TmSparkline_Summary`) makes the graphic name its own numbers instead of "Sparkline chart". `Color` overrides the stroke/fill of Line/Bar/Area (any CSS colour, typically a `var(--tm-*)` token; null keeps the built-in blue; `Pie` keeps its categorical palette). `ShowMinMax` adds a `min … max` corner caption that is `aria-hidden` (the numbers are already in the label, so announcing them twice would be a duplicate). `ShowLastPoint` rings the final value on Line/Area. `ShowTooltip` adds a per-point/bar card, a focus stop with `→`/`←`/`Home`/`End`/`Esc`, and ONE polite live region announcing `Point {n} of {m}: {value}`; the active marker is bigger AND ringed, so the state never relies on colour alone. The card is positioned INSIDE the sparkline's box, because a bubble above it would be clipped by the table cell, grid area or card header a sparkline usually lives in.
  - **Surface:** `AriaLabel`, `Color`, `ShowMinMax`, `ShowLastPoint`, `ShowTooltip`, `Element`.
  - **CSS classes:** `.tm-sparkline__point`/`--active`, `.tm-sparkline__bar--active`, `.tm-sparkline__last-point`, `.tm-sparkline__minmax`, `.tm-sparkline__tooltip`; the one new animated subject `.tm-sparkline__point` is enumerated in the `animations.css` reduced-motion block.
- **`TmSparkline.Element` and `TmSkeleton.Element` (phrasing-content roots).** Additive: `TmRootElement.Div` (the default) renders the `<div>` both components have always rendered. `Element="TmRootElement.Span"` renders a `<span>` root instead — including the sparkline's empty state — and an undefined enum value falls back to `div`. The two parameters share the new `TmRootElement` enum (`Tempo.Blazor.Components.Common`), so a typo can no longer silently pick `div`. This closes the phase-1 carry-forward that a whole-card `TmStatCard` target (`<a>`/`<button>`) nested a block `<div>` in an inline element: `TmStatCard` now passes `Element="TmRootElement.Span"` for its sparkline and its three loading skeletons, so its children are phrasing content everywhere. The default card, the default sparkline and the default skeleton are byte-identical to 2.9.x. The sparkline's min/max caption also steps aside (`visibility: hidden`) while the tooltip card is on, so the two top-corner captions never overlap in a narrow cell.
- **Wireframe:** the `TmChart` schema gained `showTooltip` and `tooltipMode` (`point`|`index`; the native sketch draws the crosshair and its card when both are on) and the `TmSparkline` schema gained `showTooltip`, `showMinMax` and `showLastPoint` (the built-in pack draws each conditionally).
- **Chart documentation:** new overlays for `ChartTooltipMode`, `ChartIndexTooltipContext` and `ChartIndexSeriesValue`; `TmChart.TooltipMode`/`TooltipIndexTemplate` and the five `TmSparkline` parameters are in the generated bundles. Docs: [docs/chart-tooltip.md](docs/chart-tooltip.md).
- **Shared data-display helpers (internal, no public surface change).** `TmStatCard`'s delta grammar, trend marker and safe-href allow-list moved into `TrendDelta`, and its CSS-colour validator into `CssColorValue`, so `TmStatCard`, `TmTrendList` and `TmBreakdownCard` share one implementation. `TmStatCard` behaviour and markup are byte-identical (its own tests still pin that).
- **Wireframe:** new `trend-list` and `breakdown-card` UI roles plus `TmTrendList` / `TmBreakdownCard` schemas and stencils; the pack draws the table layout, the delta/sparkline switches, the declared total, the strip, the period chips and the loading state conditionally.
- **New `TmAnimatedNumber`** (`Tempo.Blazor.Components.DataDisplay`): an odometer-style number that counts up to its target. The FINAL formatted value is what the document contains — one node, so a screen reader and a copy/paste meet the number exactly once, and the first paint already shows the target — while `tm-animated-number.js` only repaints that same text between frames. `Announce` (default `false`) is the only live-region opt-in and renders exactly one polite, atomic region; the visual span then steps out of the accessibility tree. Reduced motion is probed once before the first animation (`prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` → no ticker at all), `Duration` is clamped to 0–10000 and `0` imports no JavaScript, `Animate="false"` is a pure-Blazor path, and a value that changes mid-animation retargets from the number on screen (`StartValue` seeds the first frame only). `Format` (default `N0`) and `Culture` (default: current culture) format the final text; `Prefix`/`Suffix` wrap it. The component is a wireframe citizen with the `animated-number` role and its own stencil. Docs: [docs/animated-number.md](docs/animated-number.md).
  - **Surface:** `Value`, `Format`, `Culture`, `Prefix`, `Suffix`, `Duration`, `StartValue`, `Animate`, `Announce`, `Class` (+ inherited `DataTestId`/`TestIdPrefix`).
  - **CSS classes:** `.tm-animated-number`, `.tm-animated-number__value`; no CSS animation is added, so the reduced-motion enumeration in `animations.css` is unchanged.
- **`TmStatCard` gains an opt-in KPI surface.** Additive: a card that passes none of the new parameters renders the EXACT 2.9.x markup (same root, same three spans, same whitespace, no `data-testid`, no extra class — pinned by `TmStatCardTests.WithoutNewParameters_RendersTheExactPreTwoTenMarkup`). New: `Delta` (`double?`, percent points) with culture-correct formatting (`+12,5 %` in Czech, `+12.5%` in English — the symbol and its spacing come from `NumberFormatInfo.PercentPositivePattern`) and an optional `DeltaFormat`; `TrendDirection` (`Auto` derives it from the delta's sign, plus `Up`/`Down`/`Flat`) with `data-trend` and the visually hidden `TmStatCard_TrendUp`/`Down`/`Flat` word so colour is never the only carrier; `PositiveIsGood` (default `true`) which inverts the TONE only, so a falling churn rate is `--positive` and still reads "Decrease"; `ComparisonLabel`; a decorative `Icon`; `Sparkline` (`double[]` through `TmSparkline`); `IsLoading` (three skeletons, a visually hidden localized "Loading" text, `aria-busy`); `NumericValue` + `AnimateValue` + `ValueFormat` + `ValuePrefix`/`ValueSuffix` + `Culture` (an embedded `TmAnimatedNumber`, `AnimateValue` off by default); and the whole-card target `Href` (`<a class="tm-stat-card tm-stat-card--interactive">`) or `OnClick` (`<button …>` — one native focus stop, `OnClick` wins over `Href`). An href renders only for a relative URL or the `http`/`https`/`mailto` scheme; a refused value (`javascript:`, `data:`, `vbscript:`, protocol-relative `//host`) means NO target at all and the card falls back to the plain `div`. The scheme is parsed by the component rather than by `Uri`, because a browser strips ASCII tab/LF/CR from a URL before reading its scheme (`Uri.TryCreate("java\tscript:…")` reports that attack as relative): an href carrying ANY control character is refused outright, and a scheme is the text before the first `/`, `?` or `#`, matched case-insensitively against the three accepted names. `SubValueColor` keeps its 2.9.0 validation. Docs: [docs/stat-card.md](docs/stat-card.md).
  - **DOM before:** `<div class="tm-stat-card">` with `.tm-stat-value`, `.tm-stat-label` and an optional `.tm-stat-subvalue`.
  - **DOM after (opt-in parts only):** the same root unless `Href`/`OnClick` is set (then `a`/`button` plus `tm-stat-card--interactive`), plus `.tm-stat-card__icon` (with `tm-stat-card--has-icon` on the root reserving the corner gutter the absolutely positioned icon needs), `.tm-stat-card__trend(--positive|--negative|--neutral)` containing the arrow, a `tm-sr-only` direction word, `.tm-stat-card__delta` and `.tm-stat-card__comparison`, `.tm-stat-card__sparkline` (which is `aria-hidden` on an interactive card so the chart's own label is not spliced into the target's accessible name) and `.tm-stat-card__skeletons`. No attribute or class is added to the default card.
  - **Wireframe:** the `stat-card` schema gained `delta`, `deltaFormat`, `comparisonLabel`, `trend`, `positiveIsGood`, `icon`, `sparkline`, `loading` and `animateValue`; the built-in pack draws each conditionally.
- **Added (core `TmActivityLog` + `TmGanttTaskPanel`): forwarding of `CommentSubmitHandler` / `CommentEditHandler`.** Both consumers of `TmActivityComments` now pass the two save handlers through additively, the same way they already forward `OnCommentSubmitted` — hosts of the activity log or the Gantt task panel can keep the draft on a failed save without dropping down to the standalone comments component. `TmGantt` itself does not forward them yet (tracked by the open Gantt remaining task). No breaking change: without the handlers the DOM, callback order and behavior are unchanged. Demo: `/activity` gained a **„Simulate failed save"** toggle on the standalone comments thread that routes posting through the handlers returning `false` (with a simulated latency) and presents the reason through a `TmAlert`. bUnit: `TmActivityLog_ForwardsCommentHandlers`, `TmActivityLog_CommentSubmitHandlerFalse_KeepsDraft`, `TmGanttTaskPanel_ForwardsCommentHandlers` (TDD, RED first). E2E (WASM, `ActivityCommentsFailureE2ETests`, 5 tests): failed submit keeps text + internal-switch state and shows the consumer alert; retry after turning the simulation off succeeds and closes; failed edit keeps the inline editor with the edited text (stored comment untouched) and saving again after disabling succeeds; the in-flight submit button carries `aria-disabled="true"` (and a second click cannot double-post); two consecutive failures keep the draft and the alert. Post-failure screenshots light/dark at 1440 and 390 in `tests/Tempo.Blazor.E2E/__screenshots__/activity-comments/fze-2/` (every capture asserts `#blazor-error-ui` hidden and PNG > 2 KB, UX-reviewed: the draft text stays visible and the alert wording matches). JSON documentation: `TmActivityLog.json` and `Scheduler/TmGanttTaskPanel.json` overlays extended with both handlers, aggregates regenerated, `validate --fail-on-drift` clean. Demo strings `TmDemo_ActivityComments_SimulateFailure*` in en/cs/sk/fr (`DemoResourceCompletenessTests` parity). Wireframe stencil: no new painted state (the failure reason is the host's alert; the component only announces through the existing aria-live status and the existing `aria-disabled` look), so no stencil change. **Breaking / Migration: none (additive)** — the two consumers only forward the handlers; hosts that do not pass them compile and render byte-identically to 2.9.x. To actually keep a draft on failure a host switches from the fire-and-forget callback to the handler:
  - **Before:** `<TmActivityLog OnCommentAdded="Save" … />` — `Save` cannot report failure, so a failed save discards the typed draft.
  - **After:** `<TmActivityLog CommentSubmitHandler="SaveAsync" … />` with `private async Task<bool> SaveAsync(TmCommentSubmission s) { try { await Save(s.Html); return true; } catch { await InvokeAsync(StateHasChanged); return false; } }` — returning `false` keeps the editor open with the draft intact; the host presents the reason through its own alert. Same for edits: `CommentEditHandler="EditAsync"` with `Func<TmCommentEdit, Task<bool>>`. Handlers are expected to convert their own failures to `false` instead of throwing (an exception still propagates like one from the legacy callbacks).

- **Added (core `TmActivityComments`): `CommentSubmitHandler` / `CommentEditHandler` — a failed save no longer discards the draft.** Two optional handlers let the host report save success back to the component: `Func<TmCommentSubmission, Task<bool>>? CommentSubmitHandler` (new comment) and `Func<TmCommentEdit, Task<bool>>? CommentEditHandler` (inline edit; new `TmCommentEdit` record with `CommentId` + `Html` in `Tempo.Blazor.Abstractions.Shared`). When set, the handler runs INSTEAD of `OnCommentSubmitted` + `OnCommentAdded` (resp. `OnCommentEdited`); returning `true` closes and clears the editor exactly like today, returning `false` keeps the editor open with the typed text, the internal-switch state and the dirty draft intact (no `OnDraftChanged` transition, focus untouched) and announces the non-save through the composer's aria-live status (`TmActivityComments_SubmitNotSaved`, en/cs/sk/fr) — the host presents the actual failure reason. A handler exception propagates like an exception from the legacy callbacks (the in-flight flag still clears in `finally`, the editor stays open); handlers are expected to convert their own failures to `false`. Purely additive: with no handler the DOM, callback order (`OnCommentSubmitted` → `OnCommentAdded`) and behavior are byte-identical to before. **Review follow-up:** the inline editor announces the non-save through its own always-rendered polite live region (the composer status is not mounted while editing), cleared on StartEdit/CancelEdit/DiscardDraft; the in-flight „Posting comment." status is reset in `finally` when an exception left it up; the post-await close is race-safe — an edit closes only when the same comment is still being edited and a new-comment submit closes only when the composer generation is unchanged, so cancelling or switching targets mid-flight no longer wipes the new draft; and both submit buttons wear `aria-disabled="true"` (with the existing `_isSubmitting` guard) instead of the native `disabled` attribute, keeping keyboard focus on the button during the save — styled with the existing disabled-look tokens in `_activity-comments.css` + the regenerated `tempo-blazor.bundled.css`.

- **Added (demo + docs + E2E, „Nové komponenty 1/7" fáze 6): `/otp-input` demo page, toast demo extensions, dokumentace a E2E/vizuální kontrola.** New demo page `/otp-input` (nav item under Components, shared by all render modes): numeric 6-digit input with a simulated „Send SMS code" flow and a demo verifier (code `123456` → `Verified`; anything else → shake + `Invalid` + polite live-region announcement + draft clear/refocus via `ShowErrorAsync`/`ClearAsync`/`FocusAsync`), an alphanumeric `Length=8` + `GroupSize=4` backup-code input (auto-uppercase echo), a masked `Length=4` PIN input and a paste/autofill behaviour section. The `/feedback` page toast area gains: an **Undo** demo (list-item delete with `ShowUndo` restore + direct restore), a **promise** demo (simulated 2 s upload with success and failure paths), a **Key dedupe** counter, a custom-content toast, a **positions & deck** section driving the shared layout container live (new demo-only scoped `DemoToastPresentationState` — per-circuit/per-user state — registered in all three demo hosts plus the InteractiveAuto WASM client; `MainLayout` binds `TmToastContainer Position/Stacked` to it — one container per app, so no second container is mounted) and an **Escape-ordering modal probe** (toast action focused via Alt+T, Escape dismisses the toast while the modal stays). Docs: new [docs/otp-input.md](docs/otp-input.md) and [docs/toast.md](docs/toast.md), `COMPONENTS.md` gains the `TmOtpInput` section (Inputs) and `AGENTS.md` category table mentions it. E2E (WASM): `OtpInputE2ETests` (11 tests — kinds/lengths/grouping/masked render, typing → verified, wrong-code shake/announce/clear, clipboard-API paste distribution, autofill-like single-`input`-event distribution, masked PIN secrecy, alphanumeric uppercasing, scoped axe scan, 390-touch/320-dark/1024-touch edge layout with no horizontal overflow); the OTP sheet keeps every cell at the 24px floor (`min-inline-size: var(--tm-space-6)`) and the row wraps per group (`tm-otp-input__group` flex items, group `min-width: 0`) instead of shrinking or overflowing on a 320px phone — the root carries `contain: inline-size` and the cells render `size="1"` so a cell input's ~20ch intrinsic minimum can never push a flex/grid host wider than its track into the page's overflow-x clip (a @container query cannot ship here — container widths are linted to the TmBreakpoints constants) and `ToastE2ETests` (15 tests — Undo restore, promise success/error in-place settle, Key dedupe identity, Alt+T focus, Escape-inside-modal ordering, pause-on-hover freeze/resume plus a timing assertion that a hovered toast outlives its 1.5 s duration and is removed after the pointer leaves, stacked-deck collapse counts, TopCenter/BottomCenter positions, CDP touch swipe-to-dismiss, 320/390/1024 edge layouts incl. a 390 dark capture, scoped axe scan) plus a segmented-mode verifier test in `SigningStepsE2ETests`. Every capture asserts `#blazor-error-ui` stays hidden and the PNG is a real capture (>2 KB); screenshots land in `tests/Tempo.Blazor.E2E/__screenshots__/otp-input/` and `toasts/` for the selected combinations of 1440/1024-touch/390/320 × light/dark and were UX-reviewed. JSON documentation: overlays already cover `TmOtpInput`/`OtpInputKind`/`TmToastContainer`/`ToastService` types from phases 1–5; bundles regenerated (`generate`, 0 generated-only items), `validate --fail-on-drift` clean. Shared helpers `TestContextHelper`/`AxeScan` extracted for the new classes. No API changes; no new localization keys (demo strings are demo-page English per existing demo-page convention, component strings stay localized).

- **Added (Signing, „Nové komponenty 1/7" fáze 5): TmOtpInput integration into `TmSigningPhoneStep`.** Two additive parameters — `CodeInputMode` (new `SigningCodeInputMode` enum: `Single` default = today's single core `TmTextInput`, `Segmented` = the core `TmOtpInput`) and `CodeLength` (default 6, the `TmOtpInput.Length`, 4–10) — swap the one-time-code entry for the segmented input: per-cell labels, paste distribution, `autocomplete="one-time-code"`, coarse-pointer 44 px cells. State mapping in `Segmented` mode: `OtpInvalid` → the input's `Invalid` state (the step shell keeps OWNING the error text — its `role="alert"` box renders the message in every mode, the input references it through `aria-describedby`; every new wrong-code report replays the shake through `ShowErrorAsync` on the rising edge of `OtpInvalid` — which then also CLEARS the wrong draft and refocuses the first cell (`ClearAsync` + `FocusAsync`) so the next full code fires `OnComplete` again; `Verified` → the input's `Verified` state (readonly cells + the verified status render in place of the single-input verified block, reusing the step's own `TmSigningStep_Verified` wording through the new additive `TmOtpInput.VerifiedText` parameter — the step skips its own live-region announcement in segmented mode so exactly ONE verified text sounds); completing the code (`OnComplete`) automatically starts the verification when a verifier is wired (`OnVerifyCode` / the runner's `OnVerifyPhoneCode`) and the manual Verify action STAYS VISIBLE in every mode (fáze 5 review); while a verify runs the segmented cells turn READONLY, never disabled (the focus stays reachable), and the otp row carries `aria-busy`; `CodeLength` is validated in `OnParametersSet` while segmented (`ArgumentOutOfRangeException` outside 4–10); a send/resend clears the previous draft and refocuses the first cell (`ClearAsync` + `FocusAsync` on the pending-focus path). The demo `/signing-components` phone step wires a demo verifier (the demo code "123456" confirms, anything else is rejected through the runner's validation cascade) so both states can be explored. `TmSigningFormRunner` forwards both parameters additively (`CodeInputMode`/`CodeLength`), the demo `/signing-components` page gained a "Phone code input mode" switch (`data-testid="signing-phone-code-mode"`) and the step keeps its `tm-signing-phone-step__otp` class on the segmented root so the otp-row flex contract holds. No new localization keys (the existing `TmSigningStep_*` / `TmOtpInput_*` keys cover every string); existing Signing E2E selectors are untouched — the default `Single` mode renders the identical DOM as before. bUnit coverage in `TmSigningPhoneStepTests` (segmented render, cell count, auto-verify with/without a verifier, verified state, runner verify-failure ownership, runner forwarding, resend clear/focus/announcement, plus the fáze 5 review coverage: Verify button in segmented mode, readonly-not-disabled + `aria-busy` while verifying, one-verifier-call under a re-entrant completion, failed-verify clear/focus + the second-wrong-code shake replay, cell `aria-describedby` ownership, `VerifiedText` wording with exactly one live text, and the `CodeLength` range validation); JSON docs overlay extended (`SigningCodeInputMode.json`, `CodeInputMode`/`CodeLength` on the step + runner), aggregates regenerated, `validate --fail-on-drift` clean.

- **Added (core toasty, „Nové komponenty 1/7" fáze 4): promise toasty, live regiony, deck a swipe.** `ToastService.PromiseAsync(operation, ToastPromiseOptions, CancellationToken)` (plus a result-less overload) shows a sticky **loading toast** (`ToastOptions.IsLoading` — the card renders the new `.tm-toast-spinner` instead of the severity icon and no progress bar), then updates it **in place** via the phase-3 `Update` path: success → `ToastSeverity.Success` with the message from `SuccessMessage(result)` and the standard 5000 ms reading time; failure → `ToastSeverity.Error` (announced assertively unless `ToastPromiseOptions.Politeness` overrides) with `ErrorMessage(exception)`, and the exception **propagates** to the caller. Cancellation is safe both ways: a fired `CancellationToken` removes the loading toast silently (a cancelled operation is not an error) and rethrows; manually dismissing the loading toast leaves the pending update a no-op. `Update` gained an optional `politeness` argument (additive; an explicit value survives a severity change). **Live regions:** `Auto` politeness now derives per severity — **Warning joins Error as assertive** (Info/Success stay polite) and an explicit `ToastOptions.Politeness` still wins (breaking behaviour note below). **Deck:** new `TmToastContainer.Stacked` parameter renders `tm-toast-container--stacked` — the newest three toasts stay fully visible, every older card collapses to a thin inert strip (pointer-events none, content `visibility: hidden`), hovering the container or moving focus inside expands the deck; pure CSS, every toast stays in the DOM. New positions `ToastPosition.TopCenter`/`BottomCenter` (`tm-toast-container--top-center`/`--bottom-center`, `translateX(-50%)`, drop-in animation, full-width without the centering offset under 640 px). **Swipe-to-dismiss:** the new `tm-toast-swipe.js` module (wired from `TmToastContainer`, touch/pen only) rides the shared `pointer-drag.js` — a horizontal drag follows the finger and dismisses past 40 % of the card width or on a ≥ 0.5 px/ms flick through the same `DismissToast` entry point as Escape; `pointercancel`/Escape/detach roll the card back, below the threshold it animates back through `.tm-toast--swipe-return` (snap only under reduced motion); vertical intent is vetoed so `touch-action: pan-y` scrolling stays native, and the close button/Escape remain the always-available alternative (WCAG 2.5.7). The card slide-in fill mode changed `forwards` → `backwards` (a forwards fill pinned `transform` over the inline swipe transform; visually identical, the end state is the identity transform). Node tests in `__tests__/tm-toast-swipe.test.mjs` (`npm run test:overlay`); localization unchanged (no new user-facing strings — the caller supplies every promise message). Docs: `TmToastContainer.json` + `ToastPromiseOptions.json`, aggregates regenerated, `validate --fail-on-drift` clean.

  - **Behaviour change (Warning announcements).** Before: only `ToastSeverity.Error` derived `ToastPoliteness.Assertive`; a Warning was announced through the polite region. After: Warning derives assertive like Error (it needs attention now). A host that relied on the polite announcement sets `Politeness = ToastPoliteness.Polite` explicitly. No API breakage — additive enum members and optional parameters only.

- **Added (core toasty, „Nové komponenty 1/7" fáze 3): model, akce, Undo, dedupe a pauza.** `ToastService` gains an additive options API on top of the unchanged `ShowSuccess/ShowInfo/ShowWarning/ShowError` helpers: `Show(ToastOptions)` (returns the toast id; `ToastOptions` carries `Message`/`Title`/`Severity`/`Duration`/`Action`/`Content`/`Politeness` and an optional `Key`), `ShowUndo(message, onUndo, …)` (10s default duration, built-in action whose label resolves through the new `TmToast_Undo` localization key in en/cs/sk/fr), `Update(id, message, title, severity, duration)` (in-place edit that restarts the auto-dismiss timer) and `Pause`/`Resume`/`PauseAll`/`ResumeAll`/`IsPaused`/`PausedIds` (pause disarms the one-shot `TimeProvider` timer and remembers the remaining time; resume re-arms exactly that remainder — all timer state is disposed on `Remove`/`Clear`/`Dispose`). `Key` dedupe replaces an existing toast **in place** — same id, same queue position — and restarts its timer (for „Saving…" → „Saved" flows). `ToastInstance` is extended additively (`Key`, `Action`, `Content`, `Politeness`); the new `ToastAction` record carries `Label`/`LabelKey`/`OnClick` (the service stays localization-free — the container resolves `LabelKey` through `ITmLocalizer` at render time). `TmToastContainer` renders the action as a **native `<button class="tm-toast-action">`** (the browser owns Enter/Space activation — one activation per key, no emulation) and the `Content` fragment in a `.tm-toast-custom` wrapper, and new `PauseOnHover` parameter (default `true`) pauses a toast's timer on `mouseenter`/`focusin` and resumes the remaining time on `mouseleave`/`focusout`; the frozen progress animation is driven by the new `tm-toast--paused` modifier (`animation-play-state: paused`). Escape is handled **in the browser** by the new `tm-toast.js` module (keydown listener on the container): it dismisses the card holding focus, sets `e.tmEscapeHandled = true` so capture-phase consumers (dialogs, the diagram editor) do not double-handle, preventDefaults and stops propagation, then asks Blazor to remove the toast. The module also returns focus to the element a removed card took it from (remembered `focusin` relatedTarget, restored only while still connected) and implements the documented **Alt+T** hotkey that focuses the newest action button (advertised through `aria-keyshortcuts="Alt+T"`, skipped while typing in a field). While the document is hidden every auto-dismiss timer pauses via the new `tm-toast-visibility.js` module (`watch`/`unwatch`, idempotent, covered by `__tests__/tm-toast-visibility.test.mjs` in `npm run test:overlay`) and resumes on return — except toasts the user is hovering/focusing at that moment. **Behavior / DOM changes (before → after):** hovering or focusing a toast now pauses its countdown (before the timer ran to completion under the cursor) — set `PauseOnHover="false"` to restore the old behavior. Toast cards no longer carry any live role: ALL announcements go through **two persistent always-present `tm-sr-only` live regions** (polite `role="status"` + assertive `role="alert"`) inside the container — empty on first render, filled title+message with a clear-then-set so a dedupe replacement announces exactly once per text change. (This SUPERSEDES the role change drafted in the first pass of this entry — non-error toasts never shipped `role="status"`; the cards briefly had `role="status"`/`role="alert"` only in the unreleased working tree.) The container root is now a labelled `role="region"` (`TmToast_RegionLabel`, en/cs/sk/fr).
