An action toast's duration is floored to the new `MinActionDuration` container parameter (pushed to `ToastService.MinActionDuration`, default 10000ms — set before showing toasts; sticky and action-less toasts are never floored). Review-round hardening: the auto-dismiss timer callback captures its own timer instance and removes the toast only while that instance still owns the id (`ReferenceEquals` under the lock), so a stale callback from a superseded timer can never remove its replacement; `Dispose` nulls `OnChange` and every post-dispose Show/Update/Remove/Resume/timer callback is a no-op; dedupe/`Update` of a paused toast keeps it paused with the FULL new duration (no timer armed) and hover/focus holds are pruned against the visible id set; cards are `@key`ed by toast id and the progress bar by the new `ToastInstance.Revision` (bumped on every in-place replacement) so the countdown animation restarts on update; the action runs **remove-first** — a double click cannot run the delegate twice and the toast closes even when the delegate throws. `tm-toast-visibility.js` keeps per-instance state (Map keyed by the .NET reference, re-watch replaces, two containers watch independently), `watch()` returns `document.hidden` and reports synchronously when the tab starts hidden, and a rejected report never surfaces as an unhandled rejection. The action colour resolves through the AA-contrast `--tm-color-primary-text` token with a `forced-colors` fallback (`border: 1px solid ButtonText; color: ButtonText`). `TmNotificationToastContainer` is intentionally unchanged (still `role="alert"`) — aligning it is a follow-up. Node tests in `__tests__/tm-toast-visibility.test.mjs` + `__tests__/tm-toast.test.mjs` (npm run test:overlay); bUnit coverage in `ToastServiceTests` (FakeTimeProvider + a manual timer provider for the stale-callback guard) and `TmToastTests`; JSON docs regenerated, `validate --fail-on-drift` clean. Node tests in `src/Tempo.Blazor/wwwroot/js/__tests__/tm-toast-visibility.test.mjs`; bUnit coverage in `ToastServiceTests` (FakeTimeProvider) and `TmToastTests`; JSON docs regenerated, `validate --fail-on-drift` clean.

- **Added (core `TmOtpInput`, „Nové komponenty 1/7" fáze 2):** paste, autofill, error and verified state. Paste is consumed in the `tm-otp-input.js` module (`ClipboardEventArgs` carries no clipboard text across the Blazor boundary): the `paste` event is cancelled, the text is read through the exported `readPastedText` helper, cleaned (spaces/dashes dropped, per-`Kind` filtering) and distributed from the pasted-into cell — a paste longer than the remaining space prefers the LAST run of accepted characters whose length is exactly the remaining count (split on non-accepted characters), so a copied "Your code: AB12CD" fills `AB12CD` instead of a truncated flat filter; only when no run matches is the flat filter truncated. Browser autofill (e.g. iOS `one-time-code`) writes the whole code in one `input` event without a usable `beforeinput` payload; `beforeinput` now reads `event.data ?? event.dataTransfer.getData("text/plain")` and returns WITHOUT `preventDefault` when both are absent (the input listener distributes the value the browser actually wrote), while `insertReplacementText` autofill carrying `dataTransfer` text distributes exactly once. New parameters: `Invalid` (root `tm-otp-input--invalid` with a one-shot `tm-otp-input-shake` animation, `aria-invalid="true"` and an `aria-describedby` pointing at the error on the group AND every cell; `Invalid` without `ErrorText` is the supported way to surface a `TmFormField`-owned message), `ErrorText`, `Verified` (cells become `readonly`, editing is blocked in the model and the module, the localized `TmOtpInput_VerifiedStatus` status renders with a check icon + span and is referenced from every cell through `aria-describedby="{Id}-status"`) and `ReadOnly`; `Disabled`/`ReadOnly`/`Verified` block every edit path (`OnCellInputAsync`, `DistributeFromAsync`, `ClearAsync`). ONE always-rendered polite live region (`tm-sr-only`, `role="status"`) carries the error/verified text — empty on first render — and re-announces via the new public `ShowErrorAsync()` (JS reflow shake restart + clear-then-set live text) for repeated wrong codes. New public methods `FocusAsync()`, `ClearAsync()` (both syncing the DOM through the new batched `setCellValues` export — one round-trip instead of per-cell `setCellValue`) and `ShowErrorAsync()`. Localization key `TmOtpInput_VerifiedStatus` ships in en/cs/sk/fr; error/status styles use `--tm-color-danger-text` / `--tm-color-success-text` with a `forced-colors` fallback (`border: 2px solid CanvasText` for both states — the token `Mark`/`ColorInput` colours are overridden in forced colors, so the thicker system border is the state boundary, WCAG 1.4.11); `.tm-otp-input--invalid` is enumerated in the `animations.css` reduced-motion block. JSON documentation overlay extended (new parameters + `FocusAsync`/`ClearAsync`/`ShowErrorAsync` methods), aggregates regenerated, `validate --fail-on-drift` clean. Node tests in `__tests__/tm-otp-input.test.mjs` (npm run test:overlay).

- **Added (core `TmOtpInput`, „Nové komponenty 1/7" fáze 1):** segmented one-time-code input in `Tempo.Blazor.Components.Inputs` (`OtpInputKind` enum, `TmOtpInput.razor`). Renders `Length` (4–10, default 6) cells in a `role="group"` with a localized label per cell, deterministic cell ids (`{Id}-cell-{i}`, `InputId` = first cell) and `AriaLabel`/`AriaLabelledBy`/`AriaDescribedBy` group parameters. All DOM input handling lives in the new `tm-otp-input.js` ES module (`attach`/`detach`, disposed in `DisposeAsync`): `beforeinput` filtering per `Kind` (`Numeric` accepts ASCII digits with `pattern="[0-9]*"`, `Alphanumeric` uppercases with `autocapitalize="characters"`), the inserted character wins on overwrite (caret-before insert), multi-character inserts (paste/autofill) distribute from the index through `DistributeFromAsync`, IME composition is skipped and committed on `compositionend`, and arrows/Home/End/auto-advance/Backspace-step-back run in JS with no circuit round-trip; `autocomplete="one-time-code"` on the first cell, `autocorrect="off"`/`spellcheck="false"` everywhere, no `maxlength`. Pointer focus landing past an empty cell redirects to the first empty cell; C# corrections push back through `setCellValue`. `OnComplete` fires exactly once per incomplete→complete transition (host resets inside the handler re-arm it; a pre-filled `Value` never fires it). Interop teardown is safe (`JSException`/`InvalidOperationException`/`TaskCanceledException`/`ObjectDisposedException` swallowed in focus paths and disposal). Cells are `flex: 0 1` 44px on coarse pointers with a single (AA-contrast) disabled dimming; localization keys `TmOtpInput_GroupLabel`/`TmOtpInput_DigitLabel`/`TmOtpInput_CharacterLabel` ship in en/cs/sk/fr. Node tests in `__tests__/tm-otp-input.test.mjs` (npm run test:overlay). Wireframe stencil entry `TmOtpInput` (role `otp-input`) added to `tempo.stencil.json`.

- **Fixed (NotionEditor final UX review, F-01):** the database block interops `window.tmNotionDb.isCoarsePointer`, but the global was never defined — the failed JS call surfaced the Blazor error bar ("An unhandled error has occurred") over every demo page. `notion-editor.js` now registers the never-throwing `tmNotionDb.isCoarsePointer` probe. The Notion E2E base additionally asserts `#blazor-error-ui` stays hidden after opening the editor and before every baseline capture (same guard as `SmokeLaneE2ETests`).
- **Fixed (NotionEditor, F-02):** the turn-into panel and the inline toolbar fill `var(--tm-bg-elevated)` (was the constant `--tm-color-white`), so their items stay readable in dark mode. A `NotionCssTokenTests` guard rejects a plain `--tm-color-white` background on any floating panel surface.
- **Changed (NotionEditor, F-03):** the aggregate-conflict banner buttons moved into their own second row — `.tm-notion-page__aggregate-actions` wraps the Reload/Reapply pair (`grid-column: 2`, flex row on desktop, stacked full-width under 640px) instead of the four-column grid squeezing them beside the message; the retry buttons gain padding, border and radius.
- **Fixed (NotionEditor demo API, F-04/F-05 root cause):** `IFieldConfig` and `IDatabaseViewConfig` are empty marker interfaces — the demo API serialized every field/view config as `{}`, so the WASM client received no Select/Status options and the table, board, gallery and record detail rendered empty chips. `Tempo.Blazor.Demo.Api` now registers a serialize-only `MarkerInterfaceJsonConverter<T>` that writes the runtime type's payload; the WASM client deserializes it through the existing per-type readers. Hosts with their own API are unaffected (the client readers already handle both shapes).
- **Fixed (NotionEditor database, F-04/F-05):** record field values delivered as `JsonElement` (a host that skips normalization) render in the record detail and the table — Select/Status unwrap a JSON string, MultiSelect enumerates a JSON array. The MultiSelect table cell also renders its chips in read mode (the chip list used to read the empty edit draft until the user started editing) and accepts an `object[]` (the shape the demo client's normalizer produces). Table row height is unified through the new `--tm-notion-db-row-height` token (default 44px): every `.tm-dbt__cell` is `height: var(--tm-dbt-row-height); box-sizing: border-box`, so cell content can no longer stretch a row past its siblings.
- **Changed (NotionEditor database, F-06):** the record detail and field editor modal footers wrap, and under 480px stack full-width (destructive group and primary action each on their own line) instead of overflowing the modal.
- **Changed (NotionEditor, F-08):** the AI panel in the sheet presentation hides its internal header (the core sheet already provides title + Done), gains `padding-inline: var(--tm-space-4)`, scrolls its mode tabs horizontally, and stretches the primary Run/Accept action full-width in the sticky footer.
- **Changed (NotionEditor, F-09):** page search is a `TmModal Size=Large` (results capped at `min(22rem, 80dvh)`) and the result hierarchy is fixed — the title renders `--tm-font-size-md` semibold, the path/meta `--tm-font-size-sm` secondary (they inherited the default size before).
- **Changed (NotionEditor database, F-10):** the timeline opens on the record nearest to today instead of a today-centred window, a mobile layout renders the record list (`[data-testid=notion-db-timeline-mobile-list]`) under the axis, and the period navigation is icon-only (`‹ ›`, the accessible name stays on `aria-label`) on mobile.
- **Changed (NotionEditor database, F-11):** on a mobile layout a calendar event is a colour dot (`.tm-dbcal--mobile` hides the clipped label); tapping the day opens the day sheet with the full record list.
- **Changed (NotionEditor, F-12/F-14):** the block-menu colour submenu swatches are 28px (44px on a coarse pointer) with the group label on its own row and an `aria-label` naming each colour, and **Delete moved to the end of the block context menu** (after a separator) — the first item / initial focus is the non-destructive Duplicate, so Enter right after opening can no longer delete the block.
- **Changed (NotionEditor, F-13):** the mobile history preview keeps one action set — the preview toolbar renders no Compare/Restore under 639px (the footer owns them) and the disabled primary dims through `--tm-opacity-disabled`.
- **Changed (NotionEditor, F-15/F-16):** the inline-toolbar turn-into panel items reuse the slash-menu SVG icons, and the top bar differentiates Blog (`file-text`) from Reading mode (`book-open`) and shows text labels (Blog / Analytics / Reading) through the existing `ToolbarLabels.Auto`.
- **Changed (NotionEditor, F-17–F-23):** the database view tabs no longer wrap (`white-space: nowrap`); the restrictions dialog names the mode select after its heading (the duplicated label is gone) and stacks the add row under 480px; the text-comment panel aligns its header/quote inset to `--tm-space-4` and its dialog Close is a ghost button; the page-comment panel hides the inline Reply on the last entry (`HideReplyOnLastEntry`, the thread footer keeps the one Reply action); the emoji picker puts Remove icon on its own row under 480px; the template gallery footer Close gains `padding: var(--tm-space-3) var(--tm-space-4)`.
- **Changed (NotionEditor E2E captures, F-23):** phone-band template and shortcuts captures are viewport screenshots (`FullPage=false`) — a region capture used to show the page below the fullscreen sheet.
- **Fixed (NotionEditor database dates):** a due date stored as an ISO string (the demo API round-trips `DateTime` as text) now formats through `NotionDatabaseValueFormatter` with the current culture. Board, gallery and list cards, and the table date cell, show the culture short date (`d`, or `g` when the field includes time) instead of `2026-06-23T12:00:00Z`. A non-date string is unchanged. An explicit `DateFieldConfig.DateFormat` still wins.
- **Fixed (core `TmNotificationToastContainer`):** a failed unread-count or toast load is logged and ignored. It no longer becomes an unhandled exception and the fixed Blazor error bar over the host page.
- **Fixed (core `TmToolbar`): a collapsed overflow copy no longer widens `scrollWidth`.** `.tm-toolbar-item--collapsed` is `position: fixed` (was `absolute`). An absolute copy is contained by the nearest `transform` / `filter` / `will-change` ancestor, and Chromium still counts it in the toolbar's `scrollWidth` — `overflow: clip` does not stop that. `offsetWidth`, which the fit measures, is unchanged, and the More menu is not clipped. Hosts that asserted `getComputedStyle(collapsed).position === "absolute"` must expect `"fixed"`.
- **Added (core `TmToolbar`): `IsInMenu` / `MoreButton`.** Additive exceptions the NotionEditor redesign rides. `IsInMenu(elementId)` reports whether the item carrying that `data-tm-toolbar-item` id currently renders only inside the "More" menu — a panel opened from such an item returns focus to `MoreButton` (the collapsed bar copy is inert); `MoreButton` exposes the rendered "More" trigger element, empty when no menu renders. No behavior change for existing hosts.
- **Added (core `TmToolbarButton`): `KeepMenuOpen`, `Element`, public `MenuId`.** Additive. `KeepMenuOpen` maps onto the "More" menu entry (the menu stays open after the action — a host that opens a second surface above it wins); `Element` exposes the bar button element; `MenuId` (the stable `data-tm-toolbar-item` id the fit measurement reports back) is now public. Existing buttons compile and render unchanged.
- **Changed (core `TmToolbar`): a measured `maxVisible` of 0 is stored as -1.** Behavior note: `tm-toolbar.js` reports 0 when nothing fits (not even a pin). The toolbar normalizes that report to -1 before partitioning, so the shared `ActionOverflowLayout` below-one clamp governs — at least one Auto button stays on the bar and a Pinned button always stays; a measured zero never produces an all-menu Auto bar. Positive measurements are unchanged; no host-visible change beyond the previously unstable zero case.
- **Added (core `ActionOverflowMenu`): `Trigger` element.** Additive exception: the rendered trigger button element is exposed (the toolbar hands it to hosts as `TmToolbar.MoreButton`). Existing call sites are unaffected.
- **Added (core `TmOverlayPanel`): `InitialFocusSelector`.** Additive exception: a trapped popover names its first-focus element (CSS selector, scoped to the panel) — a menu whose `role` lives on an inner element passes its first item so a nested submenu cannot win the initial move. Null keeps the focus-scope default (the first focusable). The sheet presentation already had `SheetInitialFocusSelector`; this is the popover-side counterpart.
- **Changed (core `ViewportProbe` / `layout-observer.js`): the viewport scope measures the window.** A `TmLayoutObserver` with `IsViewportScope=true` (or the internal probe an overlay opens when no viewport scope cascades) now measures `window.innerWidth` instead of its own zero-content box, so the first classification is not stuck on an unreadable probe box. Content-scoped observers still measure their own container.
- **Fixed (core `tm-sheet.js`): stopping a sheet drops the stored viewport.** A tracked sheet root no longer keeps the stale `--tm-sheet-viewport` length after its tracking stops, so a later band or host is not clipped by it (covered by the overlay node-test lane).
- **Added (core `TmLayoutContext`): `IsCoarsePointer`.** Additive. A cascaded context now also carries whether the primary pointer is coarse (`matchMedia('(pointer: coarse)')`), independent of the width band. `TmLayoutObserver` reports it through `layout-observer.js` when the query flips (never from `pointermove`) and stamps `data-pointer="coarse|fine"` on its root; a forced observer does not measure and inherits the ancestor's signal. False until a report arrives, so existing hosts keep today's fine-pointer reading. `CommentPresentation=Auto` opens the comment dialog/sheet on a coarse pointer even at a desktop width; `Popover` still pins the bubble. **Before → After:** the `TmLayoutObserver` root carried no pointer signal → it now always stamps `data-pointer="coarse|fine"` on its root (`fine` until the first report arrives).
- **NotionEditor redesign (phases 1–9), consolidated.** The editor is a `TmEditorShell`: `LayoutMode` (`Auto`, desktop ≥ 1024 / tablet 640–1023 / mobile < 640 of the editor container), `Chrome` (`Full` / `Minimal` / `None`), `InspectorContent` (null renders no right region), `ShellPanelPresentation` (`Overlay` default, `Main` replaces the page) and `CommentPresentation` (`Auto` default: popover on desktop, `TmModal` on touch/narrow). The contract, frozen `data-testid`s and `data-tm-group` values live in [docs/notion-editor.md](docs/notion-editor.md). Each breaking item below already has its before/after; the index is the map.

### NotionEditor 2.10.0 — Breaking / Migration index

| Change | Before | After | Detail |
|---|---|---|---|
| Palette aliases | `--tm-notion-option-*-bg/fg/solid`, `--tm-notion-color-*`, `--tm-notion-text-{color}`, `--tm-notion-bg-{color}`, `--tm-notion-border-width` | `--tm-notion-option-*-wash/ink/swatch`, `--tm-notion-option-text-*-ink/wash`, `--tm-border-width` | phase 10, below |
| Pickers | `Shared/TmNotionEmojiPicker`, `UI/TmNotionColorPicker` | `UI/TmNotionEmojiPicker`; the inline toolbar owns colour | phase 6 |
| Page comments | `TmNotionPageCommentSection` | `TmNotionPageCommentPanel` | phase 5 |
| Top bar DOM | flat `.tm-notion-topbar` buttons | `TmToolbar`, `data-tm-group` `navigation \| collaboration \| tools \| modes \| primary` | phase 3 |
| Dialogs and menus | package backdrops and z-index bands | core `TmModal` / `TmOverlayPanel` / `TmSidePanel` | phases 4, 6, 7 |
| Database toolbar | always-visible `.tm-db__tool-btn` row | `data-tm-group` `views \| tools \| primary`; compact tools live in More | phase 8 |
| Timeline classes | `.tm-dbt` / `.tm-dbt__*` | `.tm-dbtl` / `.tm-dbtl__*` (the table keeps `.tm-dbt`) | phase 9 |
| Comment default | bubble at every width | `CommentPresentation=Auto` (popover on a fine desktop pointer; dialog/sheet on a coarse pointer or a narrow layout) | phase 4 |
| History close / restore confirm | local `.tm-nph__close-btn`, `.tm-nph-confirm` | the core modal close (`.tm-nph-host .tm-modal-close`) and `TmDialog` (`[data-testid=notion-history-restore-confirm]`) | phase 7 |
| Spreadsheet edit footer | `.tm-notion-spreadsheet-edit-modal__footer` | the shared tempo footer `[data-testid=notion-tempo-modal-footer]` (Save/Discard classes unchanged) | phase 7 |
| Calendar week | always Monday | `CultureInfo` `FirstDayOfWeek` | phase 9 |
| Bulk target | one click executed | two-step: select, then the footer confirms | phase 4 |
| Media insert | a pick inserted | a pick selects; Insert or a double-click confirms | phase 7 |
| History compare | click previewed and selected | click previews; the checkbox picks; Compare orders by `EditedAt` | phase 7 |
| Relative time | eight package keys | `TmRelativeTime.Resolve` and `TmRelativeTime_*` | phase 9 |

- **Breaking: NotionEditor history close, restore confirm, and spreadsheet edit footer (phase 11 hosts).** These DOM moves landed with the phase-7 shell; phase 11 is the migration hosts and tests must follow. `TmNotionPageHistory` and `TmNotionSpreadsheetEditModal` stay editor chrome — no wireframe stencil and no new role.
  - **History close.** Before: a button inside the panel, `.tm-nph__close-btn`. After: the core `TmModal` header close, `button.tm-modal-close` under the overlay `.tm-nph-host`. The inner close is not rendered.
  - **Restore confirm.** Before: a box inside the panel, `.tm-nph-confirm`, confirmed by a local OK control. After: a sibling `TmDialog` (`[data-testid=notion-history-restore-confirm]`); confirm is `button.tm-dialog-btn-ok` inside that dialog, not inside `.tm-nph`.
  - **Spreadsheet edit footer.** Before: `.tm-notion-spreadsheet-edit-modal__footer` inside the editor body. After: the shared tempo footer `[data-testid=notion-tempo-modal-footer]` on the modal overlay. Save and Discard keep `.tm-notion-spreadsheet-edit-modal__btn--primary` and `__btn--discard`.

- **Breaking: NotionEditor palette aliases removed (phase 10).** The "remove by Fáze 10" aliases and their dark-theme copies are gone. A host stylesheet that named one now names the canonical token.
  - **Before:** `color: var(--tm-notion-color-red); background: var(--tm-notion-bg-red); border-width: var(--tm-notion-border-width);`
  - **After:** `color: var(--tm-notion-option-text-red-ink); background: var(--tm-notion-option-text-red-wash); border-width: var(--tm-border-width);`
  - Chip roles: `--tm-notion-option-{color}-wash` / `-ink` / `-swatch` (was `-bg` / `-fg` / `-solid`). `{color}` is `gray | red | orange | yellow | green | blue | purple | pink | brown`.

- **Breaking: NotionEditor database board, calendar and timeline (phase 9).**
  - **Timeline classes.** Before: the timeline root and its children shared the table prefix (`.tm-dbt`, `.tm-dbt__zoom-group`, `.tm-dbt__gantt`, `.tm-dbt__bar`, `.tm-dbt__bar-resize`). After: the timeline is `.tm-dbtl` and every timeline child is `.tm-dbtl__*` (`.tm-dbtl__zoom-group`, `.tm-dbtl__gantt`, `.tm-dbtl__bar`, `.tm-dbtl__bar-resize`). The table keeps `.tm-dbt` / `.tm-dbt__*`. A drag adds `.tm-dbtl--dragging` (was `.tm-dbt--dragging`).
  - **Calendar week start.** Before: the grid always started on Monday. After: it follows `CultureInfo.CurrentCulture.DateTimeFormat.FirstDayOfWeek` (en-US Sunday, cs-CZ Monday). To keep Monday under an en-US UI, set the current culture's `DateTimeFormat.FirstDayOfWeek = DayOfWeek.Monday` before the view renders.
  - **Timeline drag.** Before: a bar moved on `mousedown` / `mousemove` through a full-screen overlay, and every move re-rendered the component. After: move and resize go through the shared `pointer-drag.js` (500 ms long-press on touch, no Blazor render on `pointermove`). Alt+Arrow moves the bar one unit; Alt+Shift+Arrow resizes it. On a mobile layout a tap opens the date sheet instead of dragging.
  - **Relative time.** Before: notifications, recent pages, trash and the block comment tooltip each formatted time themselves (`Notion_Notifications_JustNow` / `MinutesAgo` / `HoursAgo` / `DaysAgo`, `TmNotionSidebarRecent_JustNow` / `MinutesAgo` / `HoursAgo` / `DaysAgo`). After: all four use `TmRelativeTime.Resolve` and those eight keys are removed. A host that overrode them should override the shared `TmRelativeTime_*` family instead. The absolute moment is on `<time datetime>` and in `title`.
  - **Counts.** Before: "+N more" and the timeline footer were one neutral string. After: `Loc.Plural` (`TmNotionDbCalendarView_More_One/_Few/_Many/_Other`, `TmNotionDbTimelineView_RecordCount_*`). A host override of the bare `TmNotionDbCalendarView_More` key still works as the fallback.
- **Breaking: NotionEditor database toolbar (phase 8).** The database toolbar is now the core `TmToolbar` (`Overflow=Menu`), not a hand-rolled row of buttons.
  - **DOM before:** a flat row of `.tm-db__tool-btn` buttons, every tool always visible, and `.tm-db__view-tabs` on every width.
  - **DOM after:** groups carry `data-tm-group` (`views | tools | primary`); each tool keeps `.tm-db__tool-btn`, `data-tool` and `data-testid`. On a compact layout the secondary tools (group, sub-items, properties, open-as-page, import/export) render only inside the toolbar "More" menu. On mobile the view tabs are replaced by `[data-testid=notion-db-view-switch]`. When a database has more than four views, the rest sit behind `[data-testid=notion-db-more-views]` ("More views") instead of a fifth tab. Hosts key off `data-tool` / `data-testid`, never a positional selector.
- **NotionEditor database phase-8 review.** List rows are `role="list"` / `role="listitem"` (a row activates the record; it is not a listbox option). `TmNotionDbTableView.CoarsePointer` is now the cascaded mobile layout OR a one-shot `matchMedia('(pointer: coarse)')` probe, and `@media (pointer: coarse)` hides `.tm-dbt__resize-handle`. The table row menu stays; a Select/Status cell renders its chip at `--tm-dbt-row-height` (short 36px, medium 44px, tall 72px — was 28/40/64, so a chip no longer clips).
  - **Before:** a list row was `role="option"` inside `role="listbox"`; row height was a `max-height` of 28/40/64px; `CoarsePointer` was true only on the mobile layout.
  - **After:** the same row is a list item; the medium row is 44px; a coarse pointer on a desktop layout also drops header drag and the resize handle.
- **NotionEditor database phase 8: shared value renderer, search, responsive views.** `TmNotionDbPropertyValue` is the one read-only renderer: a Select/Status/MultiSelect reads as a colored pill, a person as initials, a checked checkbox as a check, and an empty value as nothing — Board, Gallery and List no longer format their own text. `ShowSearch` (default off) filters the records already loaded and warns when more pages exist (the provider contract is unchanged). `IsPage` (default false) is what shows the mobile action bar; an inline block keeps the compact toolbar. `LayoutMode` (default `Auto`) follows the cascaded layout. A coarse pointer disables the table header drag and the column resize handle; column order then changes from the Properties panel.
  - **Before:** `<TmNotionDatabaseBlock Block="..." />` rendered plain text for every field value and had no search field.
  - **After:** the same call is unchanged (`ShowSearch` off, `IsPage` false, `LayoutMode=Auto`). The editor passes `ShowSearch="true"`, so a database block inside `TmNotionEditor` shows the search field; a host that embeds the block directly and wants search passes `ShowSearch="true"`. A database that fills the page passes `IsPage="true"`. Column order moves with the Properties panel up/down buttons (`ReorderFieldsAsync`); a coarse pointer no longer drags the header.

- **Breaking: NotionEditor phase-7 dialogs.** Four contracts changed.
  - **Media insert is two-step on every tab.** Before: picking a file or confirming an embed URL inserted immediately, and Enter on a library option both selected and confirmed. After: a click only selects; Insert (or a double-click) confirms, and Enter is not emulated on the native option buttons. A coarse pointer gets a "Choose file" label, the supported formats, and a preview of the selected file.
  - **History compare is an explicit pick.** Before: clicking a version both previewed and selected it, and Compare used the pick order. After: a click only previews; the checkbox and Space pick, and Compare orders the pair by `EditedAt` (older first). The footer is Secondary Compare, Primary Restore, then Back with an icon. Mobile is list, then preview, then Back, and offers no side-by-side diff.
  - **AI menu.** Before: the modes were plain buttons, Accept was always primary, and the menu never sheeted on mobile. After: the modes are a `tablist` (`aria-selected`, `aria-controls`, arrow keys, Home/End, focus follows the selection), Accept is primary only once a result exists, and on mobile the menu is a bottom sheet with a sticky footer.
  - **Tempo edit modals.** Before: each modal owned its footer and a dirty Discard closed immediately. After: the three modals share an internal `TmNotionTempoEditorModal` (not published) with Discard then Save; a dirty Discard or Escape opens a confirm and does not close until it is confirmed.
- **Breaking: `TmNotionShareDialog.ConfirmRevoke` defaults to true.** Before: omitting it revoked an active link on the first click. After: the first click asks, and a host that wants the old one-click revoke passes `ConfirmRevoke="false"`.
- **NotionEditor phase 7: share, restrictions, history, media, AI, Tempo edit modals.** Share, restrictions and history ride `TmModal` (Escape closes; revoke confirms before the provider call; restrictions keep the footer outside the scroll). History on mobile is list then preview with Back. The AI menu modes are a `tablist` (`aria-selected`, arrow keys); Accept is primary only after a result, and Copy calls `tmNotionEditor.copyToClipboard`. Diagram, Spreadsheet and Wireframe edit modals share `TmNotionTempoEditorModal`: fullscreen, header title + ×, footer Discard then Save, dirty discard confirms first, a missing package disables Save. The embedded editor resolves its own container (`LayoutMode=Auto`), so a narrow panel gets that editor's mobile chrome.
  - **Before:** each Tempo edit modal owned its own footer and a custom loading spinner; a dirty Discard closed immediately; the AI modes were plain buttons and Accept was always primary.
  - **After:** the three modals render `TmNotionTempoEditorModal` (`data-testid="notion-tempo-modal-discard"` / `notion-tempo-modal-save`). Legacy classes (`tm-notion-diagram-edit-modal__btn--primary`, `tm-notion-spreadsheet-edit-modal__btn--discard`, the wireframe equivalents, and the `__loading` status classes) still ride the same elements. A dirty Discard opens `data-testid="notion-tempo-modal-discard-confirm"` and does not close until that confirm.
- **NotionEditor phase-5 UX.** The notification sheet keeps its visible title; filter and Mark-all buttons, My Tasks filter pills and the audit chevron grow to `--tm-touch-target` on a coarse pointer. The audit chevron is labelled "Details for {0} {1}". Resolved comment threads no longer dim the whole card: the Resolved label uses `--tm-color-success-text` and the actions use `--tm-text-secondary`. The analytics chart axis labels use `--tm-font-size-xs` and short `M/d` labels so the last tick is not clipped.
- **Drawer popover box.** A modal `TmDrawer` root is a top-layer popover. The UA reset (`:where(.tm-drawer[popover])`) sets `inset`/`width`/`height` to `auto`, so a side sheet and a bottom sheet had no box: the panel's `height: 100%` resolved against auto and the slide-in finished off-screen. `.tm-drawer[popover].tm-drawer--right|left|bottom` now pins `inset: 0` and `max-block-size: 100dvh`. The panel animation and transform are unchanged. `.tm-drawer__body` scrolls (`overflow: auto`, `min-block-size: 0`). Hosts must not re-pin `.tm-drawer__panel` position, animation or transform.
- **Breaking: `TmNotionEditor` shell.** The editor root is now `TmEditorShell`. `LayoutMode` (`TmLayoutMode`, default `Auto`) resolves desktop, tablet and mobile from the editor container. `Chrome` is `Full` (default), `Minimal` or `None`. `InspectorContent` is an empty right-slot. Below desktop the sidebar is a drawer of the editor, not a viewport-fixed panel, and it starts closed. Floating menus (slash, emoji, color, type switcher, token, status) use the core overlay; the JS clamps `adjustSlashMenuPosition`, `adjustEmojiPickerPosition`, `adjustColorPickerPosition`, `adjustTypeSwitcherPosition` and `isNarrowViewport` are gone.
  - **Before:** `<TmNotionEditor DataProvider="..." />` always rendered the full top bar, and a narrow viewport pinned the sidebar to the window.
  - **After:** the same call is unchanged (`Chrome=Full`, `LayoutMode=Auto`). A public host passes `Chrome="NotionEditorChrome.Minimal"`. A host that needs no chrome passes `Chrome="NotionEditorChrome.None"`.
- **NotionEditor shell panels: one open panel, `ShellPanelPresentation`.** The Tasks / Blog / Analytics / Audit panels are single-state now (at most one open; opening another closes the first) and present through the new `ShellPanelPresentation` parameter: `Overlay` (default) rides the core `TmSidePanel` — docked next to the page on desktop, a side sheet on tablet, a full-height sheet on mobile — while the page stays mounted; `Main` keeps the pre-phase-3 hosting (the panel replaces the page in the main region). All four panels share `TmNotionPanelHeader` (h2 title, ×, Escape). The mobile action bar invokes the page's own actions (`NotionPageActions` through the cascaded context): Add block opens the slash menu at the focused/last block, Comments expands the page comments panel, Page settings opens the ⋯ menu; the bar's More sheet holds audit / blog / analytics / share / reading / presentation / watch with their `data-testid`s. With `ShowSidebar=false` and no `InspectorContent` the editor renders no left/right regions and no mobile bar.
  - **Before:** the four panels were four independent booleans rendering inline `--main` asides; the mobile bar's Add/Comments were no-ops; Escape on the drawer was handled by the editor's own keydown.
  - **After:** one `_openShellPanel`, the core overlay/sheet owns drawer Escape, focus return and close; the bar delegates to the page.
- **NotionEditor canvas remount on the mobile band (accepted).** The core `TmEditorShell` renders a different DOM branch on the mobile layout, so the canvas subtree remounts when the layout crosses into the mobile band: open block UI (e.g. a spreadsheet edit modal) closes and per-page unsaved local edits are lost. Editor-level state (current page, navigation, aggregate session) survives — see decision `NOTION-EDITOR-SHELL-CANVAS-REMOUNT`. The inline formatting toolbar intentionally keeps its JS viewport clamp (`adjustInlineToolbarPosition`) instead of a core overlay anchor — see decision `NOTION-INLINE-TOOLBAR-SELECTION-CLAMP`.
- **NotionEditor phase-3 topbar DOM (hosts keying off the old bar, migrate).** The top bar is now ONE core `TmToolbar` (`Overflow="Menu"`, "More" for the entries the fit leaves out), not a hand-rolled flex row of `<button>`s.
  - **DOM before:** a flat `.tm-notion-topbar` row of bespoke icon buttons (`.tm-notion-header-btn`, …); every tool was always on the bar.
  - **DOM after:** `TmToolbar` groups carry `data-tm-group` (`navigation | collaboration | tools | modes | primary`); tool buttons wear `.tm-notion-topbar__tool`; on the tablet/mobile band Secondary tools render only inside the "More" menu — a collapsed bar copy keeps `data-testid` but is inert, the menu entry owns `data-menu-testid` (an `OverflowOnly` entry owns `data-testid` inside the menu). Tests click through the `ClickNotionCommand` helper or `[data-menu-testid]`, never positional selectors.
- **NotionEditor phase-3 sidebar: live, container-driven.** The page tree measures the editor's own container, not the viewport, and follows live resizes.
  - **Before:** the sidebar classified once from the viewport and a narrow window pinned it fixed over the page; a desktop browser at 1280 px with a host shell still docked it.
  - **After:** the same container breakpoints as the shell (desktop from 1024 px of the editor container); below that it is the editor's drawer (starts closed), and dragging the host split / resizing the window flips the presentation without a reload.
- **`TmNotionPublicPage` layout (phase 3).** The public page renders through the same container-driven shell contract: its header is the page header alone (no editor topbar), the width caps and paddings moved from the dead `.tm-notion-page-wrapper` rules onto `.tm-notion-main` custom properties, and the fullscreen presentation modifier is a root rule in the package stylesheet (a scoped single-segment selector could never match the child-component root).
  - **Before:** `.tm-notion-page-wrapper` carried `max-width`/padding; the public host overrode wrapper classes.
  - **After:** hosts size the component and pass `LayoutMode`; no wrapper classes exist to target.
- **NotionEditor phase-3 review batch B (UI polish, robustness, evidence).**
  - The topbar title keeps a readable `8ch` minimum with an ellipsis and hides on the mobile band (the page H1 already carries it); the toolbar's inline-end overflow dissolves into a `--tm-notion-topbar-bg` gradient instead of clipping into a dark block, and the core toolbar surface inside the bar reads as one bar in both themes.
  - `(pointer: coarse)`: the topbar icons, status-picker swatches and the Content-by-label "Add label" action reach `--tm-touch-target`; color-picker swatches now expose the localized colour name as their accessible name.
  - The mobile editor root no longer forces `100dvh` (it escapes a fixed-height host and breaks fullPage captures the same way) and the demo editor container went back to a viewport-independent height for the same reason.
  - The three `async void` event handlers (remote block change, collaboration cursor, notification change) fence their work: an exception escaping one used to take the whole circuit down.
  - The Server demo `_Host` gained the standard `#components-reconnect-modal`, so a transient SignalR blip reconnects instead of showing the fatal error banner.
  - New `NotionResponsiveShellE2ETests` (Smoke): desktop/1440 band checks, 1024-touch 44px targets, 390/320 no-horizontal-overflow, live resize 1440→800, a narrow-container host (`?stage=500` proves container-driven classification at a desktop viewport), the 1280 tablet drawer + More, and Escape closes the drawer/More overlay with focus returning to the trigger. Phase-3 screenshots (light + dark) for the shell bands, More sheet, hosted My Tasks, drawer, public page and the color/slash overlays land in `tests/Tempo.Blazor.E2E/__screenshots__/notion-*/phase-3/`.
  - **E2E migration note:** the shell UNMOUNTS a closed panel (the phase-2 `tm-notion-sidebar--hidden` / `tm-notion-sidebar-overlay` markup is gone); tests key off the panel being absent or carrying `--visible` instead.
- **`layout-observer.js` 0-width guard.** A transient 0-size `ResizeObserver` record no longer re-classifies the layout: Chromium reports degenerate 0-size content boxes for a frame while the viewport is re-emulated (a Playwright fullPage capture, print preview, a hidden→shown transition), and classifying one used to flip the whole shell to mobile — the editor canvas remounted and every open piece of UI state was lost. Records with a width below 1 px are ignored; the last good mode keeps standing.
- **`TmSidePanel.ShowHeader`.** Additive, default `true` (every existing panel is unchanged). A host whose content renders its own header passes `ShowHeader="false"` to opt out of the built-in header row: the docked panel and the sheet render no header title and no close button, and the accessible name falls back to the localized default. The NotionEditor shell panels use it in the `Overlay` presentation so the panel header is not duplicated.
- **`TmToolbar` collapsed item no longer steals clicks.** The copy a collapsed item leaves on the bar stays in the DOM at the inline start (its width keeps the fit measurement stable) but is now parked under the visible buttons with `z-index: -1` — it used to remain in the hit-test tree and swallow clicks aimed at the pinned button underneath.
- **`TmTextArea.FocusAsync()`** moves focus to the textarea (no-op until it has rendered). Additive; nothing existing changes.
- **`TmToggle.AriaDescribedBy`.** Additive. Rendered as `aria-describedby` on the inner `role="switch"` input, not on the wrapper. Null (the default) renders no attribute, so existing toggles are unchanged. A hint belongs here — splatting `aria-describedby` through `AdditionalAttributes` lands on the wrapper and does not describe the switch.
- **Comment entry model: `TmCommentEntry.IsInternal` and `Badges`.** Additive on `Tempo.Blazor.Abstractions`. `IsInternal` (default `false`) marks a comment the rendering component distinguishes visually; the component never hides internal content — the consumer or server filters it. `Badges` is a `List<TmCommentBadge>` (`Text`, `Tone`, optional `Icon` and `Title`); `TmCommentBadgeTone` is `Neutral`, `Info`, `Success`, `Warning`, `Danger`, `Accent`. `TmCommentEntry.IsValid` is unchanged.
- **`TmActivityComments` paints internal comments and consumer badges.** An internal entry gets `tm-comment-item--internal`, `data-internal="true"`, a warning wash from `--tm-comment-internal-bg` / `--tm-comment-internal-accent` (dark mode is the token override, not a component `[data-theme=dark]` block), and a lock `TmBadge` (`IconNames.Lock`, `TmActivityComments_InternalBadge` + `TmActivityComments_InternalBadgeTitle` in a `tm-sr-only` span, not an `aria-label`) — colour is not the only cue. Valid `Badges` render in `.tm-comment-meta` as subtle pill `TmBadge`s (`tm-comment-badge`, `data-badge-tone`). Tone mapping: Info/Success/Warning/Danger match `BadgeVariant` by name; **Neutral → Default** and **Accent → Primary** (`TmBadge` has no Accent variant; Primary is emphasis, not a status). Invalid badges (blank `Text`) are skipped. Every item now carries `data-comment-id` and `data-internal="true"|"false"`. No new animation, so no reduced-motion rule.
  - **DOM before:** `<li class="tm-comment-item">` and a meta row of author, time, and an optional `(edited)` span.
  - **DOM after:** the same `<li>` plus `data-comment-id` and `data-internal`. An internal entry also gets `tm-comment-item--internal`. When `IsInternal` is false and `Badges` is empty, the meta children are unchanged. An internal entry appends a warning `TmBadge.tm-comment-internal-label` (`IconNames.Lock` + localized text, with the title repeated in a `tm-sr-only` span) and is pulled back by `--tm-comment-internal-inset` so its avatar lines up with the thread. Each valid badge appends a `TmBadge` (`.tm-badge.tm-comment-badge`, capped by `--tm-comment-badge-max-width`) after that; a set `Title` is repeated in a `tm-sr-only` span, and a null `Badges` list renders nothing. `.tm-comment-meta` now wraps (`flex-wrap`) so a long badge or several badges stay inside the thread.
- **`TmActivityComments` composer mentions and internal switch.** Additive. `SupportsMentions` + `MentionProvider` pass through to the new-comment `TmRichEditorSimple` and the inline editor. Without a provider, `SupportsMentions=true` leaves autocomplete off (no exception, no empty picker). `ShowInternalToggle` (default false) adds a labelled `TmToggle` (`role="switch"`, `TmActivityComments_InternalToggle`) in the new-comment footer only; the inline editor never shows it. On paints `tm-comment-editor--internal` with the same `--tm-comment-internal-*` tokens as an internal comment, and a visually-hidden live region announces the mode. The switch is disabled while the post is in flight and resets to off after a successful post, cancel, or `DiscardDraftAsync`. `TmCommentDraftState` gains an optional `IsInternal` (default false; existing three-argument constructions are unchanged) — it is not part of the dirty decision. New `TmCommentSubmission(Html, IsInternal)` and `OnCommentSubmitted`. **Document order, pinned:** `OnCommentSubmitted`, then `OnCommentAdded`, same HTML. `OnCommentAdded` still fires and is unchanged. An edit does not raise `OnCommentSubmitted`. Effectively empty content raises neither.
  - **DOM before:** `.tm-comment-editor` with the editor and Submit / Cancel (or Save / Cancel).
  - **DOM after:** the same, plus `SupportsMentions`/`MentionProvider` on the editor when both are set. With `ShowInternalToggle`, the new-comment footer starts with `.tm-comment-internal-toggle` (a `TmToggle`) and a `tm-sr-only` hint; an internal composer also has `tm-comment-editor--internal`. No new `data-*` attribute.
- **`TmActivityComments.CommentActions`.** Optional `RenderFragment<TmCommentEntry>?`. Rendered after the built-in Edit and Delete buttons, inside `.tm-comment-actions`, wrapped by `.tm-comment-actions__custom`, once per comment with that entry. The consumer supplies the button and any confirmation dialog (the demo toggles internal/public through `TmDialog`, including the warning that notifications already sent cannot be recalled). The component does not interpret the fragment and never hides an internal comment. The actions row renders when the comment can be edited or deleted, or when the fragment is set; it is omitted when none of those apply, and it is hidden on the comment currently being edited (other comments keep theirs). The wrapper is not focusable and handles no keys, so tab order is unchanged — put a native button in the fragment.
  - **DOM before:** `.tm-comment-actions` rendered whenever the comment was not being edited, even with no Edit and no Delete button.
  - **DOM after:** the row renders only when `CanEdit`, `CanDelete`, or `CommentActions` applies. When `CommentActions` is set, a `<span class="tm-comment-actions__custom">` follows the built-in buttons and contains the fragment. No new `data-*` attribute.
- **Docs:** the stale `ICommentEntry` documentation overlay (the interface was removed in 2.0.0) is gone from the abstractions bundle, and `TmCommentReaction.IsValid` is documented as a property, not a field.
- **Comment surface passthrough.** `TmActivityLog` and `TmGanttTaskPanel` already owned the comment callbacks, so `CommentActions`, `SupportsMentions`, `MentionProvider`, `ShowInternalToggle` and `OnCommentSubmitted` are forwarded. Defaults stay off. The log raises the host callbacks in the same order as `TmActivityComments`. The task panel still posts one `TmCommentEntry` through its existing `OnCommentAdded`; `IsInternal` on that entry is the composer flag captured from `OnCommentSubmitted` (that callback fires first and does not post a second entry). Neither host hides an internal comment. `TmGantt` does not forward the new comment parameters yet; only a standalone `TmGanttTaskPanel` exposes them.
- **Wireframe:** `TmActivityComments` stencil states `showInternalComment`, `showBadges`, `showCustomActions`, `composerInternal` (all default false, so the pre-2.10 drawing is unchanged). Roles stay `list-view` and `text-area`.
- **Breaking: NotionEditor phase 4 — every page/sidebar/DB/block-text comment dialog on the core surface (N1 + N3 + DB-3 + P3).** No Notion dialog declares its own backdrop or z-index after this phase; all ride the core `TmModal` / `TmDialog` (centred dialog on desktop, `MobilePresentation=Auto` sheet on mobile) or the anchored `TmOverlayPanel` popover. Focus trap, Escape and focus return come from the core surface.
  - **Cover & icon dialogs (`TmNotionPageHeader`).** The cover dialog is a core `TmModal` (title, ×, footer Cancel/Set cover) and the preset grid is `auto-fill minmax(44px,1fr)` with a ✓ and `aria-pressed` on the current preset. The inline emoji picker is a titled `TmModal` ("Choose icon") instead of the anchored overlay popover.
    - **DOM before:** `.tm-notion-cover-dialog` + `.tm-notion-cover-dialog-backdrop` inline cards in the header; the picker was a `TmOverlayPanel` anchored at the icon.
    - **DOM after:** `.tm-modal-overlay` (core) — `.tm-notion-cover-dialog-backdrop` and the cover dialog's fixed positioning are gone; content classes (`.tm-notion-cover-dialog__input/__preset`, `.tm-notion-emoji-picker__*`) are kept.
  - **`TmNotionPageInfoPanel`.** Now a core `TmModal` (Small, sheet on mobile): the page title is the subtitle, users render through `TmAvatar` (image or initials fallback), facts and metrics carry lucide icons, the footer is a Close button. Escape raises `VisibleChanged(false)`.
    - **DOM before:** `.tm-page-info-backdrop` + a fixed `.tm-page-info` aside.
    - **DOM after:** the core overlay owns the surface; `.tm-page-info__*` content classes are kept.
  - **Sidebar bulk (`TmNotionPageTree`).** The bulk target picker is a core `TmModal` with a title naming the action and count ("Move pages (3) to…" / "Copy pages (3) to…", `TmNotionPageTree_BulkMoveTitle`/`_BulkCopyTitle`), an APG flat `role="listbox"` (`aria-level` per depth, roving tabindex) of the loaded pages with lazy children, and a two-step selection: a row click or Enter only marks `aria-selected="true"`, the sticky footer Cancel/Select (`notion-page-bulk-target-select`) is the ONLY confirmation path. Arrow keys move the selection (with DOM focus), Home/End jump to the ends, ArrowRight/ArrowLeft expand/collapse a node (the pointer caret is an aria-hidden affordance of the same action). Selected pages and their whole subtrees are excluded (a cycle is rejected in the UI). The bulk delete is a core danger `TmDialog` — Escape cancels and initial focus lands on Cancel.
    - **Behavior before:** one click on a target (or "Top level") executed immediately; the confirm was an inline card; Enter on a target confirmed; Arrow keys only moved an invisible selection.
    - **Behavior after:** two-step (`aria-selected` → "Select"); Enter SELECTS only — it never confirms (no double activation); the delete confirm is `.tm-dialog` — the `notion-page-bulk-delete-confirm-button` test id is gone, use `[data-testid="notion-page-bulk-delete-confirm"] .tm-dialog-btn-ok`. `TmNotionPageTree_BulkDeleteMessage` is now a PLURAL FAMILY read through `Loc.Plural` (`_One`/`_Other` in English, `_One`/`_Few`/`_Many`/`_Other` in Czech and Slovak, `_One`/`_Many`/`_Other` in French) — a host overriding the plain key must override the family forms (see [docs/localization-plurals.md](docs/localization-plurals.md)).
  - **`TmNotionSidebarTrash`.** Rows are cards with the page icon/emoji and the parent path resolved from the loaded tree (new `.tm-nst-item__path`); the inline confirm order is "Cancel | Yes, delete" (secondary first, destructive last); actions are permanently visible on coarse pointers with 44 px targets.
  - **Database dialogs (DB-3).** `TmNotionDbFieldEditor`, `TmNotionDbImportExport`, `TmNotionDbRecordDetail` and `TmNotionDbTemplateEditor` ride the core `TmModal` (record detail and template editor: Large dialog / fullscreen sheet via `AutoFullscreen`) with fixed footers — duplicate separated left, the destructive Delete separated from the confirm group, Ghost Close BEFORE the primary Save/Import/Export on the right; ReadOnly hides the destructive actions. The autosave surfaces (record detail, template editor, the properties panel) close through a localized **"Done"** (`TmNotionDb_Done`, Q9) — the footer button, × and Escape ALL commit a pending title/name edit first (Escape never blurs the textarea, so a typed-but-unblurred title used to be lost), then raise `OnClose`. While a property cell is being edited the dialogs set `CloseOnEscape=false`: Escape cancels the cell only; `notion-editor.js` marks a cell-edit Escape `tmEscapeHandled` in the window-capture phase so the enclosing trap cannot also close the dialog (the slash/mention/token menus are `TmOverlayPanel`s — overlay.js already consumes their Escape). The properties panel, the filter/sort/group bars and the template menu are anchored `TmOverlayPanel` popovers (sheet on mobile); the properties panel shows a subtitle, `TmToggle` visibility switches, the locked primary field and a sticky "Done" action. The Field editor's select options gained ↑/↓ reorder buttons (non-drag alternative, WCAG 2.5.7) and localized color names. Import/Export presents the mapping rows as cards under 600 px with a large "Choose file" target.
    - **DOM before:** `.tm-dbrd__overlay`, `.tm-dbte__overlay`, `.tm-dbie__overlay` fixed overlays with `z-index: var(--tm-z-modal)`; `.tm-db__panel` was an inline toolbar panel; the DB float/context menus carried `.tm-db__floatmenu-backdrop`/`.tm-db__ctx-backdrop` z-banded backdrops.
    - **DOM after:** the core `TmModal`/`TmOverlayPanel` owns every surface; those overlay/backdrop classes are gone (the menus keep a transparent fixed backdrop without a z-index claim). Content classes (`.tm-dbrd__*`, `.tm-dbte__*`, `.tm-dbie__*`, `.tm-dbfe__*`, `.tm-db__panel`, `.tm-db__floatmenu`, `.tm-db__ctx-menu`) are kept.
  - **Comment presentation (`CommentPresentation`, NO1).** New `TmNotionEditor.CommentPresentation` (`Popover | Dialog | Auto`, default `Auto`, cascaded through the editor context). `Auto` keeps the anchored popover bubble (`.tm-nbcp`/`.tm-ntcp`) on a desktop layout and opens the core `TmModal` on a touch or narrow (tablet / mobile) layout; `Dialog` always opens the modal. The block dialog is titled "Block comment (N)" with a footer Close; two or more threads on a wide dialog render master/detail (`tm-nbcp--split`, ≥720 px), a narrow dialog keeps one column with ← navigation. The text dialog is titled "Text comment" and shows the whole quote (clamped to four lines with a "Show full quote" toggle; the popover still truncates at 60 chars). The popovers ride the core `TmOverlayPanel` (browser top layer: Escape, outside click and anchor tracking) pinned to a zero-size fixed anchor span at the bubble position — no own backdrop, no z-index, no false `aria-modal`, and the card no longer claims `role="dialog"` inside the `TmModal` (the core focus scope is the dialog there).
    - **DOM before:** `.tm-nbcp-backdrop` / `.tm-ntcp-backdrop` + a host-computed fixed card at `z-index: var(--tm-z-popover)` with `aria-modal="true"`.
    - **DOM after:** a `.tm-nbcp-anchor` / `.tm-ntcp-anchor` zero-size fixed span + the core `TmOverlayPanel` popover (`role="dialog"`, top layer); the dialog/sheet is the core `TmModal`. All `tm-nbcp__*` / `tm-ntcp__*` content hooks are unchanged.
    - **Migration:** a host that needs the bubble at EVERY width (the pre-2.10 behaviour on touch devices) pins it: `<TmNotionEditor CommentPresentation="NotionCommentPresentation.Popover" />`.
  - **Localization.** New keys in all four tables: `TmNotionPageTree_BulkMoveTitle`/`_BulkCopyTitle`/`_BulkSelect`/`_BulkExpand`, `TmNotionComment_BlockDialogTitle`/`_TextDialogTitle`/`_ShowFullQuote`, `TmNotionDbFieldEditor_Color_*` (9 localized colour names), `TmNotionDbFieldEditor_MoveOptionUp`/`_MoveOptionDown`, `TmNotionDbTemplateEditor_EditTitle`, `TmNotionDbImportExport_ChooseFile`, `TmNotionDatabaseBlock_PropertiesSubtitle`, `TmNotionDatabaseBlock_FieldLocked`, `TmNotionDb_Done` ("Done" / "Hotovo" / "Hotovo" / "Terminé" — the autosave close action). `TmNotionPageTree_BulkDeleteMessage` became the plural family `TmNotionPageTree_BulkDeleteMessage_One/_Few/_Many/_Other` (see the bulk entry above).
  - **Docs:** `NotionCommentPresentation` enum overlay + the new `CommentPresentation`/`Presentation`/`Show` parameters documented; aggregates regenerated and `validate --fail-on-drift` is clean.


> 2.10.0 also ships every 2.9.1 entry below; when upgrading from 2.9.0 read both Breaking / Migration
> sections.
>
> Email template editor plan (`planning/tm-email-template-editor-2.10.md`). The full breaking-change
> summary is **B1–B17** in §3.11 of that document; a task-oriented before/after for every item is
> `docs/email-templates/MIGRATION-2.9-to-2.10.md` and the hosting contract is
> `docs/email-templates/HOSTING.md`.
>
> Editor-redesign follow-up (Modeling/DiagramEditor F9–F15b of the Modeling redesign plan). The
> follow-up is almost entirely ADDITIVE: the DiagramEditor embedded-viewer API (`ShowPageTabs`,
> `FitToViewAsync`/`FitOnDocumentLoad`, `ShowMobileZoomOverlay`, `MinimapInitiallyCollapsed` —
> Fáze 9), the Escape topmost-layer contract (Fáze 10), the `TmModal.HeaderActions` slot (Fáze 10),
> the issues filter/sort (Fáze 11), the `ParentId` tree hierarchy (Fáze 12) and the notation
> palette + preview legend (Fáze 15) all default to the previous behavior. The genuinely breaking
