  page. The formatting is cached on the payload strings, so the per-tick re-render of a streaming call does
  not re-parse unchanged JSON.
- **Accessibility** — exactly ONE live region per component: the card announces its status transition
  ("Search: Done") and the copy confirmation through one sibling `role="status"`, the panel announces the
  finished reasoning, the pill IS its own region. Disclosures are native buttons with `aria-expanded`;
  `aria-controls` is emitted **only while the region it names is rendered**, so a collapsed card, run or
  reasoning panel never carries a dangling id. Every action's accessible NAME carries the tool name
  (`TmToolCallCard_CopyFor` "Copy details of {0}", `_DetailsFor` "Details of {0}", `_RetryFor` "Retry {0}")
  — inside a grouped run the same three buttons repeat per card, and "Copy tool call" × N is not a usable
  list of buttons (WCAG 2.4.6); the Retry button keeps the short visible verb, which the accessible name
  still contains (WCAG 2.5.3), and it disables itself while the host's re-run is in flight so a double
  click cannot fire `OnRetry` twice. The payload `<pre>` blocks are `tabindex="0"` so a long JSON stays
  keyboard-scrollable, every control reaches the 44 px `--tm-touch-target` floor on a coarse pointer, both
  stylesheets carry a forced-colors block (focus rings and active states ride the system `Highlight` colour
  — a `Highlight`-coloured label over `Canvas` has no contrast guarantee — and the in-flight Retry, which
  `forced-color-adjust: none` pins to `CanvasText` like every other button, switches to the system
  `GrayText` so the disabled state survives the mode instead of looking enabled), and the shimmer/spinner
  pair has its `prefers-reduced-motion` block — under reduce the text stays and only the motion goes
  (`background-clip: text` is dropped so the label cannot vanish). The shimmer's gradient ENDS paint with
  `--tm-color-text-secondary`, the same ink that fallback settles on: the ends are what the reader sees for
  most of the sweep, so they cannot be the host-overridable muted alias. The spinner's two dimensions and
  its stroke come from `--tm-space-4` / `--tm-border-width`, never from a hardcoded `1rem` / `2px`.
- **Assets and strings** — `_content/Tempo.Blazor.AI/css/components/_ai-tool-call.css` and
  `_ai-thinking.css` (imported by the entry stylesheet, tokens only — no colour literal, no raw palette
  step, no `[data-theme]` block) and new keys `TmToolCallCard_*` (including the `_CopyFor` / `_DetailsFor` /
  `_RetryFor` accessible-name templates), `TmToolCallGroup_*`, `TmThinkingIndicator_*`,
  `TmReasoningPanel_*`, `TmAiDuration_*` in en/cs/sk/fr. No new JS: Copy reuses the existing
  `ai-message.js` `copyText`.
- **Verification** — `TmToolCallCardTests` (statuses, fake-clock ticking and stopping, disclosure wiring
  including the absent-`aria-controls`-while-collapsed contract, pretty-printed and invalid JSON, a payload
  arriving after the first render, redaction with its lock glyph, Copy including a refused clipboard write,
  Retry gating and its in-flight disable, the accessible names carrying the tool name, the single live
  region, Czech labels), `TmToolCallGroupTests` (summary segments, English and Czech
  plural wording, omitted duration while running, collapse, retry forwarding), `TmThinkingIndicatorTests`,
  `TmReasoningPanelTests`, `AiToolCallFormattingTests`, `TmToolCallCssTests` (class coverage, touch floor,
  forced colors, the system-colour focus ring, the `GrayText` disabled Retry, the shimmer endpoints pinned to
  the reduced-motion ink, the tokenised spinner, reduced-motion coverage), plus the
  extended `TmAiMessageTests` (grouping rules, retry plumbing, the streaming reasoning state). JSON
  documentation overlays for all four components,
  regenerated `tempo-blazor-ai.json` / `tempo-blazor-all.json`, `validate --fail-on-drift` clean. The
  code-behind moved to `TmAiMessage.razor.cs` to stay under the 1200-line ceiling; the roving action
  toolbar's mechanism stays in the `.razor` file `ToolbarRoleGuardTests` scans. `TmOverlayPanelDialogNamingTests`
  now registers the `TmAiMessage` renderer its sweep was missing, so the two dialog-role panels (source
  preview, feedback reason) are actually measured for WCAG 4.1.2 instead of being reported unmeasurable.

**No breaking changes** — new components, one additive `TmAiMessage` parameter and additive localization
keys. A host that bound `Message` keeps the same rendered turn; the tool-call and reasoning parts now
render richer content behind a disclosure instead of a one-line label.

### AI conversation package — `TmAiMessage` (plan 7f21f26b, phase 3)

One conversation turn as a component: the ordered parts through the safe markdown pipeline, citation
chips with a source preview, source cards, follow-up chips and the action toolbar. Contract:
[docs/ai-message.md](docs/ai-message.md).

- **`TmAiMessage`** (`Tempo.Blazor.Components.AI`) — `Message`, `ShowAvatar`, `ShowActions`,
  `ShowSources`, `ShowFollowUps`, `AvatarTemplate`, `ActionsTemplate`, `OnRegenerate`, `OnFeedback`,
  `OnFollowUp`, `OnCitationClick`, `OnRetry`, `ActiveVersionIndexChanged`, `ReadAloud`, `Class`
  (+ the inherited `DataTestId` / `TestIdPrefix`). The root carries the frozen `data-role`
  (`user`/`assistant`/`system`/`tool`) and `data-status` (`pending`/`streaming`/`completed`/`stopped`/
  `failed`) contract, and the user turn mirrors itself (`--user`, `flex-direction: row-reverse`) while
  its text stays left-aligned.
- **Actions** — copy sends the message's plain text (`AiMessageText.ToPlainText`, applied per text part,
  no markdown markers) and announces "Copied" through a sibling `role="status"` live region; regenerate,
  thumbs up/down and read-aloud render only when the host binds their handler (no dead buttons). A
  negative rating is raised immediately and again with the optional reason; the reason popover is
  dismissible and never required. Read aloud is opt-in (`ReadAloud`), feature-detected, and reports the
  end of an utterance back so the toggle returns to "Read aloud" by itself.
- **Model additions (Abstractions, still UI-free)** — `AiMessage.Versions` + `AiMessageVersion`,
  `AiMessage.ActiveVersionIndex` (**nullable; `null` = the newest version**, out-of-range values clamp
  through the new `EffectiveVersionIndex`), `AiMessage.ActiveParts` / `ActiveText`,
  `AiMessage.Feedback` + `AiFeedback` / `AiFeedbackRating`, `AiMessage.FollowUps`. `AiMessage.Sources`,
  `FindSource` and `ActiveText` follow the ACTIVE version; `Text` stays the live parts. The switcher
  shows the reader's choice immediately and the host's own index wins on the next change.
- **`AiMessageText.ToPlainText`** (`Tempo.Blazor.AI.Markdown`) — the plain-text projection behind copy
  and speech: markers dropped, block structure kept (one line per paragraph, list item, code line and
  table row), link/image targets never travel. It walks the SAME safe markdown pipeline as the
  renderer.
- **Accessibility** — the action bar is `role="toolbar"` with `aria-label`/`aria-orientation` and a
  roving tabindex (one computed tab stop, Arrow Left/Right/Up/Down with wrapping, Home/End, focus
  through `ElementReference.FocusAsync` — no second JS gesture module; see the decision
  `AI-MESSAGE-ACTION-BAR-ROVING`); the version switcher is a separate `role="group"`; a failed turn is
  a `role="alert"` block with Retry; the preview and reason popovers are the core `TmOverlayPanel`
  (`role="dialog"`, named, Escape + outside-click, `ConstrainHeight`) rendered as SIBLINGS of the
  toolbar so a keydown in the reason textarea never reaches the roving handler; every control reaches
  the 44 px `--tm-touch-target` floor on a coarse pointer; a forced-colors block covers the surfaces.
  **Focus order (review round)** — both popovers take focus INTO themselves from `OnOpened` (the
  preview on its Close button, the reason form on its textarea) and the reason form is a real modal
  dialog (`TrapFocus="true"`); closing hands focus back — the reason form restores the thumbs-down
  button and moves the roving tab stop with it, the preview returns to the citation chip that opened
  it (through the module's new `focusCitation`, because the chip lives in markdown-generated markup) —
  while an outside click deliberately does not pull focus back. The copy button keeps a stable
  accessible name (the confirmation travels through the live region) and the single live region now
  also announces the streaming → stopped transition.
- **Security** — the source-card and preview links pass through `AiMarkdownUrlPolicy`: a refused
  scheme is plain text (never an `href`), a surviving link gets `target="_blank"` with
  `rel="noopener noreferrer nofollow"`. Answer text still renders only through `TmMarkdownView`.
- **Assets** — `_content/Tempo.Blazor.AI/css/components/_ai-message.css` (imported by the entry
  stylesheet, tokens only, no animation of its own — the streaming caret stays the package's single
  reduced-motion subject) and the ES module `_content/Tempo.Blazor.AI/js/ai-message.js`
  (`copyText`, `isSpeechSupported`, `speak`, `stopSpeaking`; no `<script>` tag, no `unsafe-inline`).
  New localization keys `TmAiMessage_*` in en/cs/sk/fr.
- **Verification** — `TmAiMessageTests` (roles, parts order, states, citation preview, source cards,
  follow-ups), `TmAiMessageActionsTests` (toolbar roving model, copy, regenerate, versions, feedback,
  read aloud), `AiMessageVersioningTests`, `AiMessageTextTests` and `TmAiMessageCssTests` (class
  coverage, touch floor, forced colors, no package animation), next to the existing package gates.
- **Test-guard fix** — `ToolbarRoleGuardTests`' mechanism assertions had been dead code since a
  scripted edit wrote literal `\n` instead of newlines, so the whole block sat inside one line
  comment; it now runs through `ToolbarMechanismCheck` (per-mechanism findings) and is itself pinned
  on a synthetic toolbar that claims the role and ships nothing. `TmAiMessage` is allow-listed with
  the Blazor-owned mechanism, so the guard keeps rejecting a toolbar without one.

**No breaking changes** — new package surface and additive model members only. `Tempo.Blazor.AI` is
new in the unreleased 2.10.0, so no released consumer sees the model additions; a host that writes
`AiMessage.ActiveVersionIndex` keeps the explicit index it sets, and leaving it `null` keeps showing
the newest generation.

**Post-hoc verification round** (`TmAiMessage`, same plan) — four defects found while re-reading the
committed phase, fixed with tests and **no public API change**:

- **Copy and Read aloud keep the block boundary between text parts.** Both used to flatten
  `string.Concat(parts)` as ONE markdown document, so an answer with a tool call (or a reasoning panel)
  between two prose blocks copied as "Let me look that up.It is 20 °C." — two blocks glued into one
  sentence, with no space, let alone a paragraph break. The component now projects each `AiTextPart`
  through `AiMessageText.ToPlainText` and joins the blocks with a blank line, which is what the reader
  sees. Pinned by
  `TmAiMessageActionsTests.Copy_KeepsTheBlockBoundaryBetweenTextPartsSeparatedByAToolCall`.
- **The version count is announced as a phrase.** The switcher put `aria-label="Version 2 of 3"` on the
  visible `<span>2/3</span>`. A span is `role="generic"`, which prohibits author-provided names, so the
  label was dropped by the accessible-name computation and a screen reader read only "2/3". The visual
  short form is now `aria-hidden` and the full phrase renders as real text in a `.tm-sr-only` span next
  to it (the same utility the message's live region uses).
- **`ReadAloud` toggled after the first render now offers the action.** The `speechSynthesis` feature
  detect sat behind `if (!firstRender)`, so a host that turned the option on later (a reader preference,
  a settings switch) never got the button — a permanently quieter component instead of a feature
  detect. The probe now runs once, on whichever render first asks for it (`_speechProbed` still caps it
  at one round trip).
- **Forced colors: the system focus ring is restored inside every opted-out surface, and the user bubble
  is no longer opted out.** `forced-color-adjust: none` INHERITS, so the version buttons, Retry, the
  follow-up chip and the source card's link kept painting the theme token ring on a `Canvas` surface
  (they now go back to `Highlight`, the rule `_markdown-view.css`, `_ai-tool-call.css` and
  `_ai-thinking.css` already carried). The same inheritance made the user bubble's opt-out strip the
  system palette from the markdown it carries — its paragraphs, links and headings kept the theme's own
  text colour on a Canvas surface, i.e. dark text on black in a dark high-contrast scheme. The bubble
  needs no opt-out at all: its author background is remapped to `Canvas` anyway. Pinned by
  `TmAiMessageCssTests.ForcedColors_RestoreTheSystemFocusRingInsideTheOptedOutSurfaces` and
  `..._TheUserBubbleDoesNotOptItsContentOutOfTheSystemPalette`.

### AI conversation package — AI models and safe markdown (plan 7f21f26b, phase 2)

The package's first real surface: the generic message/streaming contract in
`Tempo.Blazor.Abstractions` and `TmMarkdownView`, the safe markdown renderer every AI component will
render answers through. Contract: [docs/ai-markdown.md](docs/ai-markdown.md).

- **Models (Abstractions, no UI dependency)** — `AiMessage`, the ordered parts
  (`AiTextPart`, `AiReasoningPart`, `AiToolCallPart`, `AiSourcesPart`), `AiSource`, `AiToolCall` and
  the `AiStreamDelta` hierarchy (`AiTextDelta`, `AiReasoningDelta`, `AiToolCallStarted/Updated/CompletedDelta`,
  `AiCitationAddedDelta`, `AiCompletedDelta`, `AiErrorDelta`) live in `Tempo.Blazor.Abstractions`
  (`Tempo.Blazor.AI.Models`), so a backend references the conversation records without Blazor or
  Markdig. `AiMessageStreamApplier` (`Tempo.Blazor.AI.Services`) folds a delta stream into a message as
  pure logic (the caller passes the timestamp) and reports whether anything changed; content that
  arrives after a terminal state is ignored and a re-delivered control delta is a no-op.
- **`TmMarkdownView`** (`Tempo.Blazor.Components.AI`) — `Markdown`, `CodeBlockTemplate`,
  `OnCitationClick`, `Class`. Rendered HTML is cached against the last input, so a parent re-render
  does not re-run Markdig.
- **`AiMarkdownRenderer`** (`Tempo.Blazor.AI.Markdown`, registered by `AddTempoBlazorAI()` through
  `TryAddSingleton`) — Markdig with raw HTML **disabled**, an explicit URL allowlist
  (http/https/mailto/relative; every other scheme, a protocol-relative target and control-character
  smuggling collapse to `#`), `target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer nofollow"` on every link and
  autolink, absolute-http(s)-only images, `cite:<id>` links rendered as citation chips, escaped code
  blocks with a copy affordance and a scrollable table wrapper. The extension set is built explicitly
  instead of `UseAdvancedExtensions()`, so `UseGenericAttributes` (attribute/event-handler injection)
  and the hosted-media embeds are not part of the pipeline.
- **Assets** — `_content/Tempo.Blazor.AI/css/components/_markdown-view.css` (tokens only) and the
  ES module `_content/Tempo.Blazor.AI/js/ai-markdown.js` (imported through `IJSObjectReference`, no
  `<script>` tag, no CSP `unsafe-inline`) that delegates the citation chips and the code-block copy
  button to the component. New localization keys `TmMarkdownView_*` (en/cs/sk/fr).
- **Security tests** — the whole shared vector set is rendered as markdown, as a link target and as an
  image target, plus a deterministic fuzz pass and a CSS token gate for the package stylesheet. The
  payloads now live in `tests/Shared/XssPayloads.cs`, which has **no sanitizer dependency**, so
  `Tempo.Blazor.Tests` links it without an `InternalsVisibleTo` into the email assemblies while the
  email test projects keep the same bytes through `SanitizerXssVectors` (that file adds the
  production-tokenizer assertions). A new assembly-level guard pins that the AI contracts live in the
  UI-free `Tempo.Blazor.Abstractions` assembly.
- **Review fixes (accessibility, contracts)** — the citation-chip hover painted `--tm-color-primary-50`,
  a light-only palette step with no dark counterpart, so the label lost contrast in the dark theme; it
  now mixes the semantic primary into `--tm-color-primary-subtle`, and
  `AiMarkdownViewCssTests.PackageCss_UsesNoRawPaletteSteps` keeps raw palette steps out of the package.
  The table wrapper is a keyboard focus stop and a **named region** (`TmMarkdownView_Table` in
  en/cs/sk/fr, `AiMarkdownRenderOptions.TableLabel`), the code `<pre>` takes `tabindex="0"` with a
  focus ring, the copy button announces through a **sibling** `role="status"` live region instead of
  renaming itself, and both the copy button and a citation chip get the 44 px `--tm-touch-target` floor
  on a coarse pointer. `CodeBlockTemplate` now documents that it must be a **stable reference** (cached
  field / method group) and that the host escapes `context.Code` (`HtmlEncoder`), and the render cache
  compares the delegate's `Method` and `Target` instead of the delegate instance. In
  `AiMessageStreamApplier`, a citation delta without a source or with an empty id is a **no-op** (not an
  exception) and an error delta after `Completed`/`Stopped` is ignored — the state machine is documented
  on `Apply`. Decision `AI-MARKDOWN-COPY-DELEGATED` records why the citation chips and the copy button
  are markup + ES-module delegation rather than Blazor components.
- **Post-hoc verification fix (forced colors)** — the `forced-colors` block opts the code card and the
  citation chip out of the system palette with `forced-color-adjust: none`, and that property is
  **inherited**, so it opted their **focus ring** out too: the citation chip, the copy button and the
  keyboard-scrollable `<pre>` (all three focus stops of an answer) kept painting the theme token ring on
  a `Canvas` surface. All three now paint `outline-color: Highlight`, the same rule
  `_ai-tool-call.css` and `_ai-thinking.css` already carry for their own controls, pinned by
  `AiMarkdownViewCssTests.ForcedColors_RestoreTheSystemFocusRing`. The link and the table wrapper are
  **not** opted out, so they keep following the system palette without a rule of their own.

**No breaking changes** — new package surface only; nothing in the core library or an existing
component changed. Hosts must load `_content/Tempo.Blazor.AI/css/tempo-blazor-ai.css` (already part of
the 2.10.0 AI package setup) and call `AddTempoBlazorAI()`, which now also registers
`AiMarkdownRenderer`.

### AI conversation package — scaffolding (plan 7f21f26b, phase 1)

New split package **`Tempo.Blazor.AI`** (`src/Tempo.Blazor.AI`, Razor SDK, net8.0/net9.0/net10.0)
for AI conversation UI. Phase 1 lands the package skeleton only; the components
(`TmMarkdownView`, `TmAiMessage`, `TmAiConversation`, `TmAiComposer`, `TmToolCallCard`,
`TmThinkingIndicator`, `TmReasoningPanel`) arrive in the follow-up phases of the same plan and the
demo page ships with them.

- **Registration** — `AddTempoBlazorAI()` (`Tempo.Blazor.Configuration.AIServiceCollectionExtensions`)
  calls `AddTempoBlazor()`, so it is idempotent next to an existing core registration.
  `AddTempoBlazorAll()` now includes it.
- **Package contract (planned)** — model and streaming contracts are planned for
  `Tempo.Blazor.Abstractions` (`Tempo.Blazor.AI.Models` / `Tempo.Blazor.AI.Services`, Fáze 2 of the
  same plan), which has zero UI dependencies, so a backend will be able to reference them without
  Blazor; phase 1 ships neither. The package references **no LLM SDK and no PromptHelper**; the
  host will supply the token stream. Markdig (BSD-2-Clause, pure managed, WebAssembly-safe) is
  already the only third-party dependency and becomes the processor behind the planned safe
  markdown pipeline.
- **Static assets** — `_content/Tempo.Blazor.AI/css/tempo-blazor-ai.css` is an `@import` manifest;
  the package ships no JS. The shared streaming caret (`.tm-ai-streaming`) and its
  `prefers-reduced-motion` block live in `css/components/_ai-streaming.css`.
- **Registration in the repo** — `TempoBlazor.slnx`, `eng/nuget-packages.txt`, `Tempo.Blazor.All`,
  the test project, `JsonDocumentation/packages.json` (bundle `tempo-blazor-ai.json`), the
  reduced-motion split-package sweep and all four demo hosts (WASM, Server, InteractiveAuto server
  and client).

**No breaking changes** — additive package, additive registration, no existing API touched. A host
that already links the core stylesheet gains one more `<link>` for the new package when it adopts
the AI components.

### Changed

- **`TmRichEditorSimple` / `MentionAutocomplete`: the mention list is a listbox the editor owns.** The content surface is a combobox only while the picker is open. The editor owns the list id (`{editorId}-mentions`) and computes `aria-activedescendant` from its highlight, so the first open already names option 0 — the dropdown no longer mints the id. Options carry `aria-selected`. An empty `@` query keeps the list open; a query with no match stays open on `.tm-rte-mention-empty` (`role="option"`, `aria-disabled="true"`, its own id). Display names wrap (`overflow-wrap: anywhere`). New key `TmRichEditor_MentionList` names the listbox. `TmRichEditorFull` still renders the same list and now keeps a no-match query open too.
  - **DOM before:** the dropdown had no role; its id was a random `tm-mention-list-*` owned by the dropdown; the content surface had no combobox attributes; a no-match query unmounted the list; names did not wrap.
  - **DOM after:** `[role=combobox][aria-expanded=true][aria-controls="{editorId}-mentions"][aria-activedescendant="{editorId}-mentions-option-N"][aria-autocomplete=list]` on `.tm-rte-editor-content`, and `[role=listbox][aria-label]` (key `TmRichEditor_MentionList`) on `.tm-rte-mention-dropdown`. Each `.tm-rte-mention-user` is `[role=option][aria-selected]`. The empty state is `[role=option][aria-disabled=true]`. In `TmRichEditorSimple` the list is a child of `.tm-rte-editor-content-wrapper` and opens under it (`inset-inline-start: 0; top: 100%`) instead of covering the toolbar.

### Signing redesign — plan summary (plan 1fba4858, phases 1–10)

`Tempo.Blazor.Signing` was rebuilt against the 22 reference screens in
`output/imagegen/tempo-reimagined/Tempo.Blazor.Signing/` (66 mockups). Binding decisions: **SI1**
every step input is a Tm component (date stays a native `<input type="date">`); **SI2** phone /
upload / external steps complete only when the host confirms them (opt-in; a bare click is not
proof); **SI3** `DefaultSignatureMode=Auto` starts Draw on a coarse pointer; **SI4** the field
list is the stepper; **SI5** geometry can be edited in px. The designer edits fully from the
tablet up (768 / 1200) and is viewing + light edits on a phone; the runner edits fully on a phone
inside a `TmDrawer` sheet. Contract: [docs/signing.md](docs/signing.md). Demo:
`/signing-from-editor` is one workspace (Edit → Place fields → Preview), `/signing-components`
shows `DocumentTitle`, `DefaultSignatureMode` and the active-steps host.

| Phase | Result |
|---|---|
| 1 | Container queries (640/768/1024/1280), token hygiene, `--tm-signing-role-1..6` (role 6 `#a16207`), dashed invalid field |
| 2 | ONE step panel (B25 — the hidden duplicate is gone), accessible names on every step input |
| 3 | Runner panel: titled header, permanent field list, action footer, completion hero; `DocumentTitle` |
| 4 | Steps on Tm components; number parses the field culture; 44 px targets |
| 5 | Runner sheet below 640; `LayoutMode`; `DefaultSignatureMode`; `signing-runner.js` |
| 6 | Active-steps host contract (OTP / upload / external) — opt-in, not proof without the host |
| 7 | Authoring panels (timeline, audit, share link, verification, comments) on the same chrome |
| 8 | Designer on `TmEditorShell`; pointer events replace mouse/HTML5 drag; inspector on Tm components |
| 9 | Runner sheet and comments panel on the shared `TmDrawer`; viewer pinch is opt-in |
| 10 | `/signing-from-editor` workspace, this summary, [docs/signing.md](docs/signing.md) |

Verification deviation (phase 10, recorded on request): the complete E2E suite was not run.
The gate that ran is the Signing set —
`FullyQualifiedName~Signing|PdfTemplateDesigner|ConditionBuilder|FormulaBuilder|RecipientRoleEditor|DocumentComments`
— plus the phase-10 captures (`TM_WRITE_BASELINES=1`).

Core additions that landed for this plan (all additive, defaults keep the old markup):

- `TmAlert.Role` — the alert role is host-settable.
- `TmSelect.SelectAttributes` — splat onto the native `<select>` (wins over the component's own).
- `TmCheckbox.InputAttributes` — splat onto the native checkbox; `aria-describedby` merges with the help id.
- `TmFileDropZone.InputAttributes` and `ShowFileList` (`false` hides the zone's own file list).
- `ButtonVariant.OutlinePrimary` — transparent fill, primary border and ink.
- `pointer-drag.js` `listenerCapture` — the drag listener captures, so a child cannot swallow the move.
- `TmContextMenu.Open()` / `IsOpenChanged` — the designer opens its one menu and hears it close.
- `TmTextArea.FocusAsync()` — moves focus to the textarea (no-op until it has rendered).
- `TmTextArea` sets `aria-invalid` from its own error and from a surrounding `TmFormField` error.
- `TmDropdown` sheet `min-height` — a phone sheet is tall enough to show its items.
- `IconNames.ShieldCheck` and `IconNames.MailX`.
- `TmMobileActionBar` renders `TmActionItem.TestId` as `data-testid` (markup change; see the `TestId` XML doc).
- `TmContextMenuItem.OnClick` is kept across close (the handler runs after the menu closes).
- `.tm-toolbar-btn--outline-primary` — transparent fill, primary border and ink on a toolbar button.

Breaking items, with the before/after, are indexed under **Breaking / Migration** below
(phases 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 7, 8, 9). Phases 6 and 10 add parameters only.

### Spreadsheet redesign — plan summary (plan 8959eebe, phases 1–8)

The `Tempo.Blazor.Spreadsheet` package was rebuilt against 57 reference mockups
(`output/imagegen/tempo-reimagined/Tempo.Blazor.Spreadsheet/`, gap analysis in
`output/imagegen/tempo-reimagined/analysis/spreadsheet.md`) under four binding decisions:

- **G2** — a phone is *viewing plus basic editing* (select, edit a value, scroll/zoom, basic format,
  filter); full editing starts at the tablet. Nothing below the tablet breakpoint is silently missing:
  the mobile command model simply does not contain the advanced tools, so the toolbar cannot re-offer
  them.
- **G6** — all 14 dialogs ride the core `TmModal` (phone: bottom sheet / fullscreen panel, focus trap,
  Escape, focus back to the grid); Find & Replace stays non-modal on purpose.
- **SP1** — grid density is a RENDER scale (`Density`, `Auto|Compact|Comfortable`) driven by
  `(pointer: coarse)`; the workbook model and every XLSX value are untouched.
- **SP2/SP3/SP4** — no Layout/Review/Formulas tabs, the document header is opt-in
  (`ShowHeader`/`Title`/`HeaderStart`/`HeaderActions`) and takes over the file actions, the formula bar
  carries ✓/✗ and the grid-line toggle.

Per phase (each entry below carries its own breaking-change contract):

| Phase | Result |
|---|---|
| 1 | Name Manager / Named Range Edit / Hyperlink / Insert Image wrapped in the core `TmFocusScope`; new `TmSpreadsheetValidationAlert` (alertdialog); roving tabindex in the Format Cells listbox and the Name Manager rows |
| 2 | Component tokens on `.tm-spreadsheet`, token-only package CSS, the canvas palette built from tokens (light/dark/indigo), active row/column header highlight, `SpreadsheetDensity`, workspace vs flat chrome, `npm run test:spreadsheet` |
| 3 | Every dialog on the core `TmModal` with the phone presentation, focus trap and focus restore; `TmSpreadsheetInsertImageDialog`; core additive `MobilePresentation.AutoFullscreen`, `TmModal.RestoreFocus`/`DialogRole`/`AriaDescribedBy` |
| 4 | Dialog content and hierarchy follow the references (core inputs, phone cards for Sort/Name Manager, SVG border icons, validation card) |
| 5 | Ribbon v2 (Home/Insert/Data/View + labelled groups, frozen `data-tm-group`), the opt-in document header, the `fx` + ✓/✗ formula bar with the named-range list, sheet tabs with underline/close/overflow arrows |
| 6 | Container-driven responsive chrome (`TmLayoutObserver` + `TmLayoutMode`), the tablet two-row model on the core overflow toolbar, the phone compact row + core `TmMobileActionBar` + sheets |
| 7 / 7b / 7c / 7d | Canvas touch interaction on the shared core `pointer-drag.js`/`pointer-gesture.js` (tap, double-tap edit, long-press menu, pinch zoom, corner drops, touch fill handle, `touch-action: pan-x pan-y`), density gutters + header font scaling, the opaque dark active header and the live theme flip, geometry getters for E2E, the 320 px dialog pass, and the class-by-class regression gate that closed two real regressions |
| 8 | Documentation (this summary, `docs/spreadsheet.md`, `COMPONENTS.md`, the demo page), the full per-project test run, and the final UX review; the phone grid now keeps `--tm-spreadsheet-grid-min-height` in a host shorter than its chrome (the Notion edit modal at 568×320 used to show no rows at all) |

What a consumer must do (details and before/after in every "Spreadsheet redesign (phase N)" entry of
`### Breaking / Migration` below):

1. **Serve `_content/Tempo.Blazor/js/` alongside `_content/Tempo.Blazor.Spreadsheet/js/`.** The canvas
   dynamically imports the shared `pointer-drag.js` / `pointer-gesture.js`; without them the grid keeps
   its mouse path, logs one warning, and touch gestures are off. A per-file CSP hash must list
   `spreadsheet-canvas.js`, `pointer-drag.js` and `pointer-gesture.js`.
2. **Import the package bundle, or the package theme layer too.** `_spreadsheet.css` reads kernel tokens;
   the dark active header lives in `wwwroot/css/theme-spreadsheet-dark.css`, which the bundle
   (`tempo-blazor-spreadsheet.css`) imports. A host that imports individual component files must import
   that theme file as well.
3. **Key off the frozen contracts, never positional DOM.** `data-tm-tab`, `data-tm-group`,
   `data-command-id`, `data-toolbar-row`/`data-toolbar-layout`, `data-layout` and the `data-testid`s are
   the host surface; the internal chrome DOM (ribbon → compact rows → phone row) changes with the
   container width by design.
4. **Host a dialog overlay outside `.tm-spreadsheet__layout`.** That wrapper is an inline-size query
   container (`contain: layout`), so a `position: fixed` descendant would be trapped inside the card —
   the component's own dialogs and sheets are siblings for exactly this reason.

Evidence: the regression lanes (`eng/release-evidence/spreadsheet-lanes-20261030/`), the final
per-project run plus the PARTIAL full E2E lane (`eng/release-evidence/spreadsheet-final-20261030/` —
shard 1 of the eight class shards plus the isolated re-run of its failures; its `README.md` holds the UX
findings table and the per-leg results) and the two perf runs
(`eng/release-evidence/spreadsheet-perf-20261029/`).

**Open / unfinished, tracked in the plan's remaining tasks:**

- **The full E2E lane is not finished** (cd641f4a). The 8-shard run was stopped in shard 1 after 4 h 40 m
  because this box runs ~60–90 s per test under concurrent load (~20–25 h for the ~1500-test suite); the
  runner writes one TRX per shard at the END, so shard 1 produced no TRX. Resume on an idle box with
  that folder's `run-e2e-shards.sh <dir> 8` (add an `OnlyShard`
  list such as `8 3,5` to repeat single shards) and then summarise with `node e2e-summary.mjs <dir>`.
  What IS proven on this tree: the isolated re-run of shard 1's 16 failures (12 green) and a plan-area
  lane that is 4/4 green (the demo density switch, the 568×320 Notion modal, both wireframe-stencil
  captures).
- **`SpreadsheetE2ETests.Phase3_Dialogs_Tablet1024Touch_StayDialogs_WithTouchSizedTargets` is red**
  (f25a9d47), and the bisect puts it on the phase-6 container-driven chrome commit (`e0febc25`): phase 5
  (`b1a8fc10`) passes, phase 7c (`32305292`), phase 7d (`50aa7fbc`) and this tree all fail identically.
  Before phase 6 a 1024 px viewport resolved the DESKTOP chrome, so *Custom sort…* sat on the ribbon;
  from phase 6 the ~700 px demo container resolves the TABLET chrome, the command moves into the row's
  core `ActionOverflowMenu` "More" panel, and that panel is anchored BELOW its trigger — with the trigger
  near the bottom of the viewport its entries are painted outside the viewport and nothing scrolls a
  top-layer panel into view. The phase-7d lane evidence recorded this group green, so the regression
  slipped between that run and now. Not fixed here: the placement is core (shared with the diagram,
  wireframe and dashboard toolbars) and `e0febc25` is outside this phase's budget — a flip-up placement
  or the documented open-on-desktop-then-resize pattern in that one spec are the two candidates.
- **The wall-clock performance budget is *Inconclusive*** (12bc2afb, fcee0469, dc12ae21):
  `SpreadsheetPerformanceE2ETests.SelectionDrag_AB_WithinBudget` measured a rAF cadence swinging between
  ~5 and ~36 fps, so the 30 % IQR guard trips in both directions and the ratio sign flips between runs;
  the deterministic counters (one header paint per selection change, unchanged content paints) are green.
  It must be re-run on an idle machine or the dedicated perf lane (`scripts/run-e2e-perf.ps1`) before the
  ≤ +10 % budget is claimed.

### Breaking / Migration

- **NotionEditor phase 7: share, restrictions, history, media and Tempo edit modals ride core overlays (N8, N9, N11, N12).** Each dialog dropped its own backdrop and `z-index`. The public test ids stay. A host that styled `.tm-npsd-backdrop`, `.tm-nprd-backdrop`, `.tm-nph-backdrop` or `.tm-media-dialog-backdrop` now styles the core `.tm-modal-overlay`.

  ```razor
  @* before: a page-owned dialog *@
  <div class="tm-npsd-backdrop"></div>
  <div class="tm-npsd" role="dialog">…</div>

  @* after: the same content inside TmModal *@
  <TmModal Show="Visible" MobilePresentation="MobilePresentation.Sheet">
      <div class="tm-npsd">…</div>
  </TmModal>
  ```

  Share revoke confirms only when `ConfirmRevoke` is set. Page history hides side-by-side diff on a mobile layout and drills from the version list into the preview. The diagram, spreadsheet and wireframe edit modals put Discard before Save.

- **NotionEditor phase 5: `TmNotionPageCommentSection` removed; shell-panel DOM changed (N2, P4–P7).**

  ```razor
  @* before *@
  <TmNotionPageCommentSection PageId="@pageId" />
  <button class="tm-notion-load-error__retry tm-notion-load-error__retry--primary">Reload</button>
  <button class="tm-notion-load-error__retry">Keep mine</button>
  <div class="tm-notion-audit__list">…</div>
  <svg class="tm-chart tm-notion-analytics__sparkline"></svg>

  @* after *@
  <TmNotionPageCommentPanel PageId="@pageId" Mode="TmNotionPageCommentPanelMode.Embedded" />
  <button class="tm-notion-load-error__retry tm-notion-load-error__retry--primary">Reload</button>
  <button class="tm-notion-load-error__retry">Keep mine</button>
  <table class="tm-notion-audit__table">…</table>
  <TmChart />
  ```

  Hosts that want the dialog pass `PageCommentsPresentation="NotionPageCommentsPresentation.Dialog"` on `TmNotionEditor`. `ShowMeta` (default `false`) is the opt-in meta row. Audit cards replace the table below 640 px.

- **Notion editor (phase 2): stored colours are palette names, not hex.** A text or background colour picked in the editor is now one of `gray`, `red`, `orange`, `yellow`, `green`, `blue`, `purple`, `pink`, `brown` (or null for the default). The swatch paints from `--tm-notion-color-{name}` and `--tm-notion-color-{name}-bg`, so dark mode and the indigo theme recompute it. A document saved before 2.10.0 still renders: `NotionColorTokens.Name` maps the legacy hex to the same name at render time, and nothing rewrites the stored JSON.

  ```html
  <!-- before: the picker stored a hex on the block -->
  <span data-color="#e03e3e" data-bg="#fbe4e4">…</span>
  <!-- after: the picker stores the palette name; the old hex still renders -->
  <span data-color="red" data-bg="red">…</span>
  ```

- **Notion editor (phase 6, NO4): one emoji picker, no colour picker.** `Shared/TmNotionEmojiPicker` and `UI/TmNotionColorPicker` are deleted. The only emoji picker is `UI/TmNotionEmojiPicker`; the callout and the page header both use it. The inline toolbar's colour panel is the only palette. Since phase 10 it paints `--tm-notion-option-text-{color}-ink` / `-wash` — the `--tm-notion-color-*` aliases this note first named are gone (see the phase-10 token entry).

  ```razor
  @* before: the callout used the Shared picker *@
  <TmNotionEmojiPicker OnSelected="HandleEmojiSelectedAsync"
                        OnRemoved="HandleEmojiRemovedAsync"
                        ShowRemoveButton="true" />
  @* after: the UI picker, opened explicitly *@
  <TmNotionEmojiPicker Visible="true"
                        OnEmojiSelected="HandleEmojiSelectedAsync"
                        OnRemoved="HandleEmojiRemovedAsync"
                        ShowRemove="true" />
  ```

  A host that rendered `UI/TmNotionColorPicker` moves to the inline toolbar palette. `OnTextColorSelected` carries the palette token name (`"brown"`), never a hex; `applyInlineColor` still receives the allowlisted legacy hex.

  The accessible name of a text swatch is `TmNotionInlineToolbar_Color{Name}` and of a background swatch `TmNotionInlineToolbar_Color{Name}Bg` (en/cs/sk/fr). The dead `TmNotionColorPicker_*` keys, including `TmNotionColorPicker_TextColor` and `TmNotionColorPicker_BgColor`, are removed. A host that overrode a picker key must override the inline-toolbar key.

  | before | after |
  |---|---|
  | `OnSelected` | `OnEmojiSelected` |
  | `ShowRemoveButton` | `ShowRemove` |
  | (always open) | `Visible` |
  | — | `Inline`, `RecentEmojis`, `LayoutMode` |

  `TmNotionColorPicker` is gone. Before, a host rendered the picker and listened to `OnTextColorSelected`. After, the inline toolbar owns the palette.

  Removed DOM classes: emoji/color backdrops, `.tm-nsp__scrim`, `.tm-nsp__dialog`, `.tm-ntg__backdrop`, `.tm-nps-backdrop`. Page search, the template gallery and the shortcuts panel render inside `TmModal` (`tm-nps-host`, `tm-ntg-host`, `tm-nsp-host`). The gallery tablist is a group with `aria-pressed`. Avatars use `TmAvatar`.

  **Inline text colour is a hex on the wire, a token on the swatch.** `document.execCommand` does not keep a CSS colour name, so the toolbar paints `var(--tm-notion-option-text-{name}-ink)` and sends the allowlisted legacy hex from `NotionColorTokens.InlineHex(name, background)`. A host that called `applyInlineColor` with `"brown"` must send that hex; the stored span is unchanged.

  ```html
  <!-- before: the toolbar handed execCommand the palette name, which the browser dropped -->
  applyInlineColor('text', 'brown')
  <!-- after: the swatch still paints the token; the call carries the one allowlisted hex -->
  applyInlineColor('text', '#64473a')
  ```

  **Select, status and multi-select colours are option tokens.** A calendar event, a timeline bar and a list chip set `--event-color` / `--bar-color` / `--chip-color` to `var(--tm-notion-option-{name}-solid)` (a legacy hex maps through `NotionColorTokens.Name`; anything else is `var(--tm-color-primary)`). Chip text mixes that colour with `var(--tm-text-primary)`, not `var(--tm-bg-surface)`, so the ink stays AA in light mode. A table cell swatch stores the palette name and the cell paints `var(--tm-notion-color-{name}-bg)`.

  **Token names.** Every package stylesheet reads a core token. The removed aliases and the core token that replaced each one:

  | before | after |
  |---|---|
  | `--tm-accent` | `--tm-color-primary` |
  | `--tm-border` | `--tm-border-color` |
  | `--tm-text-2` | `--tm-text-secondary` |
  | `--tm-bg-2` | `--tm-bg-surface-secondary` |
  | `--tm-hover` | `--tm-color-surface-hover` |
  | `--tm-primary` | `--tm-color-primary` |
  | `--tm-green` | `--tm-color-success` |

  A `z-index` no longer carries a numeric fallback (`var(--tm-z-popover, 200)`, `1040`, `1000`, `1060`): the core token is defined, and the fallback was a second, wrong band. The shortcuts panel rides `--tm-z-modal`; the status picker rides `--tm-z-popover`.

  **Removed dead classes.** `.tm-notion-media-*` duplicates, the bookmark / embed / file-link / page-link copies that lived on the block sheet, the duplicated table rules and the status-chip CSS that had moved into the cell stylesheet. A host selecting those copies from the block sheet must use the component's own sheet.

  **Package CSS reads core tokens.** Database views, comment panels, menus, dialogs and the editor shell no longer fall back to a hex or to the undefined `--tm-accent` / `--tm-border` / `--tm-text-2` aliases. The only literals left are the data palettes in `_notion-variables.css` and `_notion-dark.css`, and every `--tm-notion-*` alias whose chain reaches a themed token is redeclared on `.tm-notion-editor`, so a nested `data-theme` recomputes it. The DOM and every `data-testid` are unchanged.

- **Notion editor (phase 1): behaviour and DOM.** Nothing was added to `INotionDatabaseProvider` or `INotionPublicShareProvider`.

  **Thread card body is a button.** The block-comment thread list item used to be a `div.tm-nbcp__thread-card` that also handled keydown, with nested resolve buttons. A button cannot contain a button, so the card stays a `div.tm-nbcp__thread-card` and its body is `button.tm-nbcp__thread-card__open`; the resolve actions stay a sibling `div.tm-nbcp__thread-card__actions`. Enter/Space selects the thread once, through the native button.

  ```html
  <!-- before -->
  <div class="tm-nbcp__thread-card" tabindex="0">…<button class="tm-nbcp__thread-card__action">…</button></div>
  <!-- after -->
  <div class="tm-nbcp__thread-card">
    <button type="button" class="tm-nbcp__thread-card__open">…</button>
    <div class="tm-nbcp__thread-card__actions"><button class="tm-nbcp__thread-card__action">…</button></div>
  </div>
  ```

  **Entry actions moved into a menu.** Reply stays an inline button (`data-testid="notion-comment-reply"`). Edit, Delete and Quote left the hover row and now live in the core `TmDropdown` (`data-testid="notion-comment-entry-menu"`, items `notion-comment-edit-menu` / `notion-comment-delete-menu` / `notion-comment-quote-menu`). A host that selected `.tm-nbcp__entry-action` for Edit or Delete must open the menu first.

  ```html
  <!-- before -->
  <button data-testid="notion-comment-edit" class="tm-nbcp__entry-action">Edit</button>
  <button data-testid="notion-comment-delete" class="tm-nbcp__entry-action">Delete</button>
  <!-- after -->
  <button data-testid="notion-comment-reply">Reply</button>
  <div data-testid="notion-comment-entry-menu" class="tm-dropdown-wrapper">…</div>
  ```

  **Audit panel close.** The shell rendered its own close button next to the panel's. The shell button is gone; the panel's own close button closes the panel through `OnClosed`.

  **Active public share is locked.** While a share is usable, Allow comments and the expiry date are disabled and a hint (`Notion_Share_LockedHint`) explains that revoking the link is how to change them. There is still no `UpdateShareAsync`.

  **Table column resize no longer re-renders per pointermove.** The live width is written to the header cell by `notion-db-column-resize.js` (it imports the shared `pointer-drag.js`; there is no second drag implementation) and `OnFieldResized` fires once, on pointerup. Alt+Arrow on the handle (`role="separator"`, `tabindex="0"`) is the non-drag alternative.

  **Smaller DOM additions, all additive:** the record detail shows a Delete button (`data-testid="notion-db-record-delete"`) only when `OnRecordDeleted` has a delegate, and confirms through `TmDialog`; the calendar "+N more" overflow is a button that opens a day list (`data-testid="notion-db-calendar-day-list"`); the table renders a record-count footer; an empty board group renders `tm-dbb__empty`. `TmNotionDbFieldEditor` and `TmNotionDbImportExport` suffix their `id`/`for`/`name` so two instances on one page no longer collide.

  **Fixed:** comment authors no longer stamp a hardcoded id — `CurrentUserId` is the author; the audit panel no longer renders a second close button next to its own; mention clicks are handled by the panel, not dropped; an active public share locks Allow comments and the expiry date and points at the hint with `aria-describedby`; the table column resize no longer re-renders per pointermove; the calendar "+N more" overflow opens the day list.

  **Added:** a database record can be deleted. The row ⋯ menu (`data-testid="notion-db-table-row-delete"`) and the record detail confirm through `TmDialog`, then raise `OnRecordDeleted`.

- **Comment surface (this release): no public-API break.** New parameters default off. Recorded DOM additions, not replacements: `data-comment-id` and `data-internal` on every `.tm-comment-item`; `tm-comment-item--internal` plus the lock badge when `IsInternal`; `data-badge-tone` pills when `Badges` has valid entries; `.tm-comment-actions__custom` when `CommentActions` is set; `.tm-comment-internal-toggle` and `tm-comment-editor--internal` when the composer switch is on. One behaviour change, already recorded above: an empty `.tm-comment-actions` row is no longer rendered when the comment has no edit, no delete and no `CommentActions`. `OnCommentAdded` is unchanged. `TmGantt` still raises `OnCommentAdded(TmCommentEntry)` once.

- **Signing redesign — breaking-change index (phases 1–9).** The full before/after for each item
  lives in the entry linked below. Nothing in phase 10 changes a public contract.

  | Item | Where |
  |---|---|
  | Container queries replace viewport `@media`; grid class moved to `__layout` / `__workspace-grid` | phase 1, Breaking / Migration |
  | Token fallbacks removed (`#fff`, `--tm-color-border`, sticky z-index) | phase 1, Breaking / Migration |
  | Role colour 6 default `#ca8a04` → `#a16207` (stored templates keep their hex) | phase 1, Breaking / Migration |
  | ONE step panel — `.tm-signing-form-runner__mobile-panel` and `data-mobile` are gone (B25) | phase 2, Breaking / Migration |
  | "Accessibility mode" toggle removed; the panel is one instance at every width | phase 3, Breaking / Migration |
  | Completion panel / footer DOM (hero, sticky action row, titled field list) | phase 3, Breaking / Migration |
  | Step inputs are Tm components; number is `type="text"` + culture parse (no `min`/`max`/`step` attrs) | phase 4, Breaking / Migration |
  | Sheet breakpoint 768 → 640; no knob for the old 768 sheet (`LayoutMode=Mobile` pins it) | phase 5, Breaking / Migration |
  | `DefaultSignatureMode=Auto` starts Draw on a coarse pointer (template format still wins) | phase 5, Breaking / Migration |
  | `MobileMode` is `[Obsolete]`; pin `LayoutMode` | phase 5, Breaking / Migration |
  | Authoring panel DOM rewritten (audit tables, role-editor cards, condition / formula / timeline) | phase 7, Breaking / Migration |
  | Designer pointer events replace `mousedown` / HTML5 drag; root is `TmEditorShell` | phase 8, Breaking / Migration |
  | Overlay callbacks take `TmSigningFieldOverlayPointerEventArgs` (was `MouseEventArgs`) | phase 8, Breaking / Migration |
  | Field inspector is built from Tm components (`TmSigningFieldEditorActions`, geometry section) | phase 8, Breaking / Migration |
  | Mobile runner sheet and comments panel are `TmDrawer`; viewer pager raises `PageRequested` | phase 9, Breaking / Migration |

- **Signing redesign (phase 9): the mobile runner sheet is the shared `TmDrawer`, the comments panel is a `TmDrawer` sheet, and the viewer / designer mobile chrome moved.** Hosts and tests that keyed off the phase-5 local sheet classes, the comments panel as an `aside`, or the viewer's old pager buttons must follow the new DOM. Public parameters are additive except where a selector assumed the old tree.

  **Runner sheet → `TmDrawer`.** Below 640px of the runner container the single step panel is no longer a CSS-positioned `aside`. It is hosted once inside a non-modal `TmDrawer` (`Position=Bottom`, `Modal=false`, `ShowHandle=false`) that shares the documents grid cell. The host is `position: sticky; inset-block-end: 0; height: 85dvh`, so the peek stays on the viewport while the document scrolls. Peek / list / full are `data-snap-index` `0` / `1` / `2` (fractions `0.28` / `0.55` / `1`) plus `--list-hidden` on the full edit. The local `--sheet-*` classes are gone. The drawer root is `pointer-events: none`; clicks land on `.tm-drawer__panel`. The runner handle (`.tm-signing-form-runner__sheet-handle`, 44px, centred) is the only `aria-expanded` toggle — there is no `.tm-sheet-handle`. Crossing the breakpoint remounts the drawer; peek/list/full state is kept, focus inside the sheet is not. Desktop and tablet keep the `aside`.

  ```html
  <!-- before (mobile) -->
  <aside class="tm-signing-form-runner__steps tm-signing-form-runner__steps--sheet-expanded tm-signing-form-runner__steps--sheet-full">
    <button class="tm-signing-form-runner__sheet-handle" aria-expanded="true"></button>
    <div class="tm-signing-form-runner__step-panel">…</div>
  </aside>
  <!-- after (mobile) -->
  <div class="tm-signing-form-runner__sheet-host" data-testid="signing-runner-steps">
    <div class="tm-drawer tm-drawer--bottom tm-drawer--inline tm-signing-form-runner__steps tm-signing-form-runner__steps--list-hidden"
         data-snap-index="2" data-snap-points="0.28,0.55,1">
      <div class="tm-drawer__panel">
        <button class="tm-signing-form-runner__sheet-handle" aria-expanded="true"></button>
        <div class="tm-signing-form-runner__step-panel">…</div>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
  ```

  ```css
  /* before */
  .tm-signing-form-runner__steps--sheet-full .tm-signing-form-runner__field-list { display: none; }
  /* after */
  .tm-signing-form-runner__steps[data-snap-index="2"] .tm-signing-form-runner__field-list,
  .tm-signing-form-runner__steps--list-hidden .tm-signing-form-runner__field-list { display: none; }
  ```

  **Comments.** `LayoutMode=Auto` follows the viewer's own container: below 640px the comment panel is a non-modal bottom `TmDrawer` (`tm-document-page-viewer__comments-sheet`). The docked shell and the drawer share one comments-shell fragment (host template, or the draft section plus the thread panel). `OnClose` and `OnNewComment` are new panel parameters; `OnCommentsClose` is the matching new viewer parameter. `OnClose` did not exist before this phase. A host that selected the comments shell as a sibling of the page column must follow the drawer on mobile.

  **Comment chrome, before → after.**

  | Before | After |
  | --- | --- |
  | Filter `role="tablist"` | `role="group"` + `aria-pressed` + a visible label (`aria-labelledby`) |
  | Text action buttons | `⋯` `TmDropdown`, permission-gated |
  | Mention chips | Inline `<mark>` |
  | Mention count on the comments toggle | Separate `.tm-document-page-viewer__mention-badge` |
  | Page label text | Page `<input>` (`PageRequested`); readonly `n / N` when that callback is unset |
  | Absolute comment time | Relative time, absolute time in `title` |
  | Composer `<textarea>` | `TmTextArea` wrapper (do not pass `class` through the splat) |
  | Designer mobile toolbar | Action bar; fit / culture live in More |
  | Runner sheet classes | `TmDrawer` (`data-snap-index`, `--list-hidden`) |

  **New parameters.** Panel: `LayoutMode`, `OnClose`, `OnNewComment`. Viewer: `LayoutMode`, `OnCommentsClose`, `EnablePinchZoom` (default `false`; the runner and the demo viewer opt in, the designer stays off). Toolbar groups: `data-tm-group` `pages` | `zoom` | `comments`.

  **Hosting.** `TmDocumentPageViewer` pinch imports `signing-runner.js`, which loads the core `pointer-gesture.js`. Serve `_content/Tempo.Blazor/js/` and list that file in the CSP. Without it, pinch is a no-op and the zoom buttons still work.

  ```html
  <!-- before (mobile) -->
  <div class="tm-document-page-viewer__comments-shell">
    <aside class="tm-document-comment-thread-panel" data-testid="document-comments-panel">…</aside>
  </div>
  <!-- after (mobile) -->
  <div class="tm-drawer tm-drawer--bottom tm-drawer--inline tm-document-page-viewer__comments-sheet" data-snap-index="0">
    <div class="tm-drawer__panel">
      <aside class="tm-document-comment-thread-panel" data-testid="document-comments-panel">…</aside>
    </div>
  </div>
  ```

  **Viewer.** `TmDocumentPageViewer` raises `PageRequested` (`EventCallback<int>`) when the page input commits a page, in addition to `PreviousPageRequested` / `NextPageRequested`. A host that only listened to the previous/next callbacks still works; a custom pager that wrote the page input must also handle `PageRequested`.

  ```razor
  @* before *@
  <TmDocumentPageViewer PreviousPageRequested="Prev" NextPageRequested="Next" />
  @* after — PageRequested is additive; wire it when the page input should navigate *@
  <TmDocumentPageViewer PreviousPageRequested="Prev" NextPageRequested="Next" PageRequested="GoTo" />
  ```

  **Designer mobile.** `TmPdfTemplateDesigner` on a mobile container (`LayoutMode` / the shell's own container, &lt; 768px) is viewing plus light edits: a `TmMobileActionBar` and one bottom sheet, not the docked palette and inspector. Tablet (768–1199, including 1024 with touch) keeps the overlay panels. `MobileMode` remains the obsolete alias of `LayoutMode=Mobile`. A selector that assumed the palette was always in the document flow must key off `data-layout` and the shell sheet, not the viewport.

  **Viewer pinch.** `TmDocumentPageViewer` attaches the shared `pointer-gesture.js` `attachPinch` on `.tm-document-page-viewer__viewport` (touch + ctrl+wheel). A commit raises the existing `ScaleChanged` with the absolute scale and sets `ZoomMode` to `Custom`. The page no longer carries `max-width: 100%`, so a scale above 1 scrolls inside the viewport instead of being clipped. There is no second pinch implementation.

- **Signing redesign (phase 8): the PDF template designer and its field overlay use pointer events, and the designer renders through `TmEditorShell`.** A host or a test that dispatched `mousedown` / `mousemove` / `mouseup` or an HTML5 drag on the designer must dispatch the pointer equivalents, and a selector that assumed the designer root was a plain `div` must follow the shell:

  ```html
  <!-- before -->
  <div class="tm-pdf-template-designer" onmousedown="..." onmousemove="..."></div>
  <!-- after -->
  <div class="tm-editor-shell tm-pdf-template-designer" data-layout="desktop">
      <div class="tm-pdf-template-designer__workspace"></div>
  </div>
  ```

  `MobileMode` stays as an obsolete alias that forces `TmLayoutMode.Mobile`; new hosts set `LayoutMode`. The shell classifies its own container with `LayoutBreakpoints` (default 768 / 1200). The toolbar is a `TmToolbar` with named groups `data-tm-group="pages|view|language|zoom|detect"`. The custom `__context-actions` menu is gone; its items are now core `TmContextMenuItem` (`role=menuitem`; class hooks via `Class`). A selector that assumed plain button children of the menu must change. One `TmContextMenu` (opened with `TmContextMenu.Open()`) carries the same item classes. A palette tap arms drawing and a second tap places a default-sized field. The designer height is `--tm-pdf-template-designer-height` (or the `Height` parameter); the old fixed height remains the default. The move and resize session is attached to the workspace element, not the document.

- **Spreadsheet redesign (phase 7c): the Sort dialog wraps its content in `div.tm-spreadsheet-sort__body`.** The wrapper is the inline-size query container the phone toolbar needs (it is the element the 320 px "stack the options" rule measures), and it carries the phone modifier `tm-spreadsheet-sort__body--mobile`. Every existing hook still matches — `.tm-spreadsheet-sort__toolbar`, `.tm-spreadsheet-sort__toggles`, `.tm-spreadsheet-sort__table`, `.tm-spreadsheet-sort__card`, `.tm-spreadsheet-sort__tool`, `__btn--ok` / `__btn--cancel` are untouched — but a selector that assumed the toolbar was a DIRECT child of the modal body must become a descendant selector:

  ```css
  /* before */
  .tm-modal-body > .tm-spreadsheet-sort__toolbar { /* host override */ }
  /* after */
  .tm-spreadsheet-sort__body .tm-spreadsheet-sort__toolbar { /* host override */ }
  ```

  The Name Manager card is a visual change, not a DOM change: the name is now ONE ellipsised line and the "Refers to" formula wraps to at most two clamped lines (the full value is in the element's `title` / `aria-label`), so a host that relied on a wrapping name must read the `title`.

- **Spreadsheet redesign (phase 6): the chrome is responsive to the CONTAINER, not the viewport, and the phone layout is viewing plus basic editing (G2).** `TmSpreadsheet` now renders through the core `TmLayoutObserver` and classifies the width of its OWN box — the root is a named inline-size query container (`container-type: inline-size; container-name: tm-spreadsheet`) — so a 390px Notion block or modal inside a 1440px page is a phone. The four `@media (max-width: 768px)` blocks of the package (`_spreadsheet.css`, `TmSpreadsheetFormulaBar.razor.css`, `TmSpreadsheetSheetTabs.razor.css`) are gone; every responsive rule is now a `@container tm-spreadsheet (width < 640px)` range query whose literal is a `TmBreakpoints` value (`TmBreakpointsTests`). New parameter `LayoutMode` (`TmLayoutMode`, default `Auto`) pins the mode for a host that already knows its surface and for tests; `Auto` is the desktop chrome until the first measurement, so static SSR is unchanged.

  | Surface | Desktop | Tablet (640–1023px of container — `TmLayoutBreakpoints.Default`) | Mobile (<640px of container) |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | Ribbon | phase-5 tab strip (`Home`/`Insert`/`Data`/`View`/`File`) | TWO compact rows over the core `TmToolbar Overflow=Menu`; **no tab strip**; row 1 = open/undo/redo/clipboard/Format Cells/image/link + "More" (advanced data tools + the workbook download live there), row 2 = font, size, B/I/U, colours, alignment, number format, %, 000, decimals, borders, Filter, Sort | ONE basic-formatting row (undo/redo, B/I/U, ONE Align dropdown, number format, %, colours + "More") |
  | Header | `ShowHeader` document header (opt-in) | same | compact header: `Title` + undo/redo + `HeaderStart`/`HeaderActions`; the document header (file actions, grid switch) does not render |
  | Status bar | present | present | **absent** — the zoom controls and the aggregations move into the action bar's "More" menu (grouped `zoom` / `summary`, the summary rows are inert information) |
  | Bottom bar | — | — | core `TmMobileActionBar`: Insert / Format / Insert image + "More" (sheet, data, zoom, summary groups) |
  | Height | `Height` (600px default) | `Height` | **`100%`** (SP3) with a `--tm-spreadsheet-mobile-min-height` (32rem) floor and a `100dvh` ceiling |
  | Grid density | `Density` | `Density` | `Density=Auto` resolves to `Comfortable` |

  The mobile height cap is not cosmetic: `height: 100%` inside an auto-height parent resolves to `auto`, and the canvas grid's size spacer is the whole scrollable sheet, so an uncapped mobile spreadsheet grew to thousands of pixels in a normal document flow (found in the phase's own screenshot review). `max-height: 100dvh` keeps the grid scrolling inside the component, like the reference's phone app.

  **New DOM wrapper (breaking for positional CSS).** The component root `.tm-spreadsheet` now contains a
  `div.tm-spreadsheet__layout` (the core layout observer's root) and everything the chrome renders sits inside
  it; every overlay — the 14 dialogs, the sheets, the filter dropdown, both context menus — is a SIBLING of
  that wrapper inside the root. A host selector that assumed direct children (`.tm-spreadsheet > .tm-spreadsheet-toolbar`)
  must become a descendant selector:

  ```css
  /* before */
  .tm-spreadsheet > .tm-spreadsheet-toolbar { /* host override */ }
  /* after */
  .tm-spreadsheet .tm-spreadsheet-toolbar { /* host override */ }
  ```

  **The compact chrome's hooks.** The tablet/mobile rows keep the frozen `data-tm-group` contract (each run of
  commands is a core `TmToolbarGroup` with `data-tm-group` = one of `clipboard | font | alignment | number |
  cells | insert | data | view | file | custom`) and add `data-toolbar-layout="tablet|mobile"` on the toolbar,
  `data-toolbar-row="primary|formatting"` on each row and `data-command-id="…"` on every command (the selects,
  the colour splits and the border split included). `data-tm-tab` does NOT exist in the compact chrome — there
  is no tab strip below the desktop breakpoint, so a spec/host that keyed off `data-tm-tab` must key off
  `data-tm-group`/`data-command-id` (or pin `LayoutMode="TmLayoutMode.Desktop"`). `CustomTools` render one
  `data-tm-group="custom"` entry per tool on the compact rows: reachable from the row's "More" on a tablet
  (their `Tab` is irrelevant there — there are no tabs) and only from More on a phone (G2).

  Removed/renamed behaviour: `.tm-spreadsheet-find` keeps its flows, but the Find & Replace panel, the header filter dropdown and the grid context menu now present as a **sheet whenever the CONTAINER is a phone** (they follow the layout the host resolved, not the viewport — new `LayoutMode` parameters on `TmSpreadsheetFindReplaceDialog`, `TmSpreadsheetFilterDropdown`, `TmSpreadsheetCanvasGrid`). The filter dropdown's mobile sheet has 44px rows and a sticky Cancel / OK bar; the grid context menu is a `TmDrawer` sheet (`tm-spreadsheet-context-sheet`).

  ```razor
  <!-- before: the layout followed the viewport; a narrow embed inside a wide page kept the desktop chrome -->
  <div style="width:390px"><TmSpreadsheet @bind-Data="@bytes" /></div>

  <!-- after: the container decides; a host (or a test) can still pin it -->
  <div style="width:390px"><TmSpreadsheet Data="@bytes" /></div>
  <TmSpreadsheet Data="@bytes" LayoutMode="TmLayoutMode.Desktop" />
  ```

  ```html
  <!-- before: viewport query, mode invisible in the DOM -->
  @media (max-width: 768px) { .tm-spreadsheet-toolbar__button { width: 24px; } }

  <!-- after: container query on the named container + the resolved mode as attributes -->
  <div class="tm-spreadsheet tm-spreadsheet--layout-mobile" data-layout="mobile">
  @container tm-spreadsheet (width < 640px) { … }
  ```

  **Review round (same phase).** The two context menus are now RENDERED BY THE HOST
  (`TmSpreadsheetContextMenu`, a sibling of the layout container): `TmSpreadsheetCanvasGrid` and
  `TmSpreadsheetSheetTabs` gained `RenderContextMenu`/`OnContextMenuRequested` and the grid two public entry
  points (`OpenColumnWidthDialog`, `OpenRowHeightDialog`), because a `position: fixed` menu inside the
  container is positioned against the card and one inside the scrolling grid is clipped. The phone's cell
  menu is a MODAL core drawer sheet (backdrop, focus trap, Escape, 44px `role="menuitem"` rows in the sans
  face, focus back to the grid) and while any sheet owns the phone layout the sticky action bar is removed
  (`tm-spreadsheet__mobile-bar--suppressed`) so it cannot cover the sheet's footer — the same fix made the
  filter sheet modal and bounded (`height: 100%` of the drawer, value list scrolls, sticky Cancel / OK) after
  its footer was measured below the fold. `ShowHeader="true"` no longer renders TWO headers on a phone: the
  document header is desktop/tablet only and the compact header renders ONLY when the host gives it content
  (undo/redo lead the mobile formatting row instead of an empty 50px row). The compact rows keep the frozen
  `data-tm-group` contract (a core `TmToolbarGroup` per run) and render `CustomTools` as
  `data-tm-group="custom"` entries. The mobile Format Cells hides the Border tab. `SpreadsheetToolbarLayout`
  and its three types are now `internal` (no public API commitment). The new public surface is
  `RenderContextMenu` + `OnContextMenuRequested` on the grid and the sheet tabs, and
  `SpreadsheetContextMenuRequest`; `TmSpreadsheetContextMenu`/`SpreadsheetContextMenuItem` are public only
  because a Razor component cannot be `internal` — both are `[EditorBrowsable(Never)]` (implementation detail).

  What is NOT offered below the tablet breakpoint (G2 — full editing starts at the tablet): Text to Columns, Remove Duplicates, Data Validation (and the invalid-data circles), the Name Manager, Paste Special, the Format Painter, the cell-border picker (including the **Borders tab of Format Cells**, which the dialog hides on the phone layout), Merge cells, the thousands separator and the workbook Open / Download. Those commands are absent from the mobile model, so the core toolbar cannot re-offer them in "More". A host that needs one on a phone passes `LayoutMode="TmLayoutMode.Tablet"` (or keeps its own button outside the spreadsheet).

- **Spreadsheet redesign (phase 7): the canvas owns `touch-action`, Comfortable draws bigger header gutters, and a DOM touch-handle layer appears on a coarse pointer.** Three separate breaking surfaces:

  1. **`touch-action: pan-x pan-y` on the grid root.** One finger pans/scrolls the grid natively (momentum included). What it BLOCKS over the grid is the browser's own **pinch-zoom and double-tap zoom** — the page can no longer be zoomed with two fingers that start on the grid, because the two-finger pinch is the core `pointer-gesture.js` gesture and zooms the SHEET (50–200 %, the same 10 % grid as the status bar) instead. Page scrolling from outside the grid is unchanged; a finger drag that starts inside the grid scrolls the grid, not the page.

     | Before | After |
     |---|---|
     | two fingers over the grid pinch-zoomed the PAGE | the pinch zooms the SHEET and page zoom is blocked over the grid |
     | the fill handle was a 10 px mouse target | the fill handle keeps the painted square; its HIT box grows with `Density` and reaches 24 px on a coarse pointer |

     A host that relies on pinch-zooming the page must leave the grid (or its embed) with `touch-action` of its own; no API is removed — `OnZoomStep` (Ctrl+wheel / the zoom buttons) is unchanged and the new `OnZoomChanged` (absolute factor, from the pinch) is additive.

  2. **The Comfortable density now scales the header GUTTERS — a geometry change, not only a paint change.** `SpreadsheetDensityScale.GutterScale` is 1.4 at Comfortable: the row-header gutter is 56 px (was 40) and the column header 28 px (was 20), and both travel in the canvas frame (`RowHeaderWidth` / `ColumnHeaderHeight`) so the canvas, the hit-testing and the component geometry cannot drift apart. A host or spec that computes a cell position from the CONSTANTS (40/20) instead of the frame's values will be off by 16 px horizontally / 8 px vertically on a coarse pointer. The workbook model (row heights, column widths, XLSX) is untouched.

  3. **New DOM inside the grid.** `.tm-spreadsheet-canvas-grid__layer` now also carries `.tm-spreadsheet-canvas-grid__touch-handles` with three `[data-touch-handle]` boxes — `start` (top-left drop), `fill` (the fill handle) and `end` (bottom-right drop, offset outside the fill handle). They are transparent hit areas positioned from the painted selection (`start`/`end` paint a 12 px circle on a coarse pointer) and the whole layer is `display: none` on `(pointer: fine)`, so a desktop host sees no new interactive element. A host selector such as `.tm-spreadsheet-canvas-grid__layer > canvas` still matches; `> *` now also matches the handle layer.

  **The cell menu has two new entries** (Fill down / Fill right) in both presentations (the anchored menu and the phone sheet), which shifts the item indexes a host spec might rely on — key off the item text instead. On a phone the anchored menu now flips above the finger when there is no room below, scrolls its own overflow and gives every entry a `--tm-touch-target` height; a long press offsets the menu from the finger (`data-anchor="touch"`).

  **Notion embed.** `TmNotionSpreadsheetBlock` renders a read-only (`Mode=Embedded`) spreadsheet and `TmNotionSpreadsheetEditModal` hosts the editor inside the Notion fullscreen modal, so both inherit the rules above: one finger scrolls the preview and a two-finger pinch zooms the SHEET rather than the Notion page; the read-only grid opens NO cell menu at all (`IsReadonly` blocks the gesture) and the host menu it would render carries no mutating entries; the long-press menu is a phone sheet inside the modal's own stacking context (the menu is a sibling of the layout container, never a child of it). Scrolling stops at the grid's edge rather than chaining to the page behind it (`overscroll-behavior` on the menu; the grid itself keeps the platform's default chaining, deliberately — a nested editor that swallows an edge scroll traps the page).

- **Spreadsheet redesign (phase 5): the ribbon is a grouped tabbed ribbon, the document header is opt-in and every toolbar glyph is an icon.** `TmSpreadsheetToolbar` now renders one tab strip (`Home`, `Insert`, `Data`, `View` and the compatibility `File` tab) above a row of named groups — `tm-spreadsheet-toolbar__group` with a visible `tm-spreadsheet-toolbar__group-label` (Clipboard, Font with the cell-border picker, Alignment, Number, Cells, Insert, Data, View, File) — whose commands are either **large** (`__button--large`, icon above the label: Undo, Redo, Paste, Insert row/column, Delete, Insert link/image) or **small** (`__button--small/--text`, e.g. Cut, Copy, the Data-tab text buttons). Every Unicode glyph is gone (`←|`, `|→`, `.0→`, `.00→`, `☐ ⊞ ▣ ◼ ▬ ▰ ═ ⊟ ▭ ▏ ▕ ⚙ ▾`): the standard marks are lucide `TmIcon`s and the cell-border, vertical-alignment and decimal marks are the package's own registered SVG set (`SpreadsheetIcons`, `tm-ss-border-*`, `tm-ss-align-*`, `tm-ss-decimal-*`). Existing selectors survive: `.tm-spreadsheet-toolbar__tab`, `__button`, `__button--text`, `__select` and every command `title` (Filter, Sort ascending, Custom sort…, Remove duplicates, Text to columns, Paste special, Data validation..., Name Manager, …).

  ```razor
  <!-- before: one trailing group, the icon name painted as text, File tools lost with the File tab -->
  <TmSpreadsheet CustomTools="@(new List<SpreadsheetCustomTool> { new() { IconName = "download", Title = "Archive", Tab = "File" } })" />

  <!-- after: one group per tool (data-tm-group="custom", data-tool-id), TmIcon + Title, and a
       File-tab tool appears as a header action while ShowHeader="true" -->
  <TmSpreadsheet ShowHeader="true"
                 CustomTools="@(new List<SpreadsheetCustomTool> { new() { Id = "archive", IconName = "download", Title = "Archive", Tab = "file" } })" />
  ```

  ```html
  <!-- before: flat icon row, no group names, text glyphs as icons -->
  <div class="tm-spreadsheet-toolbar__group">
    <button class="tm-spreadsheet-toolbar__button" title="Increase Indent">←|</button>
    <button class="tm-spreadsheet-toolbar__button" title="Increase decimal places">.0→</button>
  </div>
  <button class="tm-spreadsheet-toolbar__button" title="Border picker">☐</button>

  <!-- after: named group + large/small buttons, icons only -->
  <div class="tm-spreadsheet-toolbar__group">
    <div class="tm-spreadsheet-toolbar__group-body">
      <button class="tm-spreadsheet-toolbar__button tm-spreadsheet-toolbar__button--icon" title="Increase Indent">
        <TmIcon Name="indent-increase" />
      </button>
      <button class="tm-spreadsheet-toolbar__button tm-spreadsheet-toolbar__button--icon" title="Increase decimal places">
        <TmIcon Name="tm-ss-decimal-increase" />
      </button>
    </div>
    <span class="tm-spreadsheet-toolbar__group-label">Alignment</span>
  </div>
  ```
  Migrations that change behaviour:
  - **Merge cells moved from the `View` tab to the `Home` tab's Alignment group.** `page.Locator(".tm-spreadsheet-toolbar__tab", new() { HasTextString = "View" })` before clicking `[title='Merge cells']` is no longer needed.
  - **Delete row/column moved behind the large `Delete` split action in the `Cells` group.** `[title='Delete row']` / `[title='Delete column']` now live in the split menu; open it via `[title='Delete options']` first (`role="menu"`).
  - **`ActiveTab` is a real parameter.** It was a public property without `[Parameter]`; it is now `[Parameter] ActiveTab` plus `[Parameter] ActiveTabChanged`, so a host can bind the active tab. Without a binding the toolbar still switches tabs internally, but a click now also raises `ActiveTabChanged`.
  - **`Insert link` / `Insert image` also render on the `Home` tab** (the reference's `Vložení` quick-access group) in addition to the `Insert` tab; both tabs never render at the same time, so `[title='Insert link']` stays unique on screen.
  - **New `ShowFileTab` (default `true`) on `TmSpreadsheet` and `TmSpreadsheetToolbar`.** With the document header on, the `File` tab is not rendered; the header owns Open / Download.
  - **Custom ribbon tools render differently.** Each `CustomTools` entry is now its own ribbon group (`data-tm-group="custom"`, `data-tool-id="<tool.Id>"`), painted as a small button with its `IconName` through `TmIcon` plus its `Title` (before, the icon name was painted as literal text and every tool shared one trailing group). The `Tab` match is case-insensitive (`"home"`, `"Home"`). Because Merge cells moved to Home, a tool that was meant to sit next to Merge must use `Tab="Home"`.
  - **A custom tool placed on `Tab="File"`** has no File tab while the document header renders; the header now renders such tools as its own actions (branded with `data-tool-id`) instead of silently dropping them.
  - **Stable group/tab contract (additive-only).** Every ribbon group carries `data-tm-group` from the frozen set `clipboard | font | alignment | number | cells | insert | links | data | view | file | custom` (Home quick-insert = `insert`, the Insert tab = `links`), every tab and tabpanel carries `data-tm-tab` (`Home|Insert|Data|View|File`), custom groups also carry `data-tool-id`, and the tab strip follows the WAI-ARIA tabs pattern (per-instance ids, `aria-controls`/`aria-labelledby`, roving `tabindex`, ArrowLeft/Right/Home/End). Hosts and tests should key off these attributes, never off localized label text or position. Contract: [docs/spreadsheet.md](docs/spreadsheet.md#ribbon-contract).
  - **The hidden XLSX input's id is per instance.** It was the fixed `tm-spreadsheet-file-input`, so a page with two spreadsheets always opened the first one's picker; it is now `tm-spreadsheet-file-input-{instance}` (no published selector used it).
- **Spreadsheet redesign (phase 5): the document header is opt-in and additive (G9/SP3).** `TmSpreadsheet` gains `ShowHeader` (default `false`), `Title`, `HeaderStart`, `HeaderActions`, `ShowFileTab` and `CustomTools`/`OnCustomToolClick`; with `ShowHeader` the component renders `header.tm-spreadsheet__header` (title on the left, host slots, `Open` / `Download` only for a host that listens to `OnOpen` / `OnDownload`, and the core `TmToggle` labelled "Show grid lines"). "Saved", the hamburger, the ⋮ menu and the document switcher of the reference are host slots, never built in. The custom-tool buttons now render `TmIcon` and their `Title` instead of the icon name as text.

  ```razor
  <!-- before: no header; file actions only inside the legacy File tab -->
  <TmSpreadsheet Height="500px" />
  <!-- after (additive, still false by default) -->
  <TmSpreadsheet ShowHeader="true" Title="Projekt Aurora"
                 OnOpen="OnOpened" OnDownload="OnDownloaded"
                 HeaderActions="@(builder => { /* Share */ })" Height="500px" />
  ```
- **Spreadsheet redesign (phase 5): formula bar and sheet tabs.** The formula bar's `fx` mark is now permanent (`tm-spreadsheet-formula-bar__fx`, previously an edit-mode decoration) and while editing it exposes the SP4 ✓ / ✗ buttons (`__confirm`, `__cancel`, localized `aria-label`s, same commit/revert paths as Enter/Escape). The name box gains a named-range dropdown (`__ref-toggle` + `__ref-list`/`__ref-item`, new `TmSpreadsheetFormulaBar.NamedRanges`; selecting an entry raises `OnNavigateToRef` with the range name, and a workbook without names renders no chevron). The sheet tabs gain `ShowTabCloseButtons` (default `true`; deleting always stays available from the right-click menu) and a pair of scroll arrows (`__scroll-button[data-direction=left|right]`) that appear only when the strip overflows. `.tm-spreadsheet-formula-bar__mode` (the old edit-only fx) is gone; `__ref`, `__display`, `__input` and the formula-bar test ids are unchanged.

- **Fixed (core `TmSelect`): a non-nullable value type at its default now emits its `value`.** Before, `SelectedValueString` returned `null` whenever the value equalled `default(TValue)`, so a select bound to `0` / an enum's first member painted a blank control; every spreadsheet dialog that switched back to such an option (Sort order "A → Z", Sort on "Values", data validation "Any"/"Stop"/type "Whole", Format Cells "General", a column index of 0) looked empty. After, a non-nullable struct default renders `FormatOptionValue(Value)` (e.g. `value="0"`, `value="Sunday"`) while the option list keeps its `selected` marker. Nullable value types and reference types keep the empty-option rules unchanged.

  ```html
  <!-- before: omitted value → the browser shows nothing selected -->
  <select class="tm-select"><option value="0" selected>Zero</option>…</select>
  <!-- after -->
  <select class="tm-select" value="0"><option value="0" selected>Zero</option>…</select>
  ```

- **Added (core `TmModal`): `InitialFocusSelector`.** An additive CSS-selector alternative to `InitialFocusTargetId`, for a target that has no stable id or a set whose first match is the right one (a checked radio, the first checkbox). The Spreadsheet's Paste Special (`input[name='ps-content']:checked`) and Remove Duplicates (`.tm-spreadsheet-dedup__column input`) use it — their previous targets were non-focusable wrapper elements. `null` keeps the previous markup (no `data-initial-focus-selector` attribute).

- **Spreadsheet redesign (phase 4): dialog content and hierarchy follow the reference mockups.** Every spreadsheet dialog body now renders core Tempo inputs for its choices, toggles and text fields (`TmSelect`, `TmTextInput`, `TmCheckbox`, `TmRadioGroup` segmented, `TmSearchInput`, `TmNumberInput`, `TmStepper`, `TmIcon`, `TmButton`) instead of raw `<select>`/`<input>` elements. The Format Cells Alignment/Font/Border/Fill tabs, the Text to Columns mode radios and the Data validation textareas stay native for now — they are rebuilt with their own tabs in a later phase. The dialog ROOT classes on the modal overlay (`tm-spreadsheet-sort`, `tm-spreadsheet-custom-filter`, `tm-spreadsheet-dedup`, `tm-spreadsheet-pastespecial`, `tm-spreadsheet-t2c`, `tm-spreadsheet-hyperlink`, `tm-spreadsheet-name-manager`, `tm-dvd`, `tm-fcd`, `tm-spreadsheet-alert`) and the action classes (`__btn--ok`, `__btn--cancel`) are unchanged; the inner DOM, the form wrapper class names and several control ids are not. The full per-dialog content contract is [docs/spreadsheet-dialogs.md](docs/spreadsheet-dialogs.md) → "Content and hierarchy (redesign phase 4)".

  ```html
  <!-- before: native controls, class on the control itself -->
  <select class="tm-dvd__select">…</select>
  <select class="tm-spreadsheet-custom-filter__op">…</select>
  ```
