  <input class="tm-spreadsheet-name-manager__filter">
  <select id="hl-type"><option value="Web">Web page</option>…</select>
  <ol class="tm-spreadsheet-t2c__steps"><li>1</li><li>2</li><li>3</li></ol>

  <!-- after: core components; Class lands on the select WRAPPER, on the text INPUT, or on the root -->
  <div class="tm-dvd__select tm-select-wrapper"><select class="tm-select">…</select></div>
  <div class="tm-spreadsheet-custom-filter__op tm-select-wrapper"><select class="tm-select">…</select></div>
  <div class="tm-spreadsheet-name-manager__filter tm-input-wrapper"><input type="search" class="tm-input"></div>
  <div id="hl-type" class="tm-radio-group" role="radiogroup">
    <label class="tm-radio-segment"><input class="tm-sr-only" type="radio">Web page</label>…
  </div>
  <div class="tm-stepper"><div class="tm-stepper-item">…Data type…</div>…</div>
  ```

  Practical migrations (all used by the repo's own Playwright specs):
  - `.tm-dvd__select`, `.tm-dvd__body` → `.tm-dvd__select select`, `.tm-dvd__form`.
  - `.tm-dvd__select` on the Error alert tab → `.tm-dvd__select select`; the `#tm-dvd-show-error`/`#tm-dvd-show-input` checkbox ids are gone (the toggles are `TmCheckbox`) — select `.tm-dvd__checks input`, in DOM order.
  - `.tm-spreadsheet-sort__table select` → `.tm-spreadsheet-sort__select select`; the phone renders `.tm-spreadsheet-sort__card` instead of the table.
  - `.tm-spreadsheet-custom-filter__op` → `.tm-spreadsheet-custom-filter__op select`; the And/Or radios are `input[name='custom-filter-join']` inside `.tm-radio-segment` labels.
  - `.tm-spreadsheet-name-manager__filter` → `.tm-spreadsheet-name-manager__filter input` (type `search`); on a mobile layout the rows are `.tm-spreadsheet-name-manager__card` (no `tbody tr`).
  - `#hl-type` is the segmented radiogroup ROOT, not a `<select>`: `page.SelectOptionAsync("#hl-type", "Web")` becomes `page.Locator("#hl-type .tm-radio-segment").First.ClickAsync()` (Web page is the first segment). `#hl-target` / `#hl-display` keep their ids on the `<input>`.
  - Paste Special: the operation is a radio column (`input[name='ps-operation']`, five options) inside `.tm-spreadsheet-pastespecial__grid`; the old `select.tm-spreadsheet-pastespecial__op` is gone.
  - Text to Columns: `<ol class="tm-spreadsheet-t2c__steps">` → the core `.tm-stepper`; the phone shows `.tm-spreadsheet-t2c__step-compact` instead. Delimiters are `.tm-spreadsheet-t2c__delim` wrappers around core checkboxes, and the preview is a `<table>` with a `<thead>` inside `.tm-spreadsheet-t2c__preview-scroll` (row selectors must use `tbody tr`).
  - Remove Duplicates: `.tm-spreadsheet-dedup__count` states "Selected N of M"; the toggles/columns are core checkboxes (`.tm-spreadsheet-dedup__column` is the checkbox WRAPPER).
  - Format Cells: the decimal places `input[type=number].tm-fcd__input--sm` → `.tm-fcd__decimal` (`TmNumberInput`, inner `.tm-number-input__input`); a mobile layout replaces `.tm-fcd__listbox[role=listbox]` with `.tm-fcd__category-select` + `.tm-fcd__number-options`; the preview's `style` now carries `text-align` from the format.
  - Validation alert: `.tm-spreadsheet-alert__icon` → `.tm-spreadsheet-alert__badge`; the card is `ModalSize.Medium`, the badge sits left of the message and there is no divider under the title.
  - Filter dropdown: the Unicode glyphs `▲ ▼ ⚙ ✕ ›` are gone (shared `TmIcon`), the panel starts with `.tm-spreadsheet-filter-dropdown__title` ("Filter and sort") and its values/select-all are core checkboxes.
  - Find & Replace keeps its `.tm-spreadsheet-find__query` / `__replace` / `__counter` / `__btn--text` classes; it gains visible `.tm-spreadsheet-find__label`s, a primary "Replace all" (`__btn--primary` on the same button) and a desktop-only `.tm-spreadsheet-find__btn--close`.

- **TmGantt redesign (phases 1–8): the breaking items at a glance.** The component contract is
  [docs/gantt.md](docs/gantt.md); each item below has its detailed entry (with the full before/after)
  in the phase bullets that follow. Everything else in the plan is opt-in or additive.
  1. *Styled subcomponent surfaces (phase 1).* The dialogs, history drawer, filter panel, workload and portfolio render styled through their own owners; a selector pinned to the old scope attribute (`[b-xxxx]`) no longer matches — use a plain class selector or `::deep`.
  2. *"New report" needs a handler (phase 1).* The button renders only with `OnNewReportRequested`.
  3. *Token-only painting (phase 2).* Day | Week | Month is a segmented control (`tm-btn-secondary` classes gone), status chips are glyph + text, "Today" is a labelled pill over a solid line, the board columns carry no hex, notification settings moved into the view-settings menu, and `GanttViewSettings.Theme` stamps `data-theme` (the `.tm-gantt--theme-dark` palette aliases are gone — override canonical tokens).
  4. *Toolbar and treegrid DOM (phase 4).* The toolbar is a core `TmToolbar` (`.tm-gantt__toolbar-group`/`__divider` gone; style `.tm-toolbar-btn` instead), "Add task" is a split button, the "%" header checkbox is the column menu, and the tree is an ARIA treegrid with a roving tab stop (`.tm-gantt__tree > .tm-gantt__tree-header` selectors go through `.tm-gantt__tree-grid`).
  5. *Task panel and panels DOM (phase 5).* Footer is Cancel | Save outside the scroller, fields are grouped sections, the history drawer is positioned against the component (opt back into the viewport with `HistoryDrawerPlacement="GanttHistoryDrawerPlacement.Viewport"`), rollback and delete ask for confirmation first, and the history rows are the shared `TmGanttHistoryList` (`.tm-gantt__sidebar-history-*` classes gone).
  6. *Dialogs are `TmModal`s (phase 6).* `.tm-gantt__dialog-overlay` and `_gantt-dialog.css` are gone — the per-dialog class moved to the overlay root, the footer order is Cancel then the primary action, and the mapping import stays disabled until Title and Start/End (or Duration) are mapped.
  7. *`LayoutMode` replaces `ContainerWidth` (phase 7, `[Obsolete]`).* The chart measures its own container; the root gained the `tm-layout` wrapper; `GanttFilterPanelMode.Auto` picks the dialog on tablet and narrower.
  8. *Mouse handlers became pointer sessions (phase 7).* No `@onmouse*` on the timeline — tests drive the `[JSInvokable]` paths (`OnDependencyDragCompleted`), and a finger disables HTML5 row drag while pressed.
  9. *Mobile container is read-mostly (phase 8).* A container that classifies mobile offers viewing, Status/Percent and Add task only — no export/import/mapping chrome, no reorder, no dependency drag, no zoom slider (`gantt-export-btn` / `gantt-import-btn` / the slider must pin `LayoutMode="TmLayoutMode.Tablet"`).
- **DiagramEditor: the area OUTSIDE the diagram page now follows the theme (phase 15b).** The `.tm-diagram-page-backdrop` rect used to pin the theme-invariant `--tm-paper-backdrop` (gray-100), so in dark mode the white page floated inside a light frame. The paint now rides the theme-aware `--tm-canvas-backdrop` token (renamed from the phase-15b `--tm-diagram-backdrop` in review; the DiagramEditor keeps a `--tm-diagram-backdrop` **alias** on `.tm-diagram-canvas`, so overrides written against that name on the canvas keep working) — `var(--tm-paper-backdrop)` (the same gray) in light themes, the workspace tone on the dark/indigo-dark theme roots — so the paper stays white and the canvas turns dark with the rest of the chrome. **Breaking: an override of `--tm-paper-backdrop` now only applies in LIGHT themes** — the dark theme roots re-map the canvas token and win over `:root` by source order, so the old override no longer reaches the dark canvas (it still restyles every surface aliased to the paper backdrop). A host that overrode `--tm-paper-backdrop` *because of the editor* should override `--tm-canvas-backdrop` instead:
  ```css
  /* before: restyling the editor's canvas backdrop (and everything aliased to the token) */
  :root { --tm-paper-backdrop: #eef2f7; }
  /* after: the canvas backdrop alone, in both themes */
  :root { --tm-canvas-backdrop: #eef2f7; }
  ```
  A host that wants the old always-light canvas back pins the light value on the theme roots:
  ```css
  [data-theme="dark"] .tm-diagram-canvas, .tm-dark .tm-diagram-canvas { --tm-diagram-backdrop: var(--tm-paper-backdrop); }
  ```
  The literal `fill="#f3f4f6"` fallback attributes on the SVG rects are unchanged (viewers without the stylesheet), and `exportViewportAsSvg` still copies the computed values, so an export carries exactly the paints the user saw.

- **TmChip pressed + removable: `aria-*` and `data-testid` additional attributes move to the toggle button (phase 15b review).** When `Pressed` and `Removable` combine, the shell wrapper used to receive ALL additional attributes, so a `data-testid` (host/E2E selectors) or an `aria-label` / `aria-describedby` (assistive tech) landed on a non-interactive `<span>` instead of the activatable `<button>`. The two kinds are routed to the pressed button now; every other attribute stays on the shell. A host that keyed a selector on the SHELL carrying those attribute kinds must key the button instead:
  ```html
  <!-- before: the shell <span class="tm-chip tm-chip__shell"> carried data-testid / aria-label -->
  .tm-chip[data-testid='severity-error'] { … }
  <!-- after: the activatable <button class="tm-chip"> carries them -->
  button.tm-chip[data-testid='severity-error'] { … }
  ```

- **TmChip: the pressed toggle is visibly pressed, and `TmModelingIssuePanel` filter chips actually style across the scope boundary (phase 15b review).** The pressed toggle `<button>` used to render with the UA button chrome (system font, ButtonFace background, outset border) and NO visible pressed state outside forced-colors mode — the focus ring also erased the pressed paint (both were box-shadows). `_chip.css` now strips the UA chrome through a zero-specificity `:where(.tm-chip--pressed)` reset (variants still win), paints an `inset` ring on `[aria-pressed="true"]` and moves the focus ring to `outline`. The Modeling issue filter chips (severity) render through the core `TmChip`, so the panel's compact sizing and severity tints key off the panel-owned chips wrapper with `::deep` — hosts that copied the old un-prefixed `.tm-modeling-issue-panel__chip…` rules from the panel's scoped stylesheet should copy the `…__chips ::deep …` form. `Disabled` chips now paint the shared `--tm-opacity-disabled` (0.5) with `cursor: not-allowed` via `.tm-chip-disabled` (the class existed unstyled before).
  ```css
  /* before: copied from the panel's own scoped stylesheet — never matched across the scope boundary */
  .tm-modeling-issue-panel__chip--error { … }
  /* after: key off the panel-owned chips wrapper with ::deep */
  .tm-modeling-issue-panel__chips ::deep .tm-chip--error { … }
  ```

- **TmModelingEditor previews now show a notation legend card by default (Fáze 15).** `ShowPreviewLegend` defaults to `true`: the desktop/tablet preview renders a collapsible "Legend" card in the canvas's top-right corner (listing only the notation shapes the document uses; collapsed above 12 nodes) and the mobile band gains a "Legend" entry in the compact header "⋯". A host that wants the pre-Fáze-15 look passes `ShowPreviewLegend="false"`:
  ```razor
  <!-- before (2.9.x): no legend -->
  <TmModelingEditor ProviderKey="erp.modeling" />

  <!-- after: the legend is part of the contract; opt out with one parameter -->
  <TmModelingEditor ProviderKey="erp.modeling" ShowPreviewLegend="false" />
  ```
  The legend never steals canvas height (it is an overlay in the canvas corner, scrolling inside a max-height card) and never covers the status bar's zoom group, the Fáze 9 mobile zoom pill or the empty-diagram hint. `TmModelingDiagramPreview.ShowLegend` itself defaults to `false` — only the editor opts in by default.
- **TmGantt phase 1: previously unstyled Gantt surfaces now render styled, and "New report" needs a callback.**
  - *Appearance.* The export, import and column-mapping dialogs, the history drawer, the filter panel, the workload grid and the portfolio used to render without any styling (a scoped-CSS isolation defect). They are styled now, with the values the stylesheet always declared. A host that overrode them with a selector written against the scoped attribute (`.tm-gantt__history-drawer[b-xxxx]`, or `::deep` from a parent) now matches the new owner's scope; write the override against the class and give it the same specificity as the component rule:
    ```css
    /* before: never matched anything (the rule was dead), so no override was needed */
    /* after: the drawer is a fixed 380px panel - narrow it if you must */
    .tm-gantt__history-drawer { width: min(320px, 95vw); }
    ```
  - *The shared dialog shell is global.* `.tm-gantt__dialog-overlay`, `.tm-gantt__dialog` and its header / title / close / body / actions are declared once in `_gantt-dialog.css` (part of `tempo-blazor.css`). A host that does not use `tempo-blazor.css` / `tempo-blazor.bundled.css` and links component styles individually must add `_content/Tempo.Blazor/css/components/_gantt-dialog.css`.
  - *"New report" is hidden without a handler.* `TmGanttReportsPanel` rendered a "New report" button that did nothing. It is now rendered only when `OnNewReportRequested` has a delegate; `TmGantt` forwards its own new `OnNewReportRequested`.
    ```razor
    <!-- before: a "New report" button that did nothing -->
    <TmGantt Items="tasks" Reports="reports" OnReportRun="Run" />

    <!-- after: the button appears only when the host handles it -->
    <TmGantt Items="tasks" Reports="reports" OnReportRun="Run" OnNewReportRequested="OpenReportEditor" />
    ```
  - *Class and DOM.* The import dialog's error box is `.tm-gantt-import__error` (it used to borrow `.tm-gantt-task-panel__error`); the Day / Week / Month buttons carry `data-testid` `gantt-view-day|week|month`, `aria-pressed`, and the active one is `tm-btn-secondary` instead of `tm-btn-ghost`; the filter operator `<option>` text is the localized label (its `value` is still the enum name); the export and mapping dialog card is wrapped in a `TmFocusScope` (`div.tm-focus-scope.tm-gantt__dialog`), so a selector `> .tm-gantt__dialog` under the overlay still works but the card now also carries `role="dialog"`.
  - *Swatch shape.* The task panel colour swatch is a circle (`border-radius: 50%`); the moved rule declared a 4px radius. Restore it with `.tm-gantt__panel-color-swatch { border-radius: 4px; }`.
  - *Date text.* History timestamps and workload column headers follow the current culture. A test or host that asserted `dd.MM.yyyy HH:mm` / `dd.MM` must use the culture's pattern (`ToString("g", culture)`).
- **TmGantt phase 2: the desktop look follows the tokens (segment, status chips, "Today" pill, solid line, workload colours, theme classes).** The Gantt now paints with the core semantic tokens only (zero colour literals and zero undefined `--tm-*` aliases in `TmGantt*.razor.css` and `_gantt-dialog.css`), so dark mode, the indigo theme and a host's own token overrides reach it. What changes on screen and in the DOM:
  - *Day | Week | Month is a segmented control.* Three `ghost`/`secondary` `TmButton`s become one `div.tm-gantt__segment[role=group]` of `button.tm-gantt__segment-btn`; the active one carries `tm-gantt__segment-btn--active` and `aria-pressed="true"`. The `data-testid`s (`gantt-view-day|week|month`) and `aria-pressed` are unchanged; the `tm-btn-secondary` / `tm-btn-ghost` classes are gone.
    ```css
    /* before */ [data-testid="gantt-view-week"].tm-btn-secondary { … }
    /* after  */ [data-testid="gantt-view-week"].tm-gantt__segment-btn--active { … }
    ```
  - *"Add task" has a visible label.* The primary button is `＋ Add task` (it was an icon-only plus); `data-testid="gantt-add-task"`, the `title` and the `aria-label` are unchanged.
  - *Status chips are glyph + text.* `.tm-gantt__status-badge` now starts with `span.tm-gantt__status-icon[aria-hidden]` (✓ done, ◉ in progress, ○ open, ⊘ closed) before the localized `GanttStatus_*` text, and takes its colours from `--tm-status-{open,inprogress,done,closed}-{bg,fg}` (the old greys/blues/greens were hard-coded hex). A selector or test that asserted the chip's whole `TextContent` equals the status text must strip the glyph: `chip.TextContent.Replace("✓", "").Trim()`. The same chip is the header of the Board columns.
  - *The Board columns carry no hex.* `TmGantt` no longer passes `KanbanColumn.Color` (`#e5e7eb`, `#dbeafe`, …): each column header is the status chip plus the count through `TmKanbanBoard`'s `ColumnHeaderTemplate`, so `.tm-kanban__header-color` is no longer rendered inside the Gantt board. `data-testid="board-column-*"` is unchanged.
  - *"Today" is a labelled pill over a solid line.* `.tm-gantt__today-marker` is a 2px **solid** `--tm-color-danger` line (it was dashed with a round dot via `::before`, which is removed) and a new `span.tm-gantt__today-label[data-testid=today-label]` with the localized `TmGantt_Today` text sits in the timeline header. It follows `GanttViewSettings.ShowTodayMarker`. `.tm-gantt__current-time-marker` (Hours zoom) is unchanged.
  - *Priority glyphs and bar edges use `--tm-priority-*`; the default bar fill is `--tm-color-primary-solid`* (it was `var(--tm-color-primary, #3b82f6)`, a fallback that pinned the blue). A bar with a `TmWorkItem.Color` is unchanged. The progress overlay is a darker tone of the bar's own colour instead of a translucent black.
  - *Workload cells.* In-capacity cells are the primary wash with `--tm-color-primary-text` (they were success green), overloaded cells the danger wash with `--tm-color-danger-text`, and an empty cell shows a dash (`–`, `aria-hidden`) with a visually hidden "No allocation" (`TmGantt_WorkloadNoAllocation`) and the class `tm-gantt__workload-cell--empty` (it was an empty box). The assignee column is `position: sticky; left: 0`, a day column is at least 2.5rem (`minmax(2.5rem, 1fr)`), and the grid is `width: max-content; min-width: 100%` with `overflow: clip`, so `.tm-gantt__workload` scrolls horizontally and the first column stays put.
  - *The root is a card on the workspace.* `.tm-gantt` takes `--tm-radius-card`, `--tm-shadow-card`, `--tm-bg-workspace` and `--tm-text-primary`; the toolbar, tree and timeline paint `--tm-bg-surface` on top, so on the default theme (workspace = page = white) nothing moves, and under `data-tm-theme="indigo"` the Gantt sits on the off-white workspace.
  - *The local theme classes carry no palette.* `GanttViewSettings.Theme` now sets `data-theme="dark"` / `"light"` on the Gantt root, so the whole token set of `tokens-dark.css` (and the indigo dark scale) applies to it; `.tm-gantt--theme-dark` / `--theme-light` are kept as an alias and only declare `color-scheme`. `Theme = Auto` follows the registered `ThemeService` (dark when `ThemeService.IsDark`, otherwise no attribute) and a host with no `ThemeService` keeps inheriting the ambient `data-theme`. A host that relied on `.tm-gantt--theme-dark` overriding `--tm-surface` / `--tm-bg-subtle` / `--tm-bg-hover` (undefined aliases that only the Gantt read) must override the canonical tokens instead:
    ```css
    /* before */ .tm-gantt--theme-dark { --tm-bg-subtle: #0b1220; }
    /* after  */ .tm-gantt[data-theme="dark"] { --tm-bg-surface-secondary: #0b1220; }
  - *Light islands are supported by the core.* `tokens-dark.css` now carries a `[data-theme="light"]` block right after the dark one, declaring exactly the properties of the dark block with the light `:root` values (and `theme-indigo.css` has the matching `:root[data-tm-theme="indigo"] [data-theme="light"]` selector), so `GanttViewSettings.Theme = Light` repaints the Gantt light even inside a dark page, and so does any `<div data-theme="light">` in a dark tree. `Theme = Dark` works inside a light page as before. The `:root` selector is unchanged; a host that overrode the light tokens on `:root` only must repeat the override on `[data-theme="light"]` to reach an island.
  - *`Theme = Light` no longer overrides a dark ancestor.* The old `.tm-gantt--theme-light` redeclared a local light palette, so a forced-light Gantt stayed light inside a dark page. `data-theme="light"` has no token block in `tokens.css` (the core defines `:root` and `[data-theme="dark"]` only), so on a dark ancestor the Gantt now keeps the ambient dark tokens; `Light` and `Auto` behave the same there. `Theme = Dark` is unaffected and works inside a light page. A host that needs a light island inside a dark page declares the light tokens on it (`.tm-gantt[data-theme="light"] { --tm-bg-surface: …; }`).
  - *Notification settings moved into the view-settings menu.* With `NotificationSettings` set, the preferences used to render inline in the toolbar row at all times; they are now a group of the view-settings menu. A test or host selector must open the menu first (`gantt-view-settings-btn`) and then query `[data-testid=notification-settings-section]`; with the menu closed the section is not in the DOM.
  - *Shadows and scrims.* Hover, tooltip, menu, drawer and dialog shadows are `--tm-shadow-*`, the dialog scrim is `--tm-bg-overlay`, the non-working-day shade is `--tm-scheduler-weekend-bg`.
- **TmGantt phase 3: internal split of the monolith (no visible change).** `TmGantt.razor` (1143 lines) is now the root plus the alternate views and the context menu; the toolbar, the task tree, the timeline and the sidebar are `TmGanttToolbar`, `TmGanttTree`, `TmGanttTimeline` and `TmGanttSidebar`, and the status chip is `TmGanttStatusChip`, each with its own `.razor.css`. The rendered DOM is byte-identical (element order, classes, `data-testid`s, attributes, text - pinned by `TmGanttMarkupSnapshotTests`), the public `[Parameter]` surface of `TmGantt` is unchanged (pinned by `TmGanttInternalSplitTests`), and no localized text was added. State, callbacks and the mouse handlers (pan, wheel, dependency drag) stay in `TmGantt` and moved unchanged; pointer events arrive with the touch phase.
  - *Performance.* The tree and the timeline skip a render pass that cannot change what they draw, so a toolbar action that only opens a menu, a panel or a dialog (filter, view settings, history, export, import, task panel) no longer repaints every row, bar and dependency line.
  - *New types.* The parts are `public` classes hidden from the editor (`[EditorBrowsable(Never)]`) taking only `Owner` - Razor cannot emit an internal component, and a host never places them; they have JSON overlay entries so the documentation guards stay closed. Place `TmGantt`, not a part.
  - *Styles.* Every rule moved with the markup it styles; the class names did not change. A host that overrides a Gantt class with a plain selector (`.tm-gantt__bar { … }`) is unaffected. A selector pinned to the Gantt's scope attribute (`.tm-gantt__bar[b-…]`, never a contract) no longer matches, because the element now carries its part's scope attribute. Use a plain class selector (`.tm-gantt__bar { … }`), or `::deep` from a host's own scoped stylesheet; both keep working:
    ```css
    /* before: pinned to the Gantt's scope attribute (generated per build) - no longer matches */
    .tm-gantt__bar[b-xxxxxxxxxx] { border-radius: 2px; }

    /* after: a plain class selector reaches the same element */
    .tm-gantt__bar { border-radius: 2px; }
    ```
  - *Status chip.* `.tm-gantt__status-badge` is rendered by `TmGanttStatusChip` instead of a render fragment of `TmGantt`; the markup (`span.tm-gantt__status-badge > span.tm-gantt__status-icon[aria-hidden]` + text) is identical.
- **TmGantt phase 4: the toolbar is a grouped core `TmToolbar`, the grid is an ARIA treegrid, and the "%" checkbox left the grid header.** All opt-in surfaces (`ToolbarLabels`, `SidebarMode`, the header slots, `ShowQuickSearch`, `WbsInTitle`) are listed under *Added*; what breaks without opting in:
  - *Toolbar DOM.* The `tm-gantt__toolbar` row used to be two `div.tm-gantt__toolbar-group`s of `TmButton`s (`button.tm-btn.tm-btn-ghost.tm-btn-sm`) separated by `span.tm-gantt__toolbar-divider`. It is now `div.tm-gantt__toolbar > div.tm-toolbar.tm-gantt__toolbar-bar[role=toolbar]` holding six labelled `role="group"` groups - `data-tm-group` = `create | structure | time | panels | data | settings` - of `button.tm-toolbar-btn` (and the split button, the Day | Week | Month segment, the zoom slider). The default is still icon-only (G14): `ToolbarLabels` defaults to `Icons`, every button keeps its `data-testid`, its `aria-label` and its tooltip, and `aria-pressed` / `aria-expanded` / `aria-haspopup` are unchanged. `.tm-gantt__toolbar-group` and `.tm-gantt__toolbar-divider` are gone (the core `.tm-toolbar-group` / `.tm-toolbar-divider` replace them).
    ```css
    /* before */ .tm-gantt__toolbar .tm-btn-ghost { … }   .tm-gantt__toolbar-divider { … }
    /* after  */ .tm-gantt__toolbar .tm-toolbar-btn { … } .tm-gantt__toolbar .tm-toolbar-divider { … }
    ```
    ```csharp
    // before (E2E / bUnit): cut.Find("button.tm-btn[data-testid='gantt-expand-all']")
    // after:                cut.Find("button.tm-toolbar-btn[data-testid='gantt-expand-all']")   // the data-testid is unchanged
    ```
  - *"Add task" is a split button.* `button[data-testid=gantt-add-task]` is now the primary half of `div.tm-split-button[data-testid=gantt-add-task-split]`; the chevron half opens "Add task above / below / add child task" for the selected task (the same insert the context menu performs; disabled without a selection). Clicking the primary half still adds a task at the end. A selector that matched `button.tm-btn-primary[data-testid=gantt-add-task]` must drop the `tm-btn-primary` class.
  - *The "%" header checkbox is removed.* The Progress header cell no longer carries `input.tm-gantt__col-toggle[data-testid=col-toggle-progress]`; column visibility is the new column menu (`div[data-testid=gantt-column-menu]`, a `TmColumnPicker` listing every rendered column of `Columns` except Title, with a Reset action). `OnColumnsChanged` fires exactly as before.
    ```csharp
    // before: cut.Find("[data-testid='col-toggle-progress']").Change(false);
    // after:
    cut.Find("[data-testid='gantt-column-menu'] .tm-column-picker-toggle").Click();
    cut.Find(".tm-column-picker-item input[data-key='Progress']").Change(false);
    ```
    `.tm-gantt__col-toggle` is deleted. `data-testid="col-header-progress"` stays.
  - *Treegrid roles and a roving tab stop.* `.tm-gantt__tree` now wraps `div.tm-gantt__tree-grid[role=treegrid]` (header `role=row` with `columnheader`s, body `role=rowgroup`, each `.tm-gantt__tree-row` `role=row` with `aria-level`, `aria-selected` and, for a parent, `aria-expanded`, its cells `role=gridcell`). Exactly one row has `tabindex="0"` (the selected / last focused / first row), the rest `-1`; ↑ ↓ Home End move, → expands then steps into the first child (a leaf's → focuses its bar), ← collapses then steps to the parent, Enter (and Space on key-up) opens the task panel. The expand button and the bulk checkbox are fenced from the row's key handler (`tabindex="-1"` on the button). Bars (`.tm-gantt__bar`) and milestones are `role="button" tabindex="-1"` with an `aria-label` of "title, start – end"; Enter / Space opens the panel, Esc / ← returns to the row. A test that queried `.tm-gantt__tree > .tm-gantt__tree-header` must go through `.tm-gantt__tree-grid`.
  - *Panel navigation.* With the default `SidebarMode = Rail` the icon rail is unchanged. `Tabs` replaces it with `div.tm-gantt__panel-tabs[role=tablist]` (rendered by the new hidden part `TmGanttPanelTabs`) above the toolbar; the five tabs are `[data-testid=panel-tab-tasks|workload|history|notifications|reports]` and open the same drawers (`sidebar-panel-*`); the Tasks tab is the chart itself.
  - *Core, additive.* `TmSplitButton` gained `Icon`, `ToggleAriaLabel` and `PrimaryAttributes` (the toggle carries no `aria-label` unless set, as before); `TmToolbarButton` gained `Badge`; `TmColumnPicker` gained `IconOnly`. None changes a default rendering (the DataTable golden snapshots are untouched).
  - *Snapshots.* `TmGanttMarkupSnapshotTests` was re-recorded on purpose for this phase (toolbar and treegrid markup); core toolbar GUID ids are normalized.
- **TmGantt phase 5: the task panel is an inspector, the history drawer sits on the component, a rollback asks first, and the Reports panel replaces the task panel.** Every new parameter is opt-in; what changes by default is the DOM and layout of the panels.
  - *Task panel footer: Cancel | Save, outside the scroller.* `div.tm-gantt-task-panel__actions` used to be the LAST child of `div.tm-gantt-task-panel__scroll` with **Save, then Cancel** (primary first, ghost second) and scrolled away with the fields. It is now a direct child of `.tm-gantt-task-panel`, after the scroller, always in view, **Cancel first, Save last (right)**; Cancel is `tm-btn-secondary` (it was `tm-btn-ghost`). The `data-testid`s `task-save` / `task-cancel` are unchanged; a test or host that clicked "the first button of the footer" or looked for the footer inside the scroller must adapt.
    ```csharp
    // before: cut.Find(".tm-gantt-task-panel__scroll .tm-gantt-task-panel__actions button:first-child")  // Save
    // after:  cut.Find(".tm-gantt-task-panel > .tm-gantt-task-panel__actions [data-testid='task-save']")
    ```
  - *Task panel sections.* The fields are grouped in `section.tm-gantt-task-panel__group[data-testid=task-section-*]` (`plan`, `progress`, `structure`, `appearance`, `description`, `attachments`, `comments`, `budget`, `timelog`, `dependencies`, plus `actions` when handled) with an `h3.tm-gantt-task-panel__group-title`. **No field was removed**; every `data-testid` (`task-title`, `task-start`, `task-end`, `task-duration`, `task-deadline`, `task-percent`, `task-estimation`, `task-timelog`, `task-milestone`, `task-parent`, `task-color-picker`, `task-description`, `attachment-list`, `comment-list`, `task-budget`, `task-actual-cost`, ...) still exists. The grid is three columns, Duration is a read-only text input (it was a `span.tm-gantt-task-panel__duration-display`), the estimate, logged-time and budget fields are `TmDecimalInput`s (`.tm-decimal-input`, a comma or a dot both parse) instead of raw `input.tm-input[type=number]`, and the percent field has a `%` suffix. Attachments are cards (`li.tm-gantt-task-panel__attachment-card`; size and upload date only when the model carries them) instead of `li.tm-gantt-task-panel__attachment-item`. The colour swatch is 32px (it was 20px) with a ring when selected.
    ```css
    /* before */ .tm-gantt-task-panel__attachment-item { … }   .tm-gantt__panel-color-swatch { width: 20px; height: 20px; }
    /* after  */ .tm-gantt-task-panel__attachment-card { … }   .tm-gantt__panel-color-swatch { width: 32px; height: 32px; }
    ```
  - *The Status field is editable.* Until now the panel could not change a task's status (`Save` copied the old one). The Status select is a draft like the Priority: **Save** raises `TmGanttTaskPanel.OnStatusChanged` (only when it differs from the task) and `TmGantt` applies it and raises its own `OnStatusChanged`, the path the board already used; Cancel reverts it.
  - *The history drawer is positioned against the component, not the viewport.* `.tm-gantt__history-drawer` was `position: fixed; height: 100vh` and covered the page; it is now `position: absolute` inside the Gantt root (`.tm-gantt { position: relative }`) and spans the component's height. A host that relied on the full-viewport panel opts back in:
    ```razor
    <!-- before: a fixed 100vh panel on the right edge of the viewport -->
    <TmGantt Items="tasks" History="history" />

    <!-- after (default): the drawer covers the Gantt only; the previous behaviour is one parameter away -->
    <TmGantt Items="tasks" History="history" HistoryDrawerPlacement="GanttHistoryDrawerPlacement.Viewport" />
    ```
    The drawer also takes focus when it opens and **Escape closes it**.
  - *Rollback asks for confirmation.* "Rollback" no longer raises `OnRollbackRequested` on the click: the drawer opens a `TmDialog` ("Roll back this change?") and raises it only on confirmation. A bUnit/E2E test that clicked `history-rollback-*` and expected the callback must confirm (`.tm-dialog-btn-ok`) too. "Time travel" is unchanged.
    ```csharp
    // before: cut.Find("[data-testid='history-rollback-e1']").Click();   // callback raised
    // after:  cut.Find("[data-testid='history-rollback-e1']").Click(); cut.Find(".tm-dialog-btn-ok").Click();
    ```
  - *One history feed.* The sidebar History panel and the drawer render the same `TmGanttHistoryList`: a typed icon in a circle, the change type, the task title (a link that selects the task and opens its panel when the task is still in the chart), the author, a **relative time** ("25 min ago", the absolute time is the `<time title>`) and, in the drawer only, Time travel / Rollback as small secondary buttons. The classes `tm-gantt__sidebar-history-row|action|task|date` are gone; `.tm-gantt__history-entry-time` is a `<time>` whose text is relative.
    ```csharp
    // before: cut.Find(".tm-gantt__sidebar-history-date").TextContent  // "6/9/2024, 10:00 AM"
    // after:  cut.Find("[data-testid='sidebar-panel-history'] .tm-gantt__history-entry-time").GetAttribute("title")  // the absolute time
    ```
  - *Task panel Delete asks first, the history drawer returns focus, the docked workload follows the timeline.* The panel's Delete action opens a `TmDialog` (`TmGantt_DeleteConfirm*`) and removes the task only on confirmation. Closing the history drawer (button or Escape) puts focus back on the control that opened it. `WorkloadPlacement="Docked"` renders only under the Day / Week / Month views (the ones with a timeline); its scroll link (`tmGantt.linkScroll`, now idempotent and returning whether a link exists) is re-established on every render and skipped, with a localized note (`TmGantt_WorkloadRangeTruncated`), when the range exceeds the 366-day axis. Attachment sizes use `TmGanttTaskPanel_SizeBytes|SizeKB|SizeMB`; `GanttHistory_CommentAdded` and the other audit actions have localized labels.
  - *Reports are a right-hand inspector.* The Reports panel is no longer one of the left-hand drawers: it renders to the right of the chart and **replaces the task panel while it is open** (one right panel at a time; closing it brings the task panel back). Cards show a type icon and a Secondary `Run` button; the report name no longer truncates.
  - *Portfolio cards.* `.tm-gantt-portfolio__project-header` is a flex row (collapse chevron, name, date range, `Tasks: N`, weighted progress bar, host actions) instead of a single text line, and the nested Gantt has no toolbar and no sidebar (`ShowToolbar="false" ShowSidebar="false"`). A card's `max-height` is 15rem (it was 240px) unless `ProjectMaxHeight` is set.
  - *Snapshots.* `TmGanttMarkupSnapshotTests.WithTaskPanel` was re-recorded on purpose (task panel markup); the normalizer now also masks per-instance `tm-decimal-*` ids.
- **TmGantt phase 6: the export, import and mapping dialogs are `TmModal`s, the filter has typed editors and a Cancel, and Import needs a valid mapping.** The public parameters of the dialogs (`IsOpen`, `OnClose`, `OnExport`, `OnImportCompleted`, `OnImportError`, `SourceColumns`, `OnImport`) are unchanged; what changes is the DOM.
  - *`.tm-gantt__dialog-overlay` is gone.* The three dialogs no longer paint their own scrim, card, header and footer; they render through the core `TmModal` (browser top layer, `role="dialog"` + `aria-modal`, the shared focus trap, Escape, focus back to the trigger, a bottom sheet on a mobile viewport). The per-dialog class (`tm-gantt__export-dialog`, `tm-gantt__import-dialog`, `tm-gantt__import-mapping-dialog`) moved from the card to the **overlay root** (`div.tm-modal-overlay`); the card is `.tm-modal` inside `.tm-focus-scope`, the title `.tm-modal-title`, the close button `.tm-modal-close`, the actions `.tm-modal-footer`. The content classes (`tm-gantt__export-*`, `__import-*`, `__mapping-*`) are kept. The global `_gantt-dialog.css` (`.tm-gantt__dialog-overlay|dialog|dialog-header|title|close|body|actions`) was deleted and removed from `tempo-blazor.css`; a host that linked it individually must drop the link, and a host that styled those classes must restyle `.tm-modal*` (or the per-dialog class on the overlay root). `.tm-gantt__dialog-close` survives only as the history drawer's close button.
    ```csharp
    // before: page.Locator(".tm-gantt__dialog-overlay")      page.Locator(".tm-gantt__dialog-close")   page.Locator(".tm-gantt__dialog-actions button").First
    // after:  page.Locator(".tm-modal-overlay.tm-gantt__import-dialog")   page.Locator(".tm-modal-close")   page.Locator("[data-testid='import-submit']")
    ```
    The footer order is **Cancel, then the primary action** (it was primary first); the primary buttons have `data-testid` `export-submit` / `import-submit` / `mapping-submit`, the cancel ones `export-cancel` / `import-cancel` / `mapping-cancel`. `TmGantt.razor` also got one more internal part, `TmGanttFilterBar` (hidden from the editor), so the file stays under 400 lines.
  - *Export.* The format tiles are a `role="radiogroup"` of native radios inside `label.tm-gantt__export-format-option` (min 120 x 96 px, a large icon, the checked tile has the primary border and tint); the radio input is visually hidden but focusable. The paper size / orientation / critical path / today line / workload / zoom options apply to PDF and PNG; Excel offers a column picker instead. The select and checkbox are now `TmSelect` / `TmCheckbox` (the old `select.tm-gantt__export-select` is `.tm-gantt__export-select select`).
  - *Import.* The source tabs are an ARIA tablist (`role="tab"`, `aria-selected`, `aria-controls`, roving `tabindex`, Left / Right / Home / End, focus follows the selection) over a `role="tabpanel"`. The file picker is an input group: **Choose file**, the chosen name ("No file chosen" until one is picked) and a **Remove file** ✕ (`data-testid="import-remove-file"`); a supported-formats hint sits under it. **Switching between the Excel and MS Project tabs drops the chosen file** (an `.xlsx` must never reach the MS Project importer). The error box is a `TmAlert` (`tm-alert tm-alert--error tm-gantt-import__error`, `data-testid="import-error"`, still `role="alert"`). The WebKit-safe native click listener on the chooser (N204) is unchanged; the input is looked up at click time so Remove file can recreate it.
    ```csharp
    // before: cut.FindAll(".tm-gantt__import-tab")[2].Click();   // a plain button row
    // after:  cut.FindAll("[role='tab']")[2].Click();             // or select it with the Arrow keys
    ```
  - *Mapping: Import is disabled until the mapping is valid.* The mapping used to import whatever was (or was not) selected. **Import now stays disabled until Task (title), Start and End or Duration are mapped**; two columns mapped to one field show a warning (the import is still allowed). The columns are pre-mapped from their header names. Each select is a `TmSelect` (`[data-testid='mapping-select-<column>'] select`), labelled by a `<label for>` with the source column name; the dialog has a subtitle. Predecessor, Assignees and WBS are new targets (importing them is not wired into the Excel importer yet).
    ```csharp
    // before: cut.Find("[data-testid='mapping-select-Name']").Change("Title");        // a bare <select>
    // after:  cut.Find("[data-testid='mapping-select-Name'] select").Change("Title");  // TmSelect wraps it
    ```
  - *Filter.* The value editor follows the field: Status and Priority are a select of the enum members (`GanttStatus_*` / `GanttPriority_*` labels, never typed), Start / End / Deadline a date input, Title text. The operators follow the field type too (Status / Priority: equals, does not equal; dates: equals, before, after, plus is empty / not empty for Deadline). The footer is **Clear all filters** (a link on the left) | **Cancel** | **Apply**; **Apply raises the whole set, Cancel throws the unapplied edits away**, and Clear all only clears the rows being edited until Apply (it used to apply an empty set at once). "+ Add filter" is its own row, an outline button. Active filters are chips (`TmFilterChip`) in `div.tm-gantt__filter-chips` under the toolbar; the Escape key and `OnClose` are unchanged for the inline panel.
    ```csharp
    // before: cut.Find("input.tm-gantt__filter-value").Change("Done");     // Status was free text
    // after:  cut.Find("select.tm-gantt__filter-value").Change("Done");    // enum member name
    ```
  - *Snapshots.* `TmGanttMarkupSnapshotTests.ListViewSidebarFilter` was re-recorded on purpose (the filter footer).
- **TmGantt phase 7: the Gantt measures its own container, the task panel can be a side sheet, and a finger can pan, link and open the menu.** Everything below is opt-in or additive except the three items flagged *Breaking*.
  - *`LayoutMode` replaces `ContainerWidth` (Breaking: `[Obsolete]`).* `TmGantt.LayoutMode` (`TmLayoutMode`, default `Auto`) measures the Gantt's **own** container (desktop from 1024 px, tablet from 640 px, otherwise mobile) through the core `TmLayoutObserver`, stamps `data-layout` + `tm-gantt--desktop|tablet|mobile` on the root and raises `ResolvedLayoutChanged`. The root is now `div.tm-layout.tm-layout--no-container > div.tm-gantt` (the chart root stays the one CSS size container, `container-name: tm-gantt`). `ContainerWidth` is `[Obsolete]`: it still overrides the Fit-to-screen measurement and, while `LayoutMode` is `Auto`, is classified like a measurement (900 → tablet), so existing hosts keep working.
    ```razor
    <!-- before: a host that knew its width told the Gantt -->
    <TmGantt Items="tasks" ContainerWidth="900" />
    <!-- after: the Gantt measures itself; pin a layout only for tests / forced presentations -->
    <TmGantt Items="tasks" />
    <TmGantt Items="tasks" LayoutMode="TmLayoutMode.Tablet" />
    ```
    `GanttFilterPanelMode.Auto` is wired now: a dialog on a tablet or narrower container, the inline strip on a desktop one (it was always inline).
  - *Tablet toolbar.* On a tablet container the toolbar is two `TmToolbar` rows (`.tm-gantt__toolbar--two-rows`; row 1 create / structure / time, row 2 panels / data / settings), each `Overflow=Menu`, so a command that does not fit leaves into its "More" menu and the toolbar never scrolls horizontally. Desktop keeps the single wrapping bar. Hosts and tests key off `data-tm-group` and the unchanged `data-testid`s.
  - *`TaskPanelMode` (new, default `Inline` = today).* `Inline` is the in-flow column at every width; `Overlay` presents the task panel (and the Reports inspector) as a core `TmSidePanel` side sheet at every width; `Auto` is `Inline` on a desktop container and the sheet on a tablet or narrower one. The sheet shows the task panel as tabs **Detail | Attachments | Comments | History** (`TmGanttTaskPanel.Tabbed`; the History tab lists the audit entries whose `EntityRef.EntityId` is the task, a draft on the Detail tab survives a tab switch and is flagged "Unsaved changes"). On a tablet or narrower container (or with a sheet presentation) **at most one right-hand surface is open**: opening the task panel, the Reports inspector or the history drawer closes the other two. A tap on a row or a bar opens the sheet — a finger or a pen tap only: a mouse click just selects (the sheet would cover the chart and swallow the row's inline double-click; Enter on the focused row opens the panel from the keyboard).
    ```razor
    <!-- before: the panel is always a column that squeezes the chart -->
    <TmGantt Items="tasks" ShowTaskPanel="true" />
    <!-- after: a column on desktop, a tabbed side sheet on a tablet -->
    <TmGantt Items="tasks" ShowTaskPanel="true" TaskPanelMode="GanttTaskPanelMode.Auto" />
    ```
  - *`GanttViewDensity.Touch` (additive).* 44 px rows; the tree rows and the timeline rows share one height (`data-density` on the root). `Comfortable` (0) and `Compact` (1) keep their values; the view-settings menu offers "Touch".
  - *Breaking: mouse handlers became pointer sessions (DOM without `@onmouse*`).* The timeline no longer renders `@onmousedown/move/up/leave`, and the dependency handles no longer render `@onmousedown/@onmouseup`. The pan (mouse only; a finger or a pen scrolls natively), the dependency drag (mouse, pen **and finger**) and the touch long-press are sessions of the core `pointer-drag.js`, attached by `gantt.js` (`tmGantt.attachTimeline / attachTree`, keyed by an id, no .NET interop per move; Escape or `pointercancel` rolls a gesture back; a dependency drag draws a ghost line with the bar under the pointer highlighted and auto-scrolls at the timeline edge). A finger or a pen scrolls the timeline natively (`touch-action: pan-x pan-y`; the CSS applies to the pen too, so a pen drag is a scroll and never the pan). Bars, milestones, dependency handles (`data-task-id`, `data-dep-end`) and tree rows (`data-task-id`) carry the hooks. A test that dispatched mouse events on the timeline must call the `[JSInvokable]` equivalents instead:
    ```csharp
    // before: cut.Find(".tm-gantt__timeline").MouseDown(new MouseEventArgs { ClientX = 10 });  cut.Instance.StartDepDrag("1", true); cut.Instance.OnDepDrop("2");
    // after:  await cut.InvokeAsync(() => cut.Instance.OnDependencyDragCompleted("1", fromEnd: true, "2"));   // what gantt.js reports; StartDepDrag / OnDepDrop still work
    ```
  - *Breaking: the tree's HTML5 drag-and-drop is turned off while a finger is down.* A touch pointer sets `draggable="false"` on the pressed row (restored on release), so the native long-press drag never fights the long-press menu; mouse and pen keep HTML5 drag-and-drop. The grip is hidden on a coarse pointer.
  - *Long-press = context menu; reorder without dragging (WCAG 2.5.7).* A 500 ms touch hold on a bar or a tree row opens the same context menu a right-click opens (anchored at the finger; the lifting finger's click does not dismiss it). The menu gained **Move up / Move down**, `Alt+ArrowUp/Down` on a focused row does the same, and the tabbed task panel's "More actions" offers both (`GanttTaskAction.MoveUp/MoveDown`, additive). All go through `OnTaskReordered` (`Before`/`After` the neighbour sibling) and are announced on a polite live region. A tablet shows a one-line instruction (`TmGantt_TouchHint`) on a coarse pointer.
  - *Script requirement.* `gantt.js` now imports the core `pointer-drag.js` and `pointer-gesture.js` from the folder it was loaded from, so `_content/Tempo.Blazor/js/` must be served as a whole (a per-file CSP hash must list both modules; the `<script>` tag list does not change):
    ```html
    <!-- before and after: unchanged -->
    <script src="_content/Tempo.Blazor/js/gantt.js"></script>
    ```
  - *Snapshots and DOM.* `TmGanttMarkupSnapshotTests` was re-recorded on purpose (the observer wrapper, `data-layout`, `data-task-id`; the observer's per-instance id is normalized).
  - *Review fixes.* The overlays render **outside** the chart root: `.tm-gantt` is a CSS size container (`container-type: inline-size`), and a container is the containing block of every fixed-position descendant, so the context menu (anchored at clientX/Y), the task/Reports `TmSidePanel` sheets and the export / import / filter / confirm dialogs were confined to (and clipped by) the chart. They are siblings of `.tm-gantt` inside the `TmLayoutObserver` `LayoutContent` now (the observer root is `tm-layout--no-container`); a host or test that queried them as descendants of `.tm-gantt` must query them page-wide. `ShowTaskPanel` is no longer assigned inside the component: internal changes raise the new `ShowTaskPanelChanged` (two-way; the parameter itself is read-only for the Gantt), and `ReconcilePanels` runs only when the parameter value or the resolved layout actually changes. Closing the task sheet over a dirty draft asks first — a localized **"Discard changes?" / Discard / Keep editing** dialog (`TmGantt_DiscardChanges*`, new keys in all four languages); Discard closes the sheet, Keep editing keeps it open with the draft. The tabbed task panel's **Move up / Move down** take `CanMoveUp` / `CanMoveDown` (the buttons disable at the row's edge; the pair hides when no reorder handler exists upstream). `gantt.js`'s `attachTimeline` / `attachTree` resolve `true` only after the sessions registered (`false` when the pointer helpers could not load), and `TmGantt` remembers its registration key only then, so a failed phase is retried on a later render instead of remembered as done. Alt+Up/Down is the shared `attachKeyboardMove`'s job again with an `accept` predicate: gantt.js passes `accept: e => !e.target.closest('input, select, textarea')`, so the chord moves the text caret inside an inline editor instead of reordering the row.
- **TmGantt phase 8: a mobile container is read-mostly (decision G2) — viewing, status / percent and adding a task.** On a container below 768 px (`LayoutMode` resolving Mobile) the chart becomes a reading surface: one pinned Title column with a two-line cell (title over the date range, 56 px rows in the tree and the timeline), the full-width Day | Week | Month segment plus chips (Sort by date | Fit to screen | Filter with an active-filter dot), a bottom `TmMobileActionBar` (Add task | Expand all | Collapse all | More) and a "More" bottom sheet (Zoom in / out, Task panel, History, Reports, View settings). Every right-hand surface is a full-height `TmSidePanel` bottom sheet: the task detail is read-only except **Status** and **Percent** (sticky Cancel | Save footer, a localized "Full editing is available on a larger screen." hint, the new `TaskBreadcrumb` slot in the sheet header), adding a task opens a minimal sheet (name, start, end), the filter editor is the dialog (bottom sheet with 44 px, two-line condition rows and the sticky Apply), history is a read-only sheet and Reports are run-only cards. **Breaking (mobile container only):** the data and structure commands are not offered — export, import and column mapping are absent from the chrome (a host that opens their dialogs programmatically still gets them as fullscreen `TmModal`s, `MobilePresentation.Auto` was already wired), reorder (drag, Move up / down, Alt+Arrow) and the dependency drag are disabled, the timeline renders no dependency handles and the tree rows are `draggable="false"` (no grip), the progress % shows beside every bar, the sidebar rail is replaced by the "More" sheet, and the desktop zoom slider is replaced by the zoom entries (a host or test that queried `gantt-export-btn` / `gantt-import-btn` / the zoom slider inside a mobile container must pin `LayoutMode="TmLayoutMode.Tablet"` (or Desktop) for the full editing chrome):
    ```razor
    <!-- before: a phone container rendered the desktop chrome squeezed -->
    <TmGantt Items="tasks" />                                  <!-- on a phone: everything, squeezed -->

    <!-- after: a phone container is read-mostly; a host that wants full editing pins tablet -->
    <TmGantt Items="tasks" />                                  <!-- on a phone: viewing + status / % / add -->
    <TmGantt Items="tasks" LayoutMode="TmLayoutMode.Tablet" /> <!-- forced full editing chrome -->
    ```
  New localized strings: `TmGantt_MobileSortByDate`, `TmGantt_MobileFullEditingHint`, `TmGantt_MobileMenuStatus`, `TmGantt_MobileMenuPercent`, `TmGantt_MobileAddNameRequired`, `TmGantt_WorkloadAllocatedOfCapacity` (en / cs / sk / fr). The workload view gains `LayoutMode` (mobile: the week of today, one person row with a utilization bar, the person column pinned) and the portfolio gains `LayoutMode` (mobile: summary line "Tasks: N • start – end", the weighted percent and a mini-gantt of bars only, tap = `OnProjectSelected`). The view-settings list moved into its own part `TmGanttViewSettings` (same markup and `data-testid`s, popover styles in `TmGanttViewSettings.razor.css`) so the More sheet can reuse it.
- **Scheduler redesign (phases 1–8c): the calendar loads what it draws, and it lays out from its own container.** `TmScheduler` now has one range for the query, the markup and the title (Timeline is one day, Agenda is `AgendaDays`, default 30), `EventTemplate` reaches every view, the toolbar is the core `TmToolbar` with named `data-tm-group`s, today's column draws a current-time line, and `LayoutMode="Auto"` renders the mobile layout under 640px. The side panel and the event detail are host slots; the mobile action bar is opt-in (`None`). Touch move and resize go through the shared `pointer-drag.js`, which `scheduler.js` loads with a dynamic import, and Alt+arrow is the non-drag alternative. The contract is [docs/scheduler.md](docs/scheduler.md). Every breaking change of the plan is listed in this section and under [Breaking / Migration (continued)](#breaking--migration-continued) with a before/after: the range and the title, `FirstDayOfWeek`, "+N more", the tinted cards, the toolbar, the now indicator, and the layout of a narrow container.

- **`TmScheduler` "+N more" label is a plural family.** Before, the overflow button formatted the plain key `TmScheduler_More`, so a host that overrode only that key kept its wording. After, the button uses `Loc.Plural("TmScheduler_More", n)`, and a host that reworded the plain key must override the family. The built-in tables already do: Czech "+1 další / +2 další / +5 dalších", Slovak "+1 ďalšia / +2 ďalšie / +5 ďalších", French "+1 autre / +2 autres", English unchanged. A custom JSON table or an `ITmLocalizer` override migrates the same way — the plain key is now only the fallback:
  ```json
  // before: one key, the host's own wording
  "TmScheduler_More": "+{0} more"

  // after: the forms the host's language needs (cs and sk also need _Few and _Many)
  "TmScheduler_More_One": "+{0} more",
  "TmScheduler_More_Other": "+{0} more"
  ```

- **`TmScheduler` narrows its own container, and a container under 640px now renders the mobile layout.** Before, the scheduler always rendered the desktop toolbar and the desktop view markup, whatever the container measured. After, `LayoutMode="Auto"` (the default) classifies the scheduler's own container: under 640px it renders the compact toolbar (`‹ title ›`, a view dropdown, and a Today icon button only when `MobileActionBar` is `None` — with `Auto` the action bar owns Today), a week date strip and a day resource picker; 640–1023px is one toolbar row whose More menu absorbs what does not fit (decision SCH-TABLET-ONE-ROW — there is no second row). A host that must keep the desktop markup at every width pins it:

  ```razor
  <!-- before: the only markup, at every width -->
  <TmScheduler View="TmScheduleViewType.Week" />

  <!-- after: opt out of the container classification -->
  <TmScheduler View="TmScheduleViewType.Week" LayoutMode="TmLayoutMode.Desktop" />
  ```

  The root gained a wrapper, `div.tm-layout.tm-scheduler-layout`, and the root itself carries `data-layout`. Print pins that layout back to desktop, so a phone prints the full week. **Give the scheduler a bounded height.** The root is `height: 100%`, which only resolves when an ancestor has a height; an unbounded host grows with the day. On a mobile layout the time-grid scroller is capped at `70dvh` so the action bar stays reachable, but a host that wants the grid to fill a panel should size the ancestor:

  ```css
  .scheduler-host { height: 640px; }
  ```

- **`TmScheduler` print from a phone is guaranteed through the toolbar, not through Ctrl+P.** The toolbar Print action calls `PrintAsync`, which awaits the desktop re-render before `window.print()`. A browser Ctrl+P raises `beforeprint`, and the component re-renders on it, but that re-render is async, so the browser may print the mobile markup (the focus day and its neighbours) before the seven columns arrive. A host that must print the full week from a phone calls `PrintAsync`.
- **`TmCalendarView` and `TmCalendarGrid` are not an ARIA grid, and a day announces a long date.** Before, `div.tm-calendar` carried `role="grid"`, `div.tm-cal-nav` carried `role="row"`, each weekday header carried `aria-label` on a generic div, and a day's accessible name was the short date (`"d"`). After, both roles are gone, the header is an `<abbr title="Monday">` (no `aria-label`), a selected day is `aria-pressed="true"`, today is `aria-current="date"`, and the day's name is the long date (`"D"`, current culture). Every in-month day is its own tab stop (`tabindex="0"`); other-month and disabled days are `tabindex="-1"`. There is no roving tabindex — Tab walks the month. A selector that matched `[role="grid"]` or `[role="row"]` inside the mini-month matches nothing now — select `.tm-calendar` and `.tm-cal-nav`. An assertion keyed on the short date (`button[aria-label="7/10/2026"]`) must use the long date.

  ```html
  <!-- before -->
  <div class="tm-calendar" role="grid">
    <div class="tm-cal-nav" role="row">…</div>
    <div class="tm-cal-header-cell" aria-label="Mon">Mon</div>
    <button class="tm-cal-day" aria-label="7/10/2026">7</button>
  </div>

  <!-- after -->
  <div class="tm-calendar">
    <div class="tm-cal-nav">…</div>
    <div class="tm-cal-header-cell"><abbr title="Monday">Mon</abbr></div>
    <button class="tm-cal-day" aria-label="Wednesday, July 10, 2026" aria-pressed="false">7</button>
  </div>
  ```

- **`TmMultiSelect` listbox moved onto the options container, and its id is referenced only while options render.** Before, the popup root carried `role="listbox"`, `aria-multiselectable="true"`, `id="{Id}-listbox"` and `Title`, and the combobox always emitted `aria-owns="{Id}-listbox"`. After, the listbox is `div.tm-multiselect__options`, which renders only when options exist. The combobox and the filter emit `aria-controls` (not `aria-owns`) only then, and `aria-activedescendant` only when that id is in the document and the index is in range. Loading, error and empty states are siblings (`role="status"` / `role="alert"`). A grouped listbox owns `role="group"` children named by their header (`role="presentation"`); an empty group key announces the localized "Other". The popup root carries no `Title`. A selector `#{Id}-listbox` matches only while options render. The popup root keeps `display: flex`.

  ```html
  <!-- before: the panel root was the listbox, always referenced -->
  <div role="combobox" aria-owns="fruits-listbox"></div>
  <div class="tm-overlay-panel tm-multiselect__popup" role="listbox" id="fruits-listbox">
    <div class="tm-multiselect__filter">…</div>
    <div class="tm-multiselect__options">…</div>
  </div>

  <!-- after: the options container is the listbox, referenced only while it renders -->
  <div role="combobox" aria-controls="fruits-listbox"></div>
  <div class="tm-overlay-panel tm-multiselect__popup">
    <div class="tm-multiselect__filter">…</div>
    <div class="tm-multiselect__options" role="listbox" id="fruits-listbox" aria-multiselectable="true">…</div>
  </div>
  ```

- **Other-month day ink no longer fades.** Before, `.tm-cal-day--other-month` set `opacity: 0.5`, which blended gray-500 down to 1.96:1 on a white surface. After, the shared rule uses `--tm-text-tertiary` at full opacity; an other-month day that is also in range uses `--tm-text-secondary`; selected, range-start and range-end keep `--tm-cal-selected-fg`.

- **Scheduler toolbar class names.** The desktop toolbar is now the core `TmToolbar`, so the hand-rolled button classes are gone. `.tm-scheduler-toolbar-nav-btn` remains, but only on the compact (mobile) row. `.tm-scheduler-toolbar-today-btn` and `.tm-scheduler-toolbar-add` are removed; Today and New event are `button.tm-toolbar-btn`, and Print lives in the More menu (`button.tm-toolbar-more`, group `data-tm-group="export"`). A selector that matched `.tm-scheduler-toolbar-today-btn` or `.tm-scheduler-toolbar-add` matches nothing now — use `[data-testid="scheduler-today"]` and `[data-testid="scheduler-add"]`.

- **The Spreadsheet Name Manager / Named Range Edit / Hyperlink dialogs are modal overlays, and the validation alerts are `alertdialog`s.** Before, the three dialogs rendered as an unstyled `<div>` in the document flow, *under* the grid (they had no stylesheet rule at all), and the validation alerts were anonymous `<div class="tm-spreadsheet-alert">` boxes with a backdrop click that dismissed even a Stop-style error. After, each dialog is an overlay card on the shared `.tm-spreadsheet-dialog-backdrop` / `.tm-spreadsheet-dialog` wrappers (plus a per-dialog hook class) inside `_spreadsheet.css`, wrapped in the core `TmFocusScope`, which supplies the dialog contract: `role="dialog"`, `aria-modal`, `aria-labelledby` (the card's `<h2>` title), the initial focus on a real control (the name field, the address field, the active name row or the New button, the URL field), the document-level Escape and the focus restore on close. The restore target is the grid root (`TmFocusScope.RestoreFocusTargetId`), not the toolbar button that opened the dialog, so closing any of them puts focus back into the spreadsheet; the Named Range Edit dialog keeps the default (back to whatever opened it inside the Name Manager). Both validation alerts moved into one component, `TmSpreadsheetValidationAlert`, which wraps the same primitive with `role="alertdialog"`, `aria-labelledby` (title) and `aria-describedby` (message): it focuses its primary action when it opens, Escape closes it, closing restores focus to the grid through the same scope-owned restore target, and a Stop-style error **ignores the backdrop click** — the value stays blocked and only the primary action (or Escape) dismisses it. The warning/information confirm keeps its backdrop-to-cancel. There is no host API for dismissing a Stop error: it is dismissed by the alert's own primary action. The E2E classes `__btn--ok`, `__btn--close` and `.tm-spreadsheet-name-manager__toolbar` are unchanged.

  **Ids and the interim classes are not a contract.** Every element id these surfaces introduce is per instance (`spreadsheet-name-manager-title-{suffix}`, `spreadsheet-validation-alert-primary-{suffix}`, …) and may change between builds; the per-dialog `__backdrop` / card classes are interim as well, because phase 3 of the redesign plan replaces the markup with the core `TmModal`. Key off the roles instead — `[role='dialog']` / `[role='alertdialog']` inside `.tm-spreadsheet` — and the stable E2E hooks listed above.

  ```html
  <!-- before: in-flow block, no role/name, no overlay, backdrop click dismisses a Stop error -->
  <div class="tm-spreadsheet-hyperlink">
    <div class="tm-spreadsheet-hyperlink__header">…</div>
  </div>
  <div class="tm-spreadsheet-dialog-backdrop" onclick="dismiss">
    <div class="tm-spreadsheet-alert">
      <h4 class="tm-spreadsheet-alert__title">Invalid value</h4>
      <button class="tm-btn tm-btn-primary tm-btn-md">OK</button>
    </div>
  </div>

  <!-- after: shared overlay wrappers + core focus scope; the alert ignores the backdrop -->
  <div class="tm-spreadsheet-dialog-backdrop tm-spreadsheet-hyperlink__backdrop">
    <div class="tm-focus-scope" role="dialog" aria-modal="true"
         aria-labelledby="spreadsheet-hyperlink-title-{suffix}"
         data-restore-target="spreadsheet-grid-{suffix}">
      <div class="tm-spreadsheet-dialog tm-spreadsheet-hyperlink">
        <h2 class="tm-spreadsheet-hyperlink__title" id="spreadsheet-hyperlink-title-{suffix}">Hyperlink</h2>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
  <div class="tm-spreadsheet-dialog-backdrop tm-spreadsheet-validation-alert__backdrop">
    <div class="tm-focus-scope" role="alertdialog" aria-modal="true"
         aria-labelledby="spreadsheet-validation-alert-title-{suffix}"
         aria-describedby="spreadsheet-validation-alert-message-{suffix}"
         data-restore-target="spreadsheet-grid-{suffix}">
      <div class="tm-spreadsheet-dialog tm-spreadsheet-alert">
        <h2 class="tm-spreadsheet-alert__title" id="spreadsheet-validation-alert-title-{suffix}">Invalid value</h2>
        <div class="tm-spreadsheet-alert__actions"><button class="tm-btn tm-btn-primary tm-btn-md">Confirm</button></div>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
  ```

- **`TmSpreadsheet` paints from tokens: the canvas, the dialogs and the chrome follow the palette, dark mode and the indigo theme.** Before, the package shipped literals that are what rendered, so no theme reached the grid: `buildPalette` kept a hardcoded blue selection wash (`rgba(37, 99, 235, 0.12)`) and six hardcoded formula-reference colours, the active auto-filter glyph was `#ffffff`, the validation circles `#e53935`, a hyperlink's ink `#2563EB`, and seven scoped dialog stylesheets carried hex colours plus hex fallbacks (`var(--tm-color-surface, #fff)`) with `z-index: 1100` and `font-size: 13px`. After, the root declares the component tokens (`--tm-spreadsheet-header-bg/-text/-active-bg/-active-text/-font`, `--tm-spreadsheet-gridline`, `--tm-spreadsheet-selection-border/-fill/-fill-alpha`, `--tm-spreadsheet-ref-0..5`) derived from core semantic tokens only — the header gutter reads `--tm-color-surface-secondary` (the same token the data table header row uses, gray-50 in light and #0f172a in dark), so the header strip is a surface of its own instead of the white cell background, and the canvas reads them through `buildPalette` — so the selection wash follows `--tm-color-primary` (dark and indigo included), the formula references follow the categorical palette, and the header labels use `--tm-font-sans` instead of a monospace literal. A host overrides any single token on `.tm-spreadsheet`; nothing in the package is a literal any more (the strict token audit's package baseline is **0**). The dialog deltas are tokenized 1:1 (radius `--tm-radius-card`/`--tm-radius-control`, text `--tm-text-*`, layers `--tm-z-modal`/`--tm-z-dropdown`/`--tm-z-popover`), and the Find/Replace input's soft glow (`--tm-shadow-focus`, 1.62:1) became the two-layer `--tm-focus-ring` (5.17:1) with a forced-colors outline.

  ```css
  /* before: the fallback is what renders, forever */
  .tm-spreadsheet-sort { background: var(--tm-color-surface, #fff); border-radius: 10px; box-shadow: 0 16px 40px rgba(15, 23, 42, 0.28); }

  /* after: a component token on the root, derived from the core token */
  .tm-spreadsheet { --tm-spreadsheet-header-bg: var(--tm-color-surface-elevated); }
  .tm-spreadsheet-sort { background: var(--tm-color-surface); border-radius: var(--tm-radius-card); box-shadow: var(--tm-shadow-xl); }
  ```

- **`TmSpreadsheet` now has a grid density, and its default changes the look on a touch device.** New `Density` parameter (`SpreadsheetDensity.Auto` default, `Compact`, `Comfortable`). `Auto` resolves to `Comfortable` on a coarse pointer (`pointer: coarse`) and to `Compact` everywhere else, so a tablet or phone renders taller rows (1.5x), larger cell text (1.25x), a bigger fill handle and larger header filter buttons **without any host code** — this is the visual change a mouse host does not see. The scale is render-only: `RowHeight`, a per-row custom height, `SpreadsheetSheet.DefaultRowHeight` and every XLSX height keep their values, so a workbook round-trips untouched. A host that must keep the old look on touch pins it:

  ```razor
  <!-- before: the only density there was -->
  <TmSpreadsheet RowHeight="20" />

  <!-- after: opt out of the touch comfort -->
  <TmSpreadsheet Density="SpreadsheetDensity.Compact" />
  ```

  The canvas grid root carries `data-density="compact|comfortable"` so a test or a host style can key off the resolved density. A host that reads pixel geometry must expect 30px rows on a touch device instead of 20px (zoom 100%). A row resize (the drag in the row header and the "Set row height" dialog) converts back to model pixels — `rendered ÷ (zoom × density row scale)`, the dialog shows the stored model height — so a comfortable grid never writes 1.5x heights into the workbook (the 150% zoom variant of the same bug is fixed alongside).

- **`TmSpreadsheet` highlights the active row and column header.** Before, every header painted the same elevated surface and the selection was only visible inside the grid. After, the row/column headers of the selection are tinted with `--tm-spreadsheet-header-active-bg`, their labels use `--tm-spreadsheet-header-active-text`, and a 2px `--tm-spreadsheet-selection-border` rail sits on the grid edge of each (a second, non-colour signal for forced-colors and colour-blind readers). The tint follows the selection range, and a selection change repaints ONLY the old and the new header strips (two dirty rects, one header-layer pass) — the header layer is never repainted wholesale for a selection. A host that overrode `.tm-spreadsheet-header-cell` colours now has to override the tokens: `.tm-spreadsheet-header-cell` is the DOM grid's class, the canvas header is painted from the tokens above.

- **`TmSpreadsheet` Full mode paints the workspace and lifts its chrome as cards.** Before, `Mode=Full` and `Mode=Embedded` shared one flat surface with 1px separators. After, the Full root carries `tm-spreadsheet--workspace` (background `--tm-bg-workspace`, a small gap and padding) and the ribbon, formula bar, grid, sheet tabs and status bar become cards (`--tm-radius-card`, `--tm-shadow-card`), while `Mode=Embedded` (the Notion block, a modal host) carries `tm-spreadsheet--chrome-flat` and keeps the flat, gapless chrome. A host selector that matched `.tm-spreadsheet` to override the background keeps working (the modifier is a second class, not a wrapper); a host that measured the grid's offset from the root must expect the workspace padding (8px) to be part of it.

- **The Spreadsheet Custom Filter's first operator select is named by its own role, not by the dialog title.** Before, that `<select>` carried `aria-label="Custom filter"` (the dialog title repeated on a control), so a screen-reader user heard the same name on the dialog and on the field. After, it reads `TmSpreadsheet_CustomFilter_FirstOperator` ("First condition operator"), and the four operand fields and the second operator carry their own names (`…_FirstValue`, `…_FirstValueTo`, `…_SecondOperator`, `…_SecondValue`, `…_SecondValueTo`). A host that overrode the visible dialog title to reword that select must override the new key instead; an automated check that asserted `aria-label="Custom filter"` on the select now matches the dialog container only.

  ```html
  <!-- before: the select repeated the dialog title -->
  <div class="tm-spreadsheet-custom-filter" role="dialog" aria-label="Custom filter">
    <select class="tm-spreadsheet-custom-filter__op" aria-label="Custom filter">…</select>

  <!-- after: dialog and field each carry their own name -->
  <div class="tm-spreadsheet-custom-filter" role="dialog" aria-label="Custom filter">
    <select class="tm-spreadsheet-custom-filter__op" aria-label="First condition operator">…</select>
  ```

- **The Spreadsheet Format Cells category picker is an ARIA listbox with a roving tabindex.** Before, the eight number categories were `<div class="tm-fcd__listbox-item">` boxes with only `@onclick` — not reachable or operable from the keyboard. After, the container is `role="listbox"` named by `aria-labelledby` (the id it points at is per instance, so the label id is **not** a contract), and it carries no `tabindex` and no `aria-activedescendant`: the roving tabindex lives on the options, where the single tab stop is the **selected** one (`tabindex="0"`, all others `-1`). Each option is `role="option"` with `aria-selected="true|false"`. ↑/↓/Home/End move the selection and the DOM focus with it (so the option scrolls into view), a click selects the option and focuses it, and Ctrl+Enter still applies the dialog from it. Consumers key off `[role='listbox'] [role='option']` (or the unchanged `.tm-fcd__listbox-item` class); the removed `#tm-fcd-category-list` container id, its `aria-activedescendant` and the old fixed option ids match nothing now.

  ```html
  <!-- before -->
  <div class="tm-fcd__listbox">
    <div class="tm-fcd__listbox-item tm-fcd__listbox-item--selected">General</div>
  </div>

  <!-- after: the container is named but not focusable; the selected OPTION is the tab stop -->
  <div class="tm-fcd__listbox" role="listbox" aria-labelledby="spreadsheet-fcd-category-label-{suffix}">
    <div class="tm-fcd__listbox-item tm-fcd__listbox-item--selected"
         role="option" tabindex="0" aria-selected="true">General</div>
    <div class="tm-fcd__listbox-item" role="option" tabindex="-1" aria-selected="false">Number</div>
  </div>
  ```

- **The Spreadsheet dialogs' element ids are per instance — except the form fields the E2E lane keys off.** Every id this phase adds (dialog titles, the validation alert's title / message / primary / cancel, the listbox label, the Name Manager title / New button / rows, the insert-image title and URL field) is stamped with a per-instance suffix and may change between builds, so none of them is a selector contract; key off the roles (`[role='dialog']`, `[role='alertdialog']`, `[role='listbox'] [role='option']`) instead. The **pre-existing** form-field ids `#nr-name`, `#nr-refers`, `#nr-scope`, `#nr-sheet`, `#nr-comment`, `#hl-type`, `#hl-target`, `#hl-subject`, `#hl-display` and `#hl-tooltip` stay stable on purpose — the published E2E lane fills them — and at most one instance of each dialog is open at a time, so they cannot collide.

- **Every Spreadsheet dialog rides the core `TmModal` — the package no longer paints a backdrop of its own.** Before, the package shipped **three** dialog families: five dialogs with their own scoped backdrop (`__backdrop` + `position: fixed` + `z-index` in the component stylesheet: Sort, Custom Filter, Remove Duplicates, Paste Special, Text to Columns), three dialogs on an interim shared `.tm-spreadsheet-dialog-backdrop` / `.tm-spreadsheet-dialog` wrapper (Name Manager, Named Range Edit, Hyperlink), and three inline blocks inside `TmSpreadsheet.razor` (`tm-fcd` Format Cells, `tm-dvd` Data Validation, and the Insert Image markup plus both validation alerts). Each family had its own header, its own close affordance, its own Escape handling and its own stacking band — two open dialogs dimmed the page twice and Escape depended on focus-trap ordering. After, **all of them** render `TmModal` (the same primitive as the rest of the library): the modal owns the fixed overlay, the dialog role, `aria-modal`, the accessible name, the initial focus, the document-level Escape, the focus restore and the mobile presentation. Gone from the package stylesheets: `.tm-spreadsheet-dialog-backdrop`, `.tm-spreadsheet-dialog`, `.tm-spreadsheet-dialog__title/__body/__actions/__label/__input`, `.tm-spreadsheet-dialog-scope`, the six `__backdrop` hooks and every dialog-card rule (`width`, `padding`, `box-shadow`, `border-radius`). The last two, the canvas grid's **column width** and **row height** dialogs (`.tm-spreadsheet-resize-dialog`, opened from the cell context menu), had kept a private `.tm-spreadsheet-resize-dialog-backdrop` with a literal `z-index` and no focus trap; they now render the same frame (`Title` = the old label, the numeric input in the body, Cancel / Apply in the footer, `RestoreFocusTargetId` = the grid root) and keep the `.tm-spreadsheet-resize-dialog__input` / `__btn--ok` / `__btn--cancel` hooks. The dialog's own root class moved from the card to the **overlay** — `.tm-spreadsheet-sort`, `.tm-spreadsheet-custom-filter`, `.tm-spreadsheet-dedup`, `.tm-spreadsheet-pastespecial`, `.tm-spreadsheet-t2c`, `.tm-spreadsheet-name-manager`, `.tm-spreadsheet-named-range-edit`, `.tm-spreadsheet-hyperlink`, `.tm-fcd`, `.tm-dvd`, the new `.tm-spreadsheet-insert-image` and `.tm-spreadsheet-alert` — so a host or an E2E spec that located a dialog by that class still finds exactly one element per dialog (now the fixed overlay instead of the card). The **card** is the modal's: `.tm-modal` inside that root; the title is `.tm-modal-title` inside `.tm-modal-header`; the close affordance is `.tm-modal-close`; the footer bar is `.tm-modal-footer`.

  ```razor
  <!-- before: the package's own overlay wrapper; the card carried the dialog class -->
  <div class="tm-spreadsheet-dialog-backdrop tm-spreadsheet-name-manager__backdrop">
    <TmFocusScope ...><div class="tm-spreadsheet-dialog tm-spreadsheet-name-manager">…</div></TmFocusScope>
  </div>

  <!-- after: the core frame; the dialog class sits on the modal overlay -->
  <TmModal Show="true" Title="…" Size="ModalSize.Large" Class="tm-spreadsheet-name-manager" …>
      <ChildContent>…</ChildContent><Footer>…</Footer>
  </TmModal>
  ```

  Migration for a host that styled or selected the old markup:
  | before | after |
  | --- | --- |
  | `.tm-spreadsheet-<dialog>__backdrop { … }` | `.tm-modal-overlay.tm-spreadsheet-<dialog>` |
  | `.tm-spreadsheet-<dialog>__title` | `.tm-spreadsheet-<dialog> .tm-modal-title` |
  | `.tm-spreadsheet-<dialog>__close` | `.tm-spreadsheet-<dialog> .tm-modal-close` |
  | `.tm-spreadsheet-<dialog>{ width/padding/border-radius }` | the modal's `Size` (`ModalSize.Small/Medium/Large`) |
  | `.tm-spreadsheet-<dialog>__actions` (footer bar) | the same class now holds only the buttons, inside `.tm-modal-footer` |
  | `#tm-fcd-…` / hardcoded card widths | `.tm-fcd` (overlay) + `Size="ModalSize.Large"` |
  | backdrop click handler on the old wrapper | `TmModal.OnClose` (`CloseOnOverlayClick`, false for a Stop alert) |

- **All Spreadsheet dialogs have a mobile presentation, and the three tall surfaces go fullscreen.** Before, a dialog was the same fixed card at every width (the only narrow rule was `.tm-spreadsheet-dialog { min-width: 100% }`, which never matched the `tm-fcd`/`tm-dvd` cards). After, each dialog renders the frame's mobile presentation: **a bottom sheet for the short forms** (Sort, Custom Filter, Remove Duplicates, Paste Special, Hyperlink, Named Range Edit, Data Validation, Insert Image, validation alerts) and **a fullscreen panel for the tall ones** (Format Cells, Text to Columns, Name Manager), where a sheet would clip the tabs, the preview or the table. The presentation is the core frame's own resolution from the viewport scope it lives in, so a Spreadsheet embedded in a narrow Notion block/modal gets the same treatment; a new `LayoutMode` parameter on each dialog pins the mode for tests and hosts. A `Dialog_...` assertion that measured the desktop card still finds it: a forced or measured desktop layout renders `tm-modal--dialog`.

  ```razor
  <!-- pin the desktop card in a narrow host (tests, a kiosk layout) -->
  <TmSpreadsheetFormatCellsDialog LayoutMode="TmLayoutMode.Desktop" … />
  ```

- **`TmSpreadsheetValidationAlert` is severity-driven, and its buttons say what they do.** Before, the component took `IsStop` (bool), `PrimaryText`/`CancelText`/`ShowCancel` and both the warning and the information style shared one path with the same default title ("Invalid value") and the same "Confirm"/"Yes" labels, with no severity icon. After, it takes `Severity` (`SpreadsheetValidationErrorStyle`: `Stop`, `Warning`, `Information`): the severity paints its own icon in `--tm-color-danger` / `--tm-color-warning` / `--tm-color-info` with a matching 3px rail on the card, and it picks the default words — `TmSpreadsheet_Validation_DefaultWarningTitle/Message` ("Value outside the recommended range" / "Keep the value anyway?") and `…DefaultInfoTitle/Message` ("Note" / "Just so you know.") — so an **Information** message no longer reads as a warning. A host that relied on a Warning or Information rule **without** its own `ErrorAlert.Title/Message` therefore sees the severity's own default text instead of "Invalid value".
