The Stop style keeps the hard block: one primary action labelled `TmSpreadsheet_Validation_Acknowledge` ("Got it"), no cancel path, a backdrop click does nothing, Escape acknowledges. Warning/Information offer `Tm_Cancel` plus `TmSpreadsheet_Validation_KeepValue` ("Use anyway"), and a backdrop click cancels. `ShowCancel` is now `bool?`: `null` (default) follows the severity. `IsStop` is **removed**; a host that set it migrates to `Severity`:

  ```razor
  <!-- before -->
  <TmSpreadsheetValidationAlert IsStop="false" ShowCancel="true"
                                PrimaryText="Yes" CancelText="Cancel" … />
  <!-- after: the severity decides the icon, the defaults and the exit paths -->
  <TmSpreadsheetValidationAlert Severity="SpreadsheetValidationErrorStyle.Warning" … />
  ```

  The alert's title moved to the frame header (`.tm-modal-title`); `.tm-spreadsheet-alert__title` matches nothing now. `.tm-spreadsheet-alert`, `__icon`, `__message` and `__actions` remain (the last one now wraps the buttons inside the frame's footer).

- **The Insert Image dialog is a component of its own.** Before, the URL field, its label and both buttons were inline markup inside `TmSpreadsheet.razor`, with no URL validation — any non-empty string reached the canvas `<img>`. After, `TmSpreadsheetInsertImageDialog` (`Tempo.Blazor.Components.Spreadsheet.Dialogs`) renders through the shared frame with the initial focus on the field, `inputmode="url"`, Enter applying from the field, and the URL validated with `Uri.TryCreate` against absolute `http`/`https`/`data:` only: Apply is disabled (and the field carries `aria-invalid` plus a `role="alert"` message using `TmSpreadsheet_InsertImage_InvalidUrl`) until the address can actually be painted. A host that re-implemented the inline markup mounts the component instead.

- **Find & Replace stays non-modal and becomes a non-modal bottom sheet on a narrow container (Q5).** Before, the panel was a floating `position: absolute` card at every width, overlapping the grid's first rows on a phone. After, the DESKTOP layout keeps the floating panel (the grid must stay usable and the highlighted matches visible — it is deliberately NOT a modal), and a mobile layout renders the same panel inside `TmDrawer` with `Modal="false"`, so there is no backdrop, the grid keeps working, the sheet has a grabber and Escape closes it. The `LayoutMode` parameter forces either presentation. Nothing else changed: `Ctrl+F`/`Ctrl+H`, Enter / Shift+Enter / Escape and every `.tm-spreadsheet-find__*` class are the same, and the panel keeps its own `role="dialog"` (non-modal). A host that positioned `.tm-spreadsheet-find` with its own absolute offsets must scope that rule to the desktop panel — the mobile sheet hosts it in `.tm-spreadsheet-find-host`.

- **The Data validation DIALOG title lost its ellipsis.** The toolbar command keeps `TmSpreadsheet_Data_DataValidation` ("Data validation..." — it opens something), but the dialog now titles itself with the new `TmSpreadsheet_Validation_Title` ("Data validation", cs "Ověření dat", sk "Validácia údajov", fr "Validation des données"). Render `Title` from your own resource if you localize the surface yourself; `.tm-dvd .tm-modal-title` is still the selector, only the text changed.

- **Core (visual change): `--tm-modal-stacked-scrim` — two stacked modals no longer dim the page twice.** `TmModal`/`TmDialog` paint `rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.5)` (light) / `0.7` (dark) on every overlay, so a dialog opened over another one reached **0.75 / 0.91** over the page and read almost black. Now the FIRST overlay paints the full page scrim and a second one (a later sibling `.tm-modal-overlay` under the same parent; a modal nested inside another modal's content still paints the full scrim) paints the light `--tm-modal-stacked-scrim` — 40 % of the same scrim colour, derived with `color-mix` from `--tm-bg-overlay`, so both themes follow automatically — and no backdrop blur. The lower dialog keeps a depth cue instead of being dimmed out, and a single modal is byte-identical to before.

  ```css
  /* restore the pre-2.10 look (two full scrims) … */
  :root { --tm-modal-stacked-scrim: var(--tm-bg-overlay); }
  /* … or no scrim at all on the stacked surface */
  :root { --tm-modal-stacked-scrim: transparent; }
  ```

- **Core (additive): `MobilePresentation.AutoFullscreen`.** A tall surface (Format Cells, Text to Columns, Name Manager) would be clipped by a bottom sheet, so the enum gained a fourth value: it follows the viewport scope like `Auto` but resolves to a fullscreen panel on a mobile layout and to the centred dialog everywhere else. `Auto` is untouched, so every existing consumer keeps its sheet, and `TmModal`/`TmDialog` only extend their resolution switch.

  ```razor
  <!-- a tabbed form, a table or a preview: fullscreen on a phone -->
  <TmModal MobilePresentation="MobilePresentation.AutoFullscreen" … />
  ```

- **Core (additive): `TmModal.RestoreFocus`.** `bool`, default `true` — the frame's focus restore can now be switched off so a host that owns the destination itself (a surface whose close action moves the focus deliberately) does not fight it. The value is forwarded to the existing `TmFocusScope.RestoreFocus`, so the default path is byte-identical to before; `false` renders `data-restore-focus="false"` and leaves the focus where the close action put it.

- **Core (additive): `TmModal.DialogRole` and `TmModal.AriaDescribedBy`, `TmFocusScope.AriaDescribedBy`.** A surface that IS a message (the Spreadsheet validation alert) can now render `role="alertdialog"` and point `aria-describedby` at its message through the shared frame, instead of dropping out of `TmModal` to hand-roll an `alertdialog`. Both default to the previous behaviour (`"dialog"`, unset), so nothing else changes.

- **Signing components respond to their CONTAINER, not the viewport (Signing redesign phase 1).**
  Every Signing stylesheet root (`tm-signing-runner`, `tm-pdf-template-designer` workspace,
  `tm-signing-field-editor-panel`, `tm-condition-builder`, `tm-formula-builder`,
  `tm-recipient-role-editor`, `tm-document-page-viewer`, `tm-document-comments-panel`,
  `tm-signing-step-shell`, `tm-signing-completion-panel`, `tm-submission-status-timeline`,
  `tm-share-link-panel`, `tm-pdf-signature-verification`, `tm-audit-trail-viewer`) is now a CSS
  size container (`container-type: inline-size`), and every width `@media` query moved to
  `@container` with the library-convention breakpoints (640 / 768 / 1024 / 1280). The visible
  behavior change: a Signing panel squeezed into a narrow column on a WIDE screen collapses exactly
  like on a phone — before, the layouts keyed off the viewport, so a narrow designer inspector or a
  runner in a half-width column kept the roomy desktop layout. On the designer the steps are named
  on its own workspace container: the right panel drops below the canvas under a 768px workspace
  and the palette stacks under 640px (the pre-change steps were viewport 1100/900). One tablet
  consequence to plan for: hosts embedding the runner in <768px columns on tablets get the mobile
  panel; pin a wider column or wait for the Phase 5 bottom sheet.
  ```css
  /* before: the runner collapsed only when the VIEWPORT was narrow */
  @media (max-width: 48rem) { .tm-signing-form-runner { grid-template-columns: minmax(0, 1fr); } }

  /* after: it collapses when the RUNNER's own container is narrow (breakpoints 640/768/1024/1280).
     A @container rule can never restyle the container itself, so the grid moved onto an inner
     element — the runner root gained `__layout`, the designer workspace gained `__workspace-grid`. */
  .tm-signing-form-runner { container: tm-signing-runner / inline-size; }
  @container tm-signing-runner (width < 768px) { .tm-signing-form-runner__layout { grid-template-columns: minmax(0, 1fr); } }
  ```
  Two documented specifics: the designer's container is the `__workspace` region and NOT the
  component root, because the root hosts the `position: fixed` context menu (a container becomes
  the containing block of fixed descendants and would displace the menu); and the temporary
  force-single-column overrides the field editor panel carried for the embedded condition builder
  are gone — the builder is a container itself and re-wraps by the width it actually gets. Host CSS
  that set `grid-template-columns` on `.tm-signing-form-runner` or
  `.tm-pdf-template-designer__workspace` directly must retarget `.tm-signing-form-runner__layout` /
  `.tm-pdf-template-designer__workspace-grid`. Every container root also declares
  `min-inline-size: 0; inline-size: 100%` — inline-size containment sizes the box as if it had no
  contents, so without these declarations a Signing component placed in a flex row (or an
  auto-sized grid track) shrink-to-fit to nothing. A host that gives the root an explicit width is
  unaffected; a host that relied on content-driven growth must size the component (or its
  flex/grid track) itself. The new
  `SigningCssTokenHygieneTests` bUnit gate keeps this honest (no width `@media`, no undefined
  tokens, no hex outside the role palette, one border alias, no white-on-primary text, sticky never
  rides `--tm-z-modal`).

- **Signing CSS token hygiene (Signing redesign phase 1).** The package stylesheets no longer carry
  colour literals outside the new role palette, scattered border aliases or white text on coloured
  fills: `var(--tm-color-on-primary, #fff)` lost its `#fff` fallback (dark mode had white-on-light
  ink), `--tm-color-border` / `--tm-z-sticky, 10` / `--tm-z-tooltip, 1090` collapsed onto the
  canonical `--tm-border-color` / `--tm-z-sticky` / `--tm-z-tooltip`, the runner's primary buttons
  and the submission timeline markers paint their text with `--tm-color-on-primary` (identical in
  light mode — inverse ink in dark mode), and the sticky mobile panel uses `--tm-z-sticky` instead
  of `--tm-z-modal`. Only a host that overrode one of the removed fallback spellings is affected.

- **Signing role colours (Signing redesign phase 1).** New `--tm-signing-role-1..6` tokens (light +
  dark, overridable) in the package's `tokens-signing.css`; `TmSigningFieldOverlay` gained `RoleColor`
  (rendered as the inline `--tm-signing-role-color` custom property plus the
  `tm-signing-field--role` class; the stylesheet derives border and background via `color-mix()`,
  the border mixing 20% primary ink into the role colour and the label ink staying plain primary
  text, and the value is allow-list sanitized — hex, `var(--tm-signing-role-N)`, rgb/hsl/oklch or a
  colour keyword; anything else is dropped),
  `TmPdfTemplateDesigner` and `TmSigningFormRunner` (new optional `SubmitterRoles` parameter) pass
  the owning submitter's colour to every overlay, and the field editor's colour input falls back to
  the field's role colour instead of a hard-coded `#2563eb`. Role colour 6 changed from `#ca8a04`
  to `#a16207` (light theme and the default palette; dark mode keeps `#facc15`) so the yellow stays
  readable as a border on light surfaces. Stored templates that already carry `#ca8a04` keep
  rendering with it — only defaults move. The `TmRecipientRoleEditor` default
  palette stays hex ON PURPOSE — it is serialized template data (`SigningRolePalette`) mirroring
  the tokens; a host that overrode role colours through stored templates is unaffected. An invalid
  field is no longer colour-only: `.tm-signing-field--invalid` adds a dashed 2px border (WCAG
  1.4.1).

- **Signing form runner renders ONE step panel, and every step input has an accessible name
  (Signing redesign phase 2, bug B25 + S2-1).** The runner used to render the step panel TWICE —
  once in the desktop steps rail and once in a mobile panel div that CSS merely hid above 768px —
  so every input, id, live region and alert existed twice in the DOM for assistive technology.
  The column vs. mobile-sheet presentation is now CSS only (`@container tm-signing-runner`), the
  sheet state lives on the rail as `tm-signing-form-runner__steps--sheet-collapsed` /
  `--sheet-expanded` (the expand / minimize buttons carry `aria-expanded` / `aria-controls`), and
  the panel exists exactly once at every width. What changes in the DOM and for hosts:
  - *Runner DOM.* `.tm-signing-form-runner__mobile-panel` (with `--expanded` / `--collapsed` /
    `--has-complete-target` and the `data-complete-target` attribute) is gone; the single
    `aside.tm-signing-form-runner__steps` carries `--sheet-collapsed` / `--sheet-expanded`, the
    `--has-complete-target` class and `data-complete-target`. A host or test that reached the
    mobile panel's content through it retargets the rail:
    ```html
    <!-- before: two rendered panels; the mobile one hidden by CSS above 768px -->
    <aside class="tm-signing-form-runner__steps">…panel…</aside>
    <div class="tm-signing-form-runner__mobile-panel tm-signing-form-runner__mobile-panel--expanded">…panel…</div>

    <!-- after: ONE panel; the mobile sheet is a presentation of the rail -->
    <aside class="tm-signing-form-runner__steps tm-signing-form-runner__steps--sheet-expanded">…panel…</aside>
    ```
    ```js
    // before
    runner.locator(".tm-signing-form-runner__mobile-panel .tm-signing-form-runner__progress");
    // after
    runner.locator(".tm-signing-form-runner__steps .tm-signing-form-runner__progress");
    ```
    `MobilePanelMode` still picks the initial sheet state; on a desktop-sized container the
    affordances are hidden and the panel always shows. Both affordances ("Sign now" expand /
    "Minimize") now ALWAYS render and CSS hides the one that does not match the sheet state —
    toggling the sheet moves keyboard focus onto the button that becomes visible. The step panel
    no longer carries the `data-mobile` attribute: `div.tm-signing-form-runner__step-panel[data-mobile="true"]`
    and `[data-mobile="false"]` selectors match nothing — the panel is one instance at every
    width, keyed by `.tm-signing-form-runner__steps--sheet-collapsed` / `--sheet-expanded`.
    ```html
    <!-- before: the panel was duplicated; the copy carried data-mobile -->
    <div class="tm-signing-form-runner__step-panel">…</div>
    <div class="tm-signing-form-runner__step-panel" data-mobile="true">…</div>

    <!-- after: one panel, no data-mobile -->
    <aside class="tm-signing-form-runner__steps tm-signing-form-runner__steps--sheet-expanded">
      <div id="tm-signing-runner-panel-…" class="tm-signing-form-runner__step-panel">…</div>
    </aside>
    ```
  - *Choice steps are real groups.* `div.tm-signing-choice-step__options[role="radiogroup"]` with
    radio inputs named `name="{field-uuid}"` is now `fieldset.tm-signing-choice-step__group >
    legend.tm-signing-choice-step__legend.tm-sr-only + div.tm-signing-choice-step__options`
    (the legend names the group), and the radios' `name` is per component instance
    (`tm-signing-choice-{guid}`) — two rendered radio groups no longer merge into one
    browser-level group and no longer share the field-uuid-derived name. A selector on
    `[role="radiogroup"]` or `input[name="{uuid}"]` retargets `fieldset.tm-signing-choice-step__group`
    / `.tm-signing-choice-step__radio`. The checkbox-group hint carries its own id and is part of
    the group's `aria-describedby`.
  - *Signature steps are nested.* `.tm-signature-capture` now renders inside
    `section.tm-signing-step-shell.tm-signing-signature-step` (the step shell supplies the title,
    the required / optional badge, the instruction and the single `role="alert"`; the capture is
    wrapped in a `role="group"` named by the step title). A selector assuming the capture is a
    top-level element retargets `.tm-signing-signature-step .tm-signature-capture`. The capture is
    deliberately driven with `Required=false` — the shell owns the required / invalid presentation
    so a required signature step shows exactly ONE alert.
  - *One validation message per step.* The runner forwards its step validation into the step shell
    (a named `TmSigningRunnerValidation` cascade the shell falls back to when the step has no
    message of its own), so a failed Next renders exactly ONE `role="alert"` — inside the step
    shell. `.tm-signing-form-runner__validation` is reserved for CompleteBlocked and completion
    errors. A selector that read the runner's validation box after a failed Next must read
    `.tm-signing-step-shell__validation`.
  - *Accessible names.* The step shell gives its title a stable per-instance HTML id
    (`tm-signing-step-title-{guid}`, `tabindex="-1"`, exposed through the new `TitleId` /
    `DescriptionId` parameters — the existing `ValidationMessageId` is now generated per instance
    when omitted — and cascaded as `TmSigningStepShellContext`) and every step input references
    it (`aria-labelledby`, plus
    `aria-describedby` for the description and the step's validation alert) and carries
    `aria-invalid="true"` while the step shows its message (on the input for single controls, on
    the `fieldset` for groups, including the runner-forwarded validation) — so `getByLabel`
    resolves every runner input; the choice step renders real `<fieldset>` groups named by a
    visually hidden `<legend>`, radio groups get a per-instance `name` (two rendered radio groups
    no longer merge), and the phone step's country / number / OTP controls carry explicit
    `aria-label`s. Ids are unique per rendered component: two runners (or two steps) showing the
    SAME field uuid never share an id.
  - *Focus.* The runner moves focus to the new step's title on every programmatic step change
    (Next / Previous / Skip, overlay click, jump to the first invalid step, blocked Complete that
    lands on another step) through the internal navigation signal the runner cascades; a page load
    never steals focus. The title's programmatic focus paints no ring (`:focus:not(:focus-visible)`);
    keyboard focus keeps the token focus ring. The progress region is an explicit
    `aria-live="polite"` status.
  - *The signature step is a component.* `TmSigningSignatureStep` (shell + `TmSignatureCapture`)
    replaces the runner's bare capture, so a signature step finally carries the title, the
    required / optional badge, the signing instruction ("Add your signature in the field below.")
    and the "appears on" hint. The shell owns the invalid presentation —
    the embedded capture is driven with `Required=false`, so the duplicate "Signature is
    required." alert the old bare capture rendered alongside the runner's message is gone; hosts
    that want the old single-capture look keep placing `TmSignatureCapture` directly.
  - *Performance.* The step plan (a pure function of `Fields` / `Pages` / values /
    `SubmitterUuid`) is cached between renders and events; every parameter set from the host
    recomputes it, so in-place `Fields` / `Pages` edits are still picked up.

- **Signing form runner is a guided wizard panel, and the completion panel colours only its hero
  (Signing redesign phase 3, S2-2 + S2-6).** The runner panel gains a titled header with a
  completed-field progress bar, the field list becomes a PERMANENT panel section, a success banner
  appears once every required field is done, and the action footer composes `TmButton`s with a
  contextual primary action. `TmSigningCompletionPanel` inherits `TmComponentBase` and restructures
  its markup. What breaks and how to migrate:
  - *"Accessibility mode" is removed (U2).* The `button.tm-signing-form-runner__accessibility-entry`
    toggle, the `tm-signing-form-runner__accessibility-list` / `__accessibility-field` rows, the
    `tm-signing-form-runner--accessibility` root class and the `TmSigningFormRunner_AccessibilityMode`
    localization key are gone — the field list is always rendered:
    ```html
    <!-- before: the list lived behind a toggle -->
    <button class="tm-signing-form-runner__accessibility-entry">Accessibility mode</button>
    <div class="tm-signing-form-runner__accessibility-list">
      <button class="tm-signing-form-runner__accessibility-field" aria-current="true">…</button>
    </div>

    <!-- after: a permanent, structured list -->
    <nav class="tm-signing-form-runner__field-list" aria-label="Fields to complete">
      <ol class="tm-signing-form-runner__field-items">
        <li class="tm-signing-form-runner__field-item">
          <button class="tm-signing-form-runner__field-button tm-signing-form-runner__field-button--active"
                  aria-current="step" data-field-uuid="…">…</button>
        </li>
      </ol>
    </nav>
    ```
    A test or host that clicked the toggle retargets the list row:
    `.tm-signing-form-runner__accessibility-field` → `.tm-signing-form-runner__field-button`
    (rows carry `data-field-uuid`, `aria-current="step"` on the active one, and a
    `.tm-signing-form-runner__field-status` chip reading Done / Required / Optional).
  - *Progress counts completed fields.* `.tm-signing-form-runner__progress` now shows the count
    span `.tm-signing-form-runner__progress-text` ("1 of 3 done", the neutral
    `TmSigningFormRunner_DoneCount` key — `{0} of {1}`, no plural forms) above a `TmProgressBar`;
    the old `TmSigningFormRunner_Progress` / `_ProgressAria` keys are gone. An assertion on
    `"Step 2 of 3"` retargets the completed-field count (`"1 of 3"`); the `aria-label` mirrors it.
  - *The primary action is contextual.* The footer is two `TmButton`s: secondary Previous
    (`button.tm-btn.tm-btn-secondary.tm-btn-lg.tm-signing-form-runner__previous`) and ONE primary —
    `button.tm-btn.tm-btn-primary.tm-btn-lg.tm-signing-form-runner__next` while later steps remain,
    otherwise `button.tm-btn.tm-btn-primary.tm-btn-lg.tm-signing-form-runner__complete`. The raw
    `button.tm-signing-form-runner__next` skin is gone (the class stays on the `TmButton`, so
    `[data-testid]`/class selectors keep working, but `button.tm-signing-form-runner__next:not(.tm-btn)`
    style overrides must be rewritten against the `tm-btn` classes). On the LAST step the primary
    already reads Complete (disabled while required work is missing) — the old always-rendered
    disabled pair Next + Complete is gone, and a Complete click can no longer land the signer on an
    empty step. "Skip" renders ONLY for an optional current field that is NOT the last step (a
    final optional step has nowhere to skip to), as a full-width text row INSIDE the sticky
    action footer (`tm-btn-link`); the old always-rendered disabled `__skip` is gone.
    ```html
    <!-- before: four always-rendered raw buttons -->
    <button class="tm-signing-form-runner__previous">…</button>
    <button class="tm-signing-form-runner__skip" disabled>…</button>
    <button class="tm-signing-form-runner__next">…</button>
    <button class="tm-signing-form-runner__complete" disabled>…</button>

    <!-- after: TmButton pair + conditional text skip -->
    <button class="tm-btn tm-btn-secondary tm-btn-lg tm-signing-form-runner__previous">…</button>
    <button class="tm-btn tm-btn-primary tm-btn-lg tm-signing-form-runner__next">…</button>
    <!-- or, when every required field is done / on the last step: -->
    <button class="tm-btn tm-btn-primary tm-btn-lg tm-signing-form-runner__complete">…</button>
    <button class="tm-btn tm-btn-link tm-signing-form-runner__skip">…</button> <!-- optional step only -->
    ```
  - *The success banner is a `TmAlert` in a polite status region.* Once `AllRequiredFieldsComplete()`
    the panel renders `div.tm-alert.tm-alert--success.tm-alert--soft.tm-signing-form-runner__all-done`
    with `role="status"` on the alert root itself (title `TmSigningFormRunner_AllDoneTitle`) — the
    "all done" news announces politely instead of interrupting as a second `role="alert"`. The
    banner uses the new `TmAlert.Role` parameter (the old `role="status"` wrapper div around the
    alert is gone).
  - *Panel chrome.* `.tm-signing-form-runner__step-panel` carries `--tm-radius-card` /
    `--tm-shadow-card` and a header (`__panel-title` / `__panel-subtitle`, keys
    `TmSigningFormRunner_PanelTitle` / `_PanelSubtitle`, subtitle "Fill in the following fields in
    the document."); the language selector moved OUT of the header into the quiet footer row
    (`.tm-signing-form-runner__footer`) next to the autosave status, compact. On a
    desktop/tablet container the panel caps at `calc(100dvh - 2 * --tm-space-4)` and scrolls
    internally with the action row (`.tm-signing-form-runner__actions`) sticky at its bottom, so
    the primary action never scrolls away (the mobile sheet keeps the old in-flow behaviour). The
    document area paints `--tm-bg-workspace` and the
    page sheet uses `--tm-shadow-card`; controls use `--tm-radius-control` and a `--tm-touch-target`
    (44 px) floor. The "Selected field" caption is an
    `<h3 class="tm-signing-form-runner__current-step-heading">` (was a `div`; same look). New
    overlay prompt: the CURRENT field shows
    `span.tm-signing-field__prompt` while it is an empty REQUIRED field ("Click to sign / fill
    in", key `TmSigningFieldOverlay_EmptyRequiredPrompt`) — other required fields stay quiet, and
    a completed-field assertion that read the overlay's whole text must skip it. The label +
    prompt head is a plain flex pair (no size container, no width-based hiding): the label keeps
    its natural width instead of truncating to a stub, and the prompt ellipsizes into the
    remaining head room.
  - *Shared type icons.* The designer palette, the document overlays and the runner field list
    render the SAME icon per field type (`SigningFieldTypeIcons`): the designer's palette icons for
    Radio (`circle-dot` → `circle`), File (`paperclip` → `file`), Stamp (`stamp` → `shield`),
    Payment (`hash` → `tag`), Heading (`heading` → `type`) and Strikethrough (`strikethrough` →
    `minus`) changed to the overlay's names (the `[data-icon]` contract E2E pinned). A selector on
    the old designer icon names retargets the new ones.
  - *Completion panel structure.* `TmSigningCompletionPanel` now inherits `TmComponentBase`
    (`DataTestId` / `TestIdPrefix`; an unmatched-attribute `data-testid` splat still wins over
    the component's own default), announces through `role="status"` on
    `div.tm-signing-completion-panel__content` (title + description — the actions stay outside
    the live region), focuses its title (`tabindex="-1"`) after the first render unless the host
    passes `FocusTitleOnRender="false"` (no scroll: the move runs with `preventScroll`), wraps
    the icon in `span.tm-signing-completion-panel__hero` and takes a new `ChildContent` slot
    between the description and the actions (`div.tm-signing-completion-panel__body`). The panel
    aligns to the START of its host cell (`align-content: start; align-self: start`) instead of
    stretching to a taller row. The WAITING state
    colours ONLY the hero circle (warning-subtle) — the card keeps the neutral surface, and the
    title grows to 2xl. Selectors that read the icon as a direct child of the panel retarget
    `.tm-signing-completion-panel__hero .tm-icon`; on a phone-width container the actions stack
    full-width at 48 px.
    ```html
    <!-- before: waiting tinted the whole card -->
    <section class="tm-signing-completion-panel" data-state="waiting">
      <svg class="tm-icon tm-icon-lg …">…</svg>
      <div class="tm-signing-completion-panel__content">…</div>

    <!-- after: the status lives in the hero circle; the card stays neutral -->
    <section class="tm-signing-completion-panel" data-state="waiting" data-testid="…">
      <span class="tm-signing-completion-panel__hero" aria-hidden="true">
        <svg class="tm-icon tm-icon-xl …">…</svg>
      </span>
      <div class="tm-signing-completion-panel__content" role="status">…</div>
      <!-- optional ChildContent renders here -->
      <div class="tm-signing-completion-panel__actions">…</div>
    </section>
    ```

- **Signing steps render on the core Tm components (Signing redesign phase 4, S2-3/SI1).** Every
  step input moved from a raw element to the core input components — the date input stays NATIVE
  (`<input type="date|month|datetime-local">`, the SI1 exception, styled with the core `tm-input`
  classes) so the mobile pickers keep working. What changes in the DOM and for hosts:
  - *Text.* The input is a `TmTextInput` / `TmTextArea` (`div.tm-input-wrapper > input.tm-input`,
    `textarea.tm-textarea`); the accessible name is still the step title id via the splatted
    `aria-labelledby`, and `maxlength` / `pattern` splat onto the native element. A "n / max"
    counter (`.tm-signing-text-step__count`) renders while the field carries a max length — the
    visible count is `aria-hidden` and a permanent visually-hidden polite live region announces
    only AT the limit (phase 4 review).
    ```css
    /* before */ input.tm-signing-text-step__input { … }
    /* after  */ .tm-signing-text-step input.tm-signing-text-step__input { … }
    /* the same class stays on the <input>; the textarea variant moved to the wrapper */
    .tm-signing-text-step__textarea { … }  /* now the TmTextArea wrapper div, not the textarea */
    ```
  - *Number (behavior change).* The input is `type="text"` + `inputmode="decimal"` and parses with
    the FIELD culture, so a Czech signer can finally type the decimal comma ("125,5") — the old
    native `type="number"` + InvariantCulture parse rejected it. The parse contract (phase 4
    review) is strict about group separators: `NumberStyles.Float` WITHOUT `AllowThousands`, so an
    en-US "1,5" is an invalid half and NOT one thousand five; only a whitespace-like group
    separator (the NBSP of cs-CZ "1 000,5") is stripped before the parse. The native `step`
    attribute is no longer applied either (it was inert on the old markup and is meaningless on a
    text input — `SigningFieldValidation.Step` stays in the model for hosts). The `min` / `max`
    attributes are gone (inert on a text input); the allowed range renders as a localized hint
    (`.tm-signing-number-step__range`, `TmSigningStep_NumberRange`, "Allowed range: 1 – 1 000 000"
    for cs-CZ) referenced from the input's `aria-describedby`. The min/max validation messages are
    unchanged.
  - *Validation commits, keystrokes flow (behavior change).* The text and number steps raise
    `ValueChanged` — and the runner's `ValuesChanged` — PER KEYSTROKE again (the runner's auto-save
    is debounced by `AutoSaveDelay`,
    so this is only a traffic change), while the validation message is computed on COMMIT (blur /
    change) — typing never fires the step's alert, and typing after a failed commit clears it.
    Same for the KBA answers. A host that showed its own "invalid" marker per keystroke now sees
    the marker only after the field commits.
  - *Choice.* The select variant renders the core `TmSelect` — the `tm-signing-choice-step__select`
    class moved from the `<select>` to the component wrapper, and the select's accessible name is
    the field label (`aria-label`). The step's plumbing reaches the NATIVE `<select>` through the
    core `TmSelect.SelectAttributes` splat (phase 4 review): the title id as `aria-labelledby`,
    the description / validation ids as `aria-describedby`, and `aria-invalid` on the select
    itself. The
    radio variant keeps the `fieldset` / visually hidden `legend` and renders the core
    `TmRadioGroup` (`.tm-radio-group`, `TmRadio` rows — the inputs no longer carry a `value`
    attribute; select radios by role/label, `getByRole('radio', { name: 'Email' })`), with the
    field type's own `circle-dot` glyph in the palette / list / header (a bare circle read like
    any bullet). The
    checkbox variants render `TmCheckbox` rows (`.tm-checkbox-wrapper` with the package
    `tm-signing-choice-step__option` / `__checkbox-row` classes; grouped checkbox fields carry
    their description as the row's help text, whose id the input references through the core
    `aria-describedby`).
    ```css
    /* before */ input.tm-signing-choice-step__radio { … }   /* the raw radio input */
    /* after  */ .tm-signing-choice-step .tm-radio-option { … }  /* the core TmRadio row */
    ```
  - *Phone.* The country select is a `TmSelect` (the `tm-signing-phone-step__country` class moved
    from the `<select>` to the wrapper) and the number input a `TmTextInput Type="tel"`; all three
    controls (country / number / OTP) now carry VISIBLE localized labels
    (`TmSigningStep_PhoneCountryLabel`, `_PhoneNumberLabel`, `_OtpLabel`) — the old aria-label
    keys (`TmSigningStep_CountryCodeAria` / `_PhoneInputAria` / `_OtpInputAria`) were removed in
    the phase-4 review, and the number's placeholder is an EXAMPLE FORMAT for the selected
    calling code ("777 123 456" for +420) instead of a repeated label. The OTP input keeps
    `inputmode="numeric"` + `autocomplete="one-time-code"`. **The default
    country code comes from the field culture** (+420 for cs, +421 for sk, otherwise +1) — the old
    hardcoded `"+1"` default opened a Czech signer's step on the wrong prefix. `CountryCode` is
    now `string?`; an explicitly passed code keeps winning over the culture default, a culture
    default the host's `CountryOptions` do not offer falls back to the FIRST option, and the
    PICKED code is component-local state (phase 4 review) — a host that does not bind
    `CountryCodeChanged` no longer sees the select snap back on the next render.
  - *Attachment.* The upload is the core `TmFileDropZone` (the custom signing icon content replaced
    the default emoji; the file input carries `aria-label` + a stable `data-testid`, and the
    description / invalid state ride the core `InputAttributes` splat — phase 4 review). The
    zone's own picked-files list is SUPPRESSED (`ShowFileList="false"`, the core addition) because
    the step renders its own cards — the same file never shows twice. Cards show a preview
    (decorative, `alt=""`) or type icon, a culturally formatted "size · type" line
    (`.tm-signing-attachment-step__meta`, "1,2 MB" under cs-CZ — the old size was culture-invariant)
    under a localized "Attached files (N)" heading; the remove action is a ghost `TmButton`
    whose accessible name carries the FILE NAME (`TmSigningStep_RemoveFile`, "Remove
    contract.pdf") and whose visible text collapses to a 44 px icon-only target on the narrow
    step container, where the card itself wraps (phase 4 review).
  - *External.* The step gains a hero icon in a primary-subtle circle — on a WIDE step container
    it sits beside the title / description in the header row (phase 4 review) — a per-type default
    description (`TmSigningStep_VerificationDescription` / `_KbaDescription` / `_PaymentDescription`,
    overridable by the field description), a culture-formatted payment amount (cs-CZ renders
    "1 500,00 Kč" — the old rendering was culture-invariant "EUR 19.50"), Start as the primary
    `TmButton` with the open link as an outline sibling (the `tm-btn` / `tm-btn-outline` classes
    are the core `_button.css` contract — keep that stylesheet shipped whenever this step renders),
    and the **verified / paid state**: the new
    `Value` parameter (the runner passes the stored field value) replaces the call to action with a
    localized "Verified" / "Paid" status once the value is `true`. The `.tm-signing-external-step__question`
    wrapper is gone (each KBA answer is a labelled `TmTextInput`).
  - *Signature.* The capture's Clear button moved INSIDE the signing surface — the step passes
    `ClearButtonPlacement="Overlay"` (the F8 core addition) by default; the new
    `TmSigningSignatureStep.ClearButtonPlacement` parameter restores the row
    (`TmSignatureClearButtonPlacement.Actions`). The step shell header now renders the field type's
    icon (`.tm-signing-step-shell__icon`, the shared `SigningFieldTypeIcons` glyph).
  - *Touch sizing.* Step inputs and actions meet the 44 px touch target (`--tm-touch-target`), 48 px
    (`--tm-space-12`) in the narrow step container; the value rows (date + Today, phone + Send code,
    external actions) stack under each other on the narrow container — with the input's height
    decided by its own content again, not the stretched row (the date / OTP input rendered ~190 px
    tall; phase 4 review). The "Today" action reads as a tonal chip (primary-subtle background,
    primary ink, no border). The step-specific styles moved
    from `_signing-step-shell.css` into the new `_signing-steps.css` (both ship via
    `tempo-blazor-signing.css`).

- **The signing runner's mobile panel is a real bottom sheet, and the sheet breakpoint moved from
  768 to 640 (Signing redesign phase 5, S2-4).** The runner now classifies its OWN container (F1):
  a new `LayoutMode` / `ResolvedLayoutChanged` pair wraps the runner root in the shared
  `TmLayoutObserver` (the Gantt pattern — the root gained a `tm-signing-form-runner--mobile` /
  `--tablet` modifier class), so a host with an app-level viewport scope gets the correct
  presentation from the first frame. The sheet presentation itself stays CSS-only under
  `@container tm-signing-runner (width < 640px)` — the sheet only pays off below the
  single-column fold, a 640–767 column keeps the docked two-column panel. There is NO knob for the
  old 768 behaviour: a host that wants the sheet at a wider container pins
  `LayoutMode="TmLayoutMode.Mobile"` (and one that must never sheet pins `Desktop`/`Tablet`).
  Below 640 the rail is a full-bleed bottom sheet with rounded TOP corners, an internal scroll
  capped at `85dvh` and the safe-area inset. The sheet logic stays contained in the runner's
  `MobileSheet` partial for the phase-9 migration onto the shared `TmDrawer`.
  - *DOM structure.* The observer wraps the runner root in a `TmLayout` container element
    (`div.tm-layout.tm-layout--mobile` / `--tablet` / `--desktop` …), so `.tm-signing-form-runner`
    is no longer the outermost element a host sees:
    ```html
    <!-- before: the runner root was the host-placed element -->
    <div class="tm-signing-form-runner …">…</div>

    <!-- after: the F1 observer adds its own wrapper around the runner root -->
    <div class="tm-layout tm-layout--mobile tm-layout--no-container">
      <div class="tm-signing-form-runner …">…</div>
    </div>
    ```
    Host CSS that targeted a PARENT of the runner (`.demo-card > .tm-signing-form-runner`) must
    retarget; selectors ON `.tm-signing-form-runner` itself are unaffected.
  - *Sheet states.* The sheet is a THREE-state CSS presentation (phase 5 review): **peek**
    (collapsed — the handle, the done count strip `.tm-signing-form-runner__sheet-progress` and
    the "Sign now" CTA stay visible above the document; the layout reserves the strip's measured
    height through the new `--tm-signing-sheet-peek-height` knob on the runner root instead of the
    old fixed `2 × space-16` padding guess), **expanded** (field list + step, capped at `85dvh`
    with an internal scroll) and **full** (`.tm-signing-form-runner__steps--sheet-full` — the
    active edit: step panel + sticky action bar visible, field list folded away). EVERY mobile
    navigation (Next / Previous / Skip / field-list tap / document overlay tap — which now also
    OPENS the collapsed sheet on the clicked field's step) lands in **full**; the handle toggles
    expanded ↔ peek, and the More menu's "Field list" switches full → expanded, scrolls the list
    into view and focuses the current row. There is deliberately NO resize-on-focus (it would
    move a pressed control mid-press when a blurred input collapsed the sheet) and no JS state.
  - *Toggles.* The HANDLE (`.tm-signing-form-runner__sheet-handle`) is the sheet's ONLY
    `aria-expanded`/`aria-controls` toggle, and it keeps focus when the state flip hides the
    focus owner. The phase-2 "Sign now" `aria-expanded` semantics are gone (it is an action, not
    a toggle) and the expanded sheet's full-width "Minimize" row is REMOVED — "Show whole
    document" in the More menu collapses to peek:
    ```html
    <!-- before (phase 2): both affordances rendered, both carried aria-expanded -->
    <button class="tm-signing-form-runner__mobile-expand" aria-expanded="false" aria-controls="…">Sign now</button>
    <button class="tm-signing-form-runner__mobile-minimize" aria-expanded="true" aria-controls="…">Minimize</button>

    <!-- after: the handle is the only toggle; More → "Show whole document" collapses -->
    <button class="tm-signing-form-runner__sheet-handle" aria-expanded="false" aria-controls="…">…</button>
    <button class="tm-signing-form-runner__mobile-expand">Sign now</button>
    ```
    Tests or scripts that clicked `.tm-signing-form-runner__mobile-minimize` use the handle (or
    the More menu's `tm-signing-form-runner__more-document` entry).
  - *Action bar.* The mobile sticky action row is `Previous (1fr) | Next/Complete (2fr — the
    primary stays the widest at 320) | ⋯ More` — the new `.tm-signing-form-runner__more` trigger
    (a core `TmDropdown`; hidden on the docked containers, where the menu simply stays closed)
    carries Skip (optional current field only), Field list, Language (expands the sheet and
    focuses the picker) and "Show whole document". The desktop Skip row is unchanged; the menu
    items render only while the trigger is visible, so no duplicated actions are exposed.
  - *Auto-scroll.* Every step landing asks the new `signing-runner.js` module to put the active
    field's document overlay above the sheet with ONE `scrollTo` — centred in the space above the
    sheet, clamped so the field never hides under it; the overlay gained a `data-field-uuid`
    anchor. Reduced motion scrolls instantly (`behavior: 'auto'`). The module is a dynamic
    `import()` — **no `<script>` tag is needed** — and a circuit without it skips silently
    (today's behaviour).
  - *Choice cards (SI1).* On the mobile layout a select-typed field with at most five options
    renders as radio CARDS (`.tm-signing-choice-step__options--cards` on the core `TmRadioGroup`,
    56px whole-card rows) instead of the system picker; an OPTIONAL select's card set gains a
    localized "None" card first (`TmSigningChoiceStep_None`) that sends the empty value — the
    system picker's selectable placeholder keeps its contract. Six or more options keep `TmSelect`
    at every width, and the desktop presentation is untouched.
    ```html
    <!-- before: the delivery field is always the system select -->
    <div class="tm-signing-choice-step tm-signing-choice-step__select">…<select>…</div>

    <!-- after (mobile layout, ≤ 5 options): the same values as whole-card radio rows -->
    <fieldset class="tm-signing-choice-step__group">
      <div class="tm-radio-group tm-signing-choice-step__options tm-signing-choice-step__options--cards">
        <label class="tm-radio-option">…None</label>
        <label class="tm-radio-option">…Paper</label>…
      </div>
    </fieldset>
    ```
  - *Signature default (SI3).* The runner gained `DefaultSignatureMode`
    (`Auto|Draw|Typed|Upload`, default `Auto` = Draw on `pointer: coarse`, Typed elsewhere). The
    template's stored `Preferences.Format` still wins over the parameter, and the signer's own tab
    pick still wins over both. A host that relied on the old always-Typed first presentation on a
    touch device pins `DefaultSignatureMode="TmSigningDefaultSignatureMode.Typed"`.
  - *`TmSigningFormRunner` is `IAsyncDisposable` instead of `IDisposable` (the sync `Dispose` is
    gone).* The runner cancels the pending autosave debounce and releases the `signing-runner.js`
    module instance when it is disposed — but Blazor's renderer calls ONLY `DisposeAsync` when a
    component implements both interfaces, so the cancellation put into the sync `Dispose` during
    phase 5 never ran and a changed value fired its debounce into a disposed component. Keeping
    `IAsyncDisposable` alone closes that hole. A host that disposed the runner explicitly — or a
    test holding it in a `using` — must switch to the async form:
    ```csharp
    // before
    runner.Dispose();
    // or
    using var runner = CreateRunner();

    // after
    await runner.DisposeAsync();
    // or
    await using var runner = CreateRunner();
    ```
    Hosts that only RENDER `<TmSigningFormRunner />` change nothing: the renderer disposes
    `IAsyncDisposable` components on its own (same shape as the `TmToastContainer` change).

- **The post-sign panels and the rule/role editors were rebuilt against the desktop references
  (Signing redesign phase 7, S1-1/S1-2/SI1).** `TmSubmissionStatusTimeline`, `TmAuditTrailViewer`,
  `TmPdfSignatureVerification`, `TmShareLinkPanel`, `TmConditionBuilder`, `TmFormulaBuilder` and
  `TmRecipientRoleEditor` changed DOM, classes and in places semantics; every visible change is
  below with its before/after. Additive API: `TmSubmissionStatusTimeline.SortDirection`
  (`SigningTimelineSortDirection`, default `Descending` — the historical newest-first order,
  Q-S9) and `HeaderContent` slots on the timeline and the audit viewer (the document
  name/status card is host content — the models stay unchanged, Q-S10). Every timestamp now
  formats through the shared `SigningDateFormatter` (local time, ambient culture) instead of
  scattered `ToString("g")` copies.

  - *Audit trail: the three `dl` card stacks are real tables.* Documents/Signers/Events render as
    `<table>` with `<th scope="col">`; the network evidence splits into two lines (IP primary,
    agent · zone secondary); signers get a `TmAvatar`; checksums render in `--tm-font-mono` with
    `overflow-wrap: anywhere`; empty values show an en dash instead of blank cells. Under a
    640px container the tables collapse to cards (the header cells are visually hidden and each
    cell re-labels itself through `data-label`):
    ```html
    <!-- before: a card per document/signer/event inside a framed section -->
    <section class="tm-audit-trail-viewer__section">
      <dl class="tm-audit-trail-viewer__document">…</dl>
    </section>

    <!-- after: a table on wide containers, cards (data-label repeats the column name) below 640 -->
    <table class="tm-audit-trail-viewer__table">
      <thead><tr><th scope="col">File name</th><th scope="col">Checksum</th></tr></thead>
      <tbody><tr><td data-label="File name">…</td><td data-label="Checksum">…</td></tr></tbody>
    </table>
    ```
    Host CSS that selected `.tm-audit-trail-viewer__document/-signer/-entry` must retarget to the
    table/row cells; the audit PDF link, the localization snapshot and the `HeaderContent` slot
    (replacing the default `<h2>`) are unchanged otherwise.
  - *Timeline: no more per-event cards.* Events are an `<ol>` list with one continuous axis
    (pseudo-element) and hairline separators; neutral/informational events paint the SOFT marker
    (`__marker--soft`), sent/completed/failed keep the solid disc; the recipient line gains the
    localized "Recipient:" prefix (`TmSubmissionStatusTimeline_RecipientPrefix`); the header
    wraps (`flex-wrap`). The item classes keep their severity modifiers
    (`__item--success/--danger/--info/--primary/--neutral`), so theme overrides survive.
    Sent events now carry `__item--primary` (previously `__item--neutral`) and the solid marker —
    overrides that styled Sent through `--neutral` must retarget.
    ```html
    <!-- before: each event was a bordered card -->
    <article class="tm-submission-status-timeline__item tm-submission-status-timeline__item--success">…</article>

    <!-- after: a list item on the shared axis (cards are gone) -->
    <ol class="tm-submission-status-timeline__items">
      <li class="tm-submission-status-timeline__item tm-submission-status-timeline__item--success">…</li>
    </ol>
    ```
  - *Verification: the status block is a `TmAlert`.* The custom status row became a core alert
    (`role="status"` for verified/not-found/loading, `role="alert"` for malformed/error) with the
    `tm-pdf-signature-verification__banner--{status}` modifier; each signature is a card with a
    `TmAvatar` header and a three-column `dl` (one column below a 640px container); the checksum
    shows the first 16 characters plus an ellipsis (the full value stays in the `title` attribute
    and on the new `TmCopyButton`); the detail keys `SignedAt`/`SigningMethod`/`Certificate`
    localize the signature card.
  - *Share panel: a real toggle and labelled fields.* The bare checkbox became a core `TmToggle`
    (`input[role="switch"]`), the link input gained a visible `label[for]`, both copy actions
    render the labelled `TmCopyButton` (`ShowLabel="true"`), the QR sits in a framed block with a
    localized scan hint (`TmShareLinkPanel_QrHint`), a separator divides the link area from the
    embed area, and the embed `<label for>` now actually points at the textarea (a11y bug fix).
    Below a 420px container the link/embed rows and the QR hint stack.
    ```html
    <!-- before: a bare checkbox with a text span, an aria-label-only input -->
    <label class="tm-share-link-panel__toggle"><input type="checkbox" …><span>Enabled</span></label>
    <input class="tm-share-link-panel__input" aria-label="Signing link" …>

    <!-- after: core switch, visible labels -->
    <div class="tm-toggle-wrapper"><input type="checkbox" role="switch" aria-checked="true" …></div>
    <label class="tm-share-link-panel__link-label" for="tm-share-link-…">Signing link</label>
    <input class="tm-share-link-panel__input tm-input" id="tm-share-link-…" …>
    ```
  - *Condition builder: core Tm components, one card, reorder buttons.* The native
    `<select>`/`<input>` controls became `TmSelect`/`TmTextInput` (the controls moved INSIDE the
    core component wrappers — `.tm-condition-builder__field` is now the `tm-select-wrapper` div,
    the native `<select>` is its child), the rows share ONE card with hairline separators, the
    add action is the dashed full-width row (`__add--dashed`), each row carries up/down reorder
    buttons (`__move-up`/`__move-down`, Q-S7 — the join operation stays positional: the leading
    row never shows an operation and normalizes back to `And` after a move), and the trash is the
    danger icon button it already was.
    ```html
    <!-- before: the control WAS the classed element -->
    <select class="tm-condition-builder__field" aria-label="Field" …>…</select>

    <!-- after: the wrapper carries the class, the native select is a child -->
    <div class="tm-select-wrapper tm-condition-builder__select tm-condition-builder__field">
      <select id="…" class="tm-select" aria-label="Field" …>…</select>…
    </div>
    ```
    Tests/hosts that changed `.tm-condition-builder__field` directly must select
    `.tm-condition-builder__field select` (or drive the component parameter).
  - *Formula builder: labelled groups, parentheses, cursor insertions.* The three palettes carry
    visible headings and `role="group"` + `aria-labelledby` (`aria-label`-on-a-`div` is gone);
    the operator grid adds `( )` (the grammar itself is unchanged — Q-S8); token cards show the
    field type under the label (`__token-label`/`__token-type`); the editor is the core
    `TmTextArea` (its error message replaces the builder's own alert row, so the invalid state is
    announced by the control itself); Save is the primary button. Insertions go through the
    `insertAtCursor` export of the package's neutral `signing-editor.js` module (dynamic
    `import()`, no script tag) and land at the textarea's cursor; a view without the module
    (bUnit, static render) still appends.
    ```html
    <!-- before: one flat toolbar with an aria-label, appended insertions -->
    <div class="tm-formula-builder__toolbar" aria-label="Formula operators">…</div>

    <!-- after: a labelled group, grid operators incl. ( ), cursor-aware insert -->
    <section class="tm-formula-builder__group" role="group" aria-labelledby="tm-formula-operators-…">
      <h3 id="tm-formula-operators-…" class="tm-formula-builder__section-title">Formula operators</h3>
      <div class="tm-formula-builder__toolbar">…<button data-operator="(">(</button>…</div>
    </section>
    ```
  - *Role editor: collapsible cards.* Each role row became a card with a header (drag handle,
    the order BADGE `__order-badge` instead of the read-only number input, the role pill painted
    in the role colour with the contrast-resolved text colour (`SigningRolePalette.ContrastTextFor`),
    a contact preview when collapsed, the reorder arrows — KEPT as the a11y alternative to drag
    & drop — the trash and the chevron toggle with `aria-expanded`/`aria-controls`). The body
    edits through `TmTextInput`/`TmSelect`; the palette swatches (`__swatch[data-color]` with
    `aria-pressed`) plus the "Custom…" native colour input replace the bare colour field; the
    drag handle hides on `(pointer: coarse)`. "Role name" stays editable, the three invite
    selects survive, and NO advanced-invitation section was added (Q-S6).
    ```html
    <!-- before: one grid row per role, the order as a read-only number input -->
    <div class="tm-recipient-role-editor__row">
      <input class="tm-recipient-role-editor__order-input" type="number" readonly value="1">
      <input class="tm-recipient-role-editor__color" type="color" value="#2563eb">…

    <!-- after: a collapsible card; header = badge + pill + preview + actions -->
    <div class="tm-recipient-role-editor__card" data-role-uuid="…">
      <header class="tm-recipient-role-editor__card-header">
        <span class="tm-recipient-role-editor__order-badge">1</span>
        <span class="tm-recipient-role-editor__role-pill" style="--tm-signing-role-color: …">Approver</span>
        <button class="tm-recipient-role-editor__toggle" aria-expanded="true" aria-controls="…">…</button>
      </header>
      <div class="tm-recipient-role-editor__card-body">
        <div class="tm-recipient-role-editor__swatches">
          <button class="tm-recipient-role-editor__swatch" data-color="#2563eb" aria-pressed="true"></button>…
        </div>…
      </div>
    </div>
    ```
    The old hooks `__order-input`, `__color` (now inside `__swatch-custom`), `__row` and the
    always-visible `__move-up`/`__move-down` header buttons moved: hosts/tests that reordered via
    the arrows find them in the card HEADER; the validation row renders inside the card body.

  - *Phase 7 review (code/UX/architect follow-up).* The panels and editors above received the
    review fixes; all additive, no host action:
    - **Role pill ink is token-driven.** `SigningRolePalette.ContrastTextFor` now picks the ink
      with the HIGHER ACTUAL WCAG contrast ratio and, for every default-palette colour (and the
      legacy `#ca8a04`), emits `var(--tm-signing-role-N-on)` instead of a computed hex. New
      per-theme token pairs `--tm-signing-role-1..6-on` in `tokens-signing.css`
      (`:root`, dark, light-island), each ≥ 4.5:1 (re-verified by test against the stylesheet).
      A colour-less (or unparsable) pill rides `var(--tm-color-on-primary)`; only a CUSTOM colour
      computes — and it takes the fixed tone classes `__role-pill--on-light` /
      `__role-pill--on-dark` (mapped to `--tm-signing-role-ink-dark` /
      `--tm-color-on-primary-fixed`) instead of an inline hex. `--tm-signing-role-ink-dark`
      (`#111827`) is declared on `:root` only and is never overridden: dark and indigo themes
      redefine `--tm-color-gray-900` to white, which would paint white text on a light custom pill.
      `ContrastTextFor` returns that token name (or `var(--tm-color-on-primary-fixed)`) for a
      custom colour — never a hex.
    - **Focus survives remove/move.** `TmRecipientRoleEditor` and `TmConditionBuilder` queue the
      focus move and apply it in `OnAfterRenderAsync` through the neutral `signing-editor.js`
      module (`focusElement`, document injectable; `SigningEditorInterop` replaces the editors'
      use of the runner's wrapper). A remove lands the focus on the surviving row's action (the
      Add action is the fallback); a move keeps the focus INSIDE the moved card/row — the
      same-direction button, or the opposite one once the edge disables it — and announces
      "{0} moved to position {1}" (`TmRecipientRoleEditor_RoleMoved` /
      `TmConditionBuilder_ConditionMoved`) through an always-rendered polite live region. Role
      cards are keyed by `role.Uuid`, condition rows by per-row Guids (`data-row-id`), so the
      DOM (and the focus) travels with the moved item. All three editors (`TmRecipientRoleEditor`,
      `TmConditionBuilder`, `TmFormulaBuilder`) are `IAsyncDisposable`: they release their
      imported module on dispose (the same shape the runner already had).
    - **Typing is never normalized mid-keystroke.** The role editor's name/full name/email/phone
      and the condition builder's value keep the RAW text while typing (no notify, no
      re-normalization per keystroke) and commit + normalize on blur or Enter.
    - **Coarse pointers get 44 px targets** on the role editor's header buttons, palette swatches
      and colour input, the condition builder's move/remove pair and the formula builder's
      operators/functions/tokens (`--tm-touch-target` under `@media (pointer: coarse)`); the
      condition builder's stacked (<768px container) move row sizes to content and aligns to the
      row start.
    - **Smaller a11y fixes:** the toggle's `aria-controls` renders only while the card is
      expanded; the order badge carries a visually-hidden "Signing order {0}"
      (`TmRecipientRoleEditor_SigningOrder`) with a decorative number; palette swatches announce
      localized colour names (`TmRecipientRoleEditor_ColorBlue`…`ColorAmber`); the share toggle's
      label is the static "Link sharing" (`TmShareLinkPanel_EnableSharing`) and the redundant
      `Disabled="false"` is gone; the audit tables carry explicit
      `table/rowgroup/row/columnheader/cell` roles (the narrow-panel card collapse would
      otherwise drop the semantics); the audit viewer renders no header at all without a trail
      and without a `HeaderContent` slot, and its avatar falls back to the signer's email; the
      verification panel shows the localized "Unknown signer"
      (`TmPdfSignatureVerification_UnknownSigner`) for a signature without name or email; the
      formula operator keys carry localized spoken names (`TmFormulaBuilder_OperatorPlus`…); the
      timeline's `mail-x` / `shield-check` icons are registered built-ins (`IconNames.MailX` /
      `IconNames.ShieldCheck`); `TmDocumentCommentItem` formats timestamps through the shared
      `SigningDateFormatter`.
### Fixed

- **Notion editor: a code block's last line is no longer hidden behind the horizontal scrollbar.** A long line used to grow a scrollbar inside the textarea while the outer `.tm-notion-code-block` (`overflow: auto`) grew a second one, and `scrollHeight` did not include the bar, so the last line sat under it. The textarea now grows by its own scrollbar chrome, the outer block no longer scrolls, and the height is recomputed on window/container resize and after `setCode`.

- **Signing: a palette or field drag no longer also draws on the page.** The palette session stops the press before the page surface's bubble listener, so a drag places or moves a field and does not start a selection box. `ButtonVariant.OutlinePrimary` is the Autodetect toolbar variant.
- **Core: `TmContextMenuItem` keeps `OnClick` across the close render.** The item copies the callback, closes the parent, then invokes it, so a menu that unmounts on close still runs the action.
- **Core: the "More" overflow menu of `TmToolbar` / `TmMobileActionBar` now stays inside the viewport.**
  The shared `ActionOverflowMenu` panel opens with `TmOverlayPanel.ConstrainHeight` in addition to the
  flip/clamp placement it already used, so a menu taller than the room on its resolved side flips above
  its trigger when that side has room and otherwise caps its height to the room it has and scrolls
  internally. Before, only flip + clamp applied: a panel taller than the viewport was pinned to the top
  margin and simply ran past the bottom edge — the Spreadsheet's tablet rows put ~18 commands and three
  expanded lists into one "More" (a 1209 px panel in a 768 px viewport, ~450 px of it off-screen), and a
  top-layer panel has no page scroll to bring those entries back, so a tablet user could not reach them
  at all. The public API is unchanged (the knob already existed on `TmOverlayPanel`) and a menu that
  fits below its trigger is placed exactly as before. Guards:
  `TmToolbarOverflowTests.MoreMenu_AsksThePanelToStayInsideTheViewport` (the options the panel opens
  with) and `SpreadsheetPhase8OverflowE2ETests` (tablet 1024×768 with a menu taller than the viewport,
  and a 430 px short window whose trigger sits near the bottom — both assert the panel and the last
  entry are inside the viewport and that the entry is clickable). Found by the phase-6 bisect of
  `SpreadsheetE2ETests.Phase3_Dialogs_Tablet1024Touch_StayDialogs_WithTouchSizedTargets`
  (plan 8959eebe, f25a9d47).

- **Spreadsheet redesign (phase 8): a host shorter than the phone chrome no longer renders an empty
  grid.** `TmSpreadsheet` keeps a new `--tm-spreadsheet-grid-min-height` (default `9rem`) floor on the
  phone grid and `.tm-spreadsheet--layout-mobile` may scroll its own box, so a host that overrides the
  phone height floor (the Notion fullscreen editor sets `--tm-spreadsheet-mobile-min-height: 0` at
  568×320 so its Save / Discard footer stays visible) shows rows again instead of a grid resolved to
  ~0px. A host tall enough for the chrome plus the floor never scrolls. Guards:
  `SpreadsheetDesignTokenTests.MobileLayout_KeepsAUsableGridFloor_WhenTheHostIsShorterThanTheChrome` and
  `SpreadsheetPhase6ResponsiveE2ETests.Phase6_NotionEditModal_At390_IsMobile_AndKeepsTheFooterInView`
  (grid ≥ 96 px and reachable by scrolling at 844 and 320 px).
- **Spreadsheet redesign (phase 8): the wireframe `TmSpreadsheet` stencil stops drawing command chips
  under the phone "More" chip.** The mobile variant used to paint the alignment/merge chips onward
  across `el.W - 30` (the "More" chip) on a 340 px element; a chip that would reach the "More" chip is
  now skipped, and no coordinate of a compact row exceeds `el.W - 18`.

### Known issues

- **Signing external / phone / attachment steps WITHOUT the host callbacks remain documented
  placeholders (SI2 — narrowed in phase 6).** When a host does NOT wire the phase-6 active-step
  callbacks, the legacy behaviour stands: clicking "Start verification" / "Checkout" marks the
  step complete WITHOUT any verification or payment taking place, the phone step sends no SMS and
  checks no OTP, and the attachment step's upload stays in the browser — the resulting field
  values are untrusted presentation state, and the "Verified" / "Paid" status reflects the STORED
  value (a tampered stored value still shows as verified). Wire the callbacks (see Added below) to
  close this: with `OnVerifyPhoneCode` / `OnAttachmentSelected` / `OnExternalStepRequested` wired,
  a phone step completes only after the host verifier answers `true`, the attachment card carries
  the host-returned upload url, and an external step completes solely after the host stores the
  provider result through `Values`. The "Known limitations / security note" wording in the XML
  docs and the JSON component documentation now describes this contract (and the SignalR note on
  reading the uploaded file at the host).

### Added
- **Core: `pointer-drag.js` listens in the capture phase when `listenerCapture` is set, and `TmContextMenu` reports open changes.** `listenerCapture` starts a gesture even when a child calls `stopPropagation`; detach removes that listener. `TmContextMenu.Open()` is public and idempotent. `IsOpenChanged` is raised from `SetOpenAsync` (toggle, `Open`, `CloseMenu` and an overlay dismiss) after the open state has changed, and the callback is awaited.
- **Signing redesign (phase 8): the field inspector is built from Tm components and its sections collapse.** `TmSigningFieldEditorPanel` renders actions, selection and an optional geometry section through `TmSigningFieldEditorActions`. New callbacks: `OnCopyRequested`, `OnDeleteRequested`, `OnCopySelectionRequested`, `OnPasteRequested`, `OnDeleteSelectionRequested`. `ShowGeometry`, `PageWidth` and `PageHeight` expose a numeric resize (WCAG 2.5.7). `TmPdfTemplateDesigner.LayoutBreakpoints` defaults to 768 / 1200. `TmContextMenu.Open()` opens the designer's one menu. The overlay pointer callbacks take `TmSigningFieldOverlayPointerEventArgs`.

- **Spreadsheet redesign (phase 8): `TmSpreadsheet` honours the core `data-testid` contract.**
  The component now derives from `TmComponentBase` and its root renders
  `data-testid="@RootTestId()"` before the splatted attributes, so `DataTestId` labels the root (and a
  host can still override it through `AdditionalAttributes`) while `TestIdPrefix` namespaces the
  internal ids (`tm-spreadsheet-header`, `-header-open`, `-header-download`, `tm-spreadsheet-mobile-header`
  → `{prefix}-…`). Without `DataTestId` the root carries no `data-testid`, so no existing DOM changes;
  guarded by `TmSpreadsheetTestIdTests`.


- **Wireframe stencil: the `TmSpreadsheet` stencil draws the tablet and phone chrome (`layoutMode`, additive).** The stencil used to preview the DESKTOP tabbed ribbon only, so a designer could not show what a spreadsheet looks like on a tablet or a phone. `TempoNativeRendererDefinitions.RenderSpreadsheet` now reads the same `layoutMode` prop (`auto | desktop | tablet | mobile`, default `auto`) the diagram editor and dashboard stencils already expose, and the `TmSpreadsheet` wireframe schema offers it in the inspector's Behavior group:

  | `layoutMode` | What the stencil draws |
  |---|---|
  | `auto` (default, and any unknown value) | the desktop chrome — tab strip + labelled ribbon groups. `auto` renders the desktop variant because a stencil communicates a chosen presentation, it does not re-flow the canvas (X11) |
  | `desktop` | the same desktop chrome |
  | `tablet` | TWO compact command rows (`data-region="command-row" data-row-count="2"`, no tab strip), then the formula bar, the grid, the sheet tabs and the status bar |
  | `mobile` | the compact header (the document title + the host action slot), ONE command row, the formula bar, the grid, the sheet tabs and the core mobile action bar (Insert / Format / Image / More) instead of the status bar |

  `showHeader` keeps its meaning on desktop and tablet, and on the mobile variant the compact header REPLACES the document header (the two are mutually exclusive in the real component, so exactly one header paints). The SVG now carries `data-layout` on the variant group and a `data-region` on every chrome block (`header`, `mobile-header`, `ribbon-tabs`, `ribbon-groups`, `command-row`, `formula-bar`, `grid`, `sheet-tabs`, `status-bar`, `action-bar`), so a spec can assert which chrome was drawn instead of matching pixels. The change is purely additive: the renderer only reuses the stencil palette constants (no new literal), no shared wireframe contract changed, and the desktop variant paints exactly what it painted before. Guarded by `WireframeSpreadsheetRendererTests` (`RenderSpreadsheet_LayoutModeAuto_IsDesktop`, `…_LayoutModeTablet_DrawsTwoCompactRows`, `…_LayoutModeMobile_DrawsCompactHeaderOneRowAndActionBar`, the unknown-value fallback and the `showHeader` interaction); documented in [docs/wireframe-editor.md](docs/wireframe-editor.md#the-tmspreadsheet-stencil-draws-every-chrome-layout).

- **Spreadsheet redesign (phase 7c): the dialogs at 320 px, the Sort phone toolbar and a canvas that follows a LIVE theme flip.**

  - **Sort on a phone is the reference's two columns.** The dialog's top bar is a two-column grid — "Add level" on the left, the "My data has headers" / "Case sensitive" checkboxes STACKED on the right (before, both wrapped onto a row under the button). Below `@container (width < 20rem)` of the dialog body the options stack UNDER the button: at 320 px readability wins over the reference (documented in [docs/spreadsheet.md](docs/spreadsheet.md#dialogs-at-320-px)). The desktop/tablet level table is unchanged and the core `TmCheckbox` roots keep their classes and `data-testid`s.
  - **Name Manager / Format Cells survive 320 px.** The Name Manager card keeps the name on one ellipsised line, WRAPS the "Refers to" formula (`overflow-wrap: anywhere`, clamped to two lines, full value in `title` + `aria-label`) and moves the scope chip under the name at `@container (width < 22rem)` — measured on the dialog's own width, so 320 (20rem) flips it and a 390 phone keeps the reference's two columns (decision `SPREADSHEET-NAME-MANAGER-320-WRAP`). Format Cells keeps its phase-4 category `TmSelect` above the options, guarded by a regression test.
  - **A live theme flip repaints the canvas.** `spreadsheet-canvas.js` now watches `data-theme` and `data-tm-theme` on `documentElement` (one `MutationObserver` per grid instance, disconnected in `dispose`) and rebuilds the palette + requests a FULL redraw, so a dark/light or indigo flip recolours the headers, the selection and the content immediately instead of waiting for a resize. Node lane: `themeAttributeChange_RebuildsThePalette` (`npm run test:spreadsheet`); E2E: `Phase7c_LiveThemeFlip_RepaintsTheCanvasWithoutResize` (no viewport nudge).
  - **Data Validation keeps its measured breakpoint.** `TmSpreadsheetDataValidationDialog` stays `ModalSize.Medium`, so the `@container (width >= 640px)` threshold still describes the OVERLAY; guarded by `DataValidationDialog_KeepsMediumSize_ForOverlayBreakpoint` and documented next to the rule.

- **Spreadsheet redesign (phase 7b): the header labels scale with the density, the dark active header is opaque, and the canvas exposes its live cell geometry.** The follow-up pass over the phase-2/6/7 carry-forwards:

  - **Comfortable scales the header LABEL too.** `drawHeaders` paints `--tm-spreadsheet-header-font` scaled by the density font scale (`resolveHeaderFont`), so the 11 px labels become 13.75 px on a 28 px Comfortable gutter instead of staying cramped next to 12.5 pt cells. The token itself is untouched — a host override still wins — and Compact paints the token exactly (no rounding drift). The `gutterScale` also travels in the canvas frame (`DensityGutterScale`) so the frame and the JS rule can never disagree.
  - **Two public JS getters replace every hardcoded 40/20 in tests and integrations.** `tmSpreadsheetCanvas.getCellCenter(root, row, col)` returns the cell centre in the root element's coordinate space and `tmSpreadsheetCanvas.getGridGutters(root)` returns `{ rowHeaderWidth, columnHeaderHeight, density, gutterScale }`. Both read the FRAME (the component already scaled the gutters), so a density change can never move a cell centre out from under a spec again; the E2E `GetCanvasCellCenterAsync` helper and the inline pixel-sample probes now call them instead of recomputing `gutter + left - scroll`.
  - **Opaque dark active header.** See Fixed — the override lives in the package's theme layer, `wwwroot/css/theme-spreadsheet-dark.css`, imported by the package bundle (`tempo-blazor-spreadsheet.css`). A host that imports the individual CSS files instead of the bundle must import that theme file too; the read-only Notion preview and the edit modal get it automatically.
  - **Wall-clock performance evidence.** New `SpreadsheetPerformanceE2ETests.SelectionDrag_AB_WithinBudget` (`TestCategory=Performance`, outside the smoke lane) runs the selection-drag scenario as an in-session A/B — the shipped `v2.9.0` canvas script served through Playwright route interception against the current build, seven alternations per arm — and reports median + IQR; `median(current) <= 1.10 x median(v2.9.0)` passes, an IQR above 30 % of the median reports **Inconclusive with the numbers**. Every run writes `eng/release-evidence/spreadsheet-perf-<yyyyMMdd>/` as `selection-drag-ab-<HHmmss>.json` + `summary-<HHmmss>.md` (a same-day re-run never overwrites the previous sample). **Current evidence (20261029): Inconclusive** — noise (IQR/median) 50–63 %, above the 30 % threshold, with the ratio's sign flipping between the two runs; the wall-clock budget is awaiting a run on an idle machine or the perf lane. Note the `v2.9.0` arm has no header-highlight layer at all, so it is not a like-for-like arm for this scenario (the deterministic counters are green: one header paint per selection change, zero content repaints, header paint < 5 ms). See [docs/spreadsheet.md](docs/spreadsheet.md#density--the-gutter-scale-and-the-hit-areas).

- **Spreadsheet redesign (phase 7): touch interaction on the canvas.** The grid's gestures now come from the shared core helpers (`pointer-drag.js` for the single pointer, `pointer-gesture.js` `attachPinch` for two fingers), loaded by a dynamic `import()` resolved from `document.currentScript.src` — the package writes no drag and no pinch of its own. On top of the recognizer:

  | Gesture | Result |
  |---|---|
  | tap | selects the cell (the compatibility click is swallowed, so the mouse and the touch path can never both act on one press) |
  | double tap (≤ 320 ms, ≤ 24 px) | opens the cell editor with the virtual keyboard the cell type asks for — `inputmode="decimal"` for a numeric/percent cell, `text` otherwise (dates included) |
  | long press (500 ms) | opens the cell menu at the finger — the phone layout's bottom sheet, the anchored menu on tablet/desktop. A 400 ms release-click guard stops the lifting finger's click from closing it again |
  | one-finger drag on a cell | the browser's native pan — the canvas never starts a drag-select from a finger |
  | drag a ROUND corner drop (top-left / bottom-right) | extends the selection, anchor preserved (drag-only) |
  | drag the fill handle | fills (unchanged fill semantics, now with a finger-sized hit box) |
  | two-finger pinch | commits one clamped 10 % zoom step through the new `OnZoomChanged` (the status bar / the phone's More menu are the WCAG 2.5.7 alternative) |

  The corner drops are **drag-only** and the four 24 px EDGE STRIPS of the first implementation are gone: a strip along the selection's edge covered the selected row/column on a phone (30 px rows vs a 44 px finger box) and swallowed the taps and long-presses meant for the cell itself. A tap on a drop does nothing; a tap on the cell next to the selection selects that cell.

  **WCAG 2.5.7 for the fill handle.** A fill is now also reachable from the cell menu's **Fill down** / **Fill right** entries and from **Ctrl+D** / **Ctrl+R** (the canvas claims both chords, so Ctrl+D does not open the browser's bookmark dialog and Ctrl+R does not reload the page). Both go through the C# `AutoFillCommand` — the same pattern engine the pointer drag's JS commit uses, but not a byte-identical code path: the command path fills **every column** (Fill down) / **every row** (Fill right) of the selection, excludes the source row/column from the target, and copies the source cell's FORMAT like Excel, all inside one `BatchCommand` (one undo step). A single-cell selection copies the cell above/left (Excel's behaviour) and an empty source is a no-op — a stray Ctrl+D never clears a cell. New resource keys, all four languages: `TmSpreadsheet_FillDown`, `TmSpreadsheet_FillRight`. New `SpreadsheetFillDirection` enum, `SpreadsheetCellStyle.CopyFrom`, and grid parameters `OnZoomChanged` / `OnFillRequested`.

  **Read-only grids do not offer the mutating menu.** `TmSpreadsheet` builds the host cell menu from `Mode`; an `Embedded` (read-only) spreadsheet offers only Format Cells, Copy, column width and row height — no Paste, Cut, Fill down/right, insert/delete or Clear. A long press inside the CURRENT selection keeps that range (Excel), so the menu's commands act on the whole block instead of collapsing it to the pressed cell.

- **Spreadsheet redesign (phase 7): the density scales the canvas header gutters, and Auto follows the pointer.** `SpreadsheetDensityScale` gained `GutterScale` (1.4 at Comfortable): the row-header gutter draws 40 × 1.4 = 56 px and the column header 20 × 1.4 = 28 px instead of staying at the compact sizes, which is what the tablet reference draws and what gives the auto-filter button a finger-sized height. The gutter values travel in the canvas frame (`RowHeaderWidth` / `ColumnHeaderHeight`), so the canvas, the hit-testing and the component geometry cannot drift apart, and the model is untouched. The auto-filter button's HIT rect grows to the touch floor on a coarse pointer (inside its own column and header gutter) while a fine pointer keeps the painted rect exactly. `Density=Auto` is no longer frozen at the first frame: a `matchMedia('(pointer: coarse)')` listener re-resolves it when the pointer kind flips (a mouse attached to a tablet, a 2-in-1 undocked) and repaints; a forced `Compact`/`Comfortable` is unaffected. The canvas's first paint already used the resolved scale (the coarse-pointer interop completes before the engine is initialised), so no compact rows are painted on a touch device.

- **Fixed (Spreadsheet formula bar): an unrelated parent render no longer overwrites a ref typed into the name box.** `TmSpreadsheetFormulaBar` re-seeded its controlled `_nameBoxValue` from `ActiveCellRef` on EVERY parent pass, so any render that landed between the keystroke and the Enter (a command-log flush after a canvas click, the viewport sync the grid's focusout schedules) patched the input back to the active cell and the Enter navigated there instead of to the typed ref. It is now seeded only when the active cell actually changed. Related: the grid takes the focus back after a canvas activation only while the focus is not already in another control (`tmSpreadsheetCanvas.isFocusOutside`), so a late frame cannot blur a control the user has moved to.

- **Signing active-steps contract (Signing redesign phase 6, S2-5/SI2), all opt-in.** The phone
  OTP, the attachment upload and the external verification become HOST-CONFIRMED steps.
  `TmSigningFormRunner` gains `OnSendPhoneCode`
  (`EventCallback<SigningPhoneCodeRequest>`), `OnVerifyPhoneCode`
  (`Func<SigningPhoneVerificationRequest, Task<bool>>`), `OnAttachmentSelected`
  (`Func<SigningAttachmentUploadRequest, Task<string?>>`), `OnExternalStepRequested`
  (`EventCallback<SigningExternalStepRequest>` — the field plus the typed KBA answers) and
  `StepContextProvider`
  (`Func<SigningField, SigningExternalStepContext?>`), with the four new contract records
  (`SigningPhoneCodeRequest`, `SigningPhoneVerificationRequest`, `SigningExternalStepContext`,
  `SigningAttachmentUploadRequest`) in the Signing package. The contract:
  - *Phone.* While `OnVerifyPhoneCode` is wired, a phone field completes ONLY after the host
    verifier answers `true` (the runner records the confirmation; a rejected code shows the
    localized "code is not valid" message and never completes the step); the typed OTP is never
    stored as the field value. `OnSendPhoneCode` receives the normalized number on every
    send/resend.
  - *Upload.* `OnAttachmentSelected` receives the picked `IBrowserFile` and its returned url is
    stored on the attachment card. Read the content in the HOST (`File.OpenReadStream`) — on
    Blazor Server browser files stream over SignalR with tight message limits. The step itself
    never reads a picked file's content beyond the optional local image thumbnail.
  - *External.* With `OnExternalStepRequested` wired, the Start/Checkout click only notifies the
