    host — the step completes solely after the host stores the provider result (value `true`)
    through `Values`; `StepContextProvider` feeds the provider page url, inline KBA questions,
    loading state, error and provider name per field. The provider link keeps
    `rel="noopener noreferrer"` and now carries a localized redirect note
    (`TmSigningStep_RedirectNote`) and provider line (`TmSigningStep_ExternalProvider`).
  Without the callbacks, today's documented behaviour stands unchanged (regression-tested): the
  typed phone completes the step, uploads stay client-side metadata and the external click stores
  `true` — presentation state, never proof that a verification, payment or upload happened.
  No breaking change without the callbacks wired. New localized keys `TmSigningStep_Verify`,
  `_Resend`, `_InvalidCode`, `_FileTooLarge`, `_TooManyFiles`, `_ExternalProvider` and
  `_RedirectNote` in en / cs / sk / fr + `MockTmLocalizer`.
- **Signing active-steps review fixes (phase 6 review) — reviewed-contract hardening.**
  - *Phone verification is bound to the NUMBER.* The runner keeps the host confirmation in a
    uuid → verified-number map (runner-internal, never in `Values`) — a phone step is verified
    only while the field's current value still equals the number the OTP was verified for, so
    editing the number (or a host-pushed value change) makes the step incomplete again. The
    verified state LOCKS the number input and the country select and replaces "Send code" with a
    Secondary **Change number** action (`TmSigningStep_ChangeNumber`) that clears the host
    confirmation and unlocks the editing.
  - *Upload contract.* A host resolver returning `null` (or throwing — cancellation aside)
    REJECTS the file: it never joins the attachments and the localized
    `TmSigningStep_UploadFailed` ("{0} could not be uploaded.") shows. The local image preview is
    presentation-only: it lives in a component-local map keyed by the attachment uuid and is
    never written into the persisted `Url` (the legacy path keeps `Url` null). The upload round
    trip is BUSY state: the drop zone disables and a spinner row announces "Uploading {name}…"
    (`TmSigningStep_Uploading`) through a polite live region, cleared in `finally`. Single-file
    mode keeps the existing attachment when nothing was accepted (a rejected replacement no
    longer drops the previous file). The platform read budget matches `MaxFiles`
    (`GetMultipleFiles(Math.Max(MaxFiles ?? 10, 1))`, the same value on
    `TmFileDropZone.MaxFileCount` — an overflow pick degrades to an empty readable set, and the
    change event still fires so the localized limit message can render). The preview data url
    uses the decoded image's content type and only PNG/JPEG/GIF/WebP picks are previewed (SVG
    skipped). `MaxFileSize` is CLIENT-REPORTED — hosts must enforce the real limit via
    `OpenReadStream(maxAllowedSize)`.
  - *External opt-in completion.* With `OnExternalStepRequested` wired, the external/KBA/payment
    field completes ONLY for the confirmed provider result — value `true` or the string
    `"true"` (case-insensitive); the string `"false"` keeps the step incomplete. Legacy rule
    unchanged without the callback.
  - *KBA submit.* The questions branch gains a "Submit answers" action
    (`TmSigningStep_SubmitAnswers`), and `OnExternalStepRequested` now carries
    `SigningExternalStepRequest` (`Field` + `IReadOnlyDictionary<string, string?> Answers`) —
    the typed KBA answers ride the request to the host and are NEVER stored as the field value.
  - *Host callback errors.* Send/Verify are guarded against double-raises; a failing
    `OnVerifyPhoneCode` / `OnSendPhoneCode` (cancellation aside) shows the localized
    `TmSigningStep_VerificationUnavailable` message, NEVER marks the step verified and starts no
    countdown; the resend countdown starts only after the host accepted the send; a send on an
    empty number returns early without raising the callback; the request records
    (`SigningPhoneCodeRequest`, `SigningPhoneVerificationRequest`) now carry non-nullable
    `Phone`. All active-step requests gained an init-only `CancellationToken` fed from a
    runner-owned source cancelled in `DisposeAsync`.
  - *Focus and announcements (WCAG 2.4.3/4.1.3).* The phone and external steps each keep ONE
    always-rendered visually-hidden `role=status` polite region announcing the phase events
    ("Code sent", "Verified"/"Paid", "Resend available" — new keys `TmSigningStep_CodeSent`,
    `_ResendAvailable`; "Loading…" reuses `_LoadingExternal`); the inserted verified/loading
    blocks carry no role of their own and the ticking countdown text is `aria-live="off"`. After
    a successful verification the runner moves focus to the step title (navigation signal);
    after send/resend the OTP input takes the focus; while the provider runs the external
    Start/Checkout action stays IN PLACE, disabled and `aria-busy`. The invalid-code error is
    owned by the OTP input (`aria-invalid` + described-by there, phone input clean) and clears
    when a new draft is typed. After a code was sent the Send action is Secondary and disabled
    while the countdown runs. The outbound provider link references the redirect note via
    `aria-describedby` (the note carries a stable id) and the external-link icon is
    aria-hidden; the verified state reads "Verified by {provider}"
    (`TmSigningStep_VerifiedBy`) when the provider names itself. The runner keeps the per-field
    code-sent state and the OTP draft, so navigating away and back restores the OTP row and the
    typed draft. `TmSigningPhoneStep` stays `IAsyncDisposable` (the Blazor renderer prefers the
    async interface when both are present — the same decision the runner documents; the
    countdown `ITimer` is released there); the countdown tick is guarded by a `_disposed` flag
    (the nested `InvokeAsync` was removed) and the countdown stops once verified. New keys in
    en / cs / sk / fr + `MockTmLocalizer`.
  - *Host-reported send state (review fix).* Inside the runner the phone step no longer trusts
    its own send click: the runner cascades `TmSigningRunnerHosted` and clears the per-field sent
    state while its dispatch runs, so the OTP row, the resend countdown and the "Code sent"
    announcement appear ONLY when the host-reported `CodeSent` parameter flips `true` — a
    THROWING/failing `OnSendPhoneCode` leaves the plain phone form with the localized
    unavailable alert (no row, no countdown, no announcement) and a successful retry raises the
    row through the same flip. A mount that arrives with `CodeSent` already true (navigating away
    and back) resumes a ticking countdown without re-announcing the send. Standalone steps keep
    the local behaviour. The after-send OTP focus moves WITHOUT `preventScroll`, so the browser
    scrolls the code row into view in every scrollable ancestor (the capped desktop panel and the
    390 bottom sheet included); the move defers past the in-flight render (a browser ignores
    focus on a disabled input), and the RUNNER additionally reveals the whole code row
    (`scrollIntoView` `block: 'nearest'` through `signing-runner.js`, honoured by the node lane)
    so the Verify action and the fresh countdown stay visible inside the mobile sheet. Also fixed
    a double-prefix normalization bug: re-sending the stored normalized number produced
    `+420420…` — a number already carrying the SELECTED calling code now keeps its digits
    verbatim.
  - *Per field+operation cancellation (review fix).* The active-step requests' runner-owned
    cancellation is now ONE source PER FIELD+OPERATION (phone send / verify, attachment upload,
    external flow, keyed by field uuid) instead of a single global source: a new request
    supersedes only its own slot's predecessor — a verify on one field no longer cancels an
    in-flight send on another. `DisposeAsync` still cancels ALL live sources, and the contract
    records' XML docs describe the narrowed scope. New tests pin the per-field/per-operation
    isolation, the request payload (field uuid + normalized phone) and the no-OTP-row-on-failure
    contract; the phase-6 capture for the rejected code scrolls the step alert into view (the
    capped desktop panel scrolls internally) and `TmSigningStepAttachment.Url`'s XML/JSON summary
    now reads "Host-provided download/storage URL (the upload result); never a client-generated
    preview."
- **TmFileDropZone: the hidden file input stays invisible when disabled.** `_file-drop-zone.css`
  pins `.tm-file-drop-zone__input, .tm-file-drop-zone__input[disabled] { opacity: 0; }` — a UA
  or host stylesheet that dims disabled inputs would otherwise paint the native file picker over
  the drop area while the zone is busy/disabled (`tempo-blazor.bundled.css` regenerated).
- **TmFileDropZone: the MaxFileCount budget degrades safely.** An overflow pick (more files than
  the budget) used to throw the platform exception; it now degrades to an empty readable set and
  the change event still fires, so a consumer can render its own localized limit message
  (additive; hosts whose picks never overflow never see a change).
- **Signing phone step runs a real resend countdown (Signing redesign phase 6).** `TmSigningPhoneStep`
  gains `Verified` (the host-confirmed state that replaces the OTP row) and `OnVerifyCode`, and the
  countdown now TICKS on the injectable `TimeProvider` (the same seam the runner's autosave uses —
  tests advance a `FakeTimeProvider`, no sleeps): "Send code" starts the
  `ResendSeconds` window (default 30), the text counts down, and at zero it becomes the real
  localized "Resend" action which re-sends and restarts the window. The timer is disposed with the
  component. A standalone host without `OnVerifyCode` renders no Verify action — the legacy
  behaviour is byte-identical.
- **Signing attachment limits and local image preview (Signing redesign phase 6).**
  `TmSigningAttachmentStep` gains `MaxFileSize` (bytes; a larger file shows the localized
  `{0} is larger than the allowed {1}` message — culturally formatted — and never joins the
  attachments), `MaxFiles` (localized `up to {0} files` message; the first files stay), `Capture`
  (the native `capture` camera attribute, Image fields only) and `UploadUrlResolver`
  (the runner's host upload hook; the resolver's url wins over the local preview). Without a host
  url, an Image pick renders a LOCAL downscaled thumbnail through the core
  `RequestImageFileAsync` (no custom JS; best-effort — a refused stream simply skips the preview;
  note the core API refuses custom `IBrowserFile` implementations, so bUnit cannot exercise the
  decoder — the rendered preview is covered by the phase-6 E2E suite against the real browser
  pipeline).
- **Signing demo: the active-steps fake host.** The `/signing-components` demo gains an
  "Active Steps Contract" runner (`signing-active-steps-demo`) wired to a demo-only host: OTP code
  `123456`, an in-memory PNG upload (with a deliberate delay so the busy state is visible) and a
  simulated provider that confirms the verification after ~400 ms — no step completes until the
  host confirms it. A "Simulate provider failure" toggle (`signing-active-steps-fail-toggle`)
  demonstrates the provider-error state, and the standalone image step carries a small
  `MaxFileSize` so the size-limit rejection is demonstrable.
- **Signing runner mobile sheet plumbing (Signing redesign phase 5), all additive.**
  `TmSigningFormRunner` gains `LayoutMode` / `ResolvedLayoutChanged` (the F1 self-classification
  pair, the Gantt pattern) and `DefaultSignatureMode` (SI3, see the Breaking / Migration entry
  above); `TmSigningChoiceStep` gains the pass-through `LayoutMode` that presents ≤5 options as
  radio cards on a mobile layout (SI1) — `Auto` does not measure; the runner passes its resolved
  mode down, standalone hosts that want the narrow presentation pass `Mobile` explicitly. The
  mobile sheet grows the `.tm-signing-form-runner__sheet-handle` toggle (its only `aria-expanded`
  control), the `.tm-signing-form-runner__sheet-progress` peek strip (its own polite status region
  while collapsed) and the `--tm-signing-sheet-peek-height` root knob, and the action row the
  `.tm-signing-form-runner__more` overflow (`TmSigningFormRunner_More`, `_ShowFields`,
  `_ShowDocument`, `_SheetExpand`, `_SheetCollapse` — en/cs/sk/fr). The unused
  `TmSigningFormRunner_Minimize` key was removed (the Minimize row is gone — see Breaking above),
  and the optional select's card set gained `TmSigningChoiceStep_None` ("None" / "Žádná" /
  "Žiadna" / "Aucun"), all four `TmResources` tables + `MockTmLocalizer`. The package's new
  `signing-runner.js` ES module (`_content/Tempo.Blazor.Signing/js/signing-runner.js`, dynamic
  `import()` — no `<script>` tag; node lane `npm run test:signing-runner`) ships
  `isCoarsePointer`, `scrollToField` (single scroll above the sheet, reduced-motion aware) and
  `focusFieldButton` (the field-list focus move), and the field overlay root now carries
  `data-field-uuid` as the scroll anchor. The runner implements `IAsyncDisposable` (only — the
  sync `Dispose` never ran next to it): disposing cancels the pending autosave debounce and
  releases the module instance, with `JSDisconnectedException` kept local everywhere.
- **Core splat hooks for host a11y plumbing (Signing redesign phase 4 review), all additive.**
  `TmSelect` gains `SelectAttributes` (splatted on the native `<select>`; entries win over the
  component's own attributes), `TmCheckbox` gains `InputAttributes` (on the native `<input>`; its
  `HelpText` block now also carries an id the input references via `aria-describedby`), and
  `TmFileDropZone` gains `InputAttributes` (on the internal file input) and `ShowFileList`
  (default `true`; `false` hides the zone's own picked-files list when the host renders the files
  itself). `TmTextArea` sets `aria-invalid="true"` while any message shows — its own `Error` or a
  field-level `TmFormField` error. The file drop area paints a visible focus ring when the
  (opacity-0) input takes keyboard focus (`:has(:focus-visible)` in `_file-drop-zone.css`).
- **Signing step fixes (Signing redesign phase 4 review).** The phone country pick survives a host
  without a bound `CountryCodeChanged` (local state + a parameter-change sync), the number parse
  is strict about group separators (see the Breaking / Migration entry), validation commits on
  blur instead of firing per keystroke, and the narrow-container date / OTP input no longer
  stretches ~190 px tall. New localized keys `TmSigningStep_MinLength` ("Use at least {0}
  characters.", the text step's commit-side minimum length) and `TmSigningStep_RemoveFile`
  ("Remove {0}", the attachment remove button's accessible name) in en / cs / sk / fr; the unused
  `TmSigningStep_CountryCodeAria` / `_PhoneInputAria` / `_OtpInputAria` keys were removed from the
  resources and the test mock together with their last callers.
- **Signing step inputs and states (Signing redesign phase 4), additive.** `TmSigningExternalStep`
  gains `Value` (the stored field value; `true` — bool or string — shows the localized
  "Verified" / "Paid" state instead of the call to action, the runner passes it), and
  `TmSigningSignatureStep` gains `ClearButtonPlacement` (default
  `TmSignatureClearButtonPlacement.Overlay`, hosts restore the row with `Actions`). The number
  step shows the localized allowed-range hint (`TmSigningStep_NumberRange`, culture-formatted), the
  text step the "n / max" counter (`TmSigningStep_CharCount`, live only at the limit), the
  attachment step the "Attached files ({0})" heading (`TmSigningStep_AttachedFiles`), the phone
  step visible labels (`TmSigningStep_PhoneCountryLabel`, `_PhoneNumberLabel`, `_OtpLabel`) and the
  external step the per-type default descriptions (`TmSigningStep_VerificationDescription`,
  `_KbaDescription`, `_PaymentDescription`) and the state strings (`_Verified`, `_Paid`) — all in
  en / cs / sk / fr.
- **Signing runner document chrome (Signing redesign phase 3, U4), all opt-in.** `TmSigningFormRunner`
  gains `DocumentTitle` (a header above the pages), `ShowDocumentToolbar` (default `false` — today's
  chrome-free look; `true` passes `ShowToolbar` / `ShowZoomControls` to
  every `TmDocumentPageViewer` and shares ONE zoom scale across all pages — zoom only, the per-page
  pagination controls come later) and the
  `DocumentHeaderActions` slot rendered next to the title. The header renders only when a title or
  slot content exists.
  ```razor
  <TmSigningFormRunner Pages="pages" Fields="fields"
                       DocumentTitle="Service order approval"
                       ShowDocumentToolbar="true">
      <DocumentHeaderActions><TmButton Variant="ButtonVariant.Ghost" Icon="info" /></DocumentHeaderActions>
  </TmSigningFormRunner>
  ```
  Runner panel additions (same phase): the permanent field list (SI4) with the localized status
  chips (the list markup lives in the internal `TmSigningRunnerFieldList` part — **not a supported
  public API; it may change without notice** — place `TmSigningFormRunner`, not the part), the
  success banner, the contextual action footer, the
  shared `SigningFieldTypeIcons` map
  and the `TmSigningFieldOverlay.Prompt` parameter (the localized empty-required call to action the
  runner passes). `TmSigningCompletionPanel` gains the `ChildContent` slot between description and
  actions, inherits `TmComponentBase` (`DataTestId` / `TestIdPrefix`) and takes `FocusTitleOnRender`
  (default `true`; pass `false` when several panels share one screen so they do not fight over the
  initial focus). Core, additive: `TmAlert` gains the `Role` parameter (default `alert`) so a host
  can render the alert as a polite `status` live region — the signing runner's all-done banner
  passes `Role="status"`. New localized keys
  `TmSigningFormRunner_PanelTitle`, `_PanelSubtitle`, `_DoneCount`, `_AllDoneTitle`,
  `_AllDoneDescription`, `_FieldListAria`, `_FieldStatusDone`, `_FieldStatusRequired`,
  `_FieldStatusOptional`, `_PageLabel`, `_SelectedField` and
  `TmSigningFieldOverlay_EmptyRequiredPrompt` in en / cs / sk / fr.
- **Signing step a11y plumbing (Signing redesign phase 2), additive.** `TmSigningSignatureStep`
  (shell + capture wrapper the runner uses for signature / initials steps — place it wherever a
  signing form needs a titled signature step; the embedded capture is deliberately driven with
  `Required=false` so a required signature step shows exactly ONE `role="alert"`, the shell's),
  `TmSigningStepShellContext` (the plain cascaded record with the title / description / validation
  ids a step's inputs reference) and `TmSigningStepShell.TitleId` / `DescriptionId` (per-instance
  ids — pass them from a host wrapper, the shell generates unique ones when omitted), and
  `TmSigningStepShell.FocusTitleAsync()` (the public best-effort focus move onto the step title;
  interop failures stay local). The existing `TmSigningStepShell.ValidationMessageId` is now
  generated per instance when omitted. New localized strings
  `TmSigningSignatureStep_Instruction`, `TmSigningStep_CountryCodeAria`,
  `TmSigningStep_PhoneInputAria` and `TmSigningStep_OtpInputAria` in en / cs / sk / fr.
- **Modeling "Open in editor" dialog: the desktop/tablet close is a TEXT `TmButton` rendered through the new `TmModal.HeaderActions` slot (Fáze 10) — the icon-only `.tm-modal-close` is DISABLED on the docked bands.** Before, the header close was the built-in icon-only `button.tm-modal-close` in every presentation. After, on the desktop/tablet band the header renders `button.tm-btn-ghost` with the localized "Close" text and an `x` icon inside `.tm-modal-header-actions` (`ShowCloseButton="false"`); the mobile fullscreen presentation keeps the icon-only close. The frozen `data-testid="modeling-open-diagram-close"` and the `data-modeling-focus="open-editor-close"` hook MOVE to whichever close is ACTIVE (the text button on the docked bands, `.tm-modal-close` on mobile). **E2E and host consumers must key off the test id, never off `.tm-modal-close`** — on the docked bands `.tm-modal-close` matches nothing now:
    ```razor
    <!-- before -->
    <button type="button" class="tm-modal-close" data-testid="modeling-open-diagram-close" aria-label="Close"><x-icon/></button>

    <!-- after (desktop/tablet) -->
    <div class="tm-modal-header-actions">
      <button type="button" class="tm-btn tm-btn-ghost" data-testid="modeling-open-diagram-close" data-modeling-focus="open-editor-close">
        <x-icon/> Close
      </button>
    </div>

    <!-- after (mobile fullscreen): the icon-only close, unchanged -->
    ```
  A host styling `.tm-modal-header-actions` may need a rule of its own (the slot is a token-only flex row with a `--tm-space-2` gap).

- **TmModelingEditor mobile presentation (Modeling redesign plan, phase 7, G2): the compact layout is a real tablist with a new order and an Issues tab.** On the editor's own mobile band (<768px of container) the old panel-tab strip (three `aria-pressed` toggle buttons ordered Tree | Preview | Inspector, with the issues docked under the Inspector tab) is replaced. A host or test that keyed the compact DOM must migrate:
  - *The panel strip is a tablist and the order changed.* The strip is now a core `TmTabs` — `div.tm-tabs[data-testid=modeling-panel-tabs] > .tm-tabs__header[role=tablist]` of `button[role=tab]` with `aria-selected`, `aria-controls`/`id` and the APG arrow keys. The tab order is **Preview | Tree | Inspector | Issues** (the preview is FIRST on mobile) and the tabs are ordered last, not first:
    ```razor
    <!-- before -->
    <nav data-testid="modeling-panel-tabs">
        <button aria-pressed="…" data-testid="modeling-panel-tab-tree">Tree</button>
        <button aria-pressed="…" data-testid="modeling-panel-tab-preview">Preview</button>
        <button aria-pressed="…" data-testid="modeling-panel-tab-inspector">Inspector</button>
    </nav>
    <!-- after -->
    <div class="tm-tabs" data-testid="modeling-panel-tabs">
        <div class="tm-tabs__header" role="tablist">
            <button role="tab" aria-selected="true" data-testid="modeling-panel-tab-preview">Preview</button>
            <button role="tab" aria-selected="false" data-testid="modeling-panel-tab-tree">Tree</button>
            <button role="tab" aria-selected="false" data-testid="modeling-panel-tab-inspector">Inspector</button>
            <button role="tab" aria-selected="false" data-testid="modeling-panel-tab-issues">Issues</button>
        </div>
    </div>
    ```
    The `data-testid`s of the tab buttons survive (`modeling-panel-tab-preview|tree|inspector` plus the new `modeling-panel-tab-issues`); `aria-pressed` on them is gone in favor of `aria-selected`. `data-active-panel` on the editor root gains a fourth value `"issues"`.
  - *The Issues tab is new and shows the whole panel.* The issues moved out of the Inspector tab: on mobile the Inspector tab stacks Source + Properties + Relations (the Relations SECTION is the LAST child, after the Properties inspector) and `data-testid="modeling-issues-panel"` is the new Issues tab body (a `TmModelingIssuePanel`, expanded). The desktop status strip (`modeling-status-strip`) does not render on mobile — the counts live in a status card (`modeling-status-card`, four tiles plus the loaded time).
  - *The compact header drops the selects.* The provider/notation/viewpoint fields moved into a "Change view" bottom sheet (a `TmModal` sheet with `data-testid="modeling-change-view-sheet"`), opened from the in-flow `TmMobileActionBar` (Reload | Change view | Issues + More with Generate diagram and Open in editor) or the header "⋯" (`tm-modeling-editor__more`). A selector that queried `select` inside the mobile header matches nothing now; query the sheet. The preview header carries no edit actions on mobile (`modeling-generate-diagram-button` / `modeling-open-in-editor-button` live in the bar's More menu as `modeling-action-generate` / `modeling-action-open-editor`), and the tree rows are not draggable (no `.tm-modeling-model-tree__drag-handle`, no `draggable`, no insert action) — G2 keeps dragging a tablet+ affordance.
  - *The mobile open-editor dialog is fullscreen.* On the editor's mobile band the dialog adds `tm-modal--fullscreen-presentation` (TmModal's own presentation) instead of the container-query-sized near-fullscreen box; the stylesheet no longer carries the `@container tm-modeling-editor (width < 768px)` dialog block. A host that styled `.tm-modeling-editor__open-editor-modal .tm-modal` for the small band must scope the override to `:not(.tm-modal--fullscreen-presentation)`.
  - New resource keys in all four tables + `MockTmLocalizer`: `TmModelingEditor_ChangeView`, `TmModelingEditor_Reload`, `TmModelingEditor_MoreOptions`.
- **Modeling: `parentId` moved out of element `Properties` (Fáze 12).** A host whose provider already carried the tree parent as a `parentId` entry in `ModelingElementDto.Properties` should move it to the new first-class `ModelingElementDto.ParentId` property — the hierarchy view (and the MCP `parentId` contract) reads ONLY the property; a stale `Properties["parentId"]` entry is ignored (and still round-trips as an opaque custom property, so nothing is lost). Hosts that never sent `parentId` in `Properties` are unaffected: the DTO change is additive and a model without `ParentId` renders the same flat tree as before.
  ```json
  // before: the parent rode inside the opaque property bag
  { "id": "e2", "name": "Subprocess", "properties": { "parentId": "e1" } }
  // after: the first-class DTO member drives the hierarchy (and the MCP contract)
  { "id": "e2", "name": "Subprocess", "parentId": "e1", "properties": {} }
  ```
- **Modeling: the inspector tablist has THREE tabs (Fáze 13).** The docked inspector's `role="tablist"` now renders **Properties | Relations | Source** (the new Relations tab owns the `modeling-tab-relations` test id and sits between the two existing ones), and the relations tab body is the new `TmModelingRelatedElementsPanel` (`data-testid` `modeling-related-panel`). E2E consumers and hosts must key off the tab test ids (`modeling-tab-properties`, `modeling-tab-relations`, `modeling-tab-source`) — never off the tab INDEX (index 1 was Source, now Relations). The mobile band has no extra tab level: the Relations SECTION renders inside the Inspector tab body (`modeling-related-panel` under the properties), so a selector that expected the Source panel directly under the mobile inspector must keep accounting for the panel above it.
  ```csharp
  // before (2.9.x): index 1 of the docked tablist was "Source"
  var tabs = cut.FindAll(".tm-modeling-editor [role=tab]");
  tabs[1].Click(); // Source

  // after: key off the tab test ids — the index shifted (Properties | Relations | Source)
  cut.Find("[data-testid='modeling-tab-source']").Click();
  ```
  ```css
  /* before: positional tab selectors (E2E/host code) */
  [role="tab"]:nth-child(2) /* was Source */
  /* after: the frozen tab test ids */
  [data-testid="modeling-tab-relations"]
  ```

### Added

- **`TmChip` gains a pressed toggle variant (phase 15b).** `Pressed` (`bool?`, default `null`) is additive: unset, the chip renders today's `<span>`; set, it renders a native `<button type="button" aria-pressed>` with the same classes plus `tm-chip--pressed`, raises `PressedChanged` with the flipped value (enable `@bind-Pressed`) and renders `disabled` from `Disabled`. With `Removable` the remove button stays a SIBLING of the toggle inside a bare `.tm-chip__shell` wrapper — a button never nests inside a button. Keyboard follows [docs/keyboard-activation-convention.md](docs/keyboard-activation-convention.md): the browser activates the native button — no Enter/Space emulation, exactly one activation per press; the focus ring is the shared `--tm-focus-ring`, the coarse-pointer floor the shared `--tm-touch-target`, and forced-colors keeps a system outline. New `ChildContent` renders trailing content (a count badge) that joins the chip's accessible name. The wireframe `TmChip` stencil gained the matching `pressed` prop.
  ```razor
  <TmChip Label="Error" Pressed="@showErrors" PressedChanged="@v => showErrors = v">
      <span class="chip-count">@errorCount</span>
  </TmChip>
  ```

- **Modeling: notation palette in the "Open in editor" dialog and a preview legend (Fáze 15 of the Modeling redesign plan).** The dialog's toolbox now pins the ACTIVE notation's stencils as the FIRST library (labelled with the notation profile's display name, order preserved) while the rest of the stencil library starts collapsed — and stays searchable across the whole library. The preview carries a collapsible legend card explaining only the notation shapes the generated document actually uses. Both run on one shared catalog and additive DiagramEditor API.
  - **DiagramEditor (all additive — defaults are today's behavior)**: `TmDiagramEditor.PreferredStencilIds` (`IReadOnlyList<string>?`, default `null` = today's toolbox) and `PreferredStencilsLabel` (`string?`) pass through to `TmDiagramToolbox`, which renders the pinned library FIRST (`data-library-id="notation-palette"`, `data-pinned="true"`), collapses every other palette while the set is active (a live search still expands matches everywhere) and treats the pinned library as the "first category" for `CollapseCategoriesExceptFirst` on the mobile Shapes sheet. Unknown preferred ids are ignored. New public `TmDiagramStencilIcon` (`StencilId`, `Size`, `Class`) — the toolbox tile preview pipeline (including the text-trimming) for hosts presenting stencils outside the toolbox; always `aria-hidden`, unknown ids render the generic fallback shape.
  - **Modeling**: new `ModelingNotationCatalog` (singleton) maps the active notation profile's semantic types to diagram stencils through the SAME `IModelingStencilMapper` the generator uses (memoized per notation, labels through the `TmModelingSemanticType_{type}` keys) and filters legend entries to the types the document uses. The dialog passes `PreferredStencilIds`/`PreferredStencilsLabel = profile.DisplayName`. Inserting from the palette creates ONLY a diagram node (with the node's own `semanticType`/`notation` data) — never a semantic model element (element creation through the Fáze 14 writer is backlog).
  - **`TmModelingDiagramLegend`** (new component, `data-testid="modeling-preview-legend"`): a collapsible card — `role="list"` entries (named by `aria-labelledby` of their plain-`<p>` group titles) with `aria-hidden` icons next to visible text and an `aria-expanded`/`aria-controls` toggle — grouped into Elements and Relationships, positioned as an overlay in the canvas's top-right corner (the embedded editor keeps its height; the zoom group, the Fáze 9 mobile zoom pill and the empty-diagram hint stay visible). Relationship entries follow the MODEL (the relationship types whose Id is among the document's edge Ids), collapsing stencil-sharing types into one row with joined labels.
  - **`TmModelingDiagramPreview`** gains `ShowLegend` (default `false`), `LegendEntries` (`IReadOnlyList<ModelingNotationCatalogEntry>?`) and `LegendDefaultExpanded` (desktop expanded — collapsed above 12 nodes — tablet collapsed through the hosting editor).
  - **Mobile**: the compact header "⋯" gains a **Legend** entry opening a `modeling-legend-sheet` bottom sheet hosting the same legend with `Collapsible="false"` (the card would cover the small preview canvas).
  - New keys in en / cs / sk / fr + `MockTmLocalizer`: `TmModelingDiagramLegend_Title`, `_Show`, `_Hide`, `_Elements`, `_Relationships`, `_Empty`, `TmModelingEditor_Legend`, `TmDiagramToolbox_PreferredDefault`.
  ```razor
  @* The editor wires both surfaces by default; a host that wants the pre-Fáze-15 look sets: *@
  <TmModelingEditor ProviderKey="erp.modeling" ShowPreviewLegend="false" />

  @* DiagramEditor-only hosts opt in to a pinned stencil library themselves *@
  <TmDiagramEditor Document="@doc" PreferredStencilIds="@myPinned" PreferredStencilsLabel="BPMN 2.0" />
  ```

- **Modeling: an editable inspector behind a write contract (Fáze 14 of the Modeling redesign plan, decision `MODELING-INSPECTOR-EDITING`).** The modeling inspector can now edit the selected element or relationship — the name, the description and the SCALAR properties (string, number, boolean; complex object/array values stay read-only, as do semantic type, notation, source metadata and governance) — with an editor-owned undo/redo stack and an explicit save contract. Everything is OPT-IN; with no opt-in the behavior is byte-identical to the read-only MO2 inspector.
  - **New Abstractions contract** (namespace `Tempo.Blazor.Modeling`): `IModelingModelWriter` (`ProviderKey` + `SaveChangesAsync(ModelingModelChangeSet, CancellationToken)` returning `ModelingModelSaveResult`) with `ModelingModelChangeSet` (`ModelId`, `ProviderKey`, `BaseVersion` = `Metadata.SourceVersion`, `Elements`, `Relationships`), `ModelingElementChange` / `ModelingRelationshipChange` (a `null` member means "unchanged") and `ModelingModelSaveResult` (`Succeeded`, `IsConflict`, `Message`, `Model?`, `Issues`). `IModelingModelProvider` is UNCHANGED — reads stay read-only.
  - **`TmModelingEditor`** gains `AllowModelEditing` (default `false`), `SaveMode` (`ModelingSaveMode.Manual` | `Immediate`, default `Manual`), `OnModelChanged` (`EventCallback<ModelingModelChangedEventArgs>` — the commit's change set + the current model, after every commit), `OnSaveCompleted` and the public `Task<ModelingModelSaveResult?> SaveModelChangesAsync()` + `bool HasPendingModelChanges`. Editing is active only when a writer is registered for the effective provider key OR `OnModelChanged` has a delegate. A reload or a provider switch with pending edits asks for confirmation (discard first); a conflict result (`IsConflict`) shows a `TmAlert` with a localized "Reload" action.
  - **`TmModelingInspector`** gains `ReadOnly` (default `true`), `OnElementEdited` / `OnRelationshipEdited`, `OnUndoRequested` / `OnRedoRequested` and a `HeaderActions` slot. Fields commit on blur/Enter (the toggle on click), an empty name shows a localized validation message and does not commit, and Escape reverts the field. The inspector header hosts the editor's undo/redo pair (`Ctrl+Z` / `Ctrl+Shift+Z`|`Ctrl+Y` with `aria-keyshortcuts` and a polite live-region announcement) — the shortcuts work only while the focus is inside the inspector, so the diagram canvas keyboard scope is never involved.
  - **Undo/redo is editor-owned**: each field commit is ONE `DiagramCommandTransaction` ("Edit element" / "Edit relationship") wrapping the new `UpdateModelingElementCommand` / `UpdateModelingRelationshipCommand`, which mutate the model DTO and synchronize the diagram document (node `Data["name"]/["label"]` by `modelElementId`, edge `Label` by relationship id) — so the model tree, the preview canvas and the open-editor dialog update in the same step.
  - **Mobile (G2 light edits)**: the Inspector tab edits exactly like the docked bands (44px targets) and while edits are pending the F5 `TmMobileActionBar` leads with sticky Save/Discard entries.
  - The demo ships an in-memory `DemoModelingModelWriter` (registered by `AddTempoBlazorModeling` for the demo provider key) and the `/modeling-editor` page exposes an "Allow editing" switch, a Manual/Immediate selector, a live last-change-set dump and a `?scenario=save-conflict` route.
  - New keys in en / cs / sk / fr + `MockTmLocalizer`: `TmModelingInspector_NameRequired`, `_EditHint`, `TmModelingEditor_EditElement`, `_EditRelationship`, `_Undo`, `_Redo`, `_UndoAction`, `_RedoAction`, `_Save`, `_Saving`, `_Saved`, `_SaveConflict`, `_SaveFailed`, `_ReloadChanges`, `_Discard`, `_DiscardChangesTitle`, `_DiscardChangesText`, `_PendingChanges`, `_Cancel`.
  ```razor
  @* How to enable editing: register a writer for your provider key (reads stay on the provider) *@
  <TmModelingEditor ProviderKey="erp.modeling"
                    AllowModelEditing="true"
                    SaveMode="ModelingSaveMode.Manual"
                    OnModelChanged="HandleModelChanged"
                    OnSaveCompleted="HandleSaveCompleted" />

  public sealed class ErpModelingWriter : IModelingModelWriter
  {
      public string ProviderKey => "erp.modeling";

      public Task<ModelingModelSaveResult> SaveChangesAsync(
          ModelingModelChangeSet changes, CancellationToken cancellationToken)
      {
          // changes.BaseVersion is the Metadata.SourceVersion the editor loaded the model with —
          // compare it with the current source version and return IsConflict on a mismatch.
          ...
      }
  }
  ```

- **`TmModelingRelatedElementsPanel` — the inspector's "Relations" tab (Fáze 13 of the Modeling redesign plan).** The modeling inspector's docked tablist is now **Properties | Relations | Source** on the desktop and tablet bands (the tablet inspector side sheet carries the same three tabs), and the mobile Inspector tab shows the Relations SECTION under the properties — no extra tab level there. The new read-only panel lists the selected element's OUTGOING and INCOMING relationships grouped with counts (`TmModelingRelated_Outgoing` / `_Incoming`, sr-only counts through the `TmModelingRelated_RelationshipCount_*` plural family) and, for a selected relationship, its source and target as navigable rows. Every element-view row carries TWO native buttons — the counterpart (semantic-type icon + display name, `modeling-related-{direction}-counterpart-{relationshipId}`, `aria-label` `TmModelingRelated_SelectElement` "{0}") and the relationship type (Link2 icon + type, `modeling-related-{direction}-relationship-{relationshipId}`, `TmModelingRelated_SelectRelationshipTo` "{0} to {1}" / `_SelectRelationshipFrom` "{0} from {1}") — never nested; a relationship-view row is one native button. A dangling counterpart renders the localized `TmModelingEditor_Unknown` fallback NON-interactively (never a dead button), a self-reference renders safely in both directions, and the empty state is localized (`TmModelingRelated_Empty`). The by-element relationship index is memoized per `Relationships` reference (a selection change or an unrelated re-render never re-scans the list, M26), rows grow to 44px targets on a coarse pointer and rows carry `data-testid` `modeling-related-{outgoing|incoming|source|target}-{relationshipId}`.
  - `TmModelingEditor` hosts the tab (`modeling-tab-relations`) between the existing two and shows the related-row count as the tab badge for the current selection (an element counts its outgoing + incoming relationships, a relationship 2). Activating a row routes through the SAME selection paths an issue or an edge pick uses (`SelectElementAsync` / `SelectRelationshipAsync` flow, including the tablet rule "a selection opens the inspector sheet") and returns the docked inspector to the Properties tab presenting the navigated item; on mobile the section updates in place inside the Inspector tab.
  - New keys in en / cs / sk / fr + `MockTmLocalizer`: `TmModelingEditor_Relations`, `TmModelingRelated_Outgoing`, `_Incoming`, `_Source`, `_Target`, `_Empty`, `_SelectElement` ({0}), `_SelectRelationshipTo` ({0}, {1}) / `_SelectRelationshipFrom` ({0}, {1}) and the `TmModelingRelated_RelationshipCount_*` plural family.
  ```razor
  <TmModelingRelatedElementsPanel Element="@_selectedElement"
                                  Relationship="@_selectedRelationship"
                                  Elements="@model.Elements"
                                  Relationships="@model.Relationships"
                                  OnElementSelected="SelectElementAsync"
                                  OnRelationshipSelected="SelectRelationshipAsync" />
  ```
- **Model tree hierarchy by `ParentId` (Fáze 12 of the Modeling redesign plan, all opt-in and additive — a model without `ParentId` looks and behaves exactly as before).**
  - `ModelingElementDto.ParentId` (`string`, default `string.Empty`, `null` normalizes to `""`, JSON `parentId`) — additive and serialization-compatible: payloads without the field deserialize unchanged. The diagram generator NEVER maps it onto `ModelingViewNodeDto.ParentNodeId` (diagram nesting stays owned by the view). The built-in BPMN relationship rules resolve Pool/SubProcess containment from `Properties["poolId"|"pool"|"subProcessId"]` with a fallback to `ParentId` (the tree edge), so the cross-pool SequenceFlow / MessageFlow validation also holds for models that report the hierarchy only through `ParentId`.
  - `ModelingTreeGrouping` (`SemanticType` | `Hierarchy` | `Auto`) and `TmModelingModelTree.Grouping` + `TmModelingEditor.TreeGrouping` pass-through. `Auto` (the default) renders the nested APG hierarchy when at least one element resolves to a valid parent and keeps the flat SemanticType groups otherwise. The hierarchy renders every element as a `role="treeitem"` at its own `aria-level` with `aria-setsize`/`aria-posinset` among the visible siblings; parents are disclosures (chevron + direct child count via the localized plural `TmModelingModelTree_ChildCount_*`, `aria-expanded`); keyboard navigation walks ONE flat visible list (Right expands / descends, Left collapses / moves to the parent) over the unchanged `modeling-editor.js` API, and indentation rides `--tm-modeling-tree-level` through `--tm-space-*` (no hard-coded pixels).
  - `CollapsedElementIds` / `CollapsedElementIdsChanged` (two-way, `IReadOnlyCollection<string>?`) — the hierarchy's collapsed nodes as a SEPARATE key space from `CollapsedGroups` (group keys stay the flat mode's semantic types; no migration). A host re-seed and every user toggle follow the same contract as `CollapsedGroups`; an external selection reveals the whole collapsed ancestor chain before scrolling into view; the filter keeps every ancestor of a match visible and expanded; `data-visible-count`/`data-rendered-count` semantics are preserved.
  - Cycle safety and depth limits are built in: a missing parent renders the element at the root, a parent cycle (and anything hanging off one) is broken deterministically to the root without recursion, and the M26 budget holds — a 200-element, 6-level hierarchy re-filters in well under 200 ms.
  - Demo: `DemoModelingModelProvider` gained a `?scenario=hierarchy` model (BPMN subprocess → activities) and `?scenario=hierarchy-large` (200 elements in 6-level chains for the filter budget); `DemoUmlModelingModelProvider` nests the classes under a UML package.
  - MCP: `modeling_apply_operations` accepts `parentId` on `add_element`/`update_element` (empty string clears the parent); a parent that does not exist or would close a cycle fails the whole batch, `delete_element` is refused while the element still has children (no cascade — delete or reparent them in the same batch), `modeling_get_model_tree` returns `parentId`, and validation reports missing parents and cycles under the new `hierarchy` issue category.
  - Localization: `TmModelingModelTree_ExpandNode` / `_CollapseNode` ({0} = the node name) and the `TmModelingModelTree_ChildCount_*` plural family in en / cs / sk / fr + `MockTmLocalizer`.
  ```razor
  <TmModelingEditor @ref="_editor" TreeGrouping="ModelingTreeGrouping.Auto"
                    @bind-CollapsedElementIds="_collapsed" … />
  ```
- **`TmModelingIssuePanel` filter bar and sorting (Fáze 11 of the Modeling redesign plan, all opt-in and additive — the default presentation and row order are unchanged).** The new `ShowFilterBar` (`bool`, default `false`) renders a bar above the list: severity chips with per-severity counts (native `aria-pressed` toggle buttons — one activation per press, 44px targets on a coarse pointer), a `TmSearchInput` over the message/category/source (case- and accent-insensitive, the model tree's search contract) and a `TmSelect` sort control with a visible label driven by the new `ModelingIssueSortMode` enum (`Input` = the input order, the default and the pre-Fáze 11 behavior; `Severity` = Error > Warning > Info, stable within a group; `Source` = by the resolved source element/relationship display name with sourceless issues last). The severity set, text and sort mode are all two-way (`SeverityFilter`/`FilterText`/`SortMode` + `*Changed`; the parameters seed the internal state and are never assigned inside the component — the hosting editor owns the state so a filter survives a dock collapse, a tablet sheet toggle and a mobile tab switch), and `Elements`/`Relationships` (optional) supply the source NAMES for the search and the Source sort. When a filter hides rows the root reports `data-visible-issue-count` next to `data-total-issue-count` (`data-issue-count` keeps the total), the header badge switches to the neutral visible-of-total formulation (localized `TmModelingIssuePanel_CountFiltered` "Issues: {0} of {1}") and an all-hidden result renders a localized no-match state with a one-press "Clear filters" action. The rendered rows are a memoized projection (key = the `Issues` reference + filter + sort + culture, M26: 500 issues recompute in a single pass and an unrelated parent re-render renders nothing); the host's `Issues` collection is never mutated and row `data-testid`s keep the ORIGINAL input index, so filter/sort state never renumbers rows. `TmModelingEditor` passes `ShowFilterBar="true"` on every band (desktop dock, tablet sheet, mobile Issues tab) and owns the state in a new `TmModelingEditor.IssueFilter.cs` partial; the mobile tab badge still shows the TOTAL count. The filter bar lives INSIDE the collapsible body, so a collapsed dock hides it with the list.
  ```razor
  <TmModelingIssuePanel Issues="@issues" ShowFilterBar="true"
                        @bind-SeverityFilter="_severities" @bind-FilterText="_text"
                        @bind-SortMode="_sortMode" Elements="@model.Elements" />
  ```

- **`TmDiagramEditor` embedded-viewer API (Fáze 9 of the Modeling redesign plan, all opt-in and additive — the knobs a nested host uses instead of CSS on the editor's internal DOM).**
  - `ShowPageTabs` (`bool`, default `true` = today) — `false` drops the `.tm-diagram-editor__page-tabs` row in EVERY layout (a single-page preview has nothing to switch); page switching stays available by setting the document's own `ActivePageIndex` (the host owns the `Document` reference), never through CSS. With neither the page tabs nor a header bar rendering (an embedded chrome-less viewer), the editor passes `Header=null` to the shell — no empty `.tm-editor-shell__header` wrapper div stays behind.
  - `FitToViewAsync(DiagramFitMode mode = DiagramFitMode.Page)` — the public zoom-to-fit (final UX review M5) gains the optional additive `mode`: the new `DiagramFitMode` enum (`Page` = today's both-axes fit, `Width` = scale by the container width only, a tall diagram stays scrollable; `diagram-editor.js` `fitToView(container, padding, mode)` keeps its two-argument contract by default). `TmDiagramCanvas.FitToView(mode)` mirrors it and is the ONE fit path — the editor's own fit button goes through it too, so the page-view margin is always applied and the zoom label reports the FINAL scale (after the margin; `addPageViewMargin` raises `OnZoomChanged` with it). The width mode TOP-aligns content shorter than the visible band instead of centering it.
  - `FitOnDocumentLoad` (`DiagramFitMode?`, default `null` = today's no-auto-fit) — fits ONCE after the first render of a NEW document identity (the same document never re-fits, a replaced document does, user zoom afterwards wins). The fit stays owed across a canvas remount (a mobile↔docked layout flip remounts `TmDiagramCanvas`): the editor re-arms it on the finally mounted canvas, which fits exactly once.
  - `ShowMobileZoomOverlay` (`bool?`, default `null` = today's rule `IsMobileLayout && ShowToolbar && Zoom`) — `true` shows the floating − | % | + | fit pill on a mobile layout even chrome-less (`ShowToolbar=false`), `false` never shows it. The docked bands keep the status-bar zoom.
  - `MinimapInitiallyCollapsed` (`bool`, default `false` = today's expanded start) — seeds the minimap card (desktop) / floating overlay (tablet) collapsed ONCE at initialization; the user's own toggle wins afterwards and the mobile X1 rule (minimap hidden, "⋯" toggle) is unchanged. The Modeling "Open in editor" dialog seeds it from the editor's resolved tablet mode.
- **`TmModal.HeaderActions` — a public slot for host actions in the header row (Fáze 10, additive; `null` default = today's DOM).** The fragment renders inside `.tm-modal-header-actions`, between `.tm-modal-header-content` and the built-in close button, INSIDE the focus scope (the Tab cycle covers it). The typical use is a host-styled close affordance — a text `TmButton` "Close" paired with `ShowCloseButton="false"` — or additional header actions. The Modeling "Open in editor" dialog uses it on the desktop/tablet band (see Breaking / Migration). New token-only rule `.tm-modal-header-actions` (flex, `--tm-space-2` gap — no new animated subject).
- **`TmGantt` desktop structure (redesign phase 4), all opt-in and additive.**
  - `ToolbarLabels` (`Icons` default | `IconsWithText` | `Auto`) maps straight onto the core `TmToolbar.Labels`; the items carry `Priority` (`Primary | Secondary`) so a later tablet / mobile phase can switch the bar to `Overflow=Menu`. The filter button shows the number of active filters as a badge (`aria-label` "Filter (2 active)"); `ShowQuickSearch` (default `false`) adds a debounced "Search tasks…" box that keeps one `Title` / `Contains` entry in `Filters` (other filters stay; emptying the box removes it) and raises `OnFiltersChanged`.
    ```razor
    <TmGantt Items="tasks" ToolbarLabels="ToolbarLabels.IconsWithText" ShowQuickSearch="true" Filters="filters" OnFiltersChanged="f => filters = f" />
    ```
  - `SidebarMode` (`Rail` default | `Tabs`), `GanttSidebarMode` is a new enum in `Tempo.Blazor.Abstractions.Models`. Host header slots `HeaderStart`, `HeaderActions`, `Title`, `Subtitle` and `ShowHeader` (default `true`; there is no header unless a slot or text is set, so today's look is unchanged). No app shell (project switcher, avatar) is built in - the host fills the slots.
    ```razor
    <TmGantt Items="tasks" SidebarMode="GanttSidebarMode.Tabs" Title="Project Aurora" Subtitle="Q2 plan">
        <HeaderActions><button @onclick="Share">Share</button></HeaderActions>
    </TmGantt>

The other `GanttColumnKey` values (`Deadline`, `Assignees`, `Estimation`, …) are still accepted and ignored.
  - Wireframe: the `TmGantt` stencil gained `toolbarLabels` (labelled buttons) and `sidebarMode` (`rail` | `tabs`) props.
  - Keys and strings: `TmGantt_Toolbar`, `TmGantt_Group*`, `TmGantt_AddTaskMore`, `TmGantt_FilterActive`, `TmGantt_SearchTasks`, `TmGantt_PanelTabs`, `TmGantt_TaskList`, `TmGantt_BulkSelectColumn`, `TmGantt_Duration`, `TmGantt_Priority`, `TmGantt_DurationDays_*`, `TmGantt_BarLabel`, `TmGantt_MilestoneLabel` in en / cs / sk / fr.

Its horizontal scroll and the timeline's are linked in the browser (`tmGantt.linkScroll` in `gantt.js`, no Blazor round trip per scroll tick). `ShowWorkloadPanel` is unchanged: it only switches on the overload computation behind the warning icons (documented now), it never draws anything.

- **`TmGantt` dialogs, filter and mapping (redesign phase 6), all opt-in and additive.**
  - `FilterPanelMode` (`GanttFilterPanelMode`: `Inline` default | `Dialog` | `Auto`) presents the filter editor as a `TmModal` (a bottom sheet on a mobile viewport) with the Clear all | Cancel | Apply footer; `Auto` behaves as `Inline` until the container layout lands (a later phase) and is subject to change - pick `Inline` or `Dialog` explicitly if you depend on the presentation. `TmGanttFilterPanel.AsDialog` is the component-level switch behind it; in the dialog presentation `TmGantt` keeps the panel mounted and drives the new `TmGanttFilterPanel.Show` parameter (so the modal restores the focus to the Filter button on close), and the `gantt-filter-panel` test id sits on the inner `div.tm-gantt__filter-panel-inner--dialog`, not on the `TmModal` overlay root.
    ```razor
    <TmGantt Items="tasks" FilterPanelMode="GanttFilterPanelMode.Dialog" />
    ```
  - `TmGanttExportDialog.PreviewContent` (`RenderFragment?`) replaces the "Preview" placeholder with the host's own preview (the live preview of the chart itself is not built-in).
    ```razor
    <TmGanttExportDialog IsOpen="open" OnExport="Export" OnClose="Close"><PreviewContent><img src="@previewUrl" alt="" /></PreviewContent></TmGanttExportDialog>
    ```
  - `TmGanttImportMappingDialog.InitialMappings` (`IReadOnlyList<GanttColumnMapping>?`) seeds the mapping (a remembered choice, a host default); the remaining columns are auto-mapped by header name (case- and diacritics-insensitive; English, Czech, French and the active locale's labels).
  - The export dialog now fills the `GanttExportOptions` fields that always existed: `IncludeCriticalPath`, `IncludeToday`, `IncludeWorkload`, `ZoomLevel` (PDF / PNG) and `Columns` (Excel; `null` while the set is the exporter's default). The mapping targets gained `Duration`, `Deadline`, `Assignees`, `Predecessor` and `WBS`; the filter fields gained `Start`, `End` and `Deadline` (`GanttHelper.ApplyFilters` compares the calendar day, culture-invariant `yyyy-MM-dd`; an unparseable value filters nothing).
  - Strings: `TmGantt_ExportFormat`, `TmGantt_ExportIncludeCriticalPath|Today|Workload`, `TmGantt_ExportColumns`, `TmGantt_ExportZoomCurrent`, `TmGantt_ImportSource`, `TmGantt_ImportNoFile`, `TmGantt_ImportRemoveFile`, `TmGantt_ImportSupportedFormats`, `TmGantt_ImportMappingHint|Duplicate|Required|EndOrDuration` and `TmGantt_ActiveFilters` in en, cs, sk and fr.
- **`TmGantt` import mapping and export preview (redesign phase 10), all additive.**
  - `GanttExcelImporter.ImportResult(Stream, IEnumerable<GanttColumnMapping>?, GanttExcelImportOptions?)` returns the full `GanttImportResult` (`Tasks`, `Dependencies`, `Warnings`) and `GanttExcelImporter.ReadHeaders(Stream)` reads a sheet's header row (empty headers are skipped); the existing `Import(...)` stays and returns only the tasks. Every target the mapping dialog offers is imported: a mapped `WBS` column builds `ParentId` hierarchies (parent = the code without its last segment), a mapped `Predecessors` column builds `GanttDependency`s (row numbers per the MS Project convention, 1 = first data row, or WBS codes; `FS|SS|FF|SF` suffix and `±N[d]` lag, case-insensitive — the same (from, to, type) trio imports once, and a token whose lag cannot be parsed, e.g. `3FS+2w` or `3+2 days`, is an unparsed value, not an unknown predecessor), a mapped `Assignees` column builds people (split on comma/semicolon, trimmed, deduplicated; `GanttExcelImportOptions.AssigneeResolver` resolves names into real users), `Duration` reads invariant days and fills `End = Start + Duration` when `End` is unmapped or unparsable, and `Deadline`, `Estimation` and `TimeLog` fill `DueDate`, `EstimationHours` and `LoggedHours`. The default header vocabulary gained `wbs`, `predecessors`, `assignees`, `resource names`, `duration`, `deadline`, `estimation` and `time log` aliases, and a sparse row (a skipped cell in the middle) no longer slides the following columns left. Parsing is culture-invariant: dates accept ISO / `dd.MM.yyyy` / `MM/dd/yyyy` strings and fall back to Excel serial numbers (OADate) for raw numeric cells, and Progress accepts `NN`, `NN%` and the stored 0–1 fraction scale (`0.5` = 50 %). Import never throws for the sheet's content: unknown predecessors, self references, cycles (DFS-detected — the closing edge is skipped), unknown WBS parents, duplicate WBS codes, duplicate headers (a header used by several columns maps its FIRST column only) and unparsable non-empty cells come back as `GanttImportWarning`s carrying `Row` (the data ordinal predecessor references use), `SheetRow` (the 1-based sheet row for display), `Column`, `Code` (`GanttImportWarningCode`) and the raw `Value` — never a ready-made message; the UI localizes them. Task ids are stable per row within one import (`{IdPrefix}{n}`): `GanttExcelImportOptions.IdPrefix` defaults to `xlsx-row-`, and the dialog mints a fresh prefix per import run (`xlsx-{8 hex}-row-`), so importing the same sheet twice never mints colliding ids.
  - The import dialog's Excel flow is wired to it: the dialog reads the headers, confirms the mapping in `TmGanttImportMappingDialog` (seeded by the new `ImportMappings` parameter) and imports the full result. The new `OnImportResultCompleted` (`EventCallback<GanttImportResult>`) fires on the dialog and on `TmGantt` in the documented order — `OnImportCompleted` carries the tasks first, then every new dependency is announced through `OnDependencyAdded`, then the full payload arrives. Warnings render as a `TmAlert` ("Row 2: unknown predecessor '9'" — the sheet row, the header row is 1) and KEEP the dialog open until the user closes it: the list expands under a "Show details" summary, the chosen file is dropped and the footer collapses to a single primary **Close**, so a completed import can never be re-run from the same dialog. A GanttXlsx package without the result API (no `ImportResult`/`ReadHeaders`) keeps today's direct import without the mapping step.
  - The export dialog's preview area gained a built-in live preview: `PreviewTasks` (`IReadOnlyList<TmWorkItem>?`; without it the neutral placeholder stays), `PreviewDependencies`, `PreviewCriticalPathIds` and `ShowBuiltInPreview` (default `true`). With tasks supplied it renders the internal `TmGanttExportPreview` — pure SVG/HTML, no JavaScript: PDF/PNG draw the miniature page in the paper's aspect ratio (A4/A3/Letter, orientation) with bars (`GanttHelper.CalculateBarPosition`, capped at 40 nodes), optional critical path, today line and workload strip; Excel shows the first 20 rows of the selected columns formatted by the shared `GanttColumnValues.Format` (the same invariant formatting `GanttXlsxExporter` now uses, so a cell and its preview never drift); XML shows the task / dependency / milestone counts. The model is memoized per option key, the sketch is one image for assistive tech — the root is `role="img"` with a localized summary label over an `aria-hidden` body, and the fullscreen mobile `<details>` branch keeps that contract by wrapping the body in a `role="img"` element under its "Show preview" summary. The host's `PreviewContent` slot keeps winning. `TmGantt` passes its visible (filtered) tasks and the dependencies between them.
  - Demo: `/gantt-portfolio` imports the shared `sample-data/gantt-import-sample.xlsx` (WBS, predecessors, assignees, one unknown predecessor) through the mapping dialog for real — no more "mapping confirmed: N columns" toast without an import.
  - Strings: `TmGantt_ImportWarning*`, `TmGantt_ImportWarningsTitle_*` (plural family), `TmGantt_ImportWarningsShowDetails`, `TmGantt_ExportPreviewAria`, `TmGantt_ExportPreviewMoreRows_*`, `TmGantt_ExportPreviewShow`, `TmGantt_ExportPreviewTasks_*`, `TmGantt_ExportPreviewCriticalPath|Today|Workload` and `TmGantt_Portrait` in en, cs, sk and fr.
- **`TmGantt` summary band and shared portfolio axis (redesign phase 11), all opt-in and additive — the default DOM is unchanged.**
  - `ShowSummaryBand` (default `false`) shows the rollup strip under the tree + timeline (above a docked workload): five cards on a desktop container — **Status of tasks** (a `TmChart` Donut with the total in its hole, `role="img"` with a localized text summary, and a legend whose entries carry the numbers so status is never colour alone), **Time spent** ("128 h of 320 h" + a `TmProgressBar`), **Milestones** ("1 / 2" + a bar), **Budget overview** ("320 000 CZK of 500 000 CZK" + a bar) and **Work breakdown** ("4 levels • 24 tasks"); a tablet renders two columns; the read-mostly mobile container renders a compact one-line strip ("24 tasks • 40 % done • 1 overdue") and a **Summary** entry in the "More" sheet that opens the full cards as a bottom sheet. A card without data hides (no cost and no budget, no estimates, no milestones). The band shows in the chart views (Day / Week / Month / List) only.
  - `GanttSummary` (record in Abstractions: `StatusCounts`, `OverdueCount`, `LoggedHours`, `EstimatedHours`, `MilestonesDone`/`MilestonesTotal`, `ActualCost`, `BudgetTotal?`, `WbsLevels`, `TaskCount`, `IsFiltered`) and `GanttHelper.ComputeSummary(nodes, today, budgetTotal)` compute it once per refresh from the **filtered** tasks (after the filters and "show closed", ignoring collapse; parents never contribute their hours/cost a second time); `SummaryBandContent` (`RenderFragment<GanttSummary>`) replaces the built-in cards with host content, `BudgetTotal` supplies the total the budget card compares against and `BudgetCurrency` (e.g. `"CZK"`) is appended to the amounts through the active culture.
    ```razor
    <TmGantt Items="tasks" ShowSummaryBand="true" BudgetTotal="500000m" BudgetCurrency="CZK" />
    <TmGantt Items="tasks" ShowSummaryBand="true">
        <SummaryBandContent Context="summary"><my-summary summary="@summary" /></SummaryBandContent>
    </TmGantt>
    ```
  - `TmGanttPortfolio.AxisMode` (`PerProject` default | `Shared`, `GanttPortfolioAxisMode` in Abstractions): **Shared** computes the union range of all projects, renders ONE sticky axis header above the cards (`GanttHelper.BuildTimelineHeaderRows` over `ZoomPreset`, default Weeks) and pins every card to it — `TimelineStart`/`TimelineEnd`, `ZoomPreset` and one tree width (`TreeWidth`, default 12rem) with `ShowTimelineHeader=false` — so the same date draws at the same x in every card. The header's horizontal scroll and the cards' timelines scroll together through the new `tmGantt.linkScrollGroup(groupId, elements)` / `unlinkScrollGroup` in `gantt.js` (the group form of `linkScroll`: pixel-mapped where the content widths match, ratio-mapped where they differ, idempotent per id, entirely in the browser — no interop per scroll tick). A collapsed card never shifts the axis (the union covers all projects).
  - On `TmGantt` itself: `TimelineStart` / `TimelineEnd` (`DateTime?`) pin the axis and override the data's range (bars outside it clip to the edge; Fit to screen measures the pinned axis), `ShowTimelineHeader` (default `true`) hides the two-row header without hiding the grid, and `TreeWidth` (a CSS length) pins the task tree's width.
  - Demo: `/gantt` gained a "Summary band" toggle (with a pinned `BudgetTotal`/`BudgetCurrency`) and `/gantt-portfolio` an "Axis" PerProject | Shared switcher. Wireframe: the `TmGantt` stencil gained `showSummaryBand` and `TmGanttPortfolio` an `axisMode` prop. Strings: `TmGantt_Summary_*` (incl. the `TmGantt_Summary_TasksCount_*`, `TmGantt_Summary_WbsLevels_*` and `TmGantt_Summary_OverdueCount_*` plural families) and `TmGanttPortfolio_SharedAxis` in en, cs, sk and fr.
  - Accessibility fixes found by the phase's axe review: the bulk-select checkboxes carry an accessible name (`TmGantt_BulkSelectTask` = "Select {0}"), the summary band's and the portfolio card's `TmProgressBar`s are named, and the shared axis header's scroll region is keyboard-reachable (`tabindex="0"`). The AllOptions markup snapshot was re-recorded for the bulk-select labels (`TM_UPDATE_SNAPSHOTS=1`); the default DOM is unchanged.
  - Phase-11 review fixes (the opt-in surfaces only; the default DOM stays unchanged):
    - The summary band's scope is the **filtered** data, ignoring collapse (`GanttHelper.FlattenAll`): collapsing a parent no longer changes the rollup, and the "Filtered" note (`IsFiltered`) is set exactly when a filter is active or closed tasks are hidden while the data has some.
    - The shared axis header is a flex row with a **leading cell** as wide as the pinned tree (`--tm-gantt-portfolio-tree-width`, `+1px` for the chart's own border) that carries the localized "Shared timeline" label, so the axis cells start exactly where every card's timeline starts; the scroll band is `flex: 1; min-width: 0` and the bands keep the cards' 1 px border. `tmGantt.linkScrollGroup` maps equal content widths **pixel-for-pixel** (clamped to the target's range — the header's scroller and a card's timeline have different client widths) and falls back to the ratio of the scrollable distance only where the content widths differ; the echo marker is recorded only for writes that actually moved the target (the same in the initial equalization), so a clamped no-op write can never swallow the user's later scroll.
    - Shared mode **locks the cards' scale**: every card is pinned to `LayoutMode.Desktop`, a pinned axis (`TimelineStart`/`TimelineEnd`) makes `TmGantt.GetEffectiveZoomPreset` return the `ZoomPreset` parameter (overriding the Day|Week|Month segment and the mobile Days default), `GetPixelPerDay` stays at zoom 100 and Ctrl+wheel zoom is ignored while pinned.
    - A pinned axis also clips **baselines** exactly like the bars (a baseline fully outside the axis renders nothing) and skips dependency lines whose endpoint bar clipped away (`Width <= 0`).
    - `ShowTimelineHeader=false` now visually hides the card's tree header too (`tm-gantt__tree-header--vh`, the sr-only clip) while keeping `role="row"` and the `columnheader` cells for assistive tech, so the first tree row stays level with the first bar.
    - ARIA of the shared header: the desktop wrapper is a plain layout element (no role/label), the scroll band is `role="region"` with the localized label, and the decorative mobile monthly band is `aria-hidden="true"`.
    - `TmGanttPortfolio` computes the union range, the header rows and the axis width once per parameter change in `OnParametersSet` (the `_unionRange` / `_axisRows` / `_axisTotalWidth` fields) instead of per render access.
- **`TmGantt` window virtualization for large data sets (redesign phase 12), opt-in and additive — the default DOM is unchanged.**
  - *Added.* `Virtualization` (`GanttVirtualizationMode` in Abstractions: `Off` default | `Auto` | `On`), `VirtualizationThreshold` (default 300 visible rows) and `OverscanRows` (default 10). With `On` (or `Auto` at or above the threshold) the tree renders only the visible window of rows plus the overscan between two `aria-hidden` spacers of the exact remaining height, and the timeline renders only the bars, baseline ghosts, progress labels and dependency handles of those rows; a dependency line renders when its y-range intersects the window even with both ends outside it. The full contract (modes, a11y, scope, the perf table) is the "Large data sets" section of [docs/gantt.md](docs/gantt.md); the demo page is `/gantt-large` (a deterministic 1 000 / 5 000 / 10 000-task generator). Measured on the 10 000-task set (all expanded, WASM): once the session attached, the DOM drops from 10 000 rows / ~428 000 chart elements to 28 rows / ~1 600 elements, the window bounds the DOM ~0.3 s after the first paint (the first paint itself is the full set in both modes since the attach gate — the pre-gate "3.1 s first render" number no longer exists), and exactly one .NET render happens per 5-row (overscan/2) scroll step.
  - *Added (a11y while virtualized).* The treegrid carries `aria-rowcount` (visible nodes + header) and every rendered row an absolute `aria-rowindex`; the rows the keyboard or a gesture still needs render pinned outside the window (roving tab stop, selection, inline edit, dragged row, drop target, the bar a focus request targets). Home / End / PageUp / PageDown now move the tab stop by page (the window span minus the overscan; 15 rows without virtualization), the jump is announced ("Row {0} of {1}", key `TmGantt_RowPosition` in en, cs, sk, fr) and the JS session scrolls the target into view. `TaskFingerprint()` is computed once per render pass (the tree gate and the timeline gate share it) — an in-place edit between passes is still detected and painted.
  - *Behaviour change: the vertical tree↔timeline scroll sync moved into `gantt.js` entirely.* `attachVirtualScroll` binds a plain scroll listener (`attachScrollSync`) that keeps the two scroll containers in step in the browser — a Blazor Server circuit no longer pays an interop round trip per scroll tick, and the C# `OnTreeScroll` / `OnTimelineBodyScroll` handlers are DELETED, so a `@onscroll` binding on the two bodies no longer exists in the DOM. With the virtualization on (and the JS session attached), the DOM contains only the window: a host or test that counted `.tm-gantt__tree-row` elements must read `aria-rowcount` instead or pass `Virtualization="Off"`, and the browser's Ctrl+F finds only rendered rows — point users at `ShowQuickSearch`. Demo: `/gantt-large` (size + mode switchers for the measurements); E2E: `GanttVirtualizationE2ETests` (TestCategory=Perf, outside the Smoke lane).
  - *The window never hides data without a browser.* The window applies only while the gantt.js session confirmed itself (`VirtualizationActive` = mode-active && attached): before the attach and on a host without the script the FULL set renders — the pre-attach first paint is the full set in the browser too, the attach + first measurement correct it to the window right after. The review round also re-anchored the window maths on the real pixel range (`gantt-virtual.mjs computeWindow`: `firstVisible = floor(top / rowHeight)`, `lastVisible = ceil((top + clientHeight) / rowHeight)`), so the partially visible edge rows stay painted at a mid-row scroll; the List view attaches the tree body as BOTH scrollers and reads the row count from the tree body's own scroll height; the session re-attaches whenever the gesture key changes (a DockedWorkload toggle, chart ↔ List), a `ResizeObserver` on the tree body re-measures on container resizes, `tmGantt.remeasureVirtual(id)` re-measures after a data change (`DrawVersion`), `updateVirtualScroll(id, rowHeight, overscan, enabled)` silences the window reports while the mode is inactive (the sync keeps running) and a flip to enabled measures immediately, and the report carries the viewport's visible row count (`OnViewportRowsChanged(first, last, visibleRows)`) that `PageRows` — the Home/End/PageUp/PageDown page size — now uses instead of the window span.
  - *A11y: the timeline body is the axis's scroll region.* `tabindex="0"` + `role="region"` + the localized `TmGantt_TimelineAxis` label moved from the pan container (which was never a keyboard target) onto `.tm-gantt__timeline-body`, unconditionally (not only while virtualizing), and the `:focus-visible` ring moved with them. A host that styled or asserted the focus ring against `.tm-gantt__timeline:focus-visible` must target `.tm-gantt__timeline-body:focus-visible`.
- **`TmSplitButton.Icon`, `TmSplitButton.ToggleAriaLabel`, `TmSplitButton.PrimaryAttributes`, `TmToolbarButton.Badge`, `TmColumnPicker.IconOnly` (additive).** An icon before the primary text, an accessible name for the chevron toggle, attributes for the primary button (a `data-testid`), a decorative count pill on a toolbar button, and an icon-only column-picker toggle (its label stays the accessible name). Inside a `TmToolbar` the column-picker toggle joins the roving tab stop whether or not it is icon-only; its label text is wrapped in `span.tm-toolbar-btn-text`. Defaults render the markup they rendered before.
- **`GanttViewSettings.ShowProgressLabel` (additive, default `false`).** Renders the completion percentage (`40%`) right of every task bar (`span.tm-gantt__bar-progress-label[data-testid=bar-progress-label]`, none for milestones). The label is a sibling of the bar inside `.tm-gantt__task-row` (positioned at the bar's right edge, so the faded completed bar does not dim it), and it steps past the deadline flame through the `tm-gantt__bar-progress-label--after-deadline` modifier when a bar has one. The view-settings menu has a "Show progress next to bars" toggle (`vset-show-progress`, key `TmGantt_ShowProgressLabel`) and the wireframe `TmGantt` stencil a `showProgressLabel` prop. New keys in all four languages: `TmGantt_ShowProgressLabel`, `TmGantt_ViewSwitcher` (the label of the Day / Week / Month group) and `TmGantt_WorkloadNoAllocation`.

- **`TmOverlayPanel.SheetTitle` and `TmOverlayPanel.SheetInitialFocusSelector`.** `SheetTitle` names the sheet header and the drawer only; it does not name the popover. Null falls back to `Title`, then `AriaLabel`, then the localized "Menu". `SheetInitialFocusSelector` is a CSS selector scoped to the sheet, the same contract as `TmDrawer.InitialFocusSelector`. When it is null, a `Role` of `menu` or `listbox` still derives the first-entry selector, so existing menu and listbox sheets are unchanged. A match that is not itself focusable falls through to the first focusable.

- **`TmScheduler` side panel and resource filter.** `SidePanel` (`RenderFragment`) and `EventDetailTemplate` (`RenderFragment<TmScheduleEvent>`) are host slots rendered through the core `TmSidePanel` with `Presentation = Auto`: docked on the right on desktop, a side sheet on tablet, a bottom sheet on mobile. The scheduler never invents the panel body. `SidePanelOpen` / `SidePanelOpenChanged` are two-way. An event click opens the detail when a template is set. Closing the panel — Escape on the docked panel too, the close button, or the backdrop — returns focus to that event through the scheduler's own root-scoped `TempoBlazor.Scheduler.focusRovingStop`; the panel passes no restore target, and the views stamp no `id` on an event element, because that id is not unique across views. The detail block carries its own `TmScheduler_CloseDetail` button, which clears only the detail: a host `SidePanel` stays open, and with no host panel the detail was the panel, so it closes. A detail whose event is no longer among the visible events closes on its own. `SidePanelTitle` names the docked header when no detail is showing; null falls back to the localized `TmSidePanel_DefaultTitle`, so the header is never just the close button. `ShowResourceFilter` (default `false`) adds the core `TmMultiSelect` as a toolbar group `data-tm-group="filter"` after `header-actions` and before `primary` (decision SCH-TOOLBAR-2); its trigger reads `TmScheduler_AllResources` or `TmScheduler_NSelected` and carries no visible label. On the compact row the filter is its own second row under the header, so it never squeezes `‹ title ›`, and its popup is the F3 bottom sheet. `SelectedResourceIds` / `SelectedResourceIdsChanged` filter Timeline rows, TimeGrid resource columns, and Month and Agenda events. An empty list keeps every resource, and so does a list whose ids match no known resource: a stale selection hides nothing. An event with no resource stays visible. A phone day whose visible resource the filter drops falls back to the first resource the filter still keeps. With both slots unset the scheduler renders no `.tm-scheduler-frame`, so the markup matches the pre-panel host. `TmMultiSelect` gains `MobilePresentation` (default `Popover`, so an existing multi-select is unchanged) and `LayoutMode`, forwarded to its popup. New resource keys, all four languages: `TmScheduler_AllResources` ("All resources"), `TmScheduler_NSelected` ("{0} selected"), `TmScheduler_OpenPanel` ("Panel"), `TmScheduler_EventDetail`, `TmScheduler_CloseDetail`.
- **`TmMultiSelect.HideLabel` and `AriaLabel`.** `HideLabel` (default `false`) suppresses the visible `<label>` while `Label` stays the accessible name of the trigger and of the listbox. `AriaLabel` overrides that name for both; null falls back to `Label`. The listbox carries that name as `aria-label`; with neither set it is named by `aria-labelledby` pointing at the combobox. The popup root itself is no longer named (see Breaking / Migration).
- **`TmSidePanel.CloseOnEscape`.** When `true`, Escape closes the DOCKED panel through `OpenChanged`. Default `false`: a docked panel is in-flow and leaves Escape to the host, so an existing panel is unchanged. The sheet presentation already closes on Escape and ignores it.
  ```razor
  <TmScheduler @bind-SelectedEvent="selected" @bind-SidePanelOpen="open"
               ShowResourceFilter="true" @bind-SelectedResourceIds="resourceIds" Resources="rooms">
      <SidePanel><TmCalendarView Compact="true" /></SidePanel>
      <EventDetailTemplate Context="evt"><h3>@evt.Title</h3></EventDetailTemplate>
  </TmScheduler>
  ```

- **`TmCalendarView.Compact`.** A mini-month for a popover: `Compact="true"` adds `tm-calendar-view--compact`, which drops the event area and shrinks the day cell. Default `false`, so an existing calendar is unchanged. The scheduler title popover uses it.
- **Toolbar More test id.** A host `data-testid` is copied onto the More entry as `data-testid` only when the button has no bar copy (`TmToolbarButton.Priority == OverflowOnly`). A button that still renders on the bar — including a collapsed Secondary — keeps `data-testid` on that button and exposes the same value as `data-menu-testid` on the menu entry, so exactly one `[data-testid]` match exists with More open. New `TmActionItem.MenuTestId` carries that value; `TmActionItem.TestId` stays the overflow-only hook.

- **`TmDropdown.OpenAsync` and `TmPopover.OpenAsync`.** Both are public. The scheduler action bar uses them: the view entry opens the compact-row dropdown, and Go to date opens the title popover after the More menu has closed.
- **`TmScheduler`: responsive layouts for tablet and mobile.** `LayoutMode` (`Auto` by default) resolves the scheduler's own container; a forced value renders that layout without a measurement. Mobile collapses the toolbar to previous, the title and next, replaces the view tabs with a dropdown, caps a month cell at `CompactMaxVisibleEvents` (default 1), shows a date strip in the week view and a resource picker in a day view that has resources, and renders agenda events as cards. `MobileActionBar` (`None` by default, `Auto` opt-in) renders the core `TmMobileActionBar` on a mobile layout with New event (only with `OnAddClick`), Today, the view switcher and a More menu holding Print and Go to date. The title popover carries a compact month (`.tm-scheduler-date-calendar`). A timeline drag label is parked on the scheduler root, so the sticky resource column no longer paints over it. New resource keys, all four languages: `TmScheduler_GoToDateLabel`, `TmScheduler_SwitchView`, `TmScheduler_ShowResources`, `TmScheduler_DateStrip`, `TmScheduler_ActionBar`, `TmScheduler_Toolbar`.
- **`TmScheduler`: the touch move keeps the grabbed point, and each view has its own keyboard hint.** A finger press records how far into the event it landed, and both the preview and the commit use that point, so the event does not jump to the fingertip. The day, column or row under the finger gets `tm-scheduler-month-day--drop-target` (the grid and timeline reuse the same tint under their own drop-target class) and loses it on release. `ShowTouchHint` (default `false`) renders a localized hint under the toolbar; CSS shows it only for `(hover: none) and (pointer: coarse)`. A draggable event points at its view hint (`TmScheduler_MoveHint_Grid`, `TmScheduler_MoveHint_Timeline`, `TmScheduler_MoveHint_Month`) and lists its Alt chords in `aria-keyshortcuts`. A read-only event is not a keyboard-move target, so it does not swallow Alt+Left/Right. The announcement names the event (`TmScheduler_EventMoved` is "{0} moved to {1}", and `TmScheduler_EventMovedToResource` adds the resource). A move across a daylight-saving boundary writes the display zone's offset for the new local time, not the machine offset.
