- **`TmScheduler`: a finger moves an event, and Alt+Arrow is the keyboard alternative.** A 400ms touch hold on an event in the month, time grid or timeline views starts a move through the shared `pointer-drag.js` (`pointerTypes: ['touch']`); a quick swipe still scrolls, and a mouse or a pen press on the event body stays HTML5 drag-and-drop. The drop snaps to `data-slot-duration` and resolves the day, minute and resource from `data-date`, `data-resource` and `data-range-*`. Escape or `pointercancel` restores the event and commits nothing. Alt+Arrow moves by one slot (or one day in the month), Alt+Shift+Arrow resizes, and a plain arrow stays the roving key. HTML5 drop, the touch release and the keyboard step share one commit path, so a read-only scheduler or a read-only event ignores all three. The scheduler announces the result on a single `role=status` live region (`TmScheduler_EventMoved`, `TmScheduler_EventResized`). While the finger moves, the event gets `tm-scheduler-event--moving` and a live time label (`.tm-scheduler-event-drag-time`). New resource keys, all four languages: `TmScheduler_MoveHint_Grid`, `TmScheduler_MoveHint_Timeline`, `TmScheduler_MoveHint_Month`, `TmScheduler_TouchHint`, `TmScheduler_EventMoved`, `TmScheduler_EventMovedToResource`, `TmScheduler_EventResized`.

- **`Tempo.Blazor.Modeling` redesign (plan "Tempo.Blazor — Redesign: Modeling"): the whole package reworked on the shared editor chrome, with a full contract in [docs/modeling-editor.md](docs/modeling-editor.md).** The plan rebuilt `TmModelingEditor` and its panels over eight phases: a CSP-safe `modeling-editor.js` ES module replaces every `eval` interop (phase 1), the panels are tokenized and the model tree becomes a real APG tree with collapsible `SemanticType` groups (phase 2, MO4), the header gets an opt-in `ShowProviderSelector`/`@bind-ProviderKey` + `ProviderDisplayName` and the preview a Primary "Open in editor" (phase 3, MO3), the "Open in editor" dialog moves onto the core `TmModal` + `TmFocusScope` with capture-phase Escape ordering against the embedded editor (phase 4, G6/G8), the desktop workspace renders through the core `TmEditorShell` — model tree | preview with a collapsible issues dock | inspector with Properties | Source tabs | status bar (phase 5, MO1), the tablet band becomes the shell's Overlay (one drawer/sheet at a time, 44px coarse targets, a non-drag tree→preview alternative; phase 6), and mobile (< 768px of the editor's own container) is viewing + light edits on a `TmTabs` Preview | Tree | Inspector | Issues strip, a status card and a `TmMobileActionBar` (phase 7, G2). Every breaking change has its before/after in [Breaking / Migration](#breaking--migration-continued); the layout, parameters and stable DOM contract are documented in the docs page.

- **`TmModelingEditor` mobile presentation: viewing + light edits (Modeling redesign plan, phase 7, G2).** The compact band is rebuilt on the shared primitives: the compact header keeps the title, the colored state badge and one "⋯" `TmDropdown` (sheet presentation on mobile, entries: Change view, Generate diagram, Open in editor — and it is the open-editor dialog's focus-return host, a `tabindex="-1"` proxy on `tm-modeling-editor__more-host`); the panel strip is a `TmTabs` tablist (Preview | Tree | Inspector | Issues with the issue-count badge, hidden at zero) where exactly ONE panel renders at a time (M26 budget — inactive tab bodies never mount); the "Change view" surface is a `TmModal` bottom sheet (F2/F3) with the shared provider select and the `TmModelingViewSelector`, closing after a picked value; a status card (`modeling-status-card`) shows the four count tiles (Elements / Relationships / Diagram nodes / Diagram edges) plus the loaded time instead of the status strip that dropped its trailing item off-screen at 390px; and the F5 `TmMobileActionBar` (`Placement=StickyContainer`, `MaxVisible=3` + More) carries Reload (the provider reload), Change view, Issues (jumps to the tab) and, behind More, Generate diagram and Open in editor — deliberately no "Settings" item. The tab strip, the status card and the bar live in one focusWithin scope (`tm-modeling-editor__mobile-shell`), so the dialog close and the focus return stay in scope. The open-editor dialog presents fullscreen on the mobile band and hands the embedded diagram editor a full-height body (the DE's own mobile mode — viewing + light edits — drives inside it). New resource keys: `TmModelingEditor_ChangeView`, `TmModelingEditor_Reload`, `TmModelingEditor_MoreOptions`.
- **`TmModelingDiagramPreview.ShowEditActions` (default `true`).** When `false` the preview header renders no buttons (the generate / open-in-editor entries are the hosting editor's action-bar items on a mobile layout) and the drop hint only paints while drops are accepted (`AllowNodeDrop`).

- **`TmModelingEditor.ShowProviderSelector`: an opt-in labeled provider select in the editor header (Modeling redesign plan, phase 3, MO3).** With `ShowProviderSelector="true"` (default `false` = today's behavior: the provider stays the labeled value chip and remains host-owned) the header renders a third labeled field next to the notation/viewpoint selects that lists every registered `IModelingModelProvider` by `ProviderKey`. Picking an entry reloads the model through that provider (keeping the loaded workspace mounted, closing the "Open in editor" dialog — the same keep-surface path the source-panel reload uses) and raises `ProviderKeyChanged` (the `@bind-ProviderKey` partner) plus `OnProviderChanged`; the editor keeps the picked key as an in-editor override until the host parameter itself changes, and an unregistered current key stays listed as an option so an unknown deep-link never silently jumps to another provider. The select mirrors the notation/viewpoint fields (label above the field, `--tm-input-height-md`), the editor root reports the effective key on `data-provider`, and the four `TmResources` tables gained `TmModelingEditor_SelectProvider` and `TmModelingEditor_LastLoaded`. The demo `/modeling-editor` page enables the selector and registers a second demo source (`tempo.demo.modeling.uml`, `DemoUmlModelingModelProvider` in the shared demo project) alongside the default mixed model.
  ```razor
  <!-- before: the provider was host-owned only -->
  <TmModelingEditor ProviderKey="_providerKey" />

  <!-- after: a labeled select over the registered providers -->
  <TmModelingEditor @bind-ProviderKey="_providerKey" ShowProviderSelector="true" OnProviderChanged="HandleProviderChanged" />
  ```

- **`TmModelingEditor` desktop workspace is the core `TmEditorShell` — the inspector presents Properties | Source tabs and the issues are a collapsible dock under the preview (Modeling redesign plan, phase 5, MO1).** The editor now resolves its presentation from its OWN container (`TmLayoutObserver`, `data-layout` on the root, `container: tm-modeling-editor / inline-size`): from 1200px of container width the workspace renders through the core shell (Header = the phase 3 header, Left = model tree, Canvas = diagram preview with the issues dock under it, Right = inspector, StatusBar = the status strip) — the right column no longer stacks (the `TmModelingEditor.razor:150-159` squeeze is gone). Below 768px of container the pre-redesign compact workspace (panel tabs, exactly one visible panel) renders until the mobile phase; between 768 and 1199 the shell's tablet dock applies (at most one expanded panel) — the pair is the DiagramEditor's 768/1200 (review fix). The docked shell is NOT pinned to the editor's resolved mode: an Auto shell measures its own container, so the nested TmDiagramEditors (preview + open-editor dialog) resolve from their own containers. What changes for hosts and tests:
  - *DOM regions moved under the shell's slots.* `modeling-model-tree-panel` and `modeling-inspector-panel` are now wrappers INSIDE the shell's docked `<aside>` elements (the aside is the landmark, the wrapper carries the frozen test id); `modeling-preview-panel` keeps its labelled `<section>` in the shell canvas region, and the issues panel is its SIBLING row (no longer nested — overlap probes compare the two rects). `data-active-panel` and all `data-*` counters stay on the editor root (now the observer element). There is still no `<main>`.
  - *The inspector's source panel is a tab now.* The docked right column is a `TmTabs` "Properties | Source" strip; only the ACTIVE tab renders its body (the M26 single-body budget). The Source tab carries a localized "Stale" badge and a `title` + `aria-describedby` hint (an sr-only span outside the tablist) while the loaded metadata is stale, and its "Load model" button drives the editor's `ReloadModelAsync` exactly as before. Selectors that assumed the source panel always rendered (`modeling-source-load-button`, `modeling-source-system`, `modeling-source-freshness-warning`) must click the Source tab first:
    ```csharp
    // before: the source panel was stacked in the inspector column
    await page.Locator("[data-testid='modeling-source-load-button']").ClickAsync();
    // after: open the Source tab, then reload (the Properties body unmounts while Source is active)
    await page.Locator("[data-testid='modeling-tab-source']").ClickAsync();
    await page.Locator("[data-testid='modeling-source-load-button']").ClickAsync();
    // ... and back for the properties body
    await page.Locator("[data-testid='modeling-tab-properties']").ClickAsync();
    ```
  - *The issues dock collapses.* `TmModelingIssuePanel` gained two-way `Collapsed` / `CollapsedChanged`; the header toggle (`modeling-issues-toggle`) carries `aria-expanded`/`aria-controls`, the body always renders so the id `aria-controls` names is never missing (a collapsed dock hides it with the `hidden` attribute — review fix), and the expanded dock row is a `clamp(10rem, 32%, 20rem)` token block. The panel's own `min-height`/`max-height` pair is GONE — the editor's canvas body owns the height (`minmax(0, 1fr) auto` collapsed, the clamped block expanded), so the list scrolls inside the dock and never overlaps the preview. Hosts that stacked the panel inside their own scroll container keep it working (it sizes to content there).
  - *The panels lost their card chrome.* `.tm-modeling-editor__panel` no longer paints its own border/radius/shadow/background — on the docked layouts the shell's aside owns the surface and the single hairline (the phase 2 double-hairline carry-forward); the compact workspace keeps flat panels on the workspace background. The compact styles now key off the root's `data-layout='mobile'` instead of viewport `@media` queries, so a 500px editor inside a wide page gets the compact workspace and a 390px viewport inside a wide container never does.
  - *New parameters.* `LayoutMode` (`Auto` default) and `InitialMode` (`Desktop`) resolve or pin the presentation; `LayoutBreakpoints` overrides the Modeling pair (768/1200) per instance; and the additive `Height` (`string?`, default `null`) sets the editor's block size — null keeps the stylesheet contract `min(768px, 100vh - 32px)`, a set value renders exactly that height (the token min-height floor is dropped with an inline `min-height: 0`) and the shell inside fills the box:
    ```razor
    <!-- before: fixed default height -->
    <TmModelingEditor ProviderKey="key" />
    <!-- after: the host owns the height -->
    <TmModelingEditor ProviderKey="key" Height="600px" />
    ```
  The `focusWithin` scope moved from the editor root to the canvas surface element (which contains the open-editor trigger AND the dialog in every layout) — the `data-modeling-focus` hooks and the ElementReference contract are unchanged. **(Superseded by the final-review single-dialog fix: the scope is the editor ROOT again — the one surface that contains the close button and every focus-return host in every layout.)** New resource keys in all four tables + `MockTmLocalizer`: `TmModelingEditor_Properties`, `TmModelingEditor_SourceStaleHint`, `TmModelingIssuePanel_Collapse`, `TmModelingIssuePanel_Expand`.
- **Modeling phase 6 review fixes: the tablet sheets start CLOSED, the editor tracks its own layout, the tree filter is bindable and the insert action is fully accessible.** The review pass over 2d869b93 changed the following — none of it is a new phase, every item tightens the phase-6 contract:
  - *The editor resolves its layout from its OWN observer.* `TmModelingEditor.razor` wires `ResolvedLayoutChanged` on its outer `<TmLayoutObserver>` (the shell's raise stays as an idempotent duplicate), and `OnInitialized` seeds the resolved mode (`LayoutMode` when forced, else `InitialMode`) — an Auto editor no longer runs a raise behind on the tablet sheet rules.
  - *Tablet sheets start closed.* `_tabletTreeOpen` / `_tabletInspectorOpen` (both `false`) are the tablet band's own flags, exactly like `TmWireframeEditor.Tablet.cs`; the shell receives `LeftOpen="@(IsTablet ? _tabletTreeOpen : _shellLeftOpen)"` (same Right) and the Open callbacks / tab toggles / `OpenInspectorOnTabletAsync` route to the tablet flags on the band. Entering the tablet also starts the issues dock COLLAPSED (`_tabletIssuesCollapsed`, tablet-only). Neither leaving the tablet nor entering it ever writes the desktop dock flags — a desktop collapse survives a tablet round trip. The preview-only "Panels" tab now carries `aria-pressed` (true exactly while both tablet sheets are closed).
  - *The open-editor dialog no longer pins the embedded editor to `_resolvedLayout`.* The dialog DE is `LayoutMode="Auto"` with `LayoutBreakpoints = new(768, 1100)`: a 1024/1180 tablet window's ~90vw body (922/1062px) resolves the DE tablet layout, a desktop body (≥1100px) resolves desktop — the pin went stale the moment the editor's container and the dialog body disagreed. The floating minimap still starts expanded in the dialog: the DE exposes no "start collapsed" knob for the tablet overlay (noted for the DE plan).
  - *Tablet preview canvas floor.* On the editor's tablet band the shell canvas row keeps a `minmax(20rem, 1fr)` preview floor (the compact and desktop sizing unchanged) and the preview raises the embedded editor's block floor to `calc(var(--tm-space-16) * 5)` under `[data-layout='tablet']`, so the touch canvas stays usable at 1024x768 / 1180x820 (E2E asserts `.tm-diagram-canvas` ≥ 240px).
  - *`TmModelingModelTree.FilterText` / `FilterTextChanged` (two-way).* The parameter seeds the internal filter and is never assigned inside the component; user edits raise the callback (and clear the transient filter-collapse set). The editor owns the value (a plain holder written by a once-built, non-component-receiver callback — a component-bound EventCallback invoke re-renders the editor per keystroke and blew the M26 tree-filter budget), so the filter survives a tree remount when the layout flips. The editor also builds its tree/preview EventCallback parameters ONCE (a method-group parameter is a new delegate per render, which re-rendered the 200-row tree on every parent pass).
  - *Insert action a11y.* The row "+" button renders only when `AllowNodeDrop && OnInsertIntoPreview.HasDelegate`, is `tabindex="-1"` (out of the tab order), and names its row with the new per-row key `TmModelingModelTree_InsertIntoPreviewNamed` ("Insert {0} into preview" en/cs/sk/fr + `MockTmLocalizer`). The keyboard path is the node treeitem's `Insert` (and `Ctrl+Enter`) — emulated on keydown, `!Repeat`-guarded, gated on the same condition, advertised with `aria-keyshortcuts="Insert Control+Enter"`. On a coarse pointer the button is a full 44x44 target (`min-width: var(--tm-touch-target)`); on `(hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)` the reserved trailing column is GONE — the row is one full-width track again (desktop tree names truncate exactly as before phase 6) and the action floats over the row's trailing edge, revealed by the core hover pair.
  - *Insert at the center of what the user SEES.* New additive `TmDiagramEditor.GetViewport()` delegates to `TmDiagramCanvas.GetViewport()` (document-space visible window; a zeroed tuple before the JS engine reports), and `TmModelingDiagramPreview.InsertAtViewportCenterAsync` uses `(x + w/2, y + h/2)` when the viewport is known, falling back to the page center otherwise.
  - *Re-review fixes (18ea09f3 follow-up).* `TmModelingModelTree` records the echo value as the last HOST-provided `FilterText` (a host reset to it — clearing the filter after the user typed — re-seeds the working copy again), the node treeitem's `aria-keyshortcuts` lists both insert paths (`Insert Control+Enter`), the tree's own heading block is hidden inside the tablet drawer via the new opt-out `TmModelingModelTree.ShowTitle` (default `true`; the sheet title already says "Model tree", the search field stays and the `role="tree"` is named by `aria-label` when the block is absent), and the M26 tree specs pin the desktop viewport (the drawer starts closed on the tablet band, where the tree and its search input do not exist).
- **`TmModelingEditor` tablet presentation is the shell's Overlay — one side sheet at a time, "Panels" tabs as the visibility switch, 44px coarse-pointer targets, and a non-drag alternative for the tree drop (Modeling redesign plan, phase 6).** The tablet band (768–1199px of the editor's own container) no longer renders the shell's docked columns with rails: it presents `TabletPanelPresentation.Overlay` (decision `EDITOR-SHELL-TABLET-PRESENTATION`) — the model tree is an overlay drawer (`modeling-tree-drawer`), the inspector a non-modal side sheet (`modeling-inspector-sheet`, closed by `modeling-sheet-close` or Escape), at most ONE open at a time over a full-width preview. The editor owns the open flags and enforces the rule itself (opening one closes the other); leaving the tablet layout hands the full desktop dock back. The `modeling-panel-tabs` row (same test ids as the compact row) now renders under the header as the VISIBILITY switch: Tree and Inspector are `aria-expanded` disclosure toggles (`aria-controls` pointing at the shell's public `LeftPanelId`/`RightPanelId`), Preview closes both. A tree selection is an editing intent — it opens the inspector sheet and yields the drawer (`data-active-panel` stays the compact branch's state). The desktop (≥1200) and compact (<768) presentations are unchanged. Before/after for hosts keying the old tablet band:
    ```razor
    <!-- before (phase 5): a forced tablet editor was the docked band — panels as columns/rails -->
    <TmModelingEditor LayoutMode="TmLayoutMode.Tablet" />
    @* .tm-editor-shell__panel asides with rails, no panel tabs *@

    <!-- after (phase 6): the same forced editor presents the overlay sheets -->
    <TmModelingEditor LayoutMode="TmLayoutMode.Tablet" />
    @* [data-testid='modeling-tree-drawer'] / [data-testid='modeling-inspector-sheet'],
       at most one in the DOM; [data-testid='modeling-panel-tabs'] toggles visibility *@
    ```
  E2E that asserted docked columns on a tablet must assert the sheets instead: probes that count the side-panel test ids keep working because they only exist in the DOM while a sheet is open (the preview panel is always there) — the tablet rule is now "the preview plus at most ONE side panel".
- **`TmModelingModelTree`: the "Insert into preview" action is the non-drag alternative (WCAG 2.5.7).** Every node row carries a sibling `+` button (`modeling-tree-insert-{elementId}` — a button must never nest inside the node button) that asks the host to reuse the element through the preview's existing drop path. The tree raises the request; the HOST owns the geometry: the new public `TmModelingDiagramPreview.InsertAtViewportCenterAsync(element)` creates the node at the center of the diagram viewport (the page center in the fit view) through the same clamp/collision logic, mutates the document, and raises the SAME `OnNodeDropped`/`ModelingNodeDroppedEventArgs` contract as a real drop — so hosts listening for tree reuse need no new wiring:
    ```razor
    <!-- before: tree reuse was drag-only (HTML5 dragstart -> preview drop) -->
    <TmModelingEditor AllowNodeDrop="true" OnNodeDropped="HandleNodeDropped" />

    <!-- after: the same path answers the accessible action too; AllowNodeDrop switches BOTH -->
    <TmModelingEditor AllowNodeDrop="@allowReuse" OnNodeDropped="HandleNodeDropped" />
    ```
  With `AllowNodeDrop="false"` (the `?scenario=drag-readonly` demo) neither the drop zone nor the alternative exists. The reveal contract is the core `.tm-reveal-on-hover` pair — hidden until hover on a fine pointer ONLY, always visible on `(hover: none)` and under `:focus-within`, `--tm-touch-target` on a coarse pointer. The action lives in the row flow (a trailing grid column), so tree rows render ~36px narrower for the node text — the same affordance column on every layout, and the drag handle shifts left with it. **(Superseded by the phase-6 review fix above: on `(hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)` the reserved trailing column is GONE — the row is one full-width track again and the action floats over the trailing edge.)** New parameters on the tree: `AllowNodeDrop` (default `true`) and `OnInsertIntoPreview`. New resource keys in all four tables + `MockTmLocalizer`: `TmModelingModelTree_InsertIntoPreview`, `TmModelingEditor_ToggleTree`, `TmModelingEditor_ToggleInspector`, `TmModelingEditor_PreviewOnly`.
- **`TmModelingEditor` coarse-pointer targets reach `--tm-touch-target` (44px), and the dialog footprint keys off the editor container.** On `(pointer: coarse)` the "Panels" tabs, the header provider select and the notation/viewpoint selects (`TmModelingViewSelector`), the tree nodes and group headers, the issue rows and the source panel's "Load model" button (default `--tm-input-height-md` ≈ 38px) all grow to the shared 44px target. The open-editor dialog footprint no longer uses a viewport `@media (max-width: 48rem)`: it is a `@container tm-modeling-editor (width < 768px)` query (the modal paints fixed, but container queries still match through the nearest ancestor container), so a 500px editor inside a wide viewport gets the compact dialog and a tablet editor keeps the ~90vw × 90vh one. The embedded dialog editor's layout is the body-decided Auto resolution on every band (final review): the dialog DE is `LayoutMode="Auto"` with `LayoutBreakpoints = new(768, 1100)` — the ~90vw body of a 1024 or 1180 window (922/1062px) resolves the DE tablet layout (one docked panel expanded + the floating minimap overlay), while a desktop dialog body (≥1100px) still resolves desktop — the shared 640/1024 pair would flip the embedded editor at both ends, and the old 768/1024 pair pinned a 1180 tablet dialog to desktop. `TmModelingSourcePanel` gained a wide-container layout: `@container tm-modeling-source-panel (width >= 640px)` lays the three metadata cells out in three columns and moves the load button into the header row via grid areas (DOM order and test ids unchanged); below 640px the rows stay stacked as before. `TmModelingIssuePanel` rows reach the 44px target on a coarse pointer. The wireframe stencil's `TmModelingEditor` entry renders a `layout` prop variant (`desktop` default; `tablet` draws the sheet, the toggle pills and the full-width issues row), mirroring the `TmScheduler` stencil's `layoutMode` pattern.
- **`TmModelingDiagramPreview` header: primary "Open in editor", wrapping layout (Modeling redesign plan, phase 3, MO3 + phase-2 review carry-forward).** The preview header contract is now locked by tests: "Open in editor" is the Primary button, "Generate diagram" the Secondary one, the header wraps (`flex-wrap: wrap` + `row-gap`) and the title breaks instead of ellipsizing, so a narrow 1024px preview column no longer truncates the title to "Dia…" or clips either button. bUnit coverage in `TmModelingEditorTests` (provider selector, chip dedupe, status-strip time, reload indicator), `TmModelingViewSelectorTests` (labels above fields, height token), `TmModelingDiagramPreviewTests` (action variants, header wrap, the widened "no diagram-editor internals in Modeling CSS" guard) and E2E in `ModelingProviderSelectorE2ETests`.
- **`TmTypedChat<TItem>`: the generic chat as a SEPARATE component composed over the non-generic `TmChat` (FZE-15, decision `TMCHAT-TYPED-COMPOSITION`).** Hosts that model the conversation as their own domain sequence no longer map it by hand into a `List<ChatMessage>`: the new wrapper takes `Items` (`IReadOnlyList<TItem>`, `[EditorRequired]`) and `MessageSelector` (`Func<TItem, ChatMessage>`, `[EditorRequired]`) and renders an inner `<TmChat>`. The selector runs in `OnParametersSet` ONCE PER NEW ITEM REFERENCE — a `ReferenceEqualityComparer` cache keyed by the item reuses the previously mapped `ChatMessage` instance for an unchanged reference (Blazor's `@key`ed row matching keeps the row's component instances alive) and evicts entries whose items disappeared; value-type items (and a null item) have no identity and are re-mapped on every parameter pass. The cache saves MAPPING WORK only — the selector must depend on nothing but the item handed to it, and replacing an item (a different reference for the same row) or replacing the selector forces the affected rows to be re-mapped; the comparison is `Equals`, so a fresh delegate of the same instance/static method (the Razor compiler builds one per render for a method group like `MessageSelector="ToChatMessage"`) does not pay a re-map on every render. A selector message with a null `Payload` gets the ITEM stored as its payload, so even a plain (non-generic) `TmChat` template can read it back with `context.PayloadAs<TItem>()`; a payload the selector sets itself wins. `ItemTemplate` (`RenderFragment<ChatItemContext<TItem>>?`) receives the new `ChatItemContext<TItem>` — the `Item` (recovered from the mapped message's payload, exact type, no second lookup dictionary) plus the full `ChatMessageContext` and the `IsOwn`/`InThread`/`Index`/`IsFirstInGroup`/`DefaultContent` shortcuts — and `UseTemplateFor` (`Func<TItem, bool>?`) restricts it with exactly the precedence `TmChat.UseTemplateFor` documents; a message whose mapped payload is NOT a `TItem` (the selector supplied its own payload) renders the built-in row — with or without a predicate — instead of reaching the template as `default(TItem)`; without an `ItemTemplate` the built-in rows render for every item. EVERY OTHER `TmChat` parameter is forwarded by attribute splatting (`OnSend`, `ComposerTemplate`, `AutoAttachComposerInput`, `RenderWindowSize`, …) — there is no IntelliSense for the forwarded parameters, and `Messages`/`MessageTemplate`/`UseTemplateFor` passed through the splat throw an `ArgumentException` naming the conflicting attribute instead of silently fighting the derived values. `TmTypedChat` also validates every forwarded value against the `TmChat` parameter it names and throws a descriptive `ArgumentException` from `OnParametersSet` when the type cannot reach it, instead of letting the chat die on an `InvalidCastException` while rendering. EventCallback pitfall: for an attribute that matches no parameter the Razor compiler has no target type, so a bare method group (`OnSend="HandleSend"`) compiles to the handler's NAME as a plain string — the error names the attribute, the expected type and the factory form to write: `OnSend="@(EventCallback.Factory.Create<ChatSendRequest>(this, HandleSend))"` (values whose type already matches pass through unchanged). The id resolution of `ScrollToItemAsync(TItem)` / `FocusItemAsync(TItem)` reads the selector cache first, so the host's selector does not re-run for an item that is already mapped. The public helpers delegate to the inner chat (`Chat`, `ScrollToBottomAsync`, `ScrollToItemAsync(TItem)`, `ScrollToMessageAsync`, `FocusItemAsync(TItem)`, `AnnounceAsync`, `FocusComposerAsync`, `HasUnsavedDraft`, `DiscardDraftAsync`) and no-op before the first render; the draft guard stays registered by the inner chat, the wrapper ships no JS and is deliberately NOT `IAsyncDisposable`. `TmChat` itself is unchanged and stays non-generic (the closed decision stands — see the ADR in [docs/chat-custom-templates.md](docs/chat-custom-templates.md)); every existing `<TmChat>` compiles unchanged. New demo section `chat-typed-section` on `/chat` (a `SupportTicketEvent` record with `TmChatBubble` in the `ItemTemplate`, sending through the forwarded `OnSend`); bUnit coverage in `TmTypedChatTests`, E2E in `ChatTypedE2ETests`.
  ```razor
  @* A ticket thread built from the host's own domain record — no manual mapping *@
  <TmTypedChat Items="_ticketEvents" MessageSelector="MapTicketEvent"
               OnSend="@(EventCallback.Factory.Create<ChatSendRequest>(this, HandleSend))">
      <ItemTemplate Context="ctx">
          <TmChatBubble Variant="ChatBubbleVariant.Pending" ActorLabel="@ctx.Item!.Actor">
              <ChildContent><span>@ctx.Item.Message</span></ChildContent>
          </TmChatBubble>
      </ItemTemplate>
  </TmTypedChat>
  ```

- **`TmChat` long conversations: opt-in render window `RenderWindowSize` / `RenderWindowStep` keeps very large chats to a bounded DOM (FZE-14, decision `TMCHAT-RENDER-WINDOW`).** A conversation with thousands of messages no longer renders thousands of keyed `.tm-chat__item` rows: the new `RenderWindowSize` (`int?`, default `null` = render EVERY row, byte-identical markup) renders only a contiguous `[Start, count)` slice of the root sequence — the TAIL — and grows it upward by `RenderWindowStep` (`int`, default 50; the size clamps to ≥ 20, the step to ≥ 10) instead of mounting `<Virtualize>` (top-anchored, estimated row heights, its spacers fight `overflow-anchor: none` + the anchor restore, and rows outside the DOM would break the `data-message-id` anchors, `focusMessage` and row reading — the ADR in [docs/chat-custom-templates.md](docs/chat-custom-templates.md)). The window rules: the first render and a replaced list window the last `N` rows; a PINNED append slides the window with the tail (the top trimmed to `count - N`); an append while the user reads ABOVE the bottom trims NOTHING (the DOM above the viewport must not change) — the trim happens when the scroller reports the return to the bottom, including behind the jump-to-new click, and reclaims only that away-append excess, refreshing the tracked keep-id onto the trimmed start so a later parameter set cannot snap the window back (a deep-link or top-edge expansion mounts its rows deliberately and drops the claim, so it survives its own restore's at-bottom report and persists until the next pinned append; a row vanishing from the list keeps the start — only a PINNED append falls back to the tail; and a merged Append+Prepend render above the bottom keeps the prepend restore while counting the appended rows behind the jump button); reaching the top edge (the scroller's near-top report or the built-in *Load older* affordance, now visible while `Start > 0` too) grows the window one step as a render PREPEND — the `chat.js` anchor restore keeps the reading position (also under `AutoScroll="Never"`, where the expansion's own `afterUpdate("prepend")` still runs) — the top-edge report is verified against the LIVE near-top geometry TWICE, 300 ms apart (the new `chat.js` scroller-handle `isNearTop()` getter), because a transient scroll clamp or a mis-aimed smooth scroll during a huge window render holds the viewport in the top band for a fraction of a second and that momentary report must not mount thousands of rows — and the host's `OnLoadOlder` fires only once `Start == 0` (and `HasMoreBefore`); a host prepend of older history keeps the previously-first rendered row and expands one step above it; the row under inline edit and the root of the open thread panel are never trimmed out. The jump-to-new click IS a return to the bottom: it trims the away-append excess immediately (and refreshes the tracked keep-id) instead of waiting for the scroller's at-bottom report, which a slow circuit can delay past the user's next action. `ScrollToMessageAsync` / `FocusMessageAsync` for an anchor above the window expand it to include the anchor (a render prepend), wait for that render to apply (a shared `TaskCompletionSource` — concurrent deep links wait on the ONE pending completion — completed by the after-render bookkeeping of a render that actually mounted rows; dispose completes it unconditionally, so a waiter never hangs) and only then run the JS navigation, so a deep link outside the window still finds and focuses its row. The thread panel is deliberately NOT windowed (threads are short). Everything data-driven is untouched: announcements and the jump-to-new count read `Messages` (never the DOM), `AutoReadReceipts` keeps its data semantics, the draft guard is independent of the window, and `ChatMessageContext.Index` / `IsFirstInGroup` are computed over the FULL sequence before the slice, so grouping does not change at the window edge. New demo section `chat-render-window-section` on `/chat` (5 000 generated messages, `RenderWindowSize="100"`, jump/focus-to-message-#10 buttons and a live rendered-row counter); bUnit coverage in `TmChatRenderWindowTests` (+ the pure `ChatRenderWindow` state rules), E2E in `ChatScrollE2ETests`/`ChatRenderWindowServerE2ETests` (WASM + Server).
  ```razor
  @* A 100k-message inbox: the DOM holds the last 100 rows and grows by 50 per top-edge visit *@
  <TmChat Messages="@_history" CurrentUser="@_user"
          RenderWindowSize="100" RenderWindowStep="50"
          OnLoadOlder="LoadOlderPageAsync" HasMoreBefore="_hasMore" />
  ```

- **`TmChat` virtual keyboard: opt-in `TrackVirtualKeyboard` keeps the narrow sticky composer above the iOS on-screen keyboard (FZE-13).** On iOS Safari (which ignores `interactive-widget`) an opening keyboard shrinks only the VISUAL viewport — the layout viewport (and with it every sticky containing block) stays put, so `position: sticky; bottom: var(--tm-chat-composer-offset, 0px)` alone leaves the composer under the keyboard; the tracker is what handles the keyboard there. The new parameter (`bool`, default `false` = today's behavior: no `visualViewport` listeners, nothing changes without the opt-in) attaches the new `chat.js` `attachViewportTracker(root, options)` after the first render (and on a parameter or scroller change), which listens to `visualViewport` `resize` AND `scroll` — iOS moves the viewport on scroll rather than resizing it — coalesces both through `requestAnimationFrame` (one style write per frame) and, ONLY on a change, writes the covered gap `round(max(0, innerHeight - (viewport.height + viewport.offsetTop)))` as the RUNTIME knob `--tm-chat-keyboard-inset` into the chat root's inline style plus a `data-tm-keyboard-open` marker. A shrink below 80 px is a collapsing browser toolbar, not a keyboard, and writes nothing (JS option `minInset`); a ZOOM keeps the current state too — while `viewport.scale` sits off 1 the tracker writes nothing new (a pinch zoom is the user resizing), a degenerate (< 2 px) viewport measures nothing, and the inset is rounded so device-pixel fractions cannot churn the inline style. While the keyboard is CLOSED the narrow-chat sticky composer and the thread overlay's reply row rest at `bottom: calc(var(--tm-chat-composer-offset, 0px) + var(--tm-chat-keyboard-inset, 0px))`; while the `data-tm-keyboard-open` marker is set they rest at `bottom: max(var(--tm-chat-composer-offset, 0px), var(--tm-chat-keyboard-inset, 0px))` — the keyboard covers the host's bottom navigation, so the LARGER of the two offsets wins instead of their sum (the composer rests ON the keyboard, not above keyboard + navigation) — the knob's default lives in the `var()` fallback and the library never declares it; while the marker is set the safe-area padding is dropped (`padding-bottom: var(--tm-space-3)`), because the keyboard covers the home indicator. The stuck composer covers MORE of the message list than the inset whenever the chat's box extends past the fold, so the tracker ALSO measures the covered list space into a second runtime knob, `--tm-chat-composer-clearance` (list bottom minus stuck composer top): while the marker is set the messages list reserves it as scroll room (`padding-bottom` + `scroll-padding-bottom`), so the rescued last row can land ABOVE the composer even when the messages themselves do not overflow the list. Closing the keyboard REMOVES the inline knobs and the marker (back to the cascade, not zeroed inline) — the same cleanup runs on dispose, which also detaches the listeners and cancels a pending frame; two chats on one page track independently. When the keyboard OPENS and the user was reading at the bottom, the tracker re-lands the list through the scroller handle's new `scrollLastMessageAboveBottom(gap)` so the last row's bottom rests exactly on the stuck composer's top edge (an older handle degrades to the instant `scrollToBottom(true)`); the rescue reads the scroller's `isPinned()` belief first (falling back to the measured `isAtBottom()`), keeps the programmatic pin bookkeeping (no spurious unread report), and a reader of older history keeps their position. Android: with the recommended `interactive-widget=resizes-content` viewport meta the LAYOUT viewport shrinks instead, the measured inset comes out ≈ 0 and the tracker never writes; on Android WITHOUT the meta (Chrome's default `resizes-visual`) the visual viewport shrinks like on iOS and the tracker lifts the composer there too. The demo phone frame (`chat-mobile-phone` on `/chat`) opts in; bUnit coverage in `TmChatViewportTests` + the CSS contract in `TmChatLayoutTests`, node coverage in the `test:overlay` lane (`chat.test.mjs`), E2E in `ChatLayoutMobileE2ETests` (a fake `window.visualViewport` injected with `AddInitScriptAsync` — Playwright cannot open a real keyboard).
  ```razor
  @* Hosts with a bottom navigation: the composer clears the nav AND the keyboard *@
  <TmChat FillParent="true" TrackVirtualKeyboard="true" Messages="_messages" CurrentUser="_user" />
  ```

- **`TmChat` composer: opt-in AUTO-ATTACH of a `ComposerTemplate` input by id (FZE-12).** A host whose custom composer carries `id="@composer.InputId"` on its input can now skip the `OnAfterRenderAsync` + `ChatComposerContext.AttachAsync` dance: the new `AutoAttachComposerInput` parameter (`bool`, default `false` = today's behavior, so nothing changes without the opt-in) makes TmChat resolve and attach the template input itself. The lookup is performed by the new `chat.js` export `attachComposerById(root, inputId, dotNetRef, options)` — scoped to THIS chat instance's root element (`root.querySelector('#' + CSS.escape(id))`, so an element with the same id elsewhere on the page never wins; `InputId` is per-TmChat-instance), internally reusing `attachComposer` (there is exactly one Enter/IME/resize implementation), with no module-level state, and it returns a `{ sync, focusIfNeeded, dispose }` handle whose `sync()` re-queries on every further TmChat render (the same node is a no-op, a replaced node is detached and re-attached, a missing node detaches — an input inside a nested host component that re-renders independently of TmChat is captured on the next TmChat render; a host that swaps the element without TmChat re-rendering still uses `AttachAsync`). The attach runs once (the serialized sync loop of the composer interop, `enterToSend`/`maxRows: 5`/`OnComposerSubmit` options identical to the built-in composer), an `EnterToSend` change disposes and re-attaches, and turning the parameter off, `ShowComposer="false"` or removing the template disposes the handle. **Precedence: an explicit `AttachAsync` ALWAYS wins** — while a host registration exists the auto handle is detached, and `AttachAsync(default)` hands the control back to the auto-attach, so the two modes never fight over Enter. `RefocusAfterSend`, `FocusComposerAsync()` and `composer.FocusAsync()` target the auto-attached input (`handle.focusIfNeeded()`, so an input that already holds focus is left alone), and a send re-measures it after the clear. Like every composer path the auto-attach is inert before interactivity (the C# `@onkeydown` fallback cannot help a template input TmChat did not render). Full contract — precedence, the render-scope rule and an example — in [docs/chat-custom-templates.md](docs/chat-custom-templates.md); new demo section `chat-autoattach-section` on `/chat` (a composer registered ONLY by the id attribute); bUnit coverage in `TmChatComposerAutoAttachTests` and node coverage in the `test:overlay` lane.
  ```razor
  @* The whole registration is the id attribute — no OnAfterRenderAsync, no AttachAsync *@
  <TmChat Messages="_messages" CurrentUser="_user" OnSend="HandleSend"
          ComposerTemplate="AutoComposer" AutoAttachComposerInput="true" />
  @code {
      private RenderFragment<ChatComposerContext> AutoComposer => context =>
          @<textarea id="@context.InputId" value="@context.Text"
                     @oninput="@(e => context.SetTextAsync(e.Value?.ToString() ?? string.Empty))" />;
  }
  ```

- **`TmChat` layout & mobile: the chat as a flex child, host-owned minimum height, sticky composer above a bottom navigation, 44px touch targets and a full-width thread overlay on a narrow chat (FZE-8).** The chat now participates in its host's layout instead of only filling it. `FillParent` (`bool`, default `false` = today's behavior) adds the `tm-chat--fill` modifier — `flex: 1 1 auto; height: auto; min-height: var(--tm-chat-min-height, 0)` (the knob's ZERO fallback, so a floor a host declared on a wrapper or `:root` keeps applying in fill mode — set the knob to 0 yourself to hand the height to the parent entirely) — for a chat sitting in a flex row/column of an app shell: it grows and shrinks with the parent's free space while the internal message scroller (itself `min-height: 0`) absorbs the difference. The hardcoded `min-height: 300px` floor became the `--tm-chat-min-height` knob (fallback `300px`, so a host that touches nothing sees no change); set it to `0` (or any floor) on a wrapper or `:root` and it cascades — the library never declares the knob, the default lives in the `var()` fallback. `.tm-chat` is now its own size container (`container-type: inline-size; container-name: tm-chat`), so the narrow-chat behaviors below branch on the CHAT's width, not the viewport — a chat in a narrow desktop column behaves mobile. Because a size container forces a definite inline size, the root also carries `contain-intrinsic-inline-size: auto 360px`: inside a shrink-to-fit host (float, table cell, grid auto column) the chat's intrinsic width is 360px instead of collapsing to 0; hosts that size the chat themselves opt out with the `tm-chat--no-container` modifier (pass it through `Class`). Template note: because the chat is a size container, UNNAMED `@container` queries in host `MessageTemplate`/`ComposerTemplate` CSS now resolve against the CHAT — give template containers their own names to keep them scoped elsewhere. On a chat narrower than the shared 640px breakpoint (`@container tm-chat (width < 640px)`) the composer is `position: sticky` with `bottom: var(--tm-chat-composer-offset, 0px)` — the knob (0 by default) is the offset the composer clears: it sticks to the bottom of the HOST SCROLLPORT (resting at the chat's own bottom edge once that is visible), and a host sets it to the height of its bottom navigation to keep the composer above that chrome while the page scrolls. The same narrow block carries the safe-area padding for the composer AND the thread overlay's reply row — `padding-bottom: calc(var(--tm-space-3) + var(--tm-chat-safe-area-bottom, env(safe-area-inset-bottom, 0px)))` — where `--tm-chat-safe-area-bottom` is the host's opt-out knob (set it to 0 when your bottom navigation already pads the safe area). The overlay's header sticks to the top of the scrollport, and with the panel open the covered body and composer get `visibility: hidden` (a screen reader would otherwise read the same messages twice). Keeping the composer above the iOS virtual keyboard is now an OPT-IN component feature (FZE-13, its own entry below): `TrackVirtualKeyboard="true"` tracks the visual viewport and lifts the sticky composer above the keyboard; the optional viewport meta `<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1, viewport-fit=cover, interactive-widget=resizes-content">` still makes the layout viewport shrink instead of being covered — so the sticky composer lands above the keyboard on Android Chrome without any JS, and the tracker measures an inset of ≈ 0 there (harmless). On the same narrow chat the thread panel overlays the FULL width (`left: 0; width: 100%`) instead of squeezing the composer into a sliver — the panel keeps its own reply input, so nothing is lost. The root clips with `overflow: hidden; overflow: clip` (the declaration pair keeps `hidden` on engines without `clip`): `clip` is visually identical but does not create a scroll container, which is what lets the sticky composer respond to the HOST's scrollport — inside an `overflow: hidden` chat a sticky element could never move. Coarse pointers get 44px targets (`--tm-touch-target`) on the send button (40px on fine pointers, unchanged), the 26px per-message action icons, the 28px thread-close and emoji buttons, the edit save/cancel pair and the reply-count badge — added under the existing `(hover: none), (pointer: coarse)` block because target size is a pointer-modality (WCAG 2.5.5/2.5.8) requirement, not a width one: a mouse user on a narrow window gains nothing from a bigger button, a finger on a wide tablet still needs 44px, and the desktop default look must not regress. The same block puts the per-message action bar INTO THE FLOW on touch (an always-revealed floating bar would cover the bubble it belongs to: `position: static`, a wrapped row under the message, the incoming/outgoing horizontal offsets reset to `auto`) and steps the composer input up to `--tm-font-size-md`. The single-row auto-resizing composer (`rows="1"`, `chat.js` `maxRows`) already satisfied the mobile composer requirement unchanged. The thread-panel styles are mirrored into the global `_chat.css` fallback for the first time (they had only ever existed in the scoped stylesheet), together with every FZE-8 rule. New demo section `chat-mobile-section` on `/chat` (`chat-fill-pane`, `chat-thread-overlay-pane`, `chat-mobile-phone` — a 375px phone frame with a fake 56px bottom navigation) where the two knobs are declared by the demo as a consumer. bUnit + CSS contract coverage in `TmChatLayoutTests`.
  ```razor
  @* A chat pane of an app shell: fill the flex parent, stick above a 56px bottom navigation *@
  <TmChat FillParent="true" Messages="_messages" CurrentUser="_user" />
  ```
  ```css
  /* Host: release the 300px floor / own the sticky offset */
  .inbox-chat { --tm-chat-min-height: 0; --tm-chat-composer-offset: 56px; }
  ```

- **`TmChat` accessibility: exactly ONE polite live region with a host-supplied, trailing-throttled announcement pipeline, labelled keyboard-scrollable message region and focus hooks (FZE-7).** The component now renders a single visually-hidden `<div class="tm-sr-only" aria-live="polite" aria-atomic="true">` and never anything else with `aria-live` — the `BannerContent` slot and the typing indicator stay silent, and the messages container is a labelled `role="region"` (deliberately NOT `role="log"`, which would imply a second live region) with `tabindex="0"` so the scrollable area is keyboard-focusable. The announcement TEXT is the host's (the library invents no sentences): `MessageAnnouncement` (`Func<ChatMessage, string?>?`) supplies the text per message — a null func or a null/whitespace result announces nothing, so a consumer without the parameter keeps today's silent chat; `BatchAnnouncement` (`Func<IReadOnlyList<ChatMessage>, string?>?`) optionally summarizes a burst; `AnnounceAsync(string text)` announces host actions ("Draft approved"). A trailing throttle (`AnnouncementThrottle`, default 1 s, driven by the injected `TimeProvider`) collapses a burst to the summary (two or more messages) or the LATEST text: a free window flushes immediately, messages arriving within the window wait, a host action announced through `AnnounceAsync` in the same window is composed WITH the held messages (both survive) and the live region's content is a `@key`ed span — every announcement replaces the span node, so even the SAME sentence is announced again with a single render. Only messages appended to the END of the rendered root list are announced — the initial load, a fill from an empty list and a PREPEND of older history are not, and a tail-replaced reload re-announces only ids the component has never seen; own messages are skipped unless `AnnounceOwnMessages` (`bool`, default `false`) is set; typing is never announced; the pending timer is cancelled in `DisposeAsync`. New focus hooks: `FocusMessageAsync(string? id)` (returns whether the row was found; the container-scoped `chat.js` `focusMessageVisible` scrolls it into view — `block: 'nearest'`, reduced-motion aware — and focuses it with `preventScroll`, safe while a thread panel duplicates the root) and automatic focus restoration onto the button that opened a thread when the thread closes (its own close button or a parameter-driven unmount — previously the focus fell to the body). The built-in composer textarea carries an `aria-label` (`ComposerAriaLabel`, default the effective placeholder — until now it had only a placeholder, which is no accessible name); the thread reply input and the inline message edit got their `aria-label`s too (`TmChat_ReplyPlaceholder` / new `TmChat_EditMessage` key). New localization keys in all four tables: `TmChat_MessagesLabel`, `TmChat_EditMessage`. The per-message action bar is no longer hover-only: `.tm-chat__item:focus-within .tm-chat__actions` reveals it for keyboard users (scoped stylesheet and global fallback). New node-independent demo section `chat-a11y-section` on `/chat`; bUnit coverage in `TmChatA11yTests`. Opening a thread through the built-in UI focuses the panel's reply input.
  ```razor
  <TmChat Messages="_messages" CurrentUser="_user"
          MessageAnnouncement="@(m => $"New message from {m.Author?.Name}: {m.Text}")"
          BatchAnnouncement="@(batch => $"{batch.Count} new messages")" />
  ```
  ```csharp
  // Host action through the same single region (e.g. after an approval flow):
  await chat.AnnounceAsync("Draft approved");
  await chat.FocusMessageAsync(messageId); // keyboard focus onto a message wrapper
  ```

- **`TmChat` composer behavior: Enter/Shift+Enter with an IME guard, auto-resize, text kept on a failed send and refocus after a send (chat.js).** A new core ES module `src/Tempo.Blazor/wwwroot/js/chat.js` (covered by `src/Tempo.Blazor/wwwroot/js/__tests__/chat.test.mjs`, the `test:overlay` Node lane) owns the composer keydown behavior and is imported by `TmChat` on first render (pattern of `TmScrollSpyNav`): `attachComposer(textarea, dotNetRef, options)` attaches a per-call (NO module-level state, so several chats on one page work independently) `keydown` listener — Enter submits through `dotNetRef.invokeMethodAsync(...)` with `preventDefault()`, Shift+Enter and Alt/Ctrl/Meta+Enter stay native, and an IME composition session NEVER submits (`event.isComposing`, or the legacy `keyCode === 229`). The IME guard has to live in JS because a net8 `KeyboardEventArgs` has no `IsComposing` (net9+ only — the C# fallback handlers guard it there under `#if NET9_0_OR_GREATER`); the C# `@onkeydown` handlers remain the fallback while the module is not attached (prerender / before interactivity, a failed import) and go quiet once it is, so Enter activates exactly once (the thread reply input and the message edit are attached the same way, routing to their own `[JSInvokable]` entry points `OnThreadComposerSubmit` / `OnEditComposerSubmit`). The module also exports `focus(el)` and `focusIfNeeded(el)` — the refocus helper that leaves an element already holding focus alone (no on-screen-keyboard close on touch) — and auto-resizes the textarea height up to `options.maxRows` (never beyond the CSS `max-height`, border-box aware; a guarded ResizeObserver re-measures when the container's width changes), re-measuring after a programmatic clear too. The send buttons and the built-in textareas carry `@onmousedown:preventDefault` (a tap must not steal focus or close the virtual keyboard) and `enterkeyhint="send"|"enter"` plus a visually-hidden submit hint (`TmChat_ComposerHint_EnterToSend` / `TmChat_ComposerHint_EnterNewLine`) merged into `aria-describedby` after `ComposerDescribedBy`. Two new parameters, both defaulting to today's behavior: `EnterToSend` (`bool`, default `true`) — `false` makes Enter a native new line in the composer, the thread reply and an open edit (only the send button or Ctrl/⌘+Enter submits); `RefocusAfterSend` (`bool`, default `true`) — after a SUCCESSFUL send the composer input is focused again (the built-in textarea, or the element a custom composer registered). New public API: `TmChat.FocusComposerAsync()` (public focus helper over the existing internal path) and `ChatComposerContext.AttachAsync(ElementReference)` — a custom composer (a `ComposerTemplate` with its own input, the BeautyFans `bindEnterSubmit` case) gets the SAME Enter/IME/auto-resize behavior and is the refocus target; call it from the host's `OnAfterRenderAsync` once the input has mounted, again when the element is replaced, with `default` to detach. **Upgrade note:** TmChat now loads the `_content/Tempo.Blazor/js/chat.js` ES module on its first render — bUnit hosts running in `JSRuntimeMode.Strict` must register it with `JSInterop.SetupModule("./_content/Tempo.Blazor/js/chat.js")` (Loose mode needs nothing). A send also no longer leaves the send button disabled when the host handler throws, and text typed while a send is in flight is kept (see **Changed**).
  ```razor
  <TmChat Messages="_messages" CurrentUser="_user" OnSend="HandleSend"
          EnterToSend="false"      @* Enter = new line; only the button sends *@
          RefocusAfterSend="true" />
  ```
  ```razor
  @* A custom composer with the same Enter/IME behavior and refocus *@
  <TmChat Messages="_messages" CurrentUser="_user" OnSend="HandleSend">
      <ComposerTemplate Context="composer">
          @{ _ctx = composer; }
          <textarea @ref="_input" value="@composer.Text"
                    @oninput="@(e => composer.SetTextAsync(e.Value?.ToString() ?? ""))"></textarea>
          <button @onclick="composer.SendAsync" disabled="@(!composer.CanSend)">Send</button>
      </ComposerTemplate>
  </TmChat>

  @code {
      private ChatComposerContext? _ctx;
      private ElementReference _input;
      private string? _attachedId;

      protected override async Task OnAfterRenderAsync(bool firstRender)
      {
          if (_ctx is not null && !string.IsNullOrEmpty(_input.Id) && _input.Id != _attachedId)
          {
              _attachedId = _input.Id; // re-attach when the element is replaced
              await _ctx.AttachAsync(_input);
          }
      }
  }
  ```

- **`TmChat` typing indicator: a host label, a host template, AT hiding and an expiry window.** Four new parameters, all defaulting to today's behaviour. `TypingLabel` (`Func<IReadOnlyList<ChatUser>, string>?`) replaces the localized "{0} is typing…" text with a host-computed label (the template wins when both are set: the label only changes the text span, the template the whole indicator). `TypingTemplate` (`RenderFragment<IReadOnlyList<ChatUser>>?`) replaces the WHOLE built-in `.tm-chat__typing-indicator` with host markup (the host's CSS scope applies — see `TmChatBubble` for a styled bubble) and receives the current `TypingUsers`; do NOT put `aria-live` or `role="status"` into the template — `TmChat` keeps one live region of its own and typing is never announced, an extra live region inside the template would only risk double announcements. `TypingAriaHidden` (`bool`, default `false`) renders `aria-hidden="true"` on the WHOLE indicator wrapper — not just the decorative dots — for hosts that convey typing through their own live region; typing is never announced by the component, and `TypingAriaHidden` applies ONLY to the built-in indicator (a `TypingTemplate` sets its own AT visibility). `TypingTimeout` (`TimeSpan?`, default `null`) auto-hides the indicator after a period of typing silence — the expiry applies to BOTH the built-in indicator and a `TypingTemplate` (an expired window renders NEITHER): the window is measured from the LAST CHANGE of `TypingUsers` (a new list instance, a different content OR an in-place mutation of the same list instance — detected against a stored content snapshot — opens a fresh window; an identical reference with unchanged content does not, so a host re-rendering with a rebuilt list on every render would extend the window forever — pass a stable reference and re-assign only on real typing signals). On expiry the indicator disappears but the host's `TypingUsers` list is never mutated; the next change reopens the window. A non-positive `TypingTimeout` (`TimeSpan.Zero` or negative) expires IMMEDIATELY — the indicator is suppressed from the next render and no timer is armed. The clock is the injected `TimeProvider` (fallback `TimeProvider.System`, so tests drive expiry with a `FakeTimeProvider`); the single-shot timer is cancelled in the new `TmChat.DisposeAsync()` (TmChat now implements `IAsyncDisposable` — additive), whose cleanup lives in a `protected virtual DisposeAsyncCore()` that SUBCLASSES OVERRIDE to add their own teardown. `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` now also stops the looping `tm-chat-typing` dots and the `tm-chat-blink` sending dots with `animation: none` (in `TmChat.razor.css` AND the `_chat.css` fallback, which also gained the previously missing `.tm-chat__sending-dots::after` base rule); the shared `animations.css` enumeration already capped their durations.
  ```razor
  <TmChat TypingUsers="_typingUsers"
          TypingLabel="@(users => $"{users[0].Name} píše…")"
          TypingTimeout="TimeSpan.FromSeconds(30)"
          TypingAriaHidden="true" />
  ```

- **`TmChat` custom message templates: `MessageTemplate` + `UseTemplateFor` and the host-owned `ChatMessage` fields (custom-templates phase 1; full contract in `docs/chat-custom-templates.md`).** `MessageTemplate` (`RenderFragment<ChatMessageContext>?`) replaces the built-in message row and `UseTemplateFor` (`Func<ChatMessage, bool>?`) keeps the override surgical. Precedence: with the template null every message renders the built-in row (today's behavior); with the template set and the predicate null the template renders for EVERY message (including the thread-panel messages); with both set the template renders only for messages the predicate accepts — `m => m.Kind == "ai-draft"` takes over exactly the special kinds while ordinary messages keep the default look. The per-message `ChatMessageContext` carries everything TmChat knows around the row: `Message` (the `ChatMessage` itself), `IsOwn`, `InThread`, `Index`, `IsFirstInGroup`, `DefaultContent` (the built-in row, so the template can fall back to the default look for ordinary kinds) and the typed accessors `PayloadAs<T>()` / `GetMetadata<T>(key, fallback)` (exact type or the fallback — no conversion is attempted). The three new host-owned `ChatMessage` fields feed it: `Kind` (a free-form string TmChat only mirrors onto the wrapper's `data-kind`), `Metadata` (an empty read-only dictionary by default, never null) and `Payload` (`[JsonIgnore]` — TmChat never serializes or logs it). TmChat keeps owning everything around the message: the wrapper element with `data-message-id`/`data-kind` (scroll anchors, read receipts), the thread filter, the draft guard and the read-receipt reporting are unaffected, and markup passed into the template carries the HOST's CSS scope (build custom rows from `TmChatBubble`, below). Additive; a host without a template renders exactly as before.
  ```razor
  <TmChat Messages="_messages" CurrentUser="_user" UseTemplateFor="@(m => m.Kind is not null)">
      <MessageTemplate Context="context">
          @if (context.Message.Kind == "ai-draft")
          {
              <TmChatBubble Variant="ChatBubbleVariant.Pending" StatusLabel="AI draft">
                  <Badge>@(context.GetMetadata<string>("reason", "AI suggestion"))</Badge>
                  <ChildContent>@context.Message.Text</ChildContent>
              </TmChatBubble>
          }
          else
          {
              @context.DefaultContent
          }
      </MessageTemplate>
  </TmChat>
  ```

- **`TmChatBubble` — presentation bubble for host-built chat templates, with variant styling through CSS custom properties.** A new `Chat` category component for markup passed into `TmChat.MessageTemplate` (which carries the HOST's CSS scope, so `TmChat.razor.css` cannot style it) and for any standalone bubble list. `ChatBubbleVariant` (its own file, `Components/Chat/ChatBubbleVariant.cs`) covers the shapes a moderated chat needs: `Incoming`, `Outgoing`, `System`, `Pill` (shares the `system` colours), `Pending` (dashed border), `Queued`, `Discarded` and `Locked`. Reserved semantics: `Discarded` renders its body as a semantic `<del>` element (strikethrough from HTML, not CSS), and `Locked` NEVER renders `ChildContent` — locked content cannot leak into the DOM even when the host passes it; the price goes through `Badge`, the hint through `Note`, the unlock button through `Actions`. The meta row renders `ActorLabel` and a machine-readable `<time datetime="…">` (UTC ISO-8601 attribute, local `HH:mm` text) separated by a middle dot (decorative, `aria-hidden`); the `Badge`, `Meta`, `Note` and `Actions` slots are rendered raw and host-owned — the component itself carries NO domain copy ("draft", "scheduled", a price, a discard reason all come from the host). Accessibility: the root carries `data-variant="{variant}"`, a new `StatusLabel` parameter renders a visually-hidden (`tm-sr-only`) status FIRST inside the bubble — the host MUST provide a visible `Badge` or a `StatusLabel` for Pending/Queued/Discarded/Locked — and `ShowVariantIcon` (default `true`) renders a decorative, `aria-hidden` `TmIcon` in the badge area (a `lock` for `Locked`, a `clock` for `Queued`). A bubble aligns itself in its row (`align-self`), shrinks to its content (`width: fit-content`, `min-width: 0`, capped by `--tm-chat-bubble-max-width` at 80 % by default; Outgoing/Pending/Queued/Discarded sit at the row end, System/Pill centre, the Pill wraps) and long words break with `overflow-wrap: anywhere`. Styling is driven by `--tm-chat-bubble-{in,out,system,pending,queued,discarded,locked}-{bg,fg,border}` plus `--tm-chat-bubble-radius`, `--tm-chat-bubble-max-width` and `--tm-chat-bubble-padding`. The library deliberately declares NO knob defaults (not on `.tm-chat`, not on `:root`): every `var()` carries its default as the FALLBACK, so an override on a wrapper, on `:root` or directly on a bubble always reaches the bubbles — and the same knobs style the built-in rows (`.tm-chat__message`/`.tm-chat__bubble`, with the variant border painted as a 1px inset `box-shadow` ring and the system row reading the `system` colours). The always-painted 1px border is compensated in the padding defaults (`calc(var(--tm-space-2-5) - var(--tm-border-width)) …`), the Pending border defaults to `--tm-border-color-strong` and the Discarded surface to `--tm-bg-muted` (visible in dark mode). Because every fallback references a semantic token and resolves on the element, dark mode works without `[data-theme="dark"]` overrides in the component stylesheet (which the strict CSS audit forbids); measured text contrast for all eight variants is ≥ 4.5:1 in both themes (lowest: outgoing light 5.17:1, outgoing dark 7.02:1). Because an undeclared knob is an undefined `--tm-*` for the strict audit (fallback or not), the 76 knob usages (59 file/token entries) are recorded as known, self-describing entries in `scripts/css-token-baseline.json` (4658 total, under the 5862 ceiling) instead of re-declaring the defaults anywhere. Additive; ships in `wwwroot/css/components/_chat.css` too.
  ```razor
  <TmChat Messages="_messages">
      <MessageTemplate Context="context">
          <TmChatBubble Variant="ChatBubbleVariant.Pending"
                        ActorLabel="@(context.Message.Author?.Name)"
                        Timestamp="context.Message.Timestamp">
              <Badge><span>AI draft</span></Badge>
              <ChildContent>@context.Message.Text</ChildContent>
              <Actions><button>Approve</button></Actions>
          </TmChatBubble>
      </MessageTemplate>
  </TmChat>
  ```

- **`TmChat` custom-templates demo and E2E coverage (FZE-9).** The `/chat` demo page
  (`Tempo.Blazor.Demo.SharedUI`) gained a **Custom Templates** section and a **Subscribe Gate**
  section exercising the whole host-owned contract end to end — AI draft / queued / discarded /
  locked / tip messages rendered through `TmChatBubble`, offline send queuing, a
  `ChatDemoQueuedCountdown` child and a composer fully replaced by `ComposerTemplate` that
  re-enables the chat through `ChatComposerContext.AttachAsync` (plus a standalone
  `TmChatBubble` alignment showcase). Covered by
  `tests/Tempo.Blazor.E2E/Chat/ChatCustomTemplatesE2ETests.cs` — 11 tests (2 Smoke: every kind
  renders + `DefaultContent`; Enter/Shift+Enter/IME), also covering bubble alignment, exactly one
  live region, tap-send focus, the jump-button scroll, load-older anchoring, the offline queue
  countdown, the approve/stop actions, reduced motion, dark tokens and the subscribe gate. The
  full custom-chat contract lives in `docs/chat-custom-templates.md`.

- **`TmScheduler` time grid: working hours, a current-time indicator, a work week and timeline lanes.** `ShowFullDay` (default `true`) keeps the full day; `false` renders only `WorkDayStart` to `WorkDayEnd` (default 08:00-17:00). Hours outside the working day are tinted only when `HighlightOffHours` (default `false`) is set, through `.tm-scheduler-timegrid-slot--offhours` and `.tm-scheduler-timeline-slot--offhours`. New tokens on `.tm-scheduler`: `--tm-scheduler-hour-height` (3rem), `--tm-scheduler-offhours-bg`, `--tm-scheduler-lane-height` (3.5rem) and `--tm-scheduler-timeline-hour-width` (5rem). `--tm-scheduler-visible-hours` is read-only and set by the component. The grid root publishes `data-range-start` and `data-range-minutes`, and the track height is `calc(var(--tm-scheduler-visible-hours, 24) * var(--tm-scheduler-hour-height))` instead of a fixed `72rem`, so a clipped range is exactly as tall as the hours it shows. `WeekDays` is `FullWeek` (default) or `WorkWeek` (five columns), and `MonthWeeks` is `Six` (default) or `Auto` (drops an empty trailing week, so June 2026 fits in 35 days). Both feed the same range the title and the data load use. A timeline row stacks overlapping events into lanes (`top` and `height` per event) and its resource column is sticky (`tm-scheduler-timeline-resource-label--sticky`). `ResourceHeaderTemplate` replaces the default resource header, which shows an initials avatar, the name and the `ResourceType`. `ScrollToTime` (`TimeSpan?`, default null) scrolls Day, Week and Timeline to that time after the first render through `TempoBlazor.Scheduler.scrollToTime`, using the same `data-range-minutes` the resize maths use; null does not scroll. `ShowEventResource` adds the resource name under a timed event. A Day view with resources hides the date header. New resource keys, all four languages: `TmScheduler_NowIndicator` ("Current time {0}"), `TmScheduler_Resources`.
  ```razor
  <TmScheduler WeekDays="TmSchedulerWeekDays.WorkWeek" ShowFullDay="false"
               WorkDayStart="@(new TimeOnly(8, 0))" WorkDayEnd="@(new TimeOnly(17, 0))" />
  ```

- **`TmScheduler` toolbar 2.0: an opt-in add button, a date popover, host slots and a selection state.** The add button (`data-testid="scheduler-add"`, plus icon, `TmScheduler_AddEvent`) renders only when `OnAddClick` has a delegate; there is no `ShowAddButton`. The title is the date popover's trigger (`role="button"`, `aria-haspopup="dialog"`, `aria-label` from `TmScheduler_GoToDateLabel` "{0}, go to date", so the name starts with the visible title). Picking a day raises `CurrentDateChanged` and navigates, and focus returns to the trigger. `Views` limits the switcher to the given views, in the given order; a `View` that is not offered is inserted at its canonical position so exactly one tab stays active. `HeaderStart` renders before navigation and `HeaderActions` after the view switcher, before the add button; an empty slot renders nothing. `ShowHeader` (default `true`) hides the toolbar row, which is the scheduler's header. `SelectedDate` and the new `SelectedEvent` / `SelectedEventChanged` are two-way: a day or slot click selects the day (`aria-selected` plus `tm-scheduler-month-day--selected` or `tm-scheduler-timegrid-col--selected`) without navigating and does not clear `SelectedEvent`. An event click selects the event, matched by `Id`, and marks it with `aria-current="true"` (it is a button, so `aria-selected` is not allowed, and `aria-pressed` would clash with the phase-8 `aria-expanded`). The view switcher is the core `TmTabs Variant="Pill"`; the scheduler body is the matching `role="tabpanel"`. New resource key, all four languages: `TmScheduler_GoToDateLabel`. `docs/segmented-control.md` keeps content switching on a tablist and a value change on `TmRadioGroup Appearance="Segmented"`.
- **`TmPopover` forwards dialog semantics.** New pass-through parameters `Role`, `TrapFocus` and `OnOpened` (forwarded to `TmOverlayPanel`), plus `TriggerAriaLabel` (the trigger's accessible name) and `FocusTriggerAsync()` which moves focus back to the trigger. A set `Role` also sets `aria-haspopup` on the trigger. All of them are additive; a popover that sets none of them renders as before.
- **`TmTabs.AriaLabel`, `TmTabPanel.TabAttributes` and `TmCalendarView.Today`.** `AriaLabel` names the tablist; null leaves it unnamed. `TabAttributes` splats onto that panel's tab button; null keeps the button byte-identical. `Today` marks the given day as today instead of the machine-local day, which a scheduler whose "today" is the user's zone needs.
- **`TmScheduler.HighlightWeekends` and `TmScheduler.AllDayEventStyle`.** Both are opt-in and default to the previous markup. `HighlightWeekends` (default `false`) adds `tm-scheduler-month-day--weekend` on a Saturday or Sunday month cell and `tm-scheduler-timegrid-col--weekend` on the matching day or week column; the wash is `--tm-scheduler-weekend-bg`. `AllDayEventStyle` is `Solid` (the default, the historical solid fill) or `Tinted`, which adds `tm-scheduler-event--tinted` and paints the shared tinted surface with `--tm-text-primary`, so the text stays at or above 4.5:1 on both themes. Today's time-grid column now carries `tm-scheduler-timegrid-col--today`, and a slot that does not start on the hour carries `tm-scheduler-timegrid-slot--half` (a dashed line). The day header is one culture-formatted line (`SchedulerRange.FormatColumnHeader` returns the weekday and the date: ("Tue", "5/12") in en-US, ("Út", "12.05") in cs-CZ), split into the existing weekday and date spans so a host selector still matches. Timed events share one surface, `.tm-scheduler-event-surface`, painted from `--tm-scheduler-event-tint` (14%), `--tm-scheduler-event-border-tint` (28%) and `--tm-scheduler-event-bar-width`.
- **`TmScheduler` agenda empty state.** An agenda range with no events now renders the shared `TmEmptyState` (calendar icon, `TmScheduler_AgendaEmptyTitle` "Nothing scheduled", `TmScheduler_AgendaEmptyDescription` "This range has no events.") inside the existing `.tm-scheduler-agenda-empty`. New resource keys, all four languages: `TmScheduler_AgendaEmptyTitle`, `TmScheduler_AgendaEmptyDescription`.
- **`TmSchedulerMonthView.CurrentDateChanged` and readable text on a light event colour.** PageUp/PageDown inside the month grid raise `CurrentDateChanged` with the target month's date; `TmScheduler` binds it to its own `CurrentDateChanged`, so a host that binds `@bind-CurrentDate` gets month paging from the keyboard. A host that renders `TmSchedulerMonthView` directly and ignores the callback keeps the current month, and the roving stop clamps to the nearest day the grid already shows. A consumer-supplied event colour keeps its solid fill. Before, white text was painted on every fill, which failed WCAG AA on the lighter colours (amber `#f59e0b` at 2.14:1, green `#10b981` at 2.53:1). Now the component sets `--event-text-color: var(--tm-scheduler-event-fg-on-light)` on that event when white text would fall below 4.5:1, so the text turns dark while the fill stays. The token is black in both themes: gray-900 flips to white in the dark theme, and a mid colour such as violet `#8b5cf6` clears 4.5:1 on black (4.96:1) but on neither white (4.23:1) nor `#111827` (4.19:1). A colour that clears white better than black keeps the theme's white text. A host that wants white text on its own light colour forces it back:
  ```css
  .tm-scheduler { --event-text-color: var(--tm-color-white); }
  ```
- **E-mail editor UX closing items (phase 8 of the follow-up plan).** The phone palette packs four tiles per row (three on a 320 px phone), so the
  whole first group clears the sheet's default snap in the demo at 390 px. The inline table grid shows a short decorative "Header" caption under each
  row switch and drops it through a named container query (`tm-email-table`, 24 rem) in a narrow inspector or sheet; the switch keeps its full
  `aria-label` (new resource key `EmailEditor_Table_RowHeaderShort`). The import dialog's structure preview is virtualized (`Virtualize`, fixed 28 px rows,
  `aria-level` / `aria-posinset` / `aria-setsize` per row, focusable scroll list) and lists EVERY block instead of stopping at 100; the state card counts are
  unchanged. Demo: the editor page ends above the fold at 1440x900 (its status bar and "Saved" badge are visible), the send page's form is
  `align-self: start`, and the editor page's chrome (switch-bar labels, select options, "Host: unsaved changes") comes from `DemoResources` in en/cs/sk/fr.
- **Wireframe stencils and roles for the e-mail components (decision EMAIL-WIREFRAME-ROLES).** `TmEmailTemplateEditor` (role `email-template-editor`),
  `TmEmailCanvasBlock` (role `email-block`), `TmEmailItemList` (`list-view`) and `TmEmailItemDialog` (`dialog`) are placeable stencils with a schema, a role and a
  declarative entry in the built-in pack; every other public e-mail component is editor chrome that resolves a role through the vocabulary by its type name.
- **`TmEmailVariablePicker.Filter` / `FilterChanged` (`@bind-Filter`) and an editor-owned inspector state.** The variable picker's search text is
  bindable; without a binding it behaves as before. `TmEmailPropertyPanel` takes the new optional `State` (`EmailInspectorState`, supplied by
  `TmEmailTemplateEditor`), which now also remembers the OPEN picker and its filter, so a desktop <-> tablet layout flip (which re-creates the
  inspector) no longer closes the picker and loses what was typed. The filter resets when the picker closes, not on a flip. The editor itself got no new
  parameter. Purely additive (decision EMAIL-VARIABLE-PICKER-FILTER).
- **`TmEmailTemplatePreview.DocumentRevision` (`long?`, optional).** A cheap change signature: when supplied, the preview decides whether to render
  again from the document reference and the revision, instead of serializing the whole document on every parent re-render. The editor passes its own
  revision; a host that does not supply it keeps the content comparison. Additive. Contract (decision EMAIL-PREVIEW-DOCUMENT-REVISION): the signature is
  (document reference, revision); an in-place edit that is not announced by a new revision is not a change, and an undo that restores earlier content
  still bumps the revision, so it costs one extra render of the same content.
- **Editor commit cost no longer grows with a serialize-per-edit.** `EditorHistoryService` stores immutable JSON snapshots with a monotonic
  `Version`; `IsDirty` is an integer version check with a string-compare fallback (no serialization per edit beyond the one history snapshot), and a commit is one
  serialization instead of a deep copy plus a second serialization (about 3x less model work at 3/52/200 blocks, measured in
  `planning/tm-email-template-editor-2.10.md`, 9.2). Behaviour is unchanged: undo onto the saved state is clean, an edit during an in-flight save stays
  dirty, a coalesced edit after a save is dirty. The snapshot no longer touches the live document (`EmailTemplateSerializer.SerializeContent` leaves out
  `UpdatedAt` itself). Measured keystroke latency on a 200-block document: in-process bUnit (Release) p95 44-61 ms for commit + render under a test
  renderer that repaints the whole tree; in the Blazor Server demo (browser `input` to the painted canvas block, 50 keystrokes) p50 8.5 ms, p95 13-22 ms
  on loopback, i.e. under the 100 ms target (new perf-lane spec `EmailEditorKeystrokePerformanceE2ETests`, bUnit `Category=Perf`; tables in the plan, 9.2).
- **`EmailTemplateSerializer.SerializeContent(EmailTemplateDocument)`.** `Serialize` without the `UpdatedAt` timestamp, without ever writing to the
  document. Additive.

- **Template sandbox audit trail (`Tempo.Blazor.EmailTemplates.Abstractions`).**
  `ITemplateSecurityAuditSink` + `TemplateSecurityEvent` (`Kind`, `Detail`, `TemplateHash`,
  `TemplateExcerpt`, `Timestamp`) report every refused sandbox operation:
  `BlockedMember`, `BlockedNamespace`, `BlockedFunction`, `BlockedUrlScheme`, `LimitExceeded`,
  `Timeout`. `BlockedUrlScheme` is emitted from the URL allow-list (B3); the enum value predates that
  pipeline so the audit contract stays stable. Register zero to many sinks in DI
  (`AddTempoEmailTemplateEngine` forwards all
  `IEnumerable<ITemplateSecurityAuditSink>`) or pass them to the `ScribanTemplateEngine`
  constructor. `Detail` names only the refused member/namespace/function — never a model value —
  `TemplateHash` is lowercase hexadecimal SHA-256 of the template, `TemplateExcerpt` is its first
  200 characters (may contain authored PII, so apply your own retention) and `Timestamp` comes from
  `TimeProvider`. Audit never breaks a render: a sink that throws is logged and swallowed.

  ```csharp
  sealed class SecurityLog(ILogger<SecurityLog> logger) : ITemplateSecurityAuditSink
  {
      public void OnEvent(TemplateSecurityEvent e) =>
          logger.LogWarning("template {Hash}: {Kind} {Detail}", e.TemplateHash, e.Kind, e.Detail);
  }

  services.AddSingleton<ITemplateSecurityAuditSink, SecurityLog>();
  services.AddTempoEmailTemplateEngine();   // picks every registered sink up automatically
  ```

- **`TemplateSecurityOptions` hardening limits.** `RegexTimeOut` (default 1 s, protects the `regex`
  filters against catastrophic backtracking), `ObjectRecursionLimit` (default 20, depth of the
  object→text conversion) and `LimitToString` (default 1,048,576 chars, single string conversion)
  join the existing `LoopLimit`, `RecursiveLimit`, `MaxOutputLength` and `Timeout`. Every limit is
  validated at engine construction and at `AddTempoEmailTemplateEngine`, so a zero/negative value
  (which Scriban would read as "unlimited") throws `ArgumentOutOfRangeException` instead of silently
  disabling a guard.

  ```csharp
  services.AddTempoEmailTemplateEngine(o => o.RegexTimeOut = TimeSpan.FromMilliseconds(200));
  ```

- **Dependency bumps.** `Scriban` 7.2.4 → 7.5.1 (sandbox `MemberFilter`, `RegexTimeOut`,
