  `ObjectRecursionLimit`, `LimitToString`), `Mjml.Net` 4.11.0 → 4.15.0, `AngleSharp` 1.5.2 → 1.8.5
  (the HTML sanitizer parses untrusted markup, so it stays on the newest parser). The MJML golden
  documents are byte-identical after the bump. The test projects that pin AngleSharp transitively
  (bunit) moved to the same 1.8.5.

  Note on the `AngleSharp` bump: the previously pinned `1.5.2` was **not** affected by
  [GHSA-pgww-w46g-26qg](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-pgww-w46g-26qg) (CVE-2026-54570, an mXSS
  via `annotation-xml` integration points) — that advisory covers all versions before `1.5.0`. The
  `NU1902` warnings the pins actually silenced came from `bunit` 2.7.2 pulling `AngleSharp` `1.4.0`
  into the UI test projects. `1.8.5` is simply the newest stable parser line for the sanitizer.

- **HTML escaping of variable values + safe URLs (`Tempo.Blazor.EmailTemplates.Abstractions`).** The
  output of every expression in the HTML/MJML body is HTML-encoded, so a value can never inject a tag,
  an attribute or a script. The subject, preheader and plain-text version stay raw (they are text), the
  literal template text is untouched and filters still see the raw value (`{{ name | string.size }}`
  measures the data, not the entities). The single opt-out is the new filter
  **`{{ value | html.trusted }}`**, whose output is always run through the HTML sanitizer first, so the
  tag/attribute allow-list keeps applying. `html.escape` now returns already-encoded markup and is
  therefore never encoded twice. See [docs/email-templates/TEMPLATE_SYNTAX.md](docs/email-templates/TEMPLATE_SYNTAX.md).

  ```csharp
  var result = await renderer.RenderAsync(document, new { name = "<script>alert(1)</script>" });
  // result.Html      → …&lt;script&gt;alert(1)&lt;/script&gt;…
  // result.TextVersion → <script>alert(1)</script>   (plain text pass is not escaped)
  ```

- **URL scheme allow-list.** Every URL is checked **after substitution**, both in the substituted MJML
  (before compilation, so a refused `background-url` never reaches the CSS/VML the compiler emits) and
  in the compiled HTML (covers raw blocks and host-set HTML attributes). `http`, `https`, `mailto`,
  `tel`, relative paths and `#fragment` pass; anything else — including `data:`, `vbscript:`, `file:`,
  `blob:` and unknown schemes, and obfuscations such as `java\tscript:` — is replaced with `#`, reported
  as a `RenderErrorSeverity.Warning` (`RenderResult.Success` stays `true`, `RenderResult.HasWarnings`
  turns `true`) and audited as `TemplateSecurityEventKind.BlockedUrlScheme`. The allow-list is a fixed
  security rule; a host cannot extend it. `HtmlContentSanitizer` now uses the same
  `UrlSchemePolicy` (so `tel:` links in rich text are kept, and character-smuggled schemes are refused).

  ```csharp
  var result = await renderer.RenderAsync(document, new { url = "javascript:alert(1)" });
  // result.Html    → <a href="#" …>
  // result.Errors  → [ RenderError { Key = RenderKeys.BlockedUrlScheme, … } ]
  ```

- **The markup guard is a linear tokenizer, and unchecked markup is never returned.** The tag scan is now
  a single-pass WHATWG-style tokenizer (`HtmlTagTokenizer`) instead of a backtracking regular expression:
  a document made of unterminated tags used to cost minutes (10 KB ≈ 2.4 s, 40 KB ≈ 36 s — quadratic),
  it is now linear (1 MB in well under a second). Every remaining regular expression inside the guard
  carries a 2 s match budget; a guard that cannot finish produces `RenderKeys.MarkupTooComplex`
  (`render.markup.too_complex`, `RenderErrorSeverity.Error`) and an empty `RenderResult.Html`.
  **Behaviour change:** `RenderResult.Html` is now `""` whenever an `Error`-severity diagnostic comes out
  of the compile or markup phase (a broken MJML structure, an unchecked body) — a host never receives a
  half-built or unchecked body. Warnings keep the complete HTML.

- **The markup tokenizer never skips content a browser may parse as tags.** Abruptly closed comments
  (`<!-->`, `<!--->`, `--!>`) and raw-text elements inside foreign content (`<svg><style>`,
  `<svg><title>`) are classic mutation-XSS vectors: the guard now scans comment payloads and the content
  of `style`/`script`/`textarea`/`title` for start tags instead of trusting the browser's raw-text state,
  while a `<!`/`<?`/`</` construct is skipped only to its first `>`. Outlook conditional comments
  (`<!--[if mso]>…<![endif]-->`) and their VML payload are scanned the same way — a legitimate
  `background-url` is untouched, so the compiled output does not change.

- **The markup guard drops markup that can rewrite a link at runtime.** SVG animation elements
  (`set`, `animate`, `animateMotion`, `animateTransform`, `discard`) and every
  `<meta http-equiv="refresh">` are removed with a warning (`RenderKeys.UnsafeElementRemoved` =
  `render.markup.unsafe_element_removed`, audited as `BlockedMember`) — a browser would run their
  `href`/`to`/`from`/`by` values after the static check. CSS is validated on a normalised copy
  (comments removed, `:`-style escapes decoded), `image-set(…)` and `@import` targets are checked like
  `url(…)`, and a stylesheet that still embeds a refused target is dropped. The tokenizer also removes the
  legacy false positives: `<img alt="a onerror=b">` and `title="href=javascript:x"` are left untouched,
  `data-onclick` survives.

- **`RenderError.Severity` (Error / Warning).** A security clean-up is a warning, not a failure:
  `RenderError` gained `RenderErrorSeverity Severity` (last optional parameter, default
  `RenderErrorSeverity.Error`), `RenderResult.Success` now means "no *error*" (`Errors.All(e => e.Severity
  != Error)`), and `RenderResult.HasWarnings` reports warnings. A blocked URL and a removed event handler
  are warnings — the HTML is complete and `Success` stays `true`, so `POST /api/email-templates/{id}/send`
  no longer answers `422` for a message that only had a link replaced with `#`; `TmEmailTemplatePreview`
  lists errors and warnings separately. Decision `EMAIL-RENDER-ERROR-SEVERITY` (D23).

- **Event-handler attributes are removed from rendered markup.** Escaping alone cannot neutralise
  `<div onclick="f('{{ x }}')">`: the browser entity-decodes the attribute value *before* it runs it as
  script. The markup guard now drops every `on*` attribute and `srcdoc` from raw markup (MJML and HTML
  pass), reports a warning (`RenderKeys.EventHandlerRemoved` = `render.markup.event_handler_removed`) and
  audits `BlockedMember` with the attribute name. `html.trusted` markup is serialized with a quote-safe
  formatter, so a value inside an attribute cannot close it — `html.trusted` belongs in element content,
  not in an attribute.

- **The URL guard also covers `srcset`, `ping`, `data`, `lowsrc`, `dynsrc`, `meta http-equiv="refresh"`
  and CSS `url(…)` inside `<style>`** (including `EmailStyle.Css`). Character references of any form
  (`&#58`, `&#0000000058;`, `&#x6A`, `&colon;`) are decoded before the scheme is judged, and a
  protocol-relative / UNC reference (`//host`, `\\host\share`, `/\host`) is refused as
  `network-path` — a "relative" link must not resolve a remote authority (SMB leak).

- **`RenderError.Key`.** A render diagnostic can now name a localization key
  (`RenderKeys.BlockedUrlScheme` = `render.url.blocked_scheme`) so a host — and
  `TmEmailTemplatePreview`, which resolves it through `ITmEmailLocalizer` — can present a localized
  message. Diagnostics that come straight from the MJML compiler keep `Key = null`.

- **`TemplateRenderOptions`.** Per-render options type threaded through
  `ITemplateEngine.Render(…, TemplateRenderOptions?)` and
  `IEmailTemplateRenderer.RenderAsync(…, TemplateRenderOptions?, CancellationToken)`. It is the
  extension point for render-scoped configuration (the culture of formatters); it deliberately has no
  escaping switch, and the renderer chooses the escaping mode per pass.

- **Audit sinks cover the URL allow-list.** `EmailTemplateRenderer` takes optional
  `IEnumerable<ITemplateSecurityAuditSink>`, `TimeProvider` and `ILogger<EmailTemplateRenderer>`
  parameters (all appended, source compatible); `AddTempoEmailTemplateEngine` forwards every registered
  sink, so `BlockedUrlScheme` events need no extra wiring. The audit detail is the scheme name only —
  never the URL.

- **Formatter culture per render (`TemplateRenderOptions.Culture`).** `TemplateRenderOptions` gained
  `CultureInfo? Culture` and `bool UseDocumentLanguageCulture`. A render now always uses an explicit
  culture: the one the host passes, else the culture of `EmailTemplateDocument.Language` when
  `UseDocumentLanguageCulture` is set, else `CultureInfo.InvariantCulture`. The renderer resolves it
  **once** and applies it to every pass (subject, preheader, body, text version), so
  `{{ price | math.format "N2" }}` renders `1 234,50` for `cs-CZ` and `{{ price }}` follows the same
  rule. An explicit `Culture` wins over the document language; an unknown document language falls back
  to the invariant culture instead of failing the render. The invariant default keeps output
  deterministic — a Czech server and an English server produce the same bytes unless the host asks
  otherwise.

  ```csharp
  await renderer.RenderAsync(document, model, new TemplateRenderOptions { Culture = new CultureInfo("cs-CZ") });
  // or: new TemplateRenderOptions { UseDocumentLanguageCulture = true }   → document.Language decides
  ```

- **Host function registry (`ITemplateFunctionProvider`).** An application can add its own template
  filters — a currency formatter, a product-name helper — without forking the engine. A provider
  exposes one namespace plus a dictionary of synchronous delegates, and the engine registers them as
  `{{ value | app.format_currency }}`. Registration is validated when `ITemplateEngine` is resolved:
  namespace `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$`, never a Scriban builtin namespace (`string`, `array`, `object`,
  `math`, `date`, `html`, `regex`, `timespan`, …), never a namespace another provider already owns,
  function names `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$`, synchronous delegates only and contract-typed parameters/return
  values (`string`, `bool`, numeric, `decimal`, `DateTime`, `DateTimeOffset`,
  `IEnumerable<T>` of those) — everything else throws `ArgumentException` at startup. A function's
  arguments run under the same member filter and limits as any other expression, its result is
  re-checked on every call (`Type`, delegates, forbidden namespaces and the internal
  `TrustedHtml`/`EscapedHtml` markers fail the render closed) and it is HTML-escaped exactly like any
  other expression output. Provider namespaces are also added to
  `TemplateSecurityOptions.FunctionNamespaces` (deep-copied by `Clone`), so a host-side template
  validator can tell a host function namespace from a data path.

  ```csharp
  services.AddSingleton<ITemplateFunctionProvider, CurrencyFunctions>();   // Namespace = "app"
  services.AddTempoEmailTemplateEngine();                                  // → {{ total | app.format_currency }}
  ```

  A provider must be a **singleton** (the registry snapshots it once; a scoped/transient registration is
  refused with `InvalidOperationException`), its namespace must not be a Scriban keyword (`for`, `this`,
  `if`, `end`, `null`, `…`), an enumerable result is materialized into a script array of scalars (so a host
  type that happens to be enumerable cannot be read through the template, and the enumeration is bounded by
  `LoopLimit`), and an exception thrown by a delegate is logged and surfaced as
  `Template function 'app.x' failed.` — never with the host exception's message (it could carry a path, a
  connection string or a value).

- **`EmailTemplateDocument.SchemaVersion` + `EmailTemplateSerializer.ReadSchemaVersion`.** The persisted
  document carries a schema version (`public static int CurrentSchemaVersion => 1`, a property, not a
  `const`). `Serialize` always stamps the current version, `Deserialize` migrates an older document to
  it (a document without the property is version 1) and a document written by a **newer** schema
  throws `EmailTemplateSerializationException` with `Key = SerializationKeys.UnsupportedSchemaVersion`
  instead of being silently mis-read. `ReadSchemaVersion(json)` reads just the header, which is what a
  host needs to decide about a migration or to show a friendly error. A non-numeric version is
  `SerializationKeys.InvalidSchemaVersion`.

- **Import limits (`EmailImportOptions`) and the reusable `EmailDocumentLimitsValidator`.** The MJML
  importer and the JSON deserializer now bound their input: `MaxInputBytes` (default **5 MB**, measured
  as a UTF-8 byte count — today's hard-coded behaviour, so this is additive, B14),
  `MaxSections` (200), `MaxBlocks` (2000) and `MaxNestingDepth` (8). Exceeding a limit is a **fatal**
  `ImportMessage` with a localization key (`import.input_too_large`,
  `validation.limits.sections|blocks|nesting`) and `ImportResult.Document` is `null` — never an
  exception. `Deserialize(json, EmailImportOptions)` applies `MaxNestingDepth` as a JSON-parser depth
  bound (a per-call copy of `Options`, the static instance stays untouched); the bound is derived from
  the model nesting depth (a block nesting level costs several JSON levels), so a document within the
  model limit always parses and a hostile payload still cannot nest without bound. The same limits are
  available server-side through `EmailDocumentLimitsValidator` before a document is saved.

  ```csharp
  var options = new EmailImportOptions { MaxInputBytes = 10 * 1024 * 1024 };
  var result = new MjmlImporter().Import(mjml, includeResolver: null, options: options);
  var violations = new EmailDocumentLimitsValidator(options).Validate(document);   // [] when it fits
  ```

- **New public `Tempo.Blazor.EmailTemplates.Abstractions.Localization.JsonStringLocalizer<T>`.** The
  core's JSON localizer lives in `Tempo.Blazor` and is `internal`, and this Abstractions package must not
  reference the Blazor package, so the implementation is published here for the email packages (and for a
  host that wants the same behaviour for its own marker type). It is `sealed` — compose it, do not derive.
  Register the resource type as a **closed** generic so it wins over an open-generic `IStringLocalizer<>`:

  ```csharp
  services.TryAddSingleton<IStringLocalizer<TmEmailResources>,
      JsonStringLocalizer<TmEmailResources>>();
  ```

- **New package `Tempo.Blazor.EmailTemplates.Engine` — the local render engine, split out of
  Abstractions (B7, decision `EMAIL-ENGINE-PACKAGE-SPLIT`).** `Tempo.Blazor.EmailTemplates.Abstractions`
  no longer carries `Scriban`, `Mjml.Net` or `AngleSharp`: the sandboxed Scriban engine, the Mjml.Net
  compiler, the AngleSharp HTML sanitizer, the render pipeline and the local preview renderer live in the
  new package, whose public types **keep their `…Abstractions.*` namespaces** (D21) — adding it is a
  `PackageReference` plus one call, never a `using` rewrite. The editor
  (`Tempo.Blazor.EmailTemplates`) references no engine at all and runs in Blazor WebAssembly.

  ```csharp
  // server (or any process that renders locally)
  builder.Services
      .AddTempoEmailTemplateEditor()    // UI + model: registry, generators, validators, import
      .AddTempoEmailTemplateEngine();   // Scriban + Mjml.Net + AngleSharp, local preview renderer

  // Blazor WebAssembly: the editor only, preview rendered by the host's server
  builder.Services.AddTempoEmailTemplateEditor();
  builder.Services.AddScoped<IEmailPreviewRenderer, MyApiPreviewRenderer>();
  ```

  Registrations are split and **order-independent**: `AddTempoEmailTemplateModel()` (Abstractions) installs
  the baseline with `TryAdd` — the BCL `ConservativeHtmlContentSanitizer`,
  `RegexTemplateVariableExtractor`, one shared `TemplateSecurityOptions` instance, the request validators
  with their closed JSON localizer and `MjmlGenerator` — and `AddTempoEmailTemplateEngine()` **replaces**
  the engine services (`AngleSharpHtmlContentSanitizer`, `ScribanTemplateVariableExtractor`,
  `ScribanTemplateValidator`, `MjmlNetCompiler`, `EmailTemplateRenderer`, `LocalEmailPreviewRenderer`).
  `AddTempoEmailTemplateEditor()` registers UI + model only, and `AddTempoEmailTemplates()` is the
  `[Obsolete]` shortcut that delegates to it. A CI-guarded test (`PackageBoundaryTests`) fails if
  Abstractions ever references Scriban/Mjml.Net/AngleSharp again, if the editor package references the
  engine, or if the engine's exact `[$(Version)]` pin on Abstractions drifts.

- **Replaceable preview renderer `IEmailPreviewRenderer` + `EmailPreviewRequest` / `EmailPreviewResult` /
  `EmailPreviewStatus` (`Tempo.Blazor.EmailTemplates.Abstractions.Rendering`, contract §3.4).** The editor
  gets its preview and HTML export through one seam, so the render may run on the server:

  ```csharp
  public interface IEmailPreviewRenderer
  {
      Task<EmailPreviewResult> RenderAsync(EmailPreviewRequest request, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default);
  }

  var request = new EmailPreviewRequest
  {
      Document = document,                 // travels as EmailTemplateSerializer JSON
      VariablesJson = sampleDataJson,
      SubstituteVariables = false,         // false keeps the {{ }} tokens (HTML export)
      CultureName = "cs-CZ",
  };
  ```

  `EmailPreviewResult` never returns `null` strings: a render error is `RenderFailed` with empty
  html/text/subject, a template *warning* (blocked URL, removed event handler) keeps `Rendered` with the
  complete HTML (D23), and a missing registration, a network error or a server failure is `Unavailable`
  with a retry. `LocalEmailPreviewRenderer` (Engine) is the default; a host that renders elsewhere
  registers its own. The preview cancels the previous render whenever a new one starts, so a stale answer
  can never overwrite a newer one, and the HTML is untrusted even when the host's own server produced it —
  it only ever lands in a `<iframe sandbox="" srcdoc>` (no `allow-scripts`, no `allow-same-origin`).

- **`TmEmailTemplatePreview` redesign: device switch, substitution switch, sample-data editor and host
  actions.** The toolbar is now three pill tab strips (Desktop / Tablet / Mobile with `monitor`, `tablet`
  and `smartphone` icons; "With sample data" / "Without substitution"; HTML / plain text) plus a
  "Refresh preview" action. The scene shows the email as paper on `--tm-color-surface-secondary` with
  `--tm-shadow-md`, centred, at the document's own content width (Desktop), 768 px (Tablet) or 390 px
  (Mobile) — the widths live in `EmailPreviewMetrics`. The sample-data editor uses `TmCodeEditor`
  (`Language="json"`, `ValidateJson`) and sits behind an "Edit data" button instead of a `<details>`
  element. New parameters: `VariablesJsonChanged`, `InitialDevice` (`EmailPreviewDevice`),
  `ShowSampleDataEditor`, `ShowViewToggle`, `FooterActions`, `CultureName`.

- **`ITemplateValidator` + `ITemplateVariableExtractor` (+ their Engine implementations).** The editor's
  validation panel no longer needs `ITemplateEngine`: it takes `ITemplateValidator` and, with no validator
  registered, shows a localized explanation that names the missing registration
  ("register `ITemplateValidator`, e.g. `Tempo.Blazor.EmailTemplates.Engine`") while the structural
  findings keep working. The variable picker and sample data fall back to
  `RegexTemplateVariableExtractor` (pure BCL) and are replaced by `ScribanTemplateVariableExtractor` when
  the engine is registered. `EmailDocumentVariableExtractor.Extract(document, ITemplateVariableExtractor)`
  is the new overload; the existing `Extract(document)` keeps the baseline behaviour.

- **Editor save contract: the host reports the outcome, the editor owns `IsDirty`/`IsSaving` (§3.2,
  D1/D2/D16).** `TmEmailTemplateEditor` asks the host through `OnSave` with an `EmailSaveRequest`
  (deep-copy `Document` snapshot, `Trigger` = `Manual` | `Shortcut` | `AutoSave` | `Programmatic`, the
  editor `Revision` the snapshot was taken at, and a `CancellationToken` cancelled when the editor is
  disposed) and shows **exactly** what the host answered: `EmailSaveResult.Saved()` clears the dirty flag
  and the badge says "Saved <relative time>", `Failed(message)` keeps the document dirty and shows the
  host's reason, `Conflict(message)` does the same **and pauses auto-save** until a successful
  **non-auto-save** save (`Manual`, `Shortcut` or `Programmatic` — `Ctrl/⌘+S` lifts the pause too) or a
  fresh `Document` instance. An exception from the handler is a failed save
  plus a log entry — never a crash and never "Saved". `IsDirty`/`IsDirtyChanged` (only fires on a
  transition), `IsSaving`, and the public `SaveAsync()` (wire it into
  `TmNavigationGuard.OnSaveAndLeave`) complete the host surface. Saving is **single-flight**: at most one
  host request runs, the Save button stays focusable (it announces `aria-disabled` instead of a native
  `disabled`, which would drop a keyboard user's focus; the click is merged), and a trigger accepted
  mid-flight merges into exactly one follow-up save (only while the document is still dirty) whose result
  answers the merged caller. An outcome that arrives after the host replaced `Document` answers only its
  caller — it never clears the new document's dirty flag or repaints its badge.

  ```razor
  <TmEmailTemplateEditor @ref="_editor" @bind-Document="_document" OnSave="SaveAsync"
                         IsDirtyChanged="d => _dirty = d" />

  @* the host mirrors IsDirtyChanged; reading _editor.IsDirty in markup would be stale at guard time *@
  <TmNavigationGuard IsDirty="_dirty"
                     OnSaveAndLeave="@(async () => _editor is not null && (await _editor.SaveAsync()).IsSaved)" />

  @code {
      async Task<EmailSaveResult> SaveAsync(EmailSaveRequest request)
      {
          try
          {
              // a 409 means a newer revision exists — the host owns the ETag/revision
              await Api.SaveAsync(request.Document, request.Revision, request.CancellationToken);
              return EmailSaveResult.Saved();
          }
          catch (HttpRequestException ex) when (ex.StatusCode == HttpStatusCode.Conflict)
          {
              return EmailSaveResult.Conflict("Someone else saved a newer revision.");
          }
          catch (Exception ex)
          {
              return EmailSaveResult.Failed(ex.Message);
          }
      }
  }
  ```

- **Save-status badge, grouped command bar, host toolbar slots and `ReadOnly` (`TmEmailTemplateEditor`).**
  `ShowSaveStatus` (default `true`) renders a badge with an icon for "Unsaved changes", "Saving…",
  "Saved <relative time>" (refreshed every minute from `TimeProvider`, the phrase from the core
  `ITmRelativeTimeFormatter`, so the plural form is the language's own), "Save failed" and
  "Version conflict" (the last two coloured through the status tokens and told apart from "Unsaved
  changes" by a stronger border and an alert-triangle icon), coloured through the status tokens.
  `ShowSaveButton` (default `true`) switches the Save button off, `ToolbarStart`
  and `ToolbarEnd` are `RenderFragment` slots for the host's own actions (back, title, "Send test email"),
  and the bar itself is grouped by task — History (Undo/Redo, which spell their labels out at a container
  width ≥ 1200 px and stay icon + `aria-label` below that) | Review (Preview, Validate) | File (Import,
  Export) | Help; every action carries `aria-keyshortcuts` and a `title`.
  A failed or conflicted save also renders a full-width `TmAlert` under the command bar
  (`[data-tm-save-alert]`, `role="alert"`) with the host's complete message, a localized hint and a
  "Try again" action (`[data-tm-save-retry]`, a `Manual` save) — the pill badge stays short and truncates
  with its text in `title`; the badge itself is **no longer a live region**: one visually hidden
  `role="status"`/`aria-live="polite"` announcer (`[data-tm-save-announcer]`) speaks a confirmed
  manual/shortcut/programmatic save and stays silent for auto-save, "Saving…" and the minute tick
  (Failed/Conflict are announced by the alert, so nothing is announced twice).
  `ReadOnly` disables **every** editing path — the toolbox tiles, canvas drag & drop and
  inline block/section actions, the inspector's controls (a native `disabled` fieldset **and** a per-method
  `if (ReadOnly) return;` in every sub-editor, because a disabled control still delivers a synthesised
  change), import, undo/redo and the document-mutating shortcuts — while preview, validation and export
  keep working; the save chrome is replaced by a read-only badge with a lock icon
  (`[data-tm-readonly-badge]`), no Save button is rendered and unsaved changes stay as secondary text.
  `SaveAsync()` answers `Failed` without calling the host. The component never changes the flag itself, and
  `Ctrl+S` / `Cmd+S` save through `OnSave` with `Trigger = Shortcut` (the browser's own "save page" default
  is cancelled for that chord only, by the package's `tm-email-save-shortcut.js` module, which guards each
  editor element separately so two editors on one page do not disarm each other). New keys in all
  four tables (`TmEmailResources{,.cs,.sk,.fr}.json`): the five save states, the retry action, the
  conflict/failure hints, the read-only badge, the save tooltip, the shortcut categories and the
  image-upload errors (`EmailEditor_Relative_*` was removed — the core formatter supplies the phrase).

- **`ImageUploadOptions` — client-side limits checked before the host's upload handler
  (`TmEmailTemplateEditor.ImageUpload`, `TmEmailPropertyPanel.ImageUpload`).** `Accept` (the `accept`
  attribute syntax, default `image/*`) and `MaxBytes` (default 5 MB) are validated **before**
  `OnImageUpload` runs; a rejected file, a handler exception and an empty URL all produce a localized error
  in the panel and leave the block's `Src` untouched.

- **Inspector metadata types (additive).** `PropertyFieldPlacement`
  (`Content`/`Style`/`Padding`/`Advanced`: which tab and which collapsible group a field belongs to),
  `PropertyChoice` (`Value` + `LabelKey` of one `Choice`/`Alignment` option), and `EmailInspectorState`
  (the state one editor remembers: the folded groups **per block type** plus `LastFocusedField`, the target
  of the caret-less variable insertion). `PropertyFieldKind` gained `Color`, `Alignment`, `Choice` and
  `Length`; `PropertyField` gained `Owner`, `Placement`, `Choices`, `SupportsTemplate`, `LabelKey`
  (`EmailEditor_Field_{Owner}_{Property}`), `SharedLabelKey` (`EmailEditor_Field_{Property}`),
  `IsNullable()` (the nullable annotation decides whether an empty value means "unset"),
  `AllowsNegative` (only letter spacing) and `SetChoice`/`TryGetLength`/`SetLength`; the alias `GetChoice`
  and the static `PropertyReflection.IsRequiredLength` were removed while the API is still unreleased —
  ask the field instead of a helper (contract §3.10). `PropertyReflection` gained
  `GetFields(target, placement)`, `OwnerOf`, `TryParseLength`, `FormatLength` and `IsValidColor`.
  `EmailInspectorState` is public because it is the type of a parameter of the public
  `TmEmailObjectFields`, not because a host is expected to build one — a standalone instance keeps its
  own state, so existing markup needs no change.
  Also additive: `LayoutSeverityRank.Of` (the one sanctioned display order of `LayoutSeverity`),
  `EmailDocumentValidator.MaxPreheaderLength` and `DocumentValidationKeys.PreheaderTooLong` (the threshold
  the recommending rule measures and names), `TmEmailTemplateToolbox.Collapsed`/`CollapsedChanged`/
  `ShowCollapseToggle`, and `TmEmailPropertyPanel.OnDuplicate`/`OnDelete`. Nothing on the document model or
  the save contract changed.

- **`TmEditorShell.MobileActionsMaxVisible` (jádro, aditivní).** How many of the shell's
  `MobileActions` stay on the mobile action bar before the rest overflow into the bar's own "More"
  menu. Default `3` — the bar's own default — so a host that never sets it keeps exactly the
  earlier behaviour; a value below `1` is rejected with `ArgumentOutOfRangeException` (a bar with
  no action would be an unreachable set of commands). The email template editor sets it to `4` so
  its D20 actions (Zpět / Znovu / Náhled / Validovat) sit on the bar instead of behind "More".

- **Dialog item editing + table-cell link/background (`Tempo.Blazor.EmailTemplates`).**
  `EmailItemEditingMode { Inline, Dialog }` and `[Parameter] ItemEditingMode` on
  `TmEmailTemplateEditor` and `TmEmailPropertyPanel` (default `Inline` = the 2.9.x behaviour). In
  `Dialog`, the social / navbar / carousel / accordion block renders a compact list
  (`TmEmailItemList`: preview + move up / move down / edit / remove) and Edit opens
  `TmEmailItemDialog` over a **copy** of the item: Save applies it as one change (one undo step),
  Cancel / Escape / an overlay click change nothing, and the core `TmModal` (a full-height bottom
  sheet with the sticky footer on a phone) restores focus to the opening button. The dialog
  validates through `Tempo.Blazor.FluentValidation` with the editor's own localizer
  (`EmailSocialElementValidator`, `EmailNavbarLinkValidator`, `EmailCarouselImageValidator`,
  `EmailAccordionItemValidator`, `EmailTableCellValidator`): a blocked URL scheme, a missing required
  text/source/alt/title, an unparsable span or a colour outside the allow-list is reported **at the
  field** (`aria-invalid` + `aria-describedby`, no pre-flagging of an untouched form) and Save — which
  is always enabled — applies nothing and moves the focus to the first invalid field; only failures
  without a field reach the dialog's `role="alert"` summary. A new item is a copy too: Add opens the
  dialog and the item is inserted only on Save, so Cancel leaves the document and the undo history
  alone. The list names its item in every row action, announces a removal in a live region and shows an
  empty state. The accordion content and a text block's content are sanitized with the pipeline's own
  `IHtmlContentSanitizer` **before** the rich editor hands them to `innerHTML` (fail-closed: with no
  sanitizer the editor receives nothing, never the raw markup).

- **`EmailTableCell.Href` + `EmailTableCell.BackgroundColor` and the policies behind them
  (`Tempo.Blazor.EmailTemplates.Abstractions`, additive — `SchemaVersion` stays `1`).**
  `Href` is emitted as `<a href>` around the cell text, `BackgroundColor` as the `bgcolor`
  attribute. Both follow the same URL rules (B3): `EmailUrlPolicy` (the public view of the one URL
  allow-list — `http`/`https`/`mailto`/`tel`, a relative path without an authority, `#`; anything
  else becomes `#` with a `render.url.blocked_scheme` warning and a `BlockedUrlScheme` audit event)
  and `EmailColorPolicy` (`#rgb`, `#rrggbb`, or a named colour from a fixed safe set — an invalid
  value is **never written**, the attribute is omitted and the render reports
  `RenderKeys.InvalidTableCellColor`, a warning). `MjmlGenerator.Generate(document, options,
  diagnostics)` is the new additive overload that collects those warnings; `MjmlImporter` reads the
  anchor and `bgcolor` back and `TextVersionGenerator` writes a linked cell as `text (url)`. The
  generator replaces a blocked cell link with `#` on its own, so the MJML export that runs **without**
  the Engine package (WASM) cannot hand out a live `javascript:`/`data:` link either. On import a cell
  whose `<a>` is not its whole content keeps its full text and no link, an invalid `bgcolor` is dropped
  and a blocked link is kept for editing — both reported as `ImportKeys.InvalidTableColor` /
  `ImportKeys.BlockedTableLink` warnings. Colours of MJML **attributes** (navbar link, accordion
  item/title, social element) follow the inspector's `PropertyReflection.IsValidColor` (hex, `rgb()`/
  `hsl()`, keyword); `EmailColorPolicy` stays the narrower allow-list of the cell `bgcolor`, and
  `TextVersionGenerator` never prints a blocked link.

- **Import dialog rebuilt (`TmEmailImportDialog`).** Two modes (MJML / JSON) as a core `TmTabs`
  strip, a `TmFileDropZone` that names the supported formats and the limit, and a `TmCodeEditor`
  instead of a bare `<textarea>`. The limits come from the new `ImportOptions`
  (`EmailImportOptions`): `MaxInputBytes` (measured in UTF-8 bytes, default 5 MB — the value the
  dialog used to hard-code) bounds both the pasted text and the read file, and the section/block/depth
  limits go to `MjmlImporter` and to `EmailTemplateSerializer.Deserialize(json, options)`. A parsed
  input shows a state card (success / warning / error, with an icon and the section, block and warning
  counts) that expands into the localized warning list, plus a section → column → block structure
  preview with the localized block names. Every failure is a localized sentence keyed by
  `SerializationKeys.*` / `ImportKeys.*` — the exception message never reaches the UI — and a failed
  parse keeps both the pasted input and the document. The footer carries Zrušit / Importovat with the
  primary action disabled until the input parses, and the document is replaced only by the caller's
  `OnImport` (one undo step in the editor).
- **Export dialog rebuilt (`TmEmailExportDialog`).** Three modes (MJML / JSON / HTML) as a core
  `TmTabs` strip with a read-only `TmCodeEditor` per mode (correct Prism language), an icon copy
  button in the code corner with a polite live-region confirmation, and a footer with Zavřít plus a
  primary “Stáhnout {MJML|JSON|HTML}”. MJML is generated with `MjmlGeneratorOptions.ForExport`
  (lossless, including `mj-html-attributes`); JSON is the canonical content JSON; HTML goes through
  `IEmailPreviewRenderer` with `SubstituteVariables = false`, so the exported file keeps the
  `{{ … }}` tokens, with explicit loading / unavailable / failed states. The download uses the
  existing core helper `tmDataTable.downloadFile` with the slugged file name
  (`{slug(name)|email-template}.{mjml|json|html}`) and the right MIME type. Generation happens on
  OPEN and on a TAB CHANGE only — the old dialog regenerated on every parent render
  (`OnParametersSet`). The dialog title is “Export” (EM5).
- **Validation dialog (`TmEmailValidationPanel`).** A per-severity count summary (errors / warnings /
  suggestions) above findings that are real `<button>` elements (keyboard operable; the old
  `<li @onclick>` broke the keyboard-activation convention) with a severity icon, a TITLE, a
  DESCRIPTION and a “Go to” action that jumps to the block. Each rule key now has
  `{rule}_Title` / `{rule}_Description` in all four tables (`ValidationKeyShape.TitleOf` /
  `DescriptionOf`), the document is validated when the dialog OPENS (not on every parent render), the
  host's `ImportOptions` limits are part of the findings, and the dialog has a Zavřít footer.
- **`TmEmailTemplateEditor.ImportOptions`** (`EmailImportOptions?`, additive): the editor forwards the
  same limits to the import dialog and the validation panel, so “what the editor accepts” and “what the
  server accepts” cannot drift apart.
- **The public surface of the import/export/validation dialogs, confirmed by the user (§3.8/§3.10 of the
  contract).** `ValidationKeyShape` (`TitleSuffix`/`DescriptionSuffix`/`TitleOf`/`DescriptionOf`) is the
  one place that composes a rule's `_Title`/`_Description` keys; `ImportKeys.BlockedLink`,
  `ImportKeys.InvalidColor` and `ImportKeys.DroppedAttribute` are the import-side audit keys (an
  unusable link, a colour the message cannot carry, an attribute the pipeline may never write — the
  detail is the tag and the name, never the value); `EmailTemplateMapper.ToDocument(contentJson,
  EmailImportOptions?)` plus the `ApplyCreate`/`ApplyUpdate` overloads let the SERVER enforce the same
  limits as the import, and `ReportEmailTemplateGalleryStore(EmailImportOptions?)` applies them to the
  report-gallery store; `TmEmailValidationPanel.ImportOptions` puts the same limits into the findings;
  `TmEmailExportDialog.LayoutMode` / `TmEmailImportDialog.LayoutMode` take the editor's already resolved
  layout. All of it is additive — the parameterless members stay.
- **`TmCopyButton.OnCopied` and `TmCodeEditor.CopyButtonCopied` (core, additive).** The copy button
  now tells its host when the text really reached the clipboard (never when the clipboard refuses the
  write), so a read-only surface can confirm the copy in its OWN live region instead of hanging a
  handler on the box around it — a click in the box is not a copy.
- **Copy / retry / large-export affordances of the export dialog.** The copy
  confirmation comes from `TmCopyButton.OnCopied` and is reset before it is set, so a SECOND copy is
  announced again; the HTML tab explains a renderer that is not configured
  (`EmailEditor_Export_HtmlNotConfiguredHelp`) or unreachable (`EmailEditor_Export_HtmlUnreachableHelp`)
  and the unreachable case offers a real retry (`data-tm-export-retry`); an export over 200 000
  characters is still complete but renders without syntax highlighting, with a line saying so
  (`EmailEditor_Export_LargeNoHighlight`). Each format's content lives in the `TmTabPanel` it belongs
  to, so the strip's `aria-controls` points at a panel that exists.
- **Import dialog: the mode follows the file/content.** The drop zone accepts
  `.mjml,.html,.json,.txt` on BOTH tabs, a `.json` file switches the mode, and a pasted document that
  starts with `{` is parsed as JSON instead of failing as MJML. The pasted text is measured against
  `EmailImportOptions.MaxInputBytes` BEFORE parsing (`EmailEditor_Import_InputTooLarge`, with the
  actual limit), and the state card carries the replace note (`EmailEditor_Import_ReplaceNote`) so the
  destructive step is stated before the user presses Import.
- **Validation panel: the good outcome and the quiet counts.** “No issues found” is a
  success card with the check icon and the success text token, a severity whose count is zero drops its
  severity colour (`tm-email-validation__count--zero`), the “syntax was not checked” note sits under the
  findings it qualifies, and “Go to” on a DOCUMENT finding opens the e-mail settings (nothing selected)
  instead of closing the dialog onto an unchanged canvas.
- **`RenderKeys.InvalidAttributeValue` / `ImportKeys.DroppedAttribute` (additive).** An attribute value
  the message cannot carry is now reported when the generator drops it, and an imported attribute the
  pipeline may never write is warned about at import (`import.dropped_attribute`) instead of living in
  the model as a value every export silently refuses.
- **Shortcuts help subtitle.** The editor passes
  `TmKeyboardShortcutsHelp.Description` (“Shortcuts work with an external keyboard.”) and lists ↑ / ↓
  as two separate key alternatives instead of one chord (F8 API).
- **Table grid: accessible, sectioned, scrollable (`TmEmailTableEditor`).** The grid is now a
  `<table>` with a `<caption>`, a localized `aria-label` on every cell ("Row {0}, column {1}"), a
  pinned control column (`position: sticky`), a visually distinct header row, a "Header" section with
  the "First row is a header" toggle, a "Rows and columns" section, and an "Edit cell" button on every
  cell that opens `TmEmailTableCellDialog` (text, link, colspan, rowspan, alignment, background, the
  row's header flag, plus a mini table preview with the edited cell highlighted) — in both item
  editing modes. The block ships its own scoped `TmEmailTableEditor.razor.css` (design tokens only),
  the actions wrap into a grid at a narrow width and the icon controls are at least 32 px
  (`--tm-touch-target` on a coarse pointer).

- **`TmChat` slots: composer, banner, header, empty state and the built-in avatars.** Hosts can
  replace the built-in composer with `<ComposerTemplate Context="composer">` (a subscribe gate, a
  PPV field, an owner note) while keeping the component's send path and draft guard: the template
  receives a live `ChatComposerContext` (`Text`, `SetTextAsync`, `SendAsync` — the same path as the
  built-in send button, including `OnSendMessage`/`OnSend` and the submitting state — plus
  `CanSend`, `Disabled`, `IsSubmitting`, `FocusAsync()` and `InputId`), so pushing the typed text
  through `SetTextAsync` keeps `HasUnsavedDraft` / `OnDraftChanged` covering a replaced composer.
  Around the built-in composer, `ComposerAddon` renders an owner note above the input and
  `ComposerFooter` a footnote below it (both only with the built-in composer — a
  `ComposerTemplate` owns the whole area). `ShowComposer="false"` drops the composer area from the
  DOM entirely (and ignores `ComposerTemplate`). `BannerContent` renders a connection banner above
  the messages — deliberately NOT a live region: put `role="status"` on content INSIDE the slot if
  it should announce, so TmChat keeps exactly one live region. `HeaderContent` renders at the very
  top, `EmptyContent` replaces the built-in empty state while the conversation is empty, and
  `ShowAvatars="false"` hides the built-in author avatars (default `true` = today's look). A host
  that sets none of the new parameters compiles and renders exactly as before.

### Fixed

- **Spreadsheet: the AutoFilter funnels render again and the context menu keeps the keyboard focus.** Two real defects the phase-7d regression gate uncovered. (1) `drawFilterButtons` pushed each funnel with `columnWidth: read(colFrame, "Width", …)`, but `colFrame` exists only in `drawSelectionOverlay` — the `ReferenceError` aborted the whole content paint inside its `requestAnimationFrame` AFTER `state.filterButtons` had been cleared, so the Filter toggle, the header dropdowns and every custom-filter spec silently stopped working with no DOM change at all. The funnel now uses its own painted cell width, and `resolveFilterButtonHitRect` takes the target's OWN box (`boundsTop`/`boundsHeight`) so the coarse-pointer hit rect stays on the funnel's row instead of jumping up into the column-header gutter (a phone tap on the funnel was impossible; a tap on the gutter opened the menu). Pinned by `spreadsheet-canvas-filter-buttons.test.mjs` (`npm run test:spreadsheet`, 3 tests, stub 2D context). (2) The grid's canvas focus restore was probe-then-focus (`isFocusOutside` → `ElementReference.FocusAsync`); the host-owned context menu focuses its first entry from its own `OnAfterRenderAsync` in the same render batch, so the probe answered "still in the grid" and the focus hop landed ~25 ms later and stole the caret back — the menu's ArrowDown / Home / End / Escape walk was dead in a real browser while every DOM assertion passed. The guard is now ONE atomic JS call (`tmSpreadsheetCanvas.focusGridUnlessFocusMovedAway`: check and focus in the same task), and the host can stand the restore down entirely through the new `TmSpreadsheetCanvasGrid.SuppressFocusRestore` (fed by the open context menu / resize dialog). Pinned by `TmSpreadsheetContextMenuFocusTests`.
- **Spreadsheet E2E (phase 7d): the specs reach a command in the COMPACT chrome, and the phone dialogs are opened from the desktop ribbon.** Since phase 6 the chrome follows the CONTAINER, so at a tablet width there is no ribbon tab strip, and a phone has no entry at all for the advanced commands (G2 keeps Data validation, Name Manager, the custom Sort, Text to columns, Remove duplicates and Paste special desktop/tablet only). The pre-phase-6 helpers clicked `.tm-spreadsheet-toolbar__tab` and timed out (30 s) on `button[title='Custom sort…']`. A shared `SpreadsheetChromeHelpers` partial now opens a command by its frozen identity — the desktop tab strip plus the button, or the compact row's `data-command-id`, or that row's "More" menu (two taps) — and EVERY spec that needs a command the phone cannot reach opens it on the desktop chrome and narrows the viewport afterwards (the phase-7c rotated-phone pattern), so the phone/tablet PRESENTATION assertions are unchanged. `SpreadsheetPhase6ResponsiveE2ETests.Phase6_NotionEditModal_At390_IsMobile_AndKeepsTheFooterInView` no longer reports `Inconclusive`: the seeded Notion page has no SAVED spreadsheet block, so the spec opens the modal through the real "Create Spreadsheet" entry point of the empty block and then asserts `data-layout="mobile"` plus the Save / Discard footer at 390 × 844 and 568 × 320. Test-only change: no component, token or DOM contract moved.
- **Core: the `TmModal` header's × is optically centred on the title line.** The header is a flex row aligned to `flex-start`, so the close box shared its TOP edge with the title's first line box (`--tm-font-size-lg` 1.125rem × `line-height` 1.3 = 23.4px) and the icon's centre sat ~4px below the title's centre in every dialog of the library. `.tm-modal-close` now declares the local knob `--tm-modal-close-size` (**2rem** on a fine pointer) and carries

  ```css
  margin-block-start: calc((var(--tm-font-size-lg) * 1.3 - var(--tm-modal-close-size)) / 2);
  width: var(--tm-modal-close-size);
  height: var(--tm-modal-close-size);
  ```

  A `@media (pointer: coarse)` block in the SAME file (`components/_modal.css`, after the base rule — `breakpoints.css` is imported before the components, so a knob declared there would lose to this file's default) republishes it as `--tm-modal-close-size: var(--tm-touch-target)`. That is what keeps the icon centred at BOTH sizes: the coarse-pointer touch floor is 44px, and a literal `2rem` offset would have put the icon 6px low on every phone. **The target size is unchanged** (2rem on a fine pointer, 44px `--tm-touch-target` on a coarse one — `breakpoints.css` still owns the `min-width`/`min-height` floor), the header keeps its padding and row order, no new animated subject is introduced, and the phone header reads ~10px shorter because the box no longer overhangs the title line. `--tm-modal-close-size` is a per-element knob, not a design token: a host that changes its modal's × size sets it on `.tm-modal-close` (any later declaration would also move the optical offset with it). The fix lives ONCE in the core stylesheet (not per package dialog) and the committed `tempo-blazor.bundled.css` is regenerated. Guarded by `TmModalTests.Modal_Header_CloseButton_SharesTitleLineBox` (markup + the component stylesheet + the media-override ordering + the bundle) and by the E2E `Phase7c_TmModal_CloseButton_IsCentredOnTheTitleLine` (|Δ| ≤ 1px) on a Spreadsheet dialog and two core demo modals (with a subtitle, with a header icon).
- **The Spreadsheet canvas follows a live theme flip (no resize needed).** The palette is a snapshot of the resolved tokens, so flipping `data-theme` / `data-tm-theme` on a live page recoloured the chrome while the canvas kept the OLD colours until the `ResizeObserver` fired (the phase-2 dark spec had to nudge the viewport to work around it). One `MutationObserver` on `documentElement` per grid instance now rebuilds the palette (`buildPalette`) and requests a FULL redraw on either attribute change; it is disconnected in `dispose`, and a host without `MutationObserver` keeps the previous resize-only behaviour.
- **The Spreadsheet active header strip is opaque in dark mode.** `--tm-spreadsheet-header-active-bg` resolved through `--tm-color-primary-subtle`, a `rgb(from ... / 0.15)` relative colour, so the 0.15-alpha wash over the dark header surface was barely visible (22 % is the NEW dark mix, not the old light value) and a translucent strip let the cell grid show through while a row was scrolled. The package theme layer (`wwwroot/css/theme-spreadsheet-dark.css`, `:where([data-theme="dark"], .tm-dark) .tm-spreadsheet` — wrapped in `:where()` so a host's own `.tm-spreadsheet` token override still wins in dark) now re-mixes the token with `color-mix(in srgb, var(--tm-color-primary) 22%, var(--tm-spreadsheet-header-bg))` — still token-only, no hex, and the core `tokens-dark.css` is untouched. The canvas mixes that `color-mix()` itself (`parseColor` / `resolveColorToken` in `spreadsheet-canvas.js`, which also parses the `color(srgb ...)` form Chromium computes), because an unregistered custom property keeps the function unevaluated and a backend that refuses it in `fillStyle` would silently keep the previous style. The node lane pins it with `buildPalette_DarkActiveHeader_IsOpaque` (alpha 1, mixed channels) and the phase-2 visual spec pixel-samples the D/5 header. The light theme's `primary-subtle` wash is unchanged.

- **`TmTabs` dynamic badges reach the header strip, with the resync bounded (phase 13 review).** The headers are built by `TmTabs` from its registered panels, so a `Badge` (or `Title`/`Icon`/`Disabled`) that changes AFTER the strip of the same pass was built — the Relations tab's related-count badge — used to lag a render. `TmTabs` re-renders ONCE to resync, and the resync is bounded to one extra render per OUTSIDE render pass (`_headerResyncRendered`): a NON-IDEMPOTENT header input (a title re-evaluated per fragment execution) used to feed the resync with a fresh value on every pass — an unbounded render loop; now it costs exactly one resync render and settles (`TmTabsTests.Non_idempotent_title_does_not_render_loop` pins ≤ 2 renders per parent render, `Badge_change_after_parent_rerender_reaches_header` pins the reach). A strip whose header inputs are static stays a single render.

- **DiagramEditor Escape closes the TOPMOST layer only — one press closes exactly ONE layer (Fáze 10, confirmed ordering).** The layer order is now the context menu > "⋯" view menu > search panel > an inline edit > a running gesture/selection > the host dialog — the REVERSE of the previous search-before-menu behavior (the search consumer ran in the capture phase before the menu's handler was even registered, so with both open the search closed and the menu stayed; now `_onSearchEscape` skips while `_menuOpen` and the view menu outranks the search panel). An Escape typed into an INLINE EDIT of the canvas (the `.tm-diagram-edge-label-input` foreignObject input, a `.tm-diagram-node__inline-input`/`-textarea` section editor, a swimlane header or a table cell) now CANCELS the edit deterministically — the value reverts, nothing is pushed to the undo stack — and is consumed (`preventDefault` + `tmEscapeHandled`), so the open-editor dialog stays open and the next Escape continues with the layer order. The consumer resolves the owner: a node editor through its registered `TmDiagramStencilShape` (new `[JSInvokable] CancelActiveEditFromJs`), everything else through the canvas' new `[JSInvokable] OnInlineEditEscape` (`CancelEdgeLabelEdit`); the Blazor `@onkeydown` Escape branches on the inputs stay as idempotent fallbacks. Node tests: `diagram-editor-escape.test.mjs`; bUnit: `TmDiagramCanvasTests.Escape_in_edge_label_input_cancels_without_command`; E2E: `ModelingOpenInEditorDialogE2ETests` (menu > search > dialog, and the inline-edit cancel).

- **`Tempo.Blazor.Modeling` final whole-plan review: a single dialog instance, a tree render gate, a tablet issues sheet, a usable canvas and a labelled mobile status (final code + UX review over the Modeling redesign).** The review pass over the whole plan implemented the following — every item tightens an existing contract, none is a new phase:
  - *The open-editor dialog is ONE instance across the 768 boundary (MAJOR).* `@OpenEditorModalContent` and `@ChangeViewSheetContent` rendered inside BOTH layout branches, so a flip across the editor's own 768px threshold tore the dialog down and rebuilt it — a new `TmDiagramEditor` instance and a fresh JS engine boot mid-session. Both fragments now render ONCE, as siblings after the `<TmLayoutObserver>` inside the editor root `<section>`; the fullscreen-vs-dialog choice rides the `TmModal` `MobilePresentation` parameter from the resolved layout, and the `focusWithin` scope moved to the editor root (the single surface that contains the close button and every focus-return host in every layout). bUnit flips the editor Tablet → Mobile → Tablet with the dialog open: the same `TmDiagramEditor` instance (reference equality) and exactly one modal.
  - *Single focus-restore owner on dialog close.* The dialog's `TmModal` now passes the new additive `RestoreFocus="false"` (forwarded to the `TmFocusScope`, which renders `data-restore-focus="false"` and skips its own restore) — the editor's `focusWithin` close path is the one owner, so a mobile close cannot race a restore target that does not exist there (the desktop preview trigger id). Default `true` keeps every other modal unchanged.
  - *The mobile band has NO tree→preview insert.* The docs said "reuse is the non-drag insert" — wrong: G2 viewing renders neither the "+" button nor the drag grip (the insert is a desktop/tablet alternative to a gesture the band cannot express); edits go through "Open in editor". The code already agreed; the wording is fixed in `docs/modeling-editor.md` and the AGENTS.md Modeling section.
  - *A snapshot render gate on `TmModelingModelTree`* (the Wireframe render-gate pattern): the tree re-renders only when a render-affecting parameter changed (the `Elements` reference, the selected element, the `CollapsedGroups` reference, the filter text, `AllowNodeDrop`, `CanInsertIntoPreview`, `ShowTitle`, `Class`, the UI culture) or an internal interaction ran (filter edit, group toggle, selection, keyboard focus move). A parent re-render that changes nothing — the editor re-rendering for its own state — no longer re-renders the 200-row tree (M26; `RenderCount` is the test seam). The editor also caches the concatenated `DisplayIssues` list keyed on the (`_model`, `_issues`) references, the mobile action-bar item list and the Source tab attributes dictionary — the per-render rebuilds were the remaining allocations on every pass. Keep `TmModelingEditor_ElementsShort` / `_RelationshipsShort` out of the long-label assumptions: the status card labels are SHORT now.
  - *DiagramEditor Escape ordering tightened* (`diagram-editor.js`, node tests in `diagram-editor-escape.test.mjs`): an Escape typed into a canvas INLINE EDIT (an input/textarea inside the editor canvas container — the edge-label foreignObject input) is consumed (`preventDefault` + `tmEscapeHandled`) even when no search panel or view menu is open, so the host dialog does not close under the caret; the canvas shortcut handler's `document.body` fallback is skipped when the canvas sits inside an `[inert]` subtree (the Modeling preview behind the open dialog — the dialog's editor owns the keys); and the selection-clear Escape sets `tmEscapeHandled` too.
  - *The `Height` parameter rejects non-CSS-length values*: anything carrying `;`/`{`/`}` (or not matching a simple length / single-`calc()` pattern) falls back to the stylesheet contract — the inline style is never an injection vector. bUnit `TmModelingEditorSingleStateTests` covers the accepted/rejected shapes and the fallback.
  - *Usable desktop canvas with zero issues (M1).* The canvas body gets a `tm-modeling-editor__canvas-body--issues-empty` modifier (`grid-template-rows: minmax(0, 1fr) auto`) when the model has no issues — the dock is a one-line empty state (`.tm-modeling-issue-panel__empty` is now a compact single line) instead of a clamped 32% block. The preview's embedded editor keeps the ZOOM toolbar group only: the search + "⋯" header-bar row is gone with its groups (the DE renders no header bar without content — a Zoom-only toolbar no longer paints a dead 48px row), and the preview header's nodes/edges summary is opt-out (`TmModelingDiagramPreview.ShowSummary`, default `true`) because the status bar already carries the counts. E2E asserts `.tm-diagram-canvas` ≥ 300px at 1440x900 with the empty dock.
  - *Tablet issues are a side sheet, not a dock (M2).* The tablet band renders a fourth `modeling-panel-tabs` entry (Issues, with the count badge) that opens a non-modal side sheet (`modeling-issues-sheet`, close button `modeling-issues-sheet-close`) under the same ONE-open rule as the tree drawer and the inspector sheet — no dock row under the canvas on this band, so the touch canvas keeps its floor with issues open. Re-review: the positioning lives on an editor-owned `tm-modeling-editor__issues-sheet-host` wrapper — the `TmFocusScope` root is a child component and never receives the editor stylesheet's scope attribute, so the sheet-anchoring rule on the scope itself was dead (the sheet painted unpositioned). The host is `position: absolute` over the canvas column's end edge (`min(20rem, 100%)` wide, `--tm-z-inline-sheet`), and the sheet body's issue list scrolls inside it.
  - *The mobile status card is labelled (M3).* Each tile shows the aria-hidden type icon, the count and a SHORT visible label (`TmModelingEditor_ElementsShort` / `_RelationshipsShort` + the existing `_Nodes`/`_Edges`, en/cs/sk/fr + `MockTmLocalizer`) that wraps to two lines (`-webkit-line-clamp: 2`) — the sr-only-only numbers were unreadable without the card's context, and a hard ellipsis cut a long cs/sk word at 320px. The card still keeps the canvas ≥180px at 320x640.
  - *The recoverable single-state screens carry a Retry button (M4)* (`modeling-editor-retry`, Secondary, `Refresh` icon, the shared `TmModelingEditor_Reload` label driving `ReloadModelAsync`) on the error screen and on the empty screen when a provider/loader is configured; the docked Left/Right panels render nothing while no workspace is mounted (the shell now receives `Left`/`Right` as VALUE attributes — the section syntax wrapped the fragment, so a null slot painted an EMPTY aside).
  - *The preview refits after a dock collapse/expand (M5).* `TmModelingDiagramPreview.RefreshViewportAsync()` (new; delegates through the new additive `TmDiagramEditor.FitToViewAsync()` — a real zoom-to-fit, the same path the document load and the Fit-to-view command use) runs from the editor's `OnAfterRenderAsync` after `SetIssuesCollapsedAsync` arms it, so the diagram refills the grown/shrunk canvas box and the zoom report follows (the earlier `relayout`-only path re-derived the scale report without re-fitting the content). Re-review: the embedded preview also pins the DE's `LayoutBreakpoints` to `(600, 1200)` — the docked canvas column sits NEAR the DE's own 768px mobile threshold (760px at 1440x900), so a width nudge during a dock toggle could flip the embedded editor between its mobile and tablet presentations and repaint a chrome row above the canvas; with the dropped mobile threshold the docked preview (a ≥ ~620px column at the editor's 1200px desktop floor) never presents the DE mobile band — the docked bands get page tabs + canvas + the status-bar zoom — while a real G2 column (≤ 600px, the 320/390 baselines) keeps the DE's compact mobile presentation, whose chrome the G2 band drops through `ShowEmbeddedEditorChrome` instead. The open-editor dialog DE keeps its own Auto + 768/1100 pair.
  - *Review minors (m1–m4, m6).* LeftWidth 260px; the tree's `__node-meta` is secondary text; the docked toolbar rows center their items and the provider field caps at `calc(var(--tm-space-16) * 5)`; the status strip icon is the alert triangle with a `--stale` warning tint while the source is stale (both bands); the mobile Inspector tab carries the "Stale" badge; the mobile title group wraps. m5 (the DE page background in dark) is a DiagramEditor-plan carry-forward. The `Height` documentation and the dialog DE contract (`docs/modeling-editor.md`) were rewritten for the Auto + 768/1100 resolution, the stale `focusSelector` mention was merged into the correct `focusWithin` entry, and the superseded phase-6 trailing-column wording is marked as such.

  - *The empty / error / loading-without-model screens keep the mobile chrome.* The compact band now ALWAYS renders the `tm-modeling-editor__mobile-shell` (compact header + "Change view" sheet + a REDUCED `TmMobileActionBar` with only Reload and Change view), with the single-state screen where the tabs would be — no tab strip, no status card, no Generate/Open tiles (they need a model). The shell is also the focus scope again on those screens, so the open-editor dialog close and the focus return stay in it. A host or test that asserted "no action bar on the error screen" must assert the reduced bar instead (`[data-action-id='reload']` / `[data-action-id='change-view']`).
  - *An issue/edge tap on mobile is an inspector intent.* The former `OpenInspectorOnTabletAsync` is `OpenInspectorForSelectionAsync`: on the tablet band it opens the inspector side sheet (unchanged) and on the mobile band it activates the Inspector panel tab, so the selection surfaces the element immediately.
  - *The dead mobile tab CSS is fixed.* The `[data-layout='mobile']` tab rules were anchored on `.tm-modeling-editor__panel-tabs`, a class that lives on the CHILD-rendered `TmTabs` root and therefore never carried the editor's scope attribute — the whole block (the tab flex/shrink/ellipsis pair, the clipped tab panel, the header touch targets) never applied, which is why the Issues tab pushed the strip wider than the editor at 320. The rules are now anchored on the editor-rendered `.tm-modeling-editor__mobile-panels` wrapper: the tab panel is a clipped flex column, the panel body is the single scroll surface (`flex: 1 1 0; height: auto; overflow: auto`), the shell itself is `overflow: clip` and never scrolls (the action bar cannot be pushed below the fold by long issue lists), and the mobile tab strip gets `flex: 1 1 auto; min-width: 0` with `padding-inline: var(--tm-space-2)` and an ellipsized label plus the new short `TmModelingEditor_TreeShort` label (en "Tree", cs/sk "Strom", fr "Arbre") — at 320px in en/cs/sk/fr the Issues tab's right edge stays inside the editor.
  - *The status card moved into the Preview tab body* (a shell-level card stole ~110px from every tab) — it is a `flex-shrink: 0` row above the scrolling panel on that one tab, `aria-atomic="true"`, with a two-tile-per-row grid (`repeat(2, minmax(0, 1fr))`, wrapping labels) and the short `TmModelingEditor_Nodes` / `TmModelingEditor_Edges` count labels (cs/sk "Uzly"/"Hrany", fr "Nœuds"/"Arêtes"); the docked status strip keeps the long forms. New resource keys in all four tables + `MockTmLocalizer`: `TmModelingEditor_TreeShort`, `TmModelingEditor_Nodes`, `TmModelingEditor_Edges`.
  - *The mobile preview fills its tab and drops the dead chrome.* The preview section is a flex column whose embedded editor host stretches over the full remaining height (no dead gap below the canvas), and on the mobile band the host passes `ShowEmbeddedEditorChrome="false"` (new parameter on `TmModelingDiagramPreview`, default `true`): the embedded `TmDiagramEditor` gets `ShowToolbar="false"` through its public API only, because its header bar would there hold ONLY the "⋯" trigger (the floating zoom pill duplicates the canvas pinch). The DE page-tabs row has no public hide switch — recorded as a remaining task for the DiagramEditor plan.
  - *The demo `/modeling-editor` page gives the editor the remaining viewport height on narrow widths* (`calc(100dvh - 11.5rem)` below 1024px), so the in-flow action bar is inside the first paint at 390x844 and 320x640 without a page scroll.
  - *Review minors.* The header "⋯" mobile sheet is titled "More options" (`TmModelingEditor_MoreOptions` — `TmDropdown` now passes its `AriaLabel` to the overlay panel, so icon-only triggers name their sheet); the open-editor dialog returns focus to the ACTUAL trigger (the action-bar "More" or the header "⋯"; `focusWithin` accepts a comma-separated priority list, the `tm-modeling-editor__more-host` div stays the fallback); the mobile Issues tab hides the collapse toggle (new `TmModelingIssuePanel.ShowToggle`, default `true`) and shows a plain heading; Generate carries the wand icon so the adjacent Reload keeps Refresh; the fullscreen mobile dialog subtitle clamps to one line; the editor selects ellipsize; the recommended-fix box wraps (`flex-wrap`, `flex: 1 1 10rem` text, `overflow-wrap: break-word` instead of `anywhere` for the fix text and the message).
  - *Behavior notes (documented, no code change).* Switching the mobile panel tabs remounts the Preview/Tree bodies (`TmTabs` renders only the active body — the M26 budget), so the preview's pan/zoom resets on every tab switch; and `AllowNodeDrop="false"` drops the tree rows' `draggable` attribute and the drag grip on EVERY layout (the non-drag "Insert into preview" alternative stays).

- **`TmModelingEditor` phase 7 re-review: the 320px preview is visible again, the state bars pin to the bottom and mobile selection focus follows the tab.**
  - *The mobile status card is ONE compact row.* The two-row label-tile grid (~110px) is gone: the card renders the four counts as a single row of numbers (`repeat(4, minmax(0, 1fr))`), each tile's label is an `sr-only` span (the `role="status"` card keeps its `aria-label`), and the loaded line is sr-only text in the same live region — the state itself stays on the header badge (MO3 dedupe). The single text line returns the height to the preview canvas at 320px.
  - *The preview's own heading block is opt-out on mobile.* New `TmModelingDiagramPreview.ShowHeader` (default `true`): the mobile band passes `false` because the header's "N nodes, M edges" summary duplicated the status card's counts in the same tab. The root gets a `tm-modeling-diagram-preview--no-header` modifier that drops the header grid row. **Mobile preview zoom is pinch-only; the zoom buttons live in "Open in editor"** (a zoom-only overlay switch for embedded viewers is a remaining task on the DiagramEditor plan).
  - *The preview canvas keeps a floor.* `.tm-modeling-diagram-preview__canvas-shell` gets `min-height: calc(var(--tm-space-16) * 3)` (also on the mobile band, where it was zeroed) — a short tab body can no longer collapse the canvas to a sliver; the panel scrolls instead. E2E measures `.tm-diagram-canvas` ≥ 180px at 320x640 and ≥ 240px at 390x844.
  - *The empty / error single-state screen is the flex remainder on mobile* (`[data-layout='mobile'] .tm-modeling-editor__mobile-shell > .tm-modeling-editor__single-state { flex: 1 1 0; min-height: 0; overflow: auto; }`), so the reduced action bar sits at the editor's bottom edge (E2E asserted on `?scenario=error` at 390) and tall error detail scrolls inside the screen.
  - *A mobile tree tap stays on the Tree tab (G2 browsing).* Only an issue or edge selection switches the mobile Inspector panel — and that switch now MOVES FOCUS onto the panel: the compact inspector aside carries `data-modeling-focus="inspector-panel"` + `tabindex="-1"` and the editor calls `focusWithin` with the new stable `TmModelingEditor.InspectorPanelFocusSelector` hook after the tab switch (progressive enhancement, swallowed without interop).
  - *The open-editor focus-return selector resets on close.* `CloseGeneratedDiagramAsync` snapshots the actual trigger list for the pending restore, then resets `_openEditorFocusReturnSelector` to `OpenInEditorFocusSelector`, so a NEXT dialog opened by the desktop preview trigger cannot inherit a stale mobile trigger. The header "⋯" open/close round-trip is pinned by bUnit and an E2E (focus returns to the `.tm-modeling-editor__more .tm-dropdown-trigger`).
  - *Fallback order fix.* The mobile shell writes `overflow: hidden; overflow: clip;` — browsers without `clip` support keep clipping instead of scrolling the shell open. The demo `/modeling-editor` page documents its narrow-viewport `100dvh` height override as DEMO-ONLY (hosts own the height through the `Height` parameter). A new cs 320 baseline (`modeling-editor-mobile-cs-320x640`) pins the compact band under the Czech culture.

- **`TmModelingEditor` phase 5 review: unforced shell, 768/1200 breakpoints, a usable issues dock and a truthful Source tab (Modeling redesign plan, review fixes).**
  - *The docked shell is no longer pinned to the editor's resolved mode.* The shell now receives `LayoutMode` / `Breakpoints` / `InitialMode` so an `Auto` shell measures its own container with the Modeling pair — the nested `TmDiagramEditor`s (the preview and the open-editor dialog) measure THEIR OWN containers instead of inheriting a forced Desktop cascade: the preview's `data-editor-layout` follows the canvas column width (a 768–1199px canvas resolves tablet under a desktop editor), and the dialog body decides its own layout through the DE's Auto resolution with the dialog pair 768/1100 (final review — never a pin to the editor's resolved mode). A forced editor (`LayoutMode` set) still pins the shell for tests and hosts.
  - *The Modeling breakpoints are 768/1200* (user decision) — the same pair as `TmDiagramEditor`, so the two editors flip layouts at the same container width; the 768–899 tablet band became 768–1199. The demo `/modeling-editor` page collapses the demo sidebar and lifts its `max-w-7xl` cap from 1400px up (the wireframe page pattern), so a 1440x900 viewport gives the editor ≥1200px of container and the 1280x800 baseline shows the docked tablet band.
  - *The issues dock is usable.* The expanded dock row is `clamp(10rem, 32%, 20rem)` of the canvas column with a 16rem MINIMUM for the canvas row and tighter list padding (two full issue rows fit at both desktop baselines), the dock header is a 0.5rem-tall strip with a 32px toggle (44px on coarse pointers), and the empty state dropped its `min-height` floor so it never clips at 1280x800. The preview's drop hint and dashed drop-zone border render only WHILE a model-tree drag is live, and the preview keeps ONE toolbar row: the Viewer group set minus `export` through `TmDiagramEditor.ToolbarGroups` (no CSS on the editor's internals).
  - *The Source tab is a truthful accessible name.* The stale marker is the localized "Stale" badge (tinted with the warning tokens via `data-stale`) instead of a "•" glyph, the tab keeps its visible label as the accessible name (no `aria-label`), and the stale hint is an sr-only span OUTSIDE the tablist referenced by `aria-describedby` (per-instance id). The dock body always renders (a collapsed dock hides it with the `hidden` attribute), so the toggle's `aria-controls` never points at a missing id; the count badge sits next to the title; the inspector tablist is named (`TmModelingEditor_Inspector`); the fr/sk collapse toggles say "panneau des problèmes" / "panel problémov".
  - *New opt-in `PersistKey`.* The shell's `PersistWidthsKey` is derived per instance — `{TestIdPrefix}-modeling-editor` by default, or the explicit `PersistKey` — so two editors on one page no longer share saved widths by accident. `Height` is documented as a CSS length only, the Properties tab attributes are cached, the view selector aligns its fields to the start (the viewpoint hint no longer shifts the row), and the compact (<768px) inspector still stacks source + properties + issues — the tabbed restyle stays phase 6/7 scope.

- **TmGantt redesign, phase 1 (B15, B21–B23, GA3): the Gantt sub-components are styled, the portfolio draws tasks, and nothing is dead UI.**
  - **B21 — the export / import / mapping dialogs, the history drawer, the filter panel, the workload grid, the portfolio and the colour swatch were unstyled.** Their rules lived in the scoped `TmGantt.razor.css`, which rewrites every selector to carry `TmGantt`'s scope attribute, so a class rendered by a child component never matched. Each rule now lives next to the component that renders the class (`TmGanttExportDialog.razor.css`, `TmGanttImportDialog.razor.css`, `TmGanttImportMappingDialog.razor.css`, `TmGanttHistoryDrawer.razor.css`, `TmGanttFilterPanel.razor.css`, `TmGanttWorkloadView.razor.css`, `TmGanttPortfolio.razor.css`, and the swatch in `TmGanttTaskPanel.razor.css`). The dialog shell shared by three components (`.tm-gantt__dialog-overlay`, `__dialog`, `__dialog-header|title|close|body|actions`) is a global sheet, `wwwroot/css/components/_gantt-dialog.css`, imported by `tempo-blazor.css` (decision `GANTT-DIALOG-SHELL-GLOBAL`). Class names are unchanged; values are moved verbatim (tokenisation is the next phase). `GanttScopedCssOwnershipTests` pins the Gantt share of the ownership baseline at zero.
  - **B22 — `TmGanttPortfolio` always rendered empty Gantts.** It passed `Data=` / `Dependencies=`, which are not parameters; it now passes `Items` / `DependencyItems`. It also inherits `TmComponentBase` (`Class`, `DataTestId`, `TestIdPrefix`, splatted attributes). Every nested Gantt gets the test-id prefix `gantt-{project.Id}`, so task bars of tasks that share an id across projects stay unique.
  - **B23 — the task panel now receives what the host gave the Gantt.** `ActiveTimerTaskId`, `OnTimerStarted` and `OnTimerStopped` were never forwarded, so the panel's timer could not start or stop. New additive parameters `OnDescriptionChanged`, `OnAttachmentUpload` and `OnAttachmentRemoved` on `TmGantt` are forwarded to the panel.
  - **B23 — no enum names or hard-coded date patterns reach the user.** Filter operators ("contains", "is before", …) and import-mapping targets are localized (`TmGantt_FilterOp_*`, existing column keys); the history drawer's empty state shows `TmGantt_HistoryEmpty`; the sidebar history uses the localized change type; history timestamps and the workload column dates follow the localizer's culture (`g` pattern, the culture's own day/month order) instead of `dd.MM.yyyy HH:mm` / `dd.MM`.
  - **B15 — `Fit to screen` no longer calls `eval`.** It measured `document.querySelector('.tm-gantt__timeline')`, which is blocked by a CSP without `unsafe-eval` and measured the first Gantt on the page (wrong inside a portfolio). It now measures its own timeline through an `ElementReference` and the new `tmGantt.getClientWidth(el)` in `gantt.js`. `ContainerWidth` is documented and overrides the measurement (tests, prerendering). The new zoom is the current level scaled by container / timeline width (the width already includes the zoom), floored to the 25 % step, so fitting twice is a no-op. The history timestamps are shown in the user's display zone (`TmGanttHistoryDrawer.TimeZone`), and the toolbar toggles expose `aria-expanded` / `aria-pressed`.
  - **Import** — the "Import" button is disabled until a file is chosen (Excel / MS Project) or the JIRA URL, token and project key are filled; it used to silently do nothing. The import error surface has its own class `tm-gantt-import__error`.
  - **Accessibility** — every icon-only toolbar / sidebar / panel / dialog button has a localized `aria-label` (including the filter row remove button and the colour swatches); the Day / Week / Month switch reports `aria-pressed` and the active view is `Secondary`; the tree expand button reports `aria-expanded`; the export and mapping dialogs are `role="dialog"` + `aria-modal` + `aria-labelledby`, trap focus and close on Escape (they move to `TmModal` in phase 6).
- **Gantt "today" and the hours-zoom marker follow the injected clock and the display zone.** `TmGantt.TodayInZone` used to return `DateTime.Today` whenever the resolved zone equalled `TimeZoneInfo.Local`, so a display zone that happened to match the machine ignored the user's zone and the injected `TimeProvider`. It now converts `TimeProvider.GetUtcNow()` (the system clock when none is registered) into the zone: no zone service keeps the machine-local day, an unresolved zone stays UTC, and a resolved zone — including one equal to `TimeZoneInfo.Local` — is converted. `GanttHelper.GetCurrentTimeOffset` gains an overload that takes the instant; the existing signature is unchanged and still reads `DateTimeOffset.Now`. The hours-zoom marker passes the zone-converted clock, so it no longer sits at `DateTime.Now` when the zone matches the machine. `TmGanttWorkloadView.Today` still defaults to `DateTime.Today`; the Gantt already passes `TodayInZone()`.
- **An event template in the time grid and the timeline is no longer clipped to one line.** Before, `EventTemplate` rendered inside `span.tm-scheduler-event-content`, whose rule is `overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis; white-space: nowrap`, so a multi-line template written for the month cell was cut to a single line. The template now renders directly into the card. The visually-hidden accessible name, the card `title` and the resize handles are unchanged. The built-in time and title stay direct children of the card and keep their own ellipsis; the timeline default does not wrap them. `span.tm-scheduler-event-content` is a host opt-in: the same rule exists under the time-grid card and the timeline card. A host that relied on the wrapper to clip its own template puts the class on its own markup:

  ```razor
  <EventTemplate Context="evt">
      <span class="tm-scheduler-event-content">@evt.Title</span>
  </EventTemplate>
  ```

  This is a visual change, not an API change: no parameter or signature was removed. A template taller than the card is still cut at the card edge.
- **`TmMultiSelect` sheet keyboard follows the panel's resolved layout.** With `MobilePresentation="Auto"` and `LayoutMode="Auto"` the listbox used to read the parameter, which stays `Auto`, so on a real phone the options had no `tabindex` and no `aria-activedescendant` even though the popup had opened as a sheet. The listbox now follows `TmOverlayPanel.IsSheet`. A forced `Sheet`, or `Auto` with `LayoutMode="Mobile"`, is unchanged.
- **Calendar and multi-select accessible markup moved.** See Breaking / Migration. The classes `.tm-calendar`, `.tm-cal-nav`, `.tm-cal-day` and `.tm-multiselect__options` are unchanged, and the popup root still keeps `display: flex`.
- **Three Spreadsheet dialogs no longer render as an unstyled block in the document flow under the grid.** The Name Manager, Named Range Edit and Hyperlink dialogs had no stylesheet rule in `Tempo.Blazor.Spreadsheet` at all, so they landed *below* the grid as raw markup. They now ship a fixed overlay on the `--tm-z-modal` band plus a card (sticky table header, `--tm-color-primary-subtle` selected row with a primary rail, header close button), and the overlay keeps the grid where it was. The card is a column capped to the viewport (`max-height` propagated from the backdrop through the focus-scope wrapper), so a long name list or a short window scrolls the middle instead of pushing the footer off screen. The DOM changes (`role="dialog"`, `aria-modal`, `aria-labelledby`) are listed under Breaking / Migration.
- **The Spreadsheet validation alerts are `alertdialog`s with a focus contract.** A Stop-style error used to be a plain box that any backdrop click dismissed; it now ignores the backdrop click entirely — the value stays blocked and only its primary action (or Escape) dismisses it. Both alerts are one component, `TmSpreadsheetValidationAlert`, wrapped in the core `TmFocusScope`: it focuses the primary action when it opens, closes on Escape, and puts focus back on the grid when it closes. A warning/information confirm keeps its backdrop-to-cancel and its deferred-commit flow — confirming still commits the deferred value, cancelling still discards it. Screen readers announce the alert as a dialog and read the title (`aria-labelledby`) and the message (`aria-describedby`).

- **The Spreadsheet Format Cells category list and the Name Manager rows are keyboard operable.** Both lists use a roving tabindex: the selected option / row is the single tab stop (`tabindex="0"`, every other `-1`) and owns the DOM focus, so ↑/↓ plus Home/End move the selection and the focus together (the item scrolls into view) and no `aria-activedescendant` is involved — the containers keep only `role` and their accessible name.
